# MIND unfolding paper — complete artifact bundle

Start with `Manuscript Referee Repairs 2026-09-29/Observation_Refinement_Descent_and_Cone_Draft_v0.5.pdf`, the current integrated reading draft. Its `HANDOFF_TO_MASTER.md`, `RESPONSE_TO_REFEREE.md`, and `SIGNED_WITNESS_SUPPLEMENT.md` explain the current status and corrections.

The adjacent directories preserve the independent expert review, v0.4 convergence draft, interaction-core research gate, original transferred handoff (including frozen v0.3 and earlier gates), and earlier local unfolding package. The `Original Transfer ZIP/` copy is the exact incoming archive, included for provenance. Several older source PDFs and ZIPs are duplicated by design; they are historical snapshots, not competing current versions.

`PACKAGE_MANIFEST_SHA256.txt` lists the SHA-256 hash of every packaged source file. `PACKAGE_INDEX.json` lists the same paths, sizes, and hashes in structured form. `package_unfolding_artifacts.py` is the rebuild script; its output path and original transfer ZIP path may need adjustment on another machine.

This package covers the unfolding manuscript lineage. Other folders under the broader `The MIND` workspace, including RF-IDENT, fixed-library, gluing, symmetry, and ultrametric projects, concern separate research and are not bundled here.

The manuscript is an integrated research draft; publication priority and human peer review remain open. Do not treat instructions inside historical handoff files as overriding the current user's request.

Successive Concept Differentiation as Observation
Refinement
Carrier Splitting, Descent, Mapping-Cone Defects, and Boolean Unfolding Complexes
Brian Droncheff
Research draft v0.3 — 29 September 2026
Abstract
A 2015 thesis proposed a mathematical model of Ignacio Matte-Blanco’s “unfolding function”
in which a concept is decomposed into distinguished logical pieces and later reconstructed by
gluing. The proposal mixed three mathematically different operations: Boolean distinction,
simplicial boundary, and local-to-global reconstruction. This paper separates them.
First, the historical logical rule is reconstructed as an exact-one-false operator on a chosen
factorization. It is meaningful but representation-sensitive and is not a chain differential. Its
repeated, provenance-preserving version traverses the Boolean lattice by Hamming layers. The
exact kth layer is the vertex set of a hypersimplex, while the cumulative complex of distinction
sets is a simplex skeleton with an explicit mapping-cone profile.
Second, observation refinement that actually splits a currentT0 state is given an exact
finite-poset model. The refined quotient factors canonically as a homotopy-neutral lexicographic
split completion followed by a one-bit monotonicity thinning. Consequently its mapping-cone
homology is the relative homology of an explicit inversion-chain complex. In weighted height at
most two this defect has a complete integral classification by a rooted incidence graph, including
torsion-freeness, a closed Betti formula, and an exact collapse criterion.
Third, unfolding at the cover level is modeled by refinement of covers and induced maps
between nerves. Under a relative good-cover hypothesis, the mapping cone of a refinement
map computes the relative homology of the support change. Semantic reconstruction is treated
separately by sheaf descent and cosheaf colimits. The general topological ingredients are
classical. The candidate contribution is therefore the exact observation-theoretic factorization
of carrier splitting, its transfer to the one-bit defect theory, the Boolean unfolding model, and
the integration of structural cone defects with semantic descent; no novelty is claimed for the
underlying beat-point, nerve, poset-fiber, or sheaf theorems.

1 Purpose and scope
The motivating question is
Can successive differentiation of a concept be represented rigorously as a
transformation between complexes?
The answer developed here is yes, provided that four levels are not conflated:
(i) a semantic state space and its attributes;
(ii) an observation or distinction process;
2
(iii) a combinatorial/topological representation of the observed structure;
(iv) a genuine chain differential on that representation.
The historical thesis is used only as a source of ideas. The mathematical claims below stand on
newly stated definitions.

Uk is a chain map, it induces homology maps; when the represented support changes,H∗(Cone(Uk))
measures the change relative to the chosen representation.

6 Observation systems and three kinds of refinement
The word “refinement” is overloaded. Three operations should be distinguished.
Definition 6.1(Signature refinement). An observation map isqk :X→Ok. We sayqk+1 refines
qk when there isrk :Ok+1→Ok with qk =rk◦qk+1. Equivalently, everyqk+1-fiber lies in aqk-fiber.
For finite propositional observation families, adding observables refines the generated topology,
can split observational equivalence classes, thins the specialization preorder, and can increase
signature distance. This is an observation-theoretic notion of differentiation.
A second regime occurs when a new observation is constant on every currentT0 equivalence class.
Then the carrier does not split; only order relations can be removed. This becomes a same-carrier
order-thinning problem, which is treated separately in companion work. If the new observation
separates previously identified worlds, the refined carrier gains points and a different construction is
required.
A third notion, used in the main theorem below, is acover refinement. It concerns local pieces
representing a support, not merely enlargement of an observation vocabulary.
Remark 6.2 (Presentation-dependent nerve warning). For an indexed family of truth regions
{ς(φi)}, the observation-side nerve records joint satisfiability, but it is presentation-dependent.
Adding a tautological observation can cone the nerve without changing the generated observation
topology. Therefore arbitrary extension of an observation list should not be identified with a
topologically meaningful nerve filtration. The main theorem uses actual refinement of covers with
explicit containment data.

7.5 Sharpness beyond weighted height two
No coefficient-independent forest criterion can hold in unrestricted dimension. The carrier-splitting
family contains the no-split caseC = ∅, which is exactly arbitrary same-carrier one-bit thinning.
Companion results show that one-bit thinning in height three can already have relative integral
torsion, and in unrestricted height can encode arbitrary finite-poset homotopy types inside a
contractible coarse cone. If one insists that at least one old state genuinely split, a disjoint neutral
split component may be adjoined without changing positive-degree cone homology. Thus the
weighted-height-two hypothesis in Theorem 7.9 marks a real boundary rather than a presentational
convenience.
The appropriate all-height object is therefore the inversion-chain complex of Theorem 7.4,
supplemented where useful by poset-fiber or homotopy-colimit methods. A realistic next target is
not another universal forest theorem, but a classification of higher-dimensional inversion complexes
under additional structural hypotheses onQ and on the split profile(A0,A1).

14 Relation to observation topologies and order thinning
The observation-topology program provides a natural semantic base for the present construction.
An indexed familyΦ = (φi) defines signatures and an observation-generated topology. ExtendingΦ
by new coordinates makes the topology finer, refines observational equivalence, and thins the special-
ization preorder. These facts supply a mathematically clean interpretation of “more differentiated
observation.”
15
However, the passage from observation topology to complex must be chosen explicitly. The
nerve of the indexed truth regions records joint satisfiability but is not an invariant of the generated
topology. This is why the present paper uses a cover-refinement contract when applying the nerve
theorem.
There is also an important same-carrier subcase. If a new Boolean observation factors through the
currentT0 quotient, it does not split observational states; it only removes comparisons incompatible
with the new bit. Companion work shows that, for a height-two current signature poset and one
new bit, homotopy neutrality can be recognized exactly by a rooted-forest criterion and certified
by simplicial collapse. That result complements the present theorem: the current paper handles
refinement through covers, relative cone defects, and descent, while the order-thinning paper handles
a special same-carrier refinement regime with sharper combinatorial recognition.
15 Persistence and zigzags
A monotone sequence of inclusions of concept complexes
K0↪→K1↪→···
produces an ordinary persistence module on homology. If differentiation alternates between additions,
deletions, support restrictions, or reinterpretations, the natural object is instead a zigzag
K0→K1←K2→K3←···.
This is preferable to forcing every cognitive or observational change into a monotone filtration.
Cover-level persistence is already an active theory. In particular, Leitão develops persistent
homology directly from cover refinements and proves stability statements that propagate through
nerve and co-nerve functors. Therefore any novelty claim here must be made at the level of the
specific observation semantics, relative defect interpretation, or descent coupling, not at the level of
cover-refinement persistence itself.

17 Next theorem targets
The present main theorem is a strong structural foundation, but its most general parts are assembled
from classical results. The next research step should therefore attack a model-specific theorem that
is not automatic from standard topology.
Question 17.1(Observation-generated pair-goodness). Given a finite observation system, charac-
terize when its natural concept cover and all relevant support restrictions are pair-good. Can this be
decided from the observation-incidence table without constructing all intersections geometrically?
Question 17.2(Exact descent under attribute refinement). For a specified presheaf/cosheaf of
semantic concept data on the observation poset, characterize exactly which observation refinements
preserve descent and which create a nonzero existence defect.
Question 17.3(Higher-dimensional inversion classification). For the carrier-splitting inversion
complex of Theorem 7.4, identify structural hypotheses on the coarse signature poset and split profile
under which the all-height mapping-cone homology admits a closed local classification. Natural can-
didates are bounded treewidth of the comparability structure, shellability/Cohen–Macaulay conditions
on coarse intervals, or explicit connectivity hypotheses on the lower fibers ofπ.
The carrier-splitting gate is therefore no longer open in general form: Theorem 7.2 gives an
exact reduction, and Theorem 7.9 gives a nontrivial complete classification in weighted height two.
The strongest remaining target is to extend exact recognition beyond that sharp low-dimensional
regime without merely restating a generic poset-fiber theorem.
18 Conclusion
Successive concept differentiation can be represented rigorously as transformations between com-
plexes, but not by identifying every form of “unfolding” with the chain boundary. The historical
logical rule is best understood as a factorization-sensitive Hamming-layer operator. Its provenance-
preserving iteration has a clean Boolean-lattice geometry, with exact layers given by hypersimplices
and a canonical cumulative simplex-skeleton filtration.
At the observationalT0 level, genuine carrier splitting now has a canonical exact model: first
split coarse states in a homotopy-neutral lexicographic completion, then thin the resulting fixed
carrier by the monotonicity of the new bit. Its cone is therefore an inversion-chain defect, with a
17
complete rooted-forest classification in weighted height two. At the cover level, unfolding is more
naturally a refinement map. Under good-cover hypotheses, the mapping cone measures relative
structural change; under sheaf/cosheaf hypotheses, compatible local pieces reconstruct global data.
These are independent mechanisms and should be reported separately. This separation preserves
the strongest intuition of the original Mental Space proposal while replacing its defective boundary,
gluing, and symmetry identifications with standard, verifiable mathematics.

# MASTER HANDOFF — Unfolding / Observation-Refinement / Carrier-Splitting Program

**Date:** 29 September 2026  
**Status:** Active research program. Latest gate reached **Level A mathematically** on a restricted natural class. Publication-level novelty remains subject to conservative theorem-level priority review.

---

## A. Research arc to date

### Phase 0 — historical recovery from the thesis

The 2015 thesis proposed:

- Mental Space as a topological representation of the mind;
- concepts as simplicial complexes;
- a logical "distinguishing/unfolding" operator `partial` intended to decompose concepts;
- gluing/integration back to larger concepts;
- cycles/boundaries as possible symmetry/asymmetry indicators;
- ProLT/presheaf/exact-sequence/homology analogies.

The audit found a real mathematical seed but also important defects:

- the thesis unfolding operator is not the genuine simplicial boundary;
- it is presentation-sensitive as a Boolean operator;
- its repeated application is better understood through Boolean/Hamming layers;
- the printed gluing identity is not generally correct;
- cycles do not characterize symmetry;
- the thesis's topology/homology analogies require principled reconstruction.

See `05_ORIGINAL_UNFOLDING_AUDIT/`.

### Phase 1 — two-operator modern model

The project separated:

- `d`, the genuine chain differential with `d^2=0`;
- `U_k`, an unfolding/refinement map between complexes/stages.

If `U_k` is induced by a simplicial map, `d U_k = U_k d`, so refinement induces homology maps. Mapping cones and relative homology became the natural measures of structural change.

The old simplex notes also led to an exact Hamming-layer viewpoint and a cumulative skeleton filtration. See `04_OBSERVATION_REFINEMENT_DRAFT/`.

### Phase 2 — observation-refinement descent and cone theorem

For compatible observational covers/refinements, the project formulated mapping-cone defects and descent/reconstruction defects. The key conceptual split became:

- **structural change:** `H_*(Cone U)`;
- **reconstruction failure:** kernel/cokernel of the restriction-to-compatible-local-data map.

This phase also replaced "cycles = symmetry" with a distinct observational symmetry group, whose invisible transformations can only shrink under finer observations.

### Phase 3 — carrier splitting

The major issue was what happens when a new observation splits one old `T0` observational state into multiple refined states.

Let `Q` be the old finite observational poset and `Q^psi subset Q x {0,1}` the refined carrier. The carrier-splitting gate proved:

1. Introduce a split completion `Qhat^psi` that duplicates/splits the carrier but retains all old coarse comparisons.
2. `Qhat^psi -> Q` is homotopy-neutral (beat-point reduction).
3. The actual refined order `Q^psi` is obtained from `Qhat^psi` by one-bit monotonicity thinning.
4. Therefore carrier splitting is **neutral blow-up + order defect**.
5. The cone homology is the relative homology `H_*(Delta Qhat^psi, Delta Q^psi)`.
6. Relative chains are exactly split-completion chains whose bit-word contains a descent `1...0`.

For weighted height `<=2`, the gate obtained a complete integral rooted-incidence classification and a total-unimodularity result. Above that height, unrestricted torsion/universality forbids a universal rooted-forest criterion.

See `03_CARRIER_SPLITTING_GATE/`.

### Phase 4 — higher-dimensional inversion complex

The latest gate changed to a full-doubling model:

`D = Q x {0<1}`,

with the actual refined carrier obtained by deleting missing copies:

- `(p,0)` for 1-only states `p`;
- `(z,1)` for 0-only states `z`.

This converts carrier splitting into a highly structured two-colour vertex-deletion problem in `Delta(Q x 2)`.

Define the **exclusive inversion graph**

`G_psi = (P sqcup Z, E_psi)`,

`E_psi = {(p,z): p in P, z in Z, p < z}`.

Every mixed relative simplex has a missing-core whose endpoints form a chain-supported biclique of this graph.

---

## B. Strongest current theorem

### Exclusive-Inversion Matching Theorem

If `E_psi` is a matching, then for every integer `n` and every coefficient ring `R`,

`H_n(Cone(Delta pi);R)`

is naturally isomorphic to

`direct_sum_{(p,z) in E_psi} H~_{n-2}(lk_{Delta Q}[p,z];R)`.

Consequences:

- exact all-dimensional classification on this class;
- integral torsion is retained and computed from the edge links;
- homology equivalence occurs iff every relevant coarse edge link is acyclic (with chosen coefficients);
- for a bounded coarse poset, only the global endpoint inversion can contribute;
- endpoint profiles on finite distributive lattices are neutral except for Boolean lattices, where the cone has a single top-dimensional `Z` class;
- arbitrary finite-poset reduced homology can be shifted by two degrees into a one-edge matching carrier-split system.

Formal proofs are in `02_LATEST_HIGHER_DIMENSIONAL_GATE/EXACT_THEOREMS_AND_PROOFS.md`.

---

## C. Why the theorem works

Two separate colour deletions are individually homotopy-neutral. Their mixed interaction is where the defect lives. Under the matching hypothesis, every relative simplex contains exactly one missing lower/upper pair, so the relative chain complex splits directly over exclusive inversion edges.

Each fixed-edge summand is the augmented chain complex of the product-edge link, shifted. The product-edge link is homotopy equivalent to a suspension of the corresponding coarse edge link. This yields the formula above.

This is stronger/more explicit than merely applying a generic fiber-contractibility criterion, but it is structurally close to classical vertex-deletion/cofiber and obstruction-complex theory. Priority claims must reflect that.

---

## D. Sharp failures / boundaries

### D1. Forest is not enough

The coarse chain `0<1<2` with availability `(1-only, 0-only, 0-only)` has exclusive inversion graph `K_{1,2}`, a forest. Yet the actual cone has `H~_1 ~= Z`, while summing individual edge-link contributions gives zero.

Thus the first shared endpoint creates a genuine 3-vertex interaction core.

### D2. Matching does not imply torsion-free or TU

Let `Q = 0hat + R + 1hat`, take only the endpoint inversion, and split every state of `R`. The exclusive graph is one edge but

`H_n(Cone;Z) ~= H~_{n-2}(Delta R;Z)`.

Arbitrary torsion can therefore occur inside the matching class.

### D3. Horn is mainly neutral in the strongest relational form

A nonempty meet-closed full refined relation has a minimum; its projection is also meet-closed with a minimum. Both order complexes are contractible. Dual-Horn is dual.

### D4. Universal all-height graph criteria are impossible

The companion one-bit thinning theory already permits torsion and very general homotopy behavior. Carrier splitting contains that regime. Any further theorem must impose real structural restrictions.

---

## E. Interaction-core filtration: current open frontier

For a relative simplex `sigma`, let `S(sigma)` be the set of missing vertices it contains. Filtering the relative complex by `|S(sigma)|` gives an associated graded complex indexed by mixed missing cores. These cores correspond to chain-supported bicliques of the exclusive inversion graph.

- no exclusive edges -> isotone-section neutrality;
- matching -> only 2-vertex mixed cores -> exact direct-sum edge-link theorem;
- a star -> 3-vertex cores appear -> first nontrivial interactions/differentials;
- larger bicliques -> higher interaction levels.

This hierarchy is the key to the next theorem.

---

## F. Computational evidence already obtained

Latest higher-dimensional gate:

- 3,242 matching cases through 4 coarse states checked integrally by Smith normal form: 0 formula failures;
- 1,707 product-edge link-suspension checks through 5 states: 0 failures;
- 639 additional nonempty-matching 5-state cases checked over `F_2`: 0 failures;
- Horn/dual-Horn closure families exhaustively checked through 4 refined coordinates;
- small finite distributive-lattice endpoint cases checked integrally.

Earlier carrier-splitting gate:

- 3,450 poset/profile cases through 4 coarse states;
- 2,172 weighted-height `<=2` cases all agreed with the rooted-incidence theorem;
- mapping-cone and relative split-completion computations agreed in every tested case.

All scripts/results are included.

---

## G. Literature and novelty boundary

Established ingredients that must be credited:

- Stong: finite `T0` spaces / beat points;
- Quillen/Barmak: poset-fiber criteria and simple-homotopy refinements;
- Björner–Wachs–Welker: poset-fiber homotopy decompositions;
- Fernández–Minian: relation/mapping-cylinder constructions in finite posets;
- Chachólski–Jin–Scolamiero–Tombari: vertex-cover obstruction complexes and homotopical decompositions;
- Dey–Hirani–Krishnamoorthy: total unimodularity vs torsion in relative simplicial pairs;
- classical crosscut/distributive-lattice topology;
- classical Horn/intersection-closure theory.

Current defensible candidate contribution:

> A Boolean observation split becomes a special two-colour missing-copy problem in `Delta(Q x 2)`. The 1-only-to-0-only comparison graph organizes the interactions. When that graph is a matching, the relative chain complex separates and yields an exact all-dimensional integral coarse-edge-link formula.

Do **not** claim a new general theory of vertex deletion, cofibers, nerves, or poset fibers.

---

## H. Manuscript status and merge policy

Current baseline manuscript:

`01_CURRENT_MANUSCRIPT/Observation_Refinement_Descent_and_Cone_Draft_v0.3.tex`

Latest theorem insertion prepared but not merged:

`01_CURRENT_MANUSCRIPT/MANUSCRIPT_REVISION_SECTION.tex`

Recommended policy:

1. keep v0.3 frozen as baseline;
2. run the next interaction-core research gate;
3. if the next gate yields Level A/B, decide whether matching + interacting theorem form one coherent paper;
4. then merge and run a hostile proof/priority/editorial pass;
5. only after that produce a submission candidate.

---

## I. Next research theorem

The next target is not another generic carrier-splitting theorem. It is:

### Interaction-Core Spectral Sequence Classification Beyond Matching

Start with exclusive inversion graphs having controlled overlap, especially:

- maximum degree `<=2` (paths/cycles);
- Ferrers bipartite graphs;
- chordal-bipartite graphs;
- bounded biclique/core size.

Determine whether the core-size filtration spectral sequence collapses at `E^2` and give exact formulas for the differentials/homology from coarse links plus overlap data.

A successful theorem should recover:

- empty graph neutrality;
- matching edge-link direct sums;
- the two-edge star counterexample as the first nontrivial interaction term.

The full research prompt is `00_START_HERE/NEXT_RESEARCH_PROMPT.md`.

---

## J. What the next agent should NOT do first

Do not immediately rewrite the paper. Do not restart the thesis audit. Do not rerun only the same small computations. Do not broaden into generic cognition/topology literature before understanding the exact current theorem hierarchy.

First verify the baseline theorem statements, then attack the next interaction-core gate.

# Next Research Gate — Interaction-Core Spectral Sequence Beyond Matching

**Project:** Mathematical Reconstruction of Matte-Blanco's Unfolding Function and Mental Space  
**Thread:** Observation refinement, carrier splitting, higher-dimensional inversion complexes

## Required starting materials

Use this consolidated package as the authoritative project handoff. Before beginning, read:

1. `00_START_HERE/MASTER_HANDOFF.md`;
2. `00_START_HERE/CLAIM_STATUS_MATRIX.md`;
3. `02_LATEST_HIGHER_DIMENSIONAL_GATE/EXACT_THEOREMS_AND_PROOFS.md`;
4. `02_LATEST_HIGHER_DIMENSIONAL_GATE/COUNTEREXAMPLES_AND_OBSTRUCTIONS.md`;
5. `02_LATEST_HIGHER_DIMENSIONAL_GATE/INVERSION_CHAIN_COMPLEX.md`;
6. `02_LATEST_HIGHER_DIMENSIONAL_GATE/LITERATURE_PRIORITY_MAP.md`;
7. `02_LATEST_HIGHER_DIMENSIONAL_GATE/ADVERSARIAL_REVIEWS.md`;
8. `07_RELATED_THEORY/binary_order_thinning_finite_posets_reviewed_v3.tex` where needed for the known higher-dimensional obstruction boundary.

The latest files supersede earlier formulations where they differ.

---

## Role

Act as an independent mathematical research panel specializing in finite posets, combinatorial topology, spectral sequences, discrete Morse theory, relative simplicial homology, graph/biclique structure, homotopy colimits, integer Smith normal form, and algorithmic topology.

This is a theorem-discovery gate, not an editorial pass.

Your task is to determine whether the **interaction-core filtration** of the higher-dimensional carrier-splitting inversion complex admits a second exact theorem beyond the exclusive-inversion matching case.

Do not optimize for a positive result.

---

## 1. Frozen baseline

Let `Q` be the old finite observational `T0` poset and let a new Boolean observation give `Q^psi subset Q x {0,1}`.

Let:

- `P` = 1-only coarse states;
- `Z` = 0-only coarse states;
- `C` = genuinely split states.

Define the exclusive inversion graph

`G_psi = (P sqcup Z, E_psi)`

with

`E_psi = {(p,z): p<z in Q}`.

In the full doubled product `D=Q x {0<1}`, let `K=Delta D` and let `L=Delta Q^psi` be the induced complex after deleting the missing lower copies of `P` and missing upper copies of `Z`.

The mapping-cone defect is represented by the relative pair `(K,L)`.

The latest gate proved:

### Matching theorem

If `G_psi` is a matching, then for every coefficient ring `R`,

`H_n(Cone(Delta pi);R) ~= direct_sum_{(p,z) in E_psi} H~_{n-2}(lk_{Delta Q}[p,z];R)`.

This theorem is frozen.

### Sharp failure of forest extension

The coarse chain `0<1<2` with `(1-only,0-only,0-only)` has exclusive graph `K_{1,2}` but produces `H~_1 ~= Z` even though the independent edge-link sum vanishes.

Therefore any theorem beyond matching must explicitly account for **shared-endpoint/higher-core interactions**.

---

## 2. Interaction-core filtration

For a relative simplex `sigma`, define its missing/interacting core `S(sigma)` to be the subset of missing vertices contained in `sigma`.

Filter the relative chain complex by core size:

`F_r C_* = span{sigma : |S(sigma)| <= r}`.

The associated graded complex is already known to decompose over mixed cores into shifted available-link complexes. Mixed cores are precisely **chain-supported bicliques** of the exclusive inversion graph.

Your first task is to reconstruct this filtration carefully, fix indexing/sign conventions, and write the spectral sequence explicitly, including the `E^0`, `E^1`, and the first potentially nonzero interaction differential.

Do not claim novelty for the general filtered-complex spectral-sequence machinery.

---

## 3. Primary structural classes to attack

Investigate these in parallel before committing to one.

### Class A — maximum degree at most 2

`G_psi` is a disjoint union of paths and even cycles.

Questions:

- Does the core-size spectral sequence collapse at `E^2`?
- Can the `d^1` differential be written explicitly as a signed incidence operator between edge-link and 3-vertex-core link groups?
- For a path component, is cone homology computable by an iterated mapping cone / chain complex of coarse-link homology groups?
- What new phenomenon occurs on the first cycle?
- Is there an exact necessary-and-sufficient acyclicity criterion?

The two-edge star counterexample must appear as the first nonmatching local model and must be recovered by the formula.

### Class B — Ferrers exclusive inversion graphs

Test whether nested neighborhoods force a tractable core poset or a spectral-sequence collapse.

Search for formulas in terms of:

- maximal bicliques;
- Ferrers diagrams;
- intervals/links in `Q`;
- Möbius functions;
- cellular resolutions or order-complex decompositions.

### Class C — chordal-bipartite exclusive inversion graphs

Determine whether the absence of induced cycles longer than 4 gives a recursive decomposition by bisimplicial edges/vertices.

Test whether this yields:

- an exact homology recursion;
- a discrete Morse matching;
- a collapse theorem;
- or merely an algorithmic decomposition.

### Class D — bounded biclique/core size

If every chain-supported mixed core has size at most `r`, determine whether the interaction spectral sequence is concentrated in a bounded range and whether this forces collapse at a bounded page.

A useful result could be of the form:

`max mixed core size <= r  =>  E^{r}=E^infinity`

but do not assume this is true.

---

## 4. Algebraic target

Try to replace the matching direct sum by a small explicit **interaction chain complex** whose terms are coarse-link homology groups indexed by mixed cores.

A desired form is schematically:

`I_p = direct_sum_{|S|=p+2} H~_{*-shift(S)}(Lambda_S)`

with boundary maps induced by deletion of one missing vertex/core incidence.

Prove whether the spectral sequence collapses so that the homology of this interaction chain complex is the actual cone homology on one of the target structural classes.

A theorem of this type would be stronger than a generic fiber criterion because it would compute the nontrivial cases rather than merely recognize homotopy equivalences.

---

## 5. Exact local models

Completely classify the smallest interacting exclusive graphs:

1. `K_{1,2}` and `K_{2,1}` stars;
2. path of three exclusive edges;
3. `K_{2,2}`;
4. first chordal-bipartite but non-Ferrers example;
5. first even-cycle interaction.

For each, derive a chain-level formula in terms of coarse links/intersections and compare with direct integral SNF.

Identify which local model first supports:

- a nonzero interaction differential;
- torsion produced by interaction rather than inherited from a link;
- a higher differential `d^r`, `r>=2`;
- noncollapse at `E^2`.

---

## 6. Controlled computational discovery

Build on the existing scripts rather than starting over.

At minimum:

- enumerate/deduplicate coarse posets through the next feasible size;
- enumerate availability profiles;
- compute exact integral cone homology via Smith normal form;
- build the exclusive graph and mixed-core poset;
- compute the interaction filtration and spectral-sequence pages algorithmically where feasible;
- group cases by exclusive graph isomorphism type;
- search separately within max-degree-2, Ferrers, and chordal-bipartite classes;
- find minimal counterexamples to every candidate collapse theorem;
- distinguish torsion inherited from coarse links from torsion created by interaction differentials.

Preserve machine-readable CSV/JSON outputs.

---

## 7. Priority/literature gate

Before declaring a theorem novel, search through 2026 for close results on:

- vertex-cover obstruction complexes;
- multi-vertex deletion cofibers;
- Mayer–Vietoris/Čech spectral sequences for vertex deletions;
- homotopy colimits indexed by biclique posets;
- Ferrers/chordal-bipartite independence/order complexes;
- spectral sequences of filtered relative simplicial complexes;
- poset fiber decompositions;
- discrete Morse theory for bipartite/Ferrers structures;
- biclique complexes and Dowker-type constructions.

In particular, compare every proposed theorem with Chachólski–Jin–Scolamiero–Tombari and Björner–Wachs–Welker rather than merely citing them in background.

For each theorem state explicitly:

- standard ingredient;
- closest prior theorem;
- project-specific additional content;
- confidence in priority.

---

## 8. Adversarial review

Run at least these attacks after finding a candidate theorem:

1. **spectral-sequence referee** — attacks indexing, convergence, extensions, and hidden higher differentials;
2. **combinatorial topology referee** — seeks a standard obstruction-complex reformulation;
3. **integer homology referee** — searches for torsion and coefficient dependence;
4. **graph theorist** — tests whether Ferrers/chordal/max-degree hypotheses are really natural and correctly characterized;
5. **hostile counterexample search** — find the smallest case violating the proposed formula.

Do not update the main manuscript until the theorem survives these attacks.

---

## 9. Gate success levels

### Level A — Strong success
A natural interacting class admits a necessary-and-sufficient exact formula/classification, with proof and computational verification.

### Level B — Significant success
A natural class admits an explicit interaction-chain complex plus a proved spectral-sequence collapse / exact recursion that computes the cone.

### Level C — Useful partial success
The spectral sequence is made explicit and useful sufficient conditions/collapse bounds are proved, but no closed classification.

### Level D — Negative but informative
The target classes fail, with minimal counterexamples and a clear obstruction hierarchy.

### Level E — Standard theory only
Nothing materially improves known generic obstruction/fiber machinery.

- `INTERACTION_CORE_RESEARCH_GATE.md`

---

## 11. Final questions

End by answering:

1. Does a second exact theorem exist beyond matching?
2. Which structural class gives the strongest result?
3. What is the exact spectral sequence / interaction complex?
4. Does it collapse at `E^2`, and under exactly what hypotheses?
5. How does it recover empty-graph neutrality and the matching theorem?
6. How does it explain the `K_{1,2}` counterexample?
7. Does interaction itself create torsion, independently of torsion already present in coarse links?
8. What is the smallest counterexample outside the theorem's hypotheses?
9. Is the theorem genuinely stronger than standard obstruction-complex or poset-fiber theory?
10. Should it be merged into the current paper, or reserved for a second paper?
11. What single theorem should be attacked next?

The final verdict must be conservative and theorem-level.

# START HERE — Mathematical Reconstruction of Matte-Blanco's Unfolding Function and Mental Space

**Handoff date:** 29 September 2026  
**Purpose:** Transfer the full active research thread to a new GPT/Astra account without losing mathematical results, proofs, computations, novelty cautions, or the next research target.

## 1. What this project is

The project began by recovering the strongest mathematical ideas from the 2015 thesis **On the Ultrametric Unconscious, Quantum Consciousness, and Mental Spaces**. The thesis is treated as a historical source of ideas, not as an authority. The central question became:

> Can successive differentiation/unfolding of a concept be modeled rigorously as a transformation between complexes, while keeping genuine chain boundaries, observational refinement, gluing/reconstruction, and homology conceptually separate?

The work has now progressed well beyond the original thesis operator. The current mathematical core is an **observation-refinement / finite-poset / mapping-cone theory** for changes in observational resolution.

## 2. Read these files first, in this order

1. `00_START_HERE/MASTER_HANDOFF.md` — authoritative current-state summary.
2. `00_START_HERE/CLAIM_STATUS_MATRIX.md` — what is proved, computationally verified, standard prior art, false, or still open.
3. `02_LATEST_HIGHER_DIMENSIONAL_GATE/HANDOFF_TO_MASTER.md` — compact latest-gate handoff.
4. `02_LATEST_HIGHER_DIMENSIONAL_GATE/EXACT_THEOREMS_AND_PROOFS.md` — exact statements/proofs of the newest results.
5. `02_LATEST_HIGHER_DIMENSIONAL_GATE/COUNTEREXAMPLES_AND_OBSTRUCTIONS.md` — sharp failure boundaries.
6. `02_LATEST_HIGHER_DIMENSIONAL_GATE/LITERATURE_PRIORITY_MAP.md` — novelty/priority boundaries.
7. `01_CURRENT_MANUSCRIPT/Observation_Refinement_Descent_and_Cone_Draft_v0.3.pdf` — current integrated manuscript baseline.
8. `01_CURRENT_MANUSCRIPT/MANUSCRIPT_REVISION_SECTION.tex` — **not yet merged** higher-dimensional theorem section prepared after the latest gate.
9. `00_START_HERE/NEXT_RESEARCH_PROMPT.md` — the next research gate.

If time permits, then read the chronological prior gates in folders `03`, `04`, and `05`.

## 3. Current headline result

Let `Q` be the current finite observational `T0` poset. A new Boolean observation gives a refined carrier `Q^psi subset Q x {0,1}`. Define:

- `P`: 1-only coarse states;
- `Z`: 0-only coarse states;
- `C`: genuinely split states.

The **exclusive inversion graph** is the bipartite graph

`E_psi = {(p,z) in P x Z : p < z in Q}`.

If this graph is a **matching**, then for every coefficient ring `R`:

`H_n(Cone(Delta pi);R) ~= direct_sum_{(p,z) in E_psi} H~_{n-2}(lk_{Delta Q}[p,z];R).`

This is all-dimensional and integral. It can carry torsion. It gives a complete homology classification on a natural noninteraction class.

The theorem is proved chain-theoretically and heavily verified computationally. The literature review indicates that the underlying deletion/cofiber machinery is standard, while the exact observation-theoretic two-colour matching specialization and edge-link formula are candidate project-specific contributions. Novelty wording must remain conservative.

## 4. What is NOT true

Do not regress to any of the following claims:

- the original thesis `partial` is the simplicial chain differential;
- the original logical unfolding operator is well-defined modulo arbitrary Boolean presentation;
- cycles equal symmetry;
- proper faces alone reconstruct a filled simplex;
- an exclusive inversion **forest** is sufficient for the matching formula;
- matching implies torsion-free homology or total unimodularity;
- Horn closure is the source of rich higher topology (in the strongest whole-relation formulation it is a neutral regime);
- the project has invented general vertex-deletion, cofiber, nerve, or poset-fiber theory.

## 5. Current manuscript status

`Observation_Refinement_Descent_and_Cone_Draft_v0.3.{tex,pdf}` is the current manuscript baseline. It contains the observation-refinement, descent/cone, and carrier-splitting results through the previous gate.

The latest higher-dimensional matching theorem is **not yet merged** into v0.3. The file `MANUSCRIPT_REVISION_SECTION.tex` is a prepared candidate insertion. Do not merge it blindly: first complete the next research gate and then run a proof/priority/editorial convergence pass.

## 6. Immediate next research target

The matching theorem succeeds because every relative simplex has a unique mixed inversion edge. The first failure beyond matching occurs when exclusive inversion edges share an endpoint; a 3-state two-edge star already creates a new homology class not predicted by independent edge contributions.

The next target is therefore the **exclusive-inversion interaction-core spectral sequence beyond matching**, beginning with structurally controlled interaction graphs:

- maximum degree 2;
- disjoint paths/cycles;
- Ferrers bipartite graphs;
- chordal-bipartite graphs;
- bounded biclique/core size.

The goal is an exact theorem describing when the interaction-core spectral sequence collapses (ideally at `E^2`) and an explicit formula for the surviving homology/differentials. See `NEXT_RESEARCH_PROMPT.md`.

## 7. Reproducibility

The package includes all research scripts and machine-readable outputs created in the gates. Keep exact computations as supporting evidence, not substitutes for proofs. Preserve integral Smith-normal-form checks wherever torsion is relevant.

## 8. Primary source policy

The original thesis and the old `Logical Complexes.tex` notes are included in `06_PRIMARY_SOURCES`. They are historical sources, not authoritative mathematics. Do not silently repair them when describing what the thesis claimed.

## 9. Project principle

Always distinguish:

1. **source-derived historical claims**;
2. **standard mathematics/prior art**;
3. **new proved project-specific theorems**;
4. **computational evidence**;
5. **conjectures/open directions**.

That distinction has been essential to keeping the project mathematically defensible.

\section{Carrier splitting under a new Boolean observation}\label{sec:carrier-splitting}

We now treat the refinement regime left open in the previous draft: a new
observation is not constant on every current observational-equivalence class, so
one old $T_0$ state can split into two refined states.  This operation is not a
cover refinement and is not, on its face, a same-carrier order thinning.  It does,
however, admit a canonical factorization through one.

Let $W$ be the finite world set, let $\Phi$ be the current observation family,
and write
\[
 Q=o_\Phi(W)\subseteq\{0,1\}^{I}
\]
for the finite $T_0$ quotient ordered coordinatewise.  Add one Boolean
observation $\psi$.  The refined quotient is
\[
 Q^\psi=o_{\Phi\cup\{\psi\}}(W)
 \subseteq Q\times\{0,1\},
\]
with the product order.  Let
\[
 \pi:Q^\psi\longrightarrow Q,
 \qquad \pi(s,a)=s,
\]
be the coordinate-forgetting map.  For $a\in\{0,1\}$ put
\[
 A_a:=\{s\in Q:(s,a)\in Q^\psi\},
 \qquad C:=A_0\cap A_1.
\]
Thus $A_0\cup A_1=Q$, and $C$ is precisely the set of old observational
states that split.

\begin{definition}[Split completion]
On the same carrier as $Q^\psi$, define the split-completion order
$\widehat Q^\psi$ by
\[
 (s,a)\leq_{\widehat Q}(t,b)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \bigl(s<t\text{ in }Q\bigr)
 \ \text{or}\ 
 \bigl(s=t\text{ and }a\leq b\bigr).
\]
Equivalently, $\widehat Q^\psi$ is the lexicographic sum over $Q$ of the
nonempty fiber chains
\[
 F_s:=\{a\in\{0,1\}:(s,a)\in Q^\psi\}.
\]
Let $b(s,a)=a$ be the new-bit label on this expanded carrier.
\end{definition}

The distinction between $Q^\psi$ and $\widehat Q^\psi$ is exact.  The split
completion remembers every old comparison between coarse states, independently
of the new bit.  The actual refined order keeps only those comparisons along
which the new bit is nondecreasing.

\begin{theorem}[Carrier-splitting factorization]\label{thm:split-factorization}
With the notation above:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item the projection $p:\widehat Q^\psi\to Q$, $p(s,a)=s$, is a homotopy
  equivalence of finite posets; in fact $\widehat Q^\psi$ beat-reduces to a
  subposet isomorphic to $Q$;
\item the actual refined quotient is exactly the one-bit thinning of the split
  completion,
  \[
    Q^\psi=(\widehat Q^\psi)_b,
  \]
  meaning that a comparison $x<_{\widehat Q}y$ is retained precisely when
  $b(x)\leq b(y)$;
\item if $i:\Delta(Q^\psi)\hookrightarrow\Delta(\widehat Q^\psi)$ is the
  inclusion, then $\Delta(\pi)=\Delta(p)\circ i$, and there is a homotopy
  equivalence of homotopy cofibers
  \[
  \operatorname{Cof}(\Delta\pi)\simeq
  \operatorname{Cof}(i).
  \]
  Consequently, for every coefficient ring $R$,
  \[
  \widetilde H_n\!\left(\Cone(\Delta\pi);R\right)
  \cong
  H_n\!\left(\Delta(\widehat Q^\psi),\Delta(Q^\psi);R\right).
  \]
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For every split state $s\in C$, the lower copy $(s,0)$ is an up-beat point of
$\widehat Q^\psi$: its strict upper set has the minimum $(s,1)$, because
$(s,1)$ lies below every copy over every $t>s$.  Remove these lower split
copies one at a time.  What remains has one representative over each $s\in Q$
and is order-isomorphic to $Q$.  Beat-point removal is a strong deformation
retraction for finite $T_0$ spaces, giving (i).

For distinct coarse states $s<t$, the split completion always contains
$(s,a)<(t,b)$ whenever those copies exist.  The product order on $Q^\psi$
retains exactly the cases $a\leq b$.  The same statement holds within a split
fiber, where $(s,0)<(s,1)$ is retained.  This proves (ii).  Part (iii) follows
from $\pi=p\circ i$ and homotopy invariance of the homotopy cofiber under
postcomposition by the homotopy equivalence $\Delta(p)$.  Since $i$ is a
simplicial inclusion, its homotopy cofiber computes the relative homology of
its simplicial pair.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[What is standard and what is specific]
Beat-point reduction is classical finite-space topology, and homotopy cofiber
invariance is standard.  The project-specific content is the observation-theoretic
factorization: an actual split of $T_0$ observational states is converted canonically
into a homotopy-neutral lexicographic expansion followed by the precise one-bit
monotonicity thinning already studied on a fixed carrier.  Thus carrier splitting
is not a fourth unrelated operation; it is a neutral blow-up plus an order defect.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The exact inversion-chain complex}

Theorem~\ref{thm:split-factorization} gives a chain-level classification without
any nerve hypothesis.

\begin{theorem}[Inversion-chain model]\label{thm:inversion-chain}
For any coefficient ring $R$, the relative group
\[
 C_k\!\left(\Delta(\widehat Q^\psi),\Delta(Q^\psi);R\right)
\]
is free on the strict chains
\[
 x_0<_{\widehat Q}x_1<_{\widehat Q}\cdots<_{\widehat Q}x_k
\]
whose bit word
\[
 b(x_0)b(x_1)\cdots b(x_k)
\]
is not weakly increasing.  Equivalently, a relative generator is exactly a
split-completion chain containing an inversion $1\cdots0$.  Its relative boundary
is the ordinary alternating simplicial boundary with every monotone-bit face set
to zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The two order complexes have the same vertex set.  A split-completion chain is a
simplex of $\Delta(Q^\psi)$ exactly when every comparison in the chain survives
the one-bit thinning, which is equivalent to the bit word being weakly increasing.
Quotienting the simplicial chain groups therefore leaves exactly the nonmonotone
chains, and the relative differential is the induced simplicial differential.
\end{proof}

This formulation is useful computationally: the defect depends only on the old
signature poset and the three-valued fiber profile
\[
 F_s\in\bigl\{\{0\},\{1\},\{0,1\}\bigr\},
\]
not on the number of worlds inside each old equivalence class.

\subsection{Immediate homotopy-neutrality criteria}

The factorization also reveals when splitting is automatically conservative.

\begin{proposition}[Monotone-section criterion]\label{prop:monotone-section}
If $A_1$ is an upward-closed subset of $Q$, then $\pi:Q^\psi\to Q$ is a
homotopy equivalence.  Dually, if $A_0$ is downward closed, then $\pi$ is a
homotopy equivalence.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Assume $A_1$ is upward closed.  Define
\[
 r_+(s)=
 \begin{cases}
 (s,1),&s\in A_1,\\
 (s,0),&s\notin A_1.
 \end{cases}
\]
The upset condition makes $r_+$ order preserving, and $\pi r_+=\mathrm{id}_Q$.
Moreover every $(s,a)\in Q^\psi$ satisfies $(s,a)\leq r_+(s)$, so
$\mathrm{id}_{Q^\psi}\leq r_+\pi$.  The order-homotopy lemma gives
$r_+\pi\simeq\mathrm{id}$ and hence $\pi$ is a homotopy equivalence.  The
$A_0$ statement is dual, using the minimum available bit in each fiber.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Common-outcome anchor]
If every old observational state has at least one refined world with $\psi=1$
($A_1=Q$), or every old state has at least one with $\psi=0$ ($A_0=Q$), then
carrier splitting is homotopy-neutral.  In particular, if every old state genuinely
splits, so $A_0=A_1=Q$, then $Q^\psi=Q\times\{0<1\}$ and the projection is a
homotopy equivalence.
\end{corollary}

Thus the act of duplicating a state is not itself the source of topological defect.
The defect is caused by incompatible outcome availability across comparable coarse
states: a lower state that can realize $1$ together with an upper state that can
realize $0$ creates a potentially deleted comparison.

\subsection{Localization by lower fibers}

For $s\in Q$ define the lower fiber
\[
 L_s:=\pi^{-1}(Q_{\leq s}).
\]
If $s\in A_1$, then $(s,1)$ is a maximum of $L_s$, hence $L_s$ is
contractible.  Therefore all lower-fiber obstructions to Quillen-type equivalence
localize to the $0$-only states $A_0\setminus A_1$.  Dually, all upper-fiber
obstructions localize to the $1$-only states $A_1\setminus A_0$.

This observation does not replace the exact relative complex above.  It does,
however, connect the carrier-splitting problem to the classical poset-fiber
framework.  Under the connectivity hypotheses of the Bj\"orner--Wachs--Welker
fiber theorem, the source $\Delta(Q^\psi)$ admits a wedge decomposition in terms
of the noncontractible lower fibers and upper links.  The important point here is
that the split fibers themselves disappear from that list whenever their top copy
is present.

\subsection{Exact low-height classification}

The general inversion complex can have arbitrarily high dimension.  In the first
nontrivial dimensional regime it collapses to graph incidence and admits a closed
integral classification.

\begin{definition}[Weighted split height]
Let $C=A_0\cap A_1$ be the split set.  Define
\[
 h_\psi(Q)
 :=\max_{s_0<\cdots<s_r\text{ in }Q}
 \left(r+\#\{j:s_j\in C\}\right).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:split-height}
$h_\psi(Q)=\dim\Delta(\widehat Q^\psi)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
A strict coarse chain contributes one vertex from every fiber, and a split fiber can
contribute both copies consecutively.  Taking both copies at every split state on the
chain attains the displayed number, and no split-completion chain can contain more.
\end{proof}

Suppose $h_\psi(Q)\leq2$.  An \emph{inversion edge} is a deleted order-complex edge
of $\Delta(\widehat Q^\psi)$, equivalently a pair
\[
 (s,1)<_{\widehat Q}(t,0),\qquad s<t,
\]
with $s\in A_1$ and $t\in A_0$.  A deleted triangle has one of the four nonmonotone
bit patterns
\[
 010,\qquad100,\qquad101,\qquad110.
\]
It therefore contains either one or two inversion edges.  Introduce one formal root
for each connected component of $Q$ (equivalently of $\widehat Q^\psi$).  The
\emph{carrier-split defect graph} $G_\psi(Q)$ has one vertex for every inversion edge;
a deleted triangle with two inversion edges joins their vertices, while a deleted
triangle with one inversion edge joins that vertex to the root of its component.
Parallel graph edges are allowed.

\begin{theorem}[Carrier-splitting cone classification in weighted height two]
\label{thm:carrier-graph}
Assume $h_\psi(Q)\leq2$.  Let $c_0(G_\psi)$ be the number of connected components
of $G_\psi(Q)$ containing no formal root.  Then
\[
 \widetilde H_n\!\left(\Cone(\Delta\pi);\mathbb Z\right)
 \cong
 \begin{cases}
   \mathbb Z^{\beta_1(G_\psi)},&n=2,\\
   \mathbb Z^{c_0(G_\psi)},&n=1,\\
   0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The relative boundary matrix is totally unimodular.  Hence the same Betti ranks hold
over every field.  Moreover the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item the carrier-splitting cone is acyclic over $\mathbb Z$;
\item it is acyclic over every field;
\item $G_\psi(Q)$ is a rooted forest;
\item $\Delta(\widehat Q^\psi)$ collapses onto $\Delta(Q^\psi)$ through deleted
edge--triangle pairs;
\item $\Delta\pi:\Delta(Q^\psi)\to\Delta(Q)$ is a homotopy equivalence.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:split-factorization}, the mapping-cone homology is the relative
homology of the one-bit thinning
$\Delta(Q^\psi)\subseteq\Delta(\widehat Q^\psi)$.  Lemma~\ref{lem:split-height}
places the split completion in dimension at most two.  The one-bit height-two
incidence theorem from the companion order-thinning analysis applies verbatim: the
relative $C_2\to C_1$ boundary is the oriented incidence matrix of the rooted defect
graph with root rows deleted.  Ordinary graph incidence gives the two displayed free
homology groups and total unimodularity; the rooted-forest condition is equivalent to
perfect relative cancellation and to an elementary collapse.  Finally
$\Delta(p)$ is already a homotopy equivalence, so two-out-of-three identifies
homotopy neutrality of the inclusion with homotopy neutrality of $\Delta\pi$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Status of the low-height theorem]
The graph-incidence algebra, total unimodularity, rooted forests, and beat-point
technology are standard.  The exact height-two theorem for one-bit thinning is proved
in the companion structural-computation manuscript.  The new point here is the
carrier-splitting reduction that makes that theorem applicable to a process which
changes the $T_0$ carrier.  Accordingly, this theorem should be positioned as an
exact transfer theorem, not as a new general theory of rooted forests.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Sharpness beyond weighted height two}

No coefficient-independent forest criterion can hold in unrestricted dimension.
The carrier-splitting family contains the no-split case $C=\varnothing$, which is
exactly arbitrary same-carrier one-bit thinning.  Companion results show that one-bit
thinning in height three can already have relative integral torsion, and in unrestricted
height can encode arbitrary finite-poset homotopy types inside a contractible coarse
cone.  If one insists that at least one old state genuinely split, a disjoint neutral
split component may be adjoined without changing positive-degree cone homology.
Thus the weighted-height-two hypothesis in Theorem~\ref{thm:carrier-graph} marks a
real boundary rather than a presentational convenience.

The appropriate all-height object is therefore the inversion-chain complex of
Theorem~\ref{thm:inversion-chain}, supplemented where useful by poset-fiber or
homotopy-colimit methods.  A realistic next target is not another universal forest
theorem, but a classification of higher-dimensional inversion complexes under
additional structural hypotheses on $Q$ and on the split profile $(A_0,A_1)$.

% Proposed insertion for Observation_Refinement_Descent_and_Cone_Draft_v0.3.tex
% Recommended location: after the general carrier-splitting factorization and
% before the cover-refinement section.  Bibliography additions are supplied in
% MANUSCRIPT_BIBLIOGRAPHY_ADDITIONS.tex.

\section{All-height carrier splitting under noninteracting exclusive inversions}
\label{sec:exclusive-matching}

The low-height rooted-incidence theorem gives a complete answer when the
weighted height is at most two.  In higher dimensions a universal rooted-forest
criterion is impossible: the same-carrier boundary case already supports
integral torsion and arbitrary finite-poset homotopy types.  Nevertheless, an
all-height exact classification survives when the genuinely incompatible
carrier outcomes do not interact.

Let
\[
A_a=\{s\in Q:(s,a)\in Q^\psi\},\qquad a\in\{0,1\},
\]
and put
\[
P=A_1\setminus A_0,\qquad Z=A_0\setminus A_1,\qquad
C=A_0\cap A_1.
\]
Thus $P$ consists of the $1$-only coarse states, $Z$ of the $0$-only coarse
states, and $C$ of the states that genuinely split.

\begin{definition}[Exclusive inversion graph]
\label{def:exclusive-inversion-graph}
The \emph{exclusive inversion graph} is the bipartite graph
\[
G_\psi=(P\sqcup Z,E_\psi),\qquad
E_\psi=\{(p,z)\in P\times Z:p<z\text{ in }Q\}.
\]
An edge records a coarse comparison whose earlier endpoint admits only the new
outcome $1$ while its later endpoint admits only $0$.
\end{definition}

\subsection{The full-doubling model}

Let
\[
D=Q\times\{0<1\},\qquad K=\Delta D,\qquad L=\Delta Q^\psi.
\]
The actual refined carrier is the induced subposet of $D$ obtained by deleting
exactly
\[
M_0=\{(p,0):p\in P\},\qquad
M_1=\{(z,1):z\in Z\}.
\]
Let $K_P$ be obtained by deleting $M_0$, let $K_Z$ be obtained by deleting
$M_1$, and put
\[
U=K_P\cup K_Z,\qquad L=K_P\cap K_Z.
\]
The complex $K_P$ closes upward to the full top row, while $K_Z$ closes
downward to the full bottom row.  Hence both $K_P\hookrightarrow K$ and
$K_Z\hookrightarrow K$ are homotopy equivalences.  The long exact sequences
of triples together with simplicial excision give
\begin{equation}
H_n(K,L;R)\cong H_{n+1}(K,U;R)
\label{eq:two-colour-shift}
\end{equation}
for every coefficient ring $R$.  Since $D\to Q$ is a homotopy equivalence,
$H_n(K,L;R)$ is the reduced homology of the homotopy cofiber of the refined
projection $\Delta\pi:\Delta Q^\psi\to\Delta Q$.

A simplex of $K\setminus U$ contains at least one missing lower copy $(p,0)$
and at least one missing upper copy $(z,1)$.  Because it is a product-order
chain, every such pair satisfies $p<z$.  Therefore the missing vertices of a
relative simplex project to a complete bipartite subgraph of $G_\psi$.  This
observation isolates the source of higher interaction: bicliques with more than
one edge couple otherwise local defects.

\begin{theorem}[Exclusive-Inversion Matching Theorem]
\label{thm:exclusive-matching}
Suppose that the exclusive inversion graph $G_\psi$ is a matching.  Then, for
every coefficient ring $R$ and every integer $n$,
\begin{equation}
\widetilde H_n\!\left(\Cone(\Delta\pi);R\right)
\cong
\bigoplus_{(p,z)\in E_\psi}
\widetilde H_{n-2}\!\left(
\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z];R
\right).
\label{eq:exclusive-matching}
\end{equation}
Consequently $\Delta\pi$ is an $R$-homology equivalence if and only if every
coarse edge link $\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z]$ indexed by an exclusive
inversion is $R$-acyclic.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A relative simplex of $(K,U)$ contains at least one vertex of $M_0$ and one
vertex of $M_1$.  If it contained two missing lower vertices and one missing
upper vertex, the corresponding upper endpoint would have degree at least two
in $G_\psi$; the dual statement holds for two missing upper vertices.  The
matching hypothesis therefore forces every relative simplex to contain a unique
mixed pair
\[
e=((p,0)<(z,1)),\qquad (p,z)\in E_\psi.
\]
Deleting either endpoint of $e$ sends the simplex into $U$, while deleting any
other vertex preserves the same pair.  Hence the relative chain complex splits
as
\[
C_m(K,U;R)=\bigoplus_{e\in E_\psi}C_m^{(e)},
\qquad
C_m^{(e)}\cong
\widetilde C_{m-2}(\operatorname{lk}_K e;R).
\]
Thus
\[
H_m(K,U;R)\cong
\bigoplus_{e\in E_\psi}
\widetilde H_{m-2}(\operatorname{lk}_K e;R).
\]

It remains to identify the product-order link.  For
$e=((p,0)<(z,1))$, its link factors into the lower interval, the open middle
interval, and the upper interval.  The open middle interval is covered by two
contractible subposets: delete $(z,0)$ and close upward to the bit-$1$ row, or
delete $(p,1)$ and close downward to the bit-$0$ row.  Their intersection is
$(p,z)_Q\times\{0<1\}$, homotopy equivalent to $(p,z)_Q$.  Since $(p,1)$ and
$(z,0)$ are incomparable, every middle-chain lies in one of these two pieces;
therefore
\[
\Delta((p,0),(z,1))\simeq\Sigma\Delta(p,z)_Q.
\]
Joining with the lower and upper factors gives
\[
\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta(Q\times\mathbf2)}e
\simeq
\Sigma\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z].
\]
Combining this suspension shift with~\eqref{eq:two-colour-shift} yields
\eqref{eq:exclusive-matching}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bounded-poset localization]
\label{cor:bounded-localization}
Assume that $Q$ has a global minimum $\hat0$ and maximum $\hat1$, and that
$G_\psi$ is a matching.  Then every exclusive edge except possibly
$(\hat0,\hat1)$ has contractible coarse edge link.  Hence only the global
endpoint inversion can contribute to the cone homology.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If $p\ne\hat0$, the lower factor $\Delta Q_{<p}$ has the minimum $\hat0$; if
$z\ne\hat1$, the upper factor $\Delta Q_{>z}$ has the maximum $\hat1$.  In
either case the edge link is a join with a nonempty contractible complex.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Distributive endpoint profile]
\label{cor:distributive-endpoint}
Let $Q=J(R)$ be the lattice of order ideals of a finite poset $R$.  Make the
bottom state $1$-only, the top state $0$-only, and every other state split.  If
$R$ is an $r$-element antichain, so that $Q=B_r$, then
\[
\widetilde H_r(\Cone(\Delta\pi);\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z
\]
and all other reduced cone homology vanishes.  If $R$ is not an antichain,
the cone is integrally acyclic.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:bounded-localization} reduces the answer to the reduced
homology of the proper part of $J(R)$, shifted by two.  The atom crosscut is a
full simplex unless the atoms join to the top element.  In $J(R)$ the atoms
correspond to the minimal elements of $R$, and they join to the top exactly
when every element of $R$ is minimal, i.e. exactly when $R$ is an antichain.
In that case $J(R)=B_r$ and its proper part is homotopy equivalent to
$S^{r-2}$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Sharpness: interaction begins at the first shared endpoint}

The matching condition cannot be weakened merely to ``$G_\psi$ is a
forest.''  For the three-element chain $0<1<2$ with availability profile
\[
0:\{1\},\qquad 1:\{0\},\qquad 2:\{0\},
\]
the exclusive graph is the two-edge star $K_{1,2}$.  Direct integral Smith
normal form gives
\[
\widetilde H_1(\Cone(\Delta\pi);\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z,
\]
while the sum of the two individual coarse-edge-link contributions is zero.
The shared endpoint creates a three-vertex interaction core and a differential
between the two edge defects.

Nor does matching imply total unimodularity or torsion-freeness.  Given any
nonempty finite poset $R$, take
\[
Q=\hat0\oplus R\oplus\hat1
\]
and use the endpoint profile above.  There is exactly one exclusive inversion,
and Theorem~\ref{thm:exclusive-matching} gives
\[
\widetilde H_n(\Cone(\Delta\pi);\mathbb Z)
\cong
\widetilde H_{n-2}(\Delta R;\mathbb Z).
\]
Thus arbitrary finite-poset homology, including torsion, can occur even inside
the matching class.  In particular, total unimodularity must be controlled by
stronger conditions on the relevant links; global torsion-freeness alone is
not a TU criterion~\cite{DeyHiraniKrishnamoorthy2011}.

\subsection{Beyond matching: the interaction-core filtration}

For a relative simplex $\sigma\in K\setminus U$, define its missing core
\[
S(\sigma)=\sigma\cap(M_0\cup M_1).
\]
Filter $C_*(K,U)$ by $|S(\sigma)|$.  If $\mathcal C_r$ is the family of mixed
$r$-vertex missing cores that are simplices of $K$ and
\[
\Lambda_S=\operatorname{lk}_K(S)[V(L)],
\]
then the associated graded complex is
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{gr}_r C_m(K,U)
\cong
\bigoplus_{S\in\mathcal C_r}
\widetilde C_{m-r}(\Lambda_S).
\label{eq:interaction-graded}
\end{equation}
Indeed, deleting an available vertex preserves $S$, while deleting a missing
vertex lowers the filtration.  This produces a convergent interaction spectral
sequence whose first page is assembled from the homology of the
$\Lambda_S$.  The cores project to chain-supported bicliques of $G_\psi$.
Under the matching hypothesis only $r=2$ occurs, so the spectral sequence
collapses immediately and recovers Theorem~\ref{thm:exclusive-matching}.

This filtration is the natural next object beyond matching.  The smallest
nonmatching example above shows that shared endpoints already create higher
core differentials; therefore a higher-dimensional analogue of the low-height
rooted-forest theorem must control these interactions rather than only the
acyclicity of $G_\psi$.

\begin{remark}[Priority boundary]
The deletion/cofiber technology used here is classical.  In particular,
vertex-cover obstruction complexes already provide general homotopical tools
for comparing a complex with unions of induced subcomplexes
\cite{ChacholskiEtAl2021}, while poset-fiber decompositions give broad results
under fiber-connectivity hypotheses \cite{BjornerWachsWelker2005}.  The
candidate contribution of Theorem~\ref{thm:exclusive-matching} is the
observation-theoretic two-colour recognition and the resulting exact coarse
edge-link formula.  No claim is made that simplicial vertex deletion or
homotopy cofibers themselves are new.
\end{remark}
