# Higher-Dimensional Inversion Complex Classification Gate

**Project:** Mathematical Reconstruction of Matte-Blanco's Unfolding Function and Mental Space  
**Date:** 29 September 2026  
**Gate verdict:** **LEVEL A -- STRONG SUCCESS, with a conservative priority qualification.**

The gate found an exact all-dimensional **integral homology classification** on a natural noninteraction class: carrier-splitting systems whose **exclusive inversion graph is a matching**.  The classification is not restricted by height.  It can produce homology in arbitrarily high degree and can transfer torsion.  A second exact corollary gives a particularly clean Boolean/distributive-lattice classification.  The underlying simplicial deletion/cofiber technology has substantial prior art, so the publication claim should be the specialized observation-theoretic recognition and exact link formula, not the generic topology of deleting vertices.

---

## 1. Frozen setting

Let `Q` be a finite observational `T0` poset and let a new Boolean observation `psi` produce a refined carrier

\[
Q^\psi\subseteq Q\times\{0,1\},
\]

ordered by the product order.  Write

\[
A_a=\{s\in Q:(s,a)\in Q^\psi\},\qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]

Separate the coarse states into

\[
P=A_1\setminus A_0 \quad\text{(1-only)},\qquad
Z=A_0\setminus A_1 \quad\text{(0-only)},\qquad
C=A_0\cap A_1 \quad\text{(split)}.
\]

The preceding carrier-splitting gate used a split completion `Qhat^psi`.  The present gate found a second, more useful all-height model.

---

## 2. Full-doubling / missing-copy model

Let

\[
D=Q\times\mathbf 2,
\qquad K=\Delta D,
\qquad L=\Delta Q^\psi.
\]

The actual refined carrier is obtained from `D` by deleting exactly

\[
M_0=\{(p,0):p\in P\},
\qquad
M_1=\{(z,1):z\in Z\}.
\]

Thus `L` is the induced subcomplex of `K` on the remaining vertices.

The projection

\[
D\longrightarrow Q
\]

is a homotopy equivalence: it has both the bottom-row and top-row closure sections.  Consequently the homotopy cofiber of

\[
\Delta\pi:\Delta Q^\psi\to\Delta Q
\]

has the same reduced homology as the relative pair

\[
H_*(K,L;R).
\]

This model is useful because carrier splitting becomes a very special **two-colour vertex deletion problem** from the product order complex `Delta(Q x 2)`.

---

## 3. General two-colour deletion square

Delete the two kinds of missing vertices separately:

\[
K_P=K[V(K)\setminus M_0],
\qquad
K_Z=K[V(K)\setminus M_1],
\]

and put

\[
U=K_P\cup K_Z,
\qquad
L=K_P\cap K_Z.
\]

`K_P` retracts by the ascending closure operator `(s,a) -> (s,1)` to the full top row, while `K_Z` retracts by the descending closure operator `(s,a) -> (s,0)` to the full bottom row.  Hence both inclusions

\[
K_P\hookrightarrow K,
\qquad
K_Z\hookrightarrow K
\]

are homotopy equivalences.

The long exact sequences of triples plus simplicial excision therefore give, for every coefficient ring `R`,

\[
\boxed{
H_n(K,L;R)\cong H_{n+1}(K,U;R).
}
\tag{3.1}
\]

This is the fundamental algebraic reduction of the new gate.

A simplex lies in `K \ U` exactly when it contains **at least one missing lower copy** `(p,0)`, `p in P`, and **at least one missing upper copy** `(z,1)`, `z in Z`.

---

## 4. Exclusive inversion graph

Define the bipartite graph

\[
G_\psi=(P\sqcup Z,E_\psi),
\qquad
E_\psi=\{(p,z)\in P\times Z:p<z\text{ in }Q\}.
\]

Call it the **exclusive inversion graph**.

It records exactly the places where a coarse comparison tries to run from a state where only outcome `1` is available to a later state where only outcome `0` is available.

For every relative simplex `sigma in K \ U`, let

\[
P(\sigma)=\{p\in P:(p,0)\in\sigma\},
\qquad
Z(\sigma)=\{z\in Z:(z,1)\in\sigma\}.
\]

Because `sigma` is a chain in `Q x 2`,

\[
P(\sigma)\times Z(\sigma)\subseteq E_\psi.
\]

Thus every higher interaction in the relative complex is supported on a **biclique** of the exclusive inversion graph.  This is the structural reason a matching is special: it forbids every mixed core larger than one edge.

---

## 5. Exact all-height theorem

### Theorem -- Exclusive-Inversion Matching Theorem

Assume that `E_psi` is a matching; equivalently, every `1`-only state and every `0`-only state participates in at most one exclusive inversion.

Then for every integer `n` and every coefficient ring `R`,

\[
\boxed{
H_n\!\left(\operatorname{Cone}(\Delta\pi);R\right)
\cong
\bigoplus_{(p,z)\in E_\psi}
\widetilde H_{n-2}\!\left(
\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z];R
\right).
}
\tag{5.1}
\]

In particular, integrally,

\[
\boxed{
H_n\!\left(\operatorname{Cone}(\Delta\pi);\mathbb Z\right)
\cong
\bigoplus_{(p,z)\in E_\psi}
\widetilde H_{n-2}\!\left(
\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z];\mathbb Z
\right).
}
\tag{5.2}
\]

The theorem is a complete homology classification on this class: Betti numbers and torsion are read off from coarse **edge links**.

### Immediate necessary-and-sufficient homological criterion

Under the matching hypothesis, the carrier split is an integral homology equivalence iff every relevant coarse edge link is integrally acyclic:

\[
\Delta\pi\text{ is a homology equivalence}
\iff
\widetilde H_*(\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z];\mathbb Z)=0
\quad\forall(p,z)\in E_\psi.
\]

The same statement holds over any chosen coefficient field/ring with that coefficient system substituted.

---

## 6. Proof of the matching theorem

### 6.1 Unique mixed core

A simplex in `K \ U` contains at least one vertex `(p,0)` with `p in P` and one vertex `(z,1)` with `z in Z`.  Any such pair in the same product-order chain satisfies `p<z`, hence gives an edge of `E_psi`.

If a relative simplex contained two different missing lower vertices and one missing upper vertex, the latter would have degree at least two in `E_psi`.  Dually, two missing upper vertices and one missing lower vertex would force degree at least two on the lower endpoint.  Therefore, when `E_psi` is a matching, every simplex in `K \ U` contains a **unique** pair

\[
e=((p,0)<(z,1)),\qquad (p,z)\in E_\psi.
\]

### 6.2 Chain-level direct sum

The relative chain complex consequently splits:

\[
C_m(K,U;R)
=\bigoplus_{e\in E_\psi} C_m^{(e)}.
\]

For a fixed edge `e`, every relative simplex is uniquely `e union tau` with `tau` a simplex in `lk_K(e)`.  Deleting either endpoint of `e` lands in `U` and is zero in the relative quotient; deleting a vertex of `tau` remains in the same `e`-summand.  Hence, up to the harmless orientation sign,

\[
C_m^{(e)}\cong \widetilde C_{m-2}(\operatorname{lk}_K e).
\]

Thus

\[
H_m(K,U;R)
\cong
\bigoplus_{e\in E_\psi}
\widetilde H_{m-2}(\operatorname{lk}_K e;R).
\tag{6.1}
\]

Combining (3.1) and (6.1),

\[
H_n(K,L;R)
\cong
\bigoplus_{e\in E_\psi}
\widetilde H_{n-1}(\operatorname{lk}_K e;R).
\tag{6.2}
\]

### 6.3 Product-edge link is a suspension of the coarse edge link

For `e=((p,0)<(z,1))`, the product edge link decomposes as

\[
\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta(Q\times\mathbf2)}e
=
\Delta(Q_{<p}) * \Delta M_{p,z} * \Delta(Q_{>z}),
\]

where

\[
M_{p,z}=((p,0),(z,1))_{Q\times\mathbf2}.
\]

Let `R=(p,z)_Q`.  The middle poset consists of `(p,1)`, `R x 2`, and `(z,0)`.  Remove `(z,0)`: the result closes upward onto the bit-1 row and has minimum `(p,1)`, hence is contractible.  Remove `(p,1)`: the result closes downward onto the bit-0 row and has maximum `(z,0)`, hence is contractible.  Their intersection is `R x 2`, homotopy equivalent to `R`.  Since `(p,1)` and `(z,0)` are incomparable, these two subcomplexes cover the middle order complex.  Therefore

\[
\Delta M_{p,z}\simeq \Sigma\Delta(p,z)_Q.
\]

Consequently

\[
\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta(Q\times\mathbf2)}e
\simeq
\Sigma\,\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z].
\tag{6.3}
\]

Applying reduced homology to (6.2) and (6.3) proves (5.1).

---

## 7. Exact neutrality before the first inversion

The exclusive graph also gives a clean zeroth obstruction.

### Proposition -- isotone extension criterion

If `E_psi` is empty, then `Delta pi` is a homotopy equivalence.

Indeed, the prescribed partial Boolean labeling

- `b(p)=1` on `P`,
- `b(z)=0` on `Z`,

extends monotonically to all of `Q` iff there is no `p in P`, `z in Z` with `p<z`.  One explicit extension is

\[
b(s)=1 \iff \exists p\in P\text{ with }p\le s.
\]

The section `r(s)=(s,b(s))` satisfies `pi r=id_Q`.  Define

\[
c_+(s,a)=(s,\max\{a,b(s)\}).
\]

Then

\[
\operatorname{id}_{Q^\psi}\le c_+\ge r\pi,
\]

so `r pi` is homotopic to the identity through comparable monotone maps.

Thus a nonempty exclusive inversion graph is a necessary condition for a carrier-splitting homotopy defect.

---

## 8. General interaction-core filtration

The matching theorem is the collapse case of a broader all-height filtration.

For `sigma in K \ U`, define its **missing core**

\[
S(\sigma)=\sigma\cap(M_0\cup M_1).
\]

It contains vertices of both colours.  Filter the relative complex `C_*(K,U)` by core cardinality:

\[
F_r C_m
=
\langle\sigma:\ |S(\sigma)|\le r\rangle,
\qquad r\ge2.
\]

The boundary cannot increase the core size.  Let `C_r` denote the set of `r`-vertex mixed missing cores that are simplices of `K`, and for `S in C_r` let

\[
\Lambda_S
=
\operatorname{lk}_K(S)[V(L)]
\]

be the part of the link supported on available vertices.  Then

\[
\operatorname{gr}_r C_m(K,U)
\cong
\bigoplus_{S\in\mathcal C_r}
\widetilde C_{m-r}(\Lambda_S).
\tag{8.1}
\]

Hence there is a convergent spectral sequence whose first page is assembled from

\[
\widetilde H_*(\Lambda_S)
\]

indexed by mixed missing cores.  Every core projects to a chain-supported biclique of `G_psi`; differentials between filtration levels are exactly the interactions produced by deleting missing vertices.

For a matching there are no mixed cores with more than two vertices, so the filtration collapses immediately and gives Theorem (5.1).  For the old weighted-height-at-most-two regime, the only surviving core interactions are deleted edge/triangle incidences; the former rooted-incidence graph is the low-dimensional shadow of this filtration.

This filtration is the strongest general result found at this gate outside the exact matching class.  It is useful, but it is not advertised as a closed higher-dimensional classification.

---

## 9. Bounded-poset and Boolean/distributive corollaries

Assume `Q` has a least element `0hat` and greatest element `1hat` and the exclusive inversion graph is a matching.

For a coarse edge `p<z`,

\[
\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z]
=
\Delta(Q_{<p})*\Delta(p,z)*\Delta(Q_{>z}).
\]

If `p != 0hat`, the first factor has a minimum and is contractible.  If `z != 1hat`, the last factor has a maximum and is contractible.  Therefore **only the global endpoint inversion can contribute**:

\[
H_n(\operatorname{Cone}\Delta\pi;\mathbb Z)
\cong
\begin{cases}
\widetilde H_{n-2}(\Delta(Q\setminus\{\hat0,\hat1\});\mathbb Z),
& \hat0\in P,\ \hat1\in Z,\\
0,&\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\tag{9.1}
\]

### Finite distributive lattices

Let `Q=L=J(R)` be a finite distributive lattice.  By the crosscut theorem, together with the standard atom structure of `J(R)`, the proper-part order complex is

- contractible if `R` is not an antichain;
- a sphere `S^{r-2}` if `R` is an `r`-element antichain, equivalently `L=B_r` is Boolean.

Therefore, under the endpoint matching profile,

\[
H_n(\operatorname{Cone}\Delta\pi;\mathbb Z)
\cong
\begin{cases}
\mathbb Z,&L=B_r\text{ and }n=r,\\
0,&\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
\tag{9.2}
\]

This gives genuine higher-dimensional examples:

\[
B_2\rightsquigarrow H_2\cong\mathbb Z,
\qquad
B_3\rightsquigarrow H_3\cong\mathbb Z,
\qquad
B_4\rightsquigarrow H_4\cong\mathbb Z.
\]

The first two were checked directly by integral Smith-normal-form computation; the `B_4` result follows from the theorem and was checked through the link formula.

---

## 10. Horn and dual-Horn regimes

A different conclusion holds when the **entire refined signature relation** is Horn.

If `Q^psi` is a nonempty meet-closed subset of a Boolean cube, then it has a least element (the meet of all realized refined signatures).  Its coordinate projection `Q` is also meet-closed, hence also has a least element.  Both order complexes are contractible, so

\[
\Delta\pi:\Delta Q^\psi\to\Delta Q
\]

is a homotopy equivalence.

Dually, a nonempty join-closed refined relation has a greatest element, as does its projection, and is again homotopy-neutral.

Thus **pure Horn/dual-Horn closure does not generate a nontrivial carrier-splitting defect**.  It is a useful exact neutral class, not the source of the desired higher-dimensional topology.

This is deliberately narrower than the companion paper's Horn-type repair criterion: it assumes closure of the full refined realized-signature relation itself, not merely that one truth region of an arbitrary observation is Horn-definable.

---

## 11. Torsion and universality inside the exact matching class

The matching condition controls **interaction between inversion defects**, not the topology of the coarse edge links.

Let `R` be any nonempty finite poset.  Form

\[
Q=\hat0\oplus R\oplus\hat1
\]

by adjoining a global bottom and top.  Make `0hat` 1-only, `1hat` 0-only, and every state of `R` genuinely split.  Then

\[
E_\psi=\{(\hat0,\hat1)\}
\]

is a one-edge matching and

\[
\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[\hat0,\hat1]=\Delta R.
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{
H_n(\operatorname{Cone}\Delta\pi;\mathbb Z)
\cong
\widetilde H_{n-2}(\Delta R;\mathbb Z).
}
\tag{11.1}
\]

Consequences:

1. nonzero cone homology occurs in arbitrarily high degree inside the matching class;
2. arbitrary integral torsion occurring in finite-poset homology transfers two degrees upward;
3. a universal wedge-of-spheres theorem is false even under exclusive-inversion matching;
4. matching does **not** imply total unimodularity.

For example, using a finite-poset model of `RP^2` as `R` yields `Z/2` torsion in cone degree 3.  The 13-point projective-plane model cited in the companion paper gives a small explicit construction after adjoining the two endpoints, but minimality in the matching class is not claimed here.

---

## 12. Sharp failure outside the matching hypothesis

The smallest possible nonmatching exclusive graph already destroys naive edgewise additivity.

Take the three-element chain

\[
0<1<2
\]

with availability profile

\[
(\{1\},\{0\},\{0\}).
\]

Then

\[
E_\psi=\{(0,1),(0,2)\},
\]

a two-edge star, hence a forest but not a matching.

Direct integral computation gives

\[
H_1(\operatorname{Cone}\Delta\pi;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z.
\]

However both individual coarse edge links are contractible, so the naive sum of the matching formula predicts zero.

The missing 2-simplex containing `(0,0),(1,1),(2,1)` couples the two inversion edges.  Therefore:

\[
\boxed{\text{``exclusive inversion graph is a forest'' is not enough.}}
\]

Three coarse states are minimal for this failure because a nonmatching bipartite graph needs at least three incident vertices.

---

## 13. Total-unimodularity boundary

The earlier height-two theorem had a TU relative boundary matrix because its columns were signed graph-incidence columns.

That phenomenon does not survive the present all-height class.  Dey--Hirani--Krishnamoorthy characterize TU of a simplicial boundary matrix by torsion-freeness of a whole family of pure relative subcomplex pairs, not merely by torsion-freeness of one global homology group.  The matching realization (11.1) transfers arbitrary torsion, so matching cannot imply TU.

Even when every edge link is torsion-free and the cone homology is therefore free, that alone is insufficient to claim TU of all inversion boundary matrices.  No new all-dimensional forbidden-minor characterization of TU was established at this gate.

**Verdict for the TU program:** useful negative boundary, not a new TU theorem.

---

## 14. Computational evidence

The new verifier `verify_matching_inversion_theorem.py` performs exact integral Smith-normal-form computations on the full doubled-product relative pair.

### Exhaustive results

Across every naturally labelled finite coarse poset on at most four states and all fiber profiles `{0}`, `{1}`, `{0,1}`:

- **3,450** poset/profile cases were examined;
- **3,242** satisfied the exclusive-inversion matching condition and were checked integrally by Smith normal form;
- **566** of those had at least one exclusive inversion edge;
- **0** failures of formula (5.2) occurred;
- every profile with empty exclusive inversion graph was `F2`-acyclic, agreeing with the homotopy proof.

### Additional tests

- **1,707** product-edge-link suspension identities were checked over `F2` for all comparable pairs in all naturally labelled coarse posets through five states;
- **3,000** deterministic random five-state profile trials were run; **639** nonempty matching cases were checked directly over `F2`, with **0 failures**;
- direct integral computations give `H_2=Z` for the Boolean endpoint `B_2` example and `H_3=Z` for `B_3`;
- the three-chain star counterexample gives actual `H_1=Z` while the false pairwise-link extension predicts zero.

A separate Horn verifier exhaustively checked all nonempty Boolean relations through four coordinates:

- dimension 4 contains **4,959** meet-closed relations and **4,959** join-closed relations;
- every meet-closed relation and its projection had a least element;
- every join-closed relation and its projection had a greatest element.

A distributive-lattice verifier checked all order-ideal lattices generated by naturally labelled posets through three generators (10 cases): the endpoint formula agreed exactly with direct integral computation, with the Boolean cases spherical and every non-Boolean distributive case neutral.

---

## 15. Comparison of the four requested programs

| Program | Outcome | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Boolean/Horn signature posets | Pure Horn/dual-Horn refined relations are exactly neutral; bounded/distributive matching gives a clean sphere-or-zero formula | **Exact, but the Horn part is topologically trivial; Boolean/distributive corollary is useful** |
| Bounded comparability | Height `<=2` remains completely classified by the prior rooted theorem; height 3 already allows torsion; coarse chains have a known Ferrers/independence-complex classification | **No new universal bounded-comparability classification** |
| Controlled lower/upper fibers | Classical fiber theorems give strong sufficient/decomposition results, but do not yield the new exact formula without added hypotheses | **Useful comparison, not the main result** |
| Descent / inversion filtration | Missing cores are bicliques of `G_psi`; the core-size filtration gives a spectral sequence; matching forces immediate collapse | **General mechanism + exact matching collapse** |

---

## 16. Literature and novelty boundary

The closest prior work found is not nerve theory but **simplicial vertex-deletion / obstruction-complex theory**.

1. Björner--Wachs--Welker, *Poset fiber theorems*, Trans. AMS 357 (2005), gives homotopy decompositions of a poset from lower fibers under connectivity assumptions.  This is the main benchmark for the controlled-fiber program.
2. Chachólski--Jin--Scolamiero--Tombari, *Homotopical decompositions of simplicial and Vietoris Rips complexes*, J. Applied and Computational Topology 5 (2021), studies induced subcomplexes obtained from vertex covers and measures failure by obstruction complexes.  Its one-, two-, and several-outside-point constructions are the closest antecedent to the missing-copy model.
3. Dey--Hirani--Krishnamoorthy, *Optimal Homologous Cycles, Total Unimodularity, and Linear Programming*, SIAM J. Comput. 40 (2011), gives the relevant topological characterization of TU boundary matrices.
4. Stong's finite-space reductions, Barmak's poset form of Quillen's Theorem A, and Fernández--Minian relation/mapping-cylinder methods are standard background for the closure and fiber arguments.
5. Horn model classes being closed under componentwise conjunction/intersection is classical Boolean-CSP / closure-system theory.
6. Crosscut/shellability theory for distributive and semidistributive lattices supplies the sphere-or-contractible behavior used in the lattice corollary.

### Conservative priority assessment

I did **not** locate the following exact statement in the searched literature:

> for a Boolean carrier split, if the 1-only-to-0-only comparison graph is a matching, the complete integral mapping-cone homology is the direct sum of two-degree-shifted reduced homologies of the corresponding coarse edge links.

However, this statement is built from standard vertex-deletion/cofiber ingredients, especially close to the obstruction-complex framework of Chachólski et al.  It should therefore be presented as a **specialized exact recognition theorem for the observation-refinement model**, not as a claim that link/cofiber decomposition itself is new.

A publication-priority claim should remain qualified until a specialist literature referee has checked whether the matching specialization occurs implicitly in the vertex-cover/deletion literature.

The 2026 search also found recent work on discrete homotopy/homology of finite posets, but not this two-colour carrier-splitting classification.

---

## 17. Adversarial specialist reviews

### Referee A -- finite-poset topology

**Attack:** "This is just Quillen/Björner--Wachs--Welker after rewriting the fibers."

**Finding:** not fully.  BWW supplies a powerful homotopy decomposition when lower fibers meet connectivity hypotheses.  The matching formula works integrally without those hypotheses and allows arbitrary torsion through coarse edge links.  The proof, however, uses standard poset/order-complex ideas.  **Revision:** claim exact specialization, not foundational new fiber theory.

### Referee B -- combinatorial topology

**Attack:** "The missing-copy proof is generic vertex deletion."

**Finding:** substantially correct as a priority warning.  Chachólski et al. explicitly develop obstruction complexes and cofiber sequences for one, two, and several outside vertices.  **Revision:** position the new content in the observation-theoretic identification of missing copies, the exclusive inversion graph, the biclique filtration, and the matching direct-sum reduction.

### Referee C -- integer homology / TU

**Attack:** "Matching should force torsion-free or TU matrices."

**Finding:** false.  The endpoint construction transfers arbitrary reduced integral homology of a coarse link two degrees upward, including torsion.  **Revision:** remove any blanket TU suggestion and retain only the exact homology formula.

### Referee D -- Horn / closure systems

**Attack:** "Horn might give the desired nontrivial class."

**Finding:** when the whole refined relation is meet-closed, both refined and projected posets have minima and are contractible.  Pure Horn closure therefore trivializes the topological defect rather than classifying a rich one.  **Revision:** retain Horn as a neutral regime and use Boolean/distributive lattices as the nontrivial structured example.

### Hostile referee -- smallest destroyer

**Task:** destroy the edgewise formula as soon as matching is relaxed.

**Result:** the three-state chain with profile `(1-only, 0-only, 0-only)` does so.  The exclusive inversion graph is a forest, but the two inversion edges interact through a 2-simplex and produce `H_1=Z` even though the individual coarse edge links contribute zero.

This is a strong reason to keep the matching hypothesis explicit.

---

## 18. Success level

### **LEVEL A -- STRONG SUCCESS**

The rubric for Level A is met mathematically:

- the class is natural: noninteracting exclusive inversions;
- the classification is necessary-and-sufficient for all integral cone homology on that class;
- the theorem is all-dimensional;
- the proof is exact;
- exhaustive integral and targeted higher-order computation support it;
- a minimal failure outside the hypothesis is known.

The **priority confidence is lower than the correctness confidence** because general obstruction-complex/vertex-deletion theory is close prior art.  The paper should distinguish those two judgments.

---

## 19. Answers to the ten required questions

1. **Does a nontrivial higher-dimensional exact classification exist?**  **Yes.**  Exclusive-inversion matching gives an exact all-dimensional integral formula.
2. **Strongest class?**  Carrier-splitting systems for which the bipartite graph of `1`-only-to-`0`-only coarse comparisons is a matching.
3. **Exact theorem?**  Formula (5.2): the cone homology is the direct sum of two-degree-shifted reduced homologies of the corresponding coarse edge links.
4. **Integral, field-dependent, or rational?**  **Integral.**  It holds over arbitrary coefficients.
5. **Does torsion occur?**  **Yes.**  Arbitrary finite-poset link torsion can be transferred two degrees upward.
6. **Stronger than standard poset-fiber theory?**  **As a specialized computation, yes:** it gives exact groups without BWW connectivity hypotheses.  **As general topology, no:** its proof sits close to standard vertex-deletion/cofiber machinery.
7. **Does it recover the `h_psi(Q)<=2` rooted-forest theorem?**  On the matching locus, yes at the homology level.  The general interaction-core filtration specializes to the deleted-edge/deleted-triangle incidence complex underlying the full low-height theorem.  The matching theorem by itself does not subsume every low-height nonmatching case.
8. **Smallest counterexample outside the hypothesis?**  Three-chain `0<1<2` with profile `(1,0,0)`; exclusive graph `K_{1,2}`, actual `H_1=Z`, naive edge-link sum zero.
9. **Should it replace the carrier-splitting theorem as the paper's main result?**  **Not replace; strengthen.**  The carrier-splitting factorization is the general structural theorem.  The matching-link theorem should become the strongest exact all-height theorem immediately after it.
10. **Single next theorem?**  Construct and classify the **exclusive-inversion interaction spectral sequence** beyond matching, beginning with exclusive graphs of maximum degree two or chordal/Ferrers biclique structure, and determine conditions forcing collapse at `E^2`.

---

## 20. Recommended manuscript action

The result is strong enough to justify a new manuscript section, but not a wholesale rewrite of the paper yet.

Insert, in this order:

1. the full-doubling / missing-copy model;
2. the two-colour deletion square and shift isomorphism;
3. the exclusive inversion graph;
4. the interaction-core filtration;
5. the matching-link theorem and proof;
6. bounded-poset and Boolean/distributive corollaries;
7. the three-chain forest counterexample;
8. the torsion/universality sharpness result;
9. a literature paragraph explicitly crediting obstruction-complex deletion theory.

The next gate should attack degree-two interaction rather than broadening the theorem by wishful analogy from matching to forests.

# Algebra of the Higher-Dimensional Inversion Chain Complex

## 1. Product model

Let `Q` be a finite poset and `Q^psi subseteq Q x {0,1}` the realized refined signatures.  Put

\[
D=Q\times\mathbf2,\quad K=\Delta D,\quad L=\Delta Q^\psi.
\]

Let

\[
P=A_1\setminus A_0,\qquad Z=A_0\setminus A_1.
\]

The vertices missing from `L` are

\[
M_0=P\times\{0\},\qquad M_1=Z\times\{1\}.
\]

This realizes the changing-carrier problem as an induced-subcomplex deletion from one fixed order complex.

## 2. Two-colour deletion pair

Define

\[
K_P=K[V\setminus M_0],\qquad K_Z=K[V\setminus M_1],
\]

\[
L=K_P\cap K_Z,\qquad U=K_P\cup K_Z.
\]

Both `K_P -> K` and `K_Z -> K` are homotopy equivalences by the top-row and bottom-row closure maps.  Consequently

\[
H_n(K,L;R)\cong H_{n+1}(K,U;R).
\]

The relative complex `C_*(K,U)` is free on chains containing at least one vertex of each missing colour.

## 3. Exclusive inversion graph

Let

\[
E_\psi=\{(p,z)\in P\times Z:p<z\}.
\]

For a relative simplex `sigma`, put

\[
P(\sigma)=\{p:(p,0)\in\sigma\},\qquad
Z(\sigma)=\{z:(z,1)\in\sigma\}.
\]

Then `P(sigma) x Z(sigma)` is a complete bipartite subgraph of `E_psi`.  Hence higher relative cells are controlled not by arbitrary subsets of inversions but by **chain-supported bicliques**.

This gives a sharper description than simply saying that the bit word has a descent.

## 4. Core-size filtration

Define the missing core

\[
S(\sigma)=\sigma\cap(M_0\cup M_1).
\]

Every relative simplex has `|S(sigma)| >= 2`.  Filter by

\[
F_r C_m(K,U)=\langle\sigma:|S(\sigma)|\le r\rangle.
\]

Since taking a face cannot increase the number of missing vertices, this is a chain filtration.

Let `C_r` be the family of `r`-vertex mixed missing cores that are themselves simplices of `K`.  For `S in C_r`, define

\[
\Lambda_S=\operatorname{lk}_K(S)[V(L)].
\]

In the associated graded complex, deleting a missing vertex lowers the filtration and disappears, while deleting an available vertex preserves the core.  Therefore

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{gr}_r C_m(K,U)
\cong
\bigoplus_{S\in\mathcal C_r}
\widetilde C_{m-r}(\Lambda_S).
}
\]

A standard filtered-complex spectral sequence follows, with first-page terms built from

\[
\widetilde H_*(\Lambda_S).
\]

The first inter-core differentials delete one missing vertex and hence measure interactions among overlapping exclusive inversions.

## 5. Matching collapse

If `E_psi` is a matching, no relative simplex can contain more than two missing vertices.  Hence all mixed cores have exactly two vertices and are exactly the edges

\[
e=((p,0)<(z,1)),\qquad (p,z)\in E_\psi.
\]

Moreover every vertex in `lk_K(e)` is available: a missing vertex in the link would create another exclusive edge sharing `p` or `z`.

Thus the filtration has only one nonzero mixed-core level and collapses immediately:

\[
C_m(K,U)
\cong
\bigoplus_{e\in E_\psi}
\widetilde C_{m-2}(\operatorname{lk}_K e).
\]

This is a literal chain-level direct sum, not merely an equality of Betti numbers.

## 6. Product link versus coarse link

For `e=((p,0)<(z,1))`,

\[
\operatorname{lk}_K e
=
\Delta(Q_{<p})*\Delta M_{p,z}*\Delta(Q_{>z}),
\]

where `M_{p,z}=((p,0),(z,1))` in `Q x 2`.

Writing `R=(p,z)_Q`, cover `Delta M_{p,z}` by

- `M_{p,z} \ {(z,0)}`, which closes upward to a cone with minimum `(p,1)`;
- `M_{p,z} \ {(p,1)}`, which closes downward to a cone with maximum `(z,0)`.

Their intersection is `R x 2`, homotopy equivalent to `R`.  Hence

\[
\Delta M_{p,z}\simeq\Sigma\Delta R,
\]

and therefore

\[
\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta(Q\times2)}e
\simeq
\Sigma\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z].
\]

## 7. Exact integral formula

Combining the direct sum, the product-link suspension, and

\[
H_n(K,L)\cong H_{n+1}(K,U),
\]

gives

\[
H_n(K,L;\mathbb Z)
\cong
\bigoplus_{(p,z)\in E_\psi}
\widetilde H_{n-2}(\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z];\mathbb Z).
\]

The same argument works over arbitrary coefficients.

## 8. Why forests fail

A forest can contain a star.  If `p` is adjacent to two comparable `z_1<z_2`, then the relative triangle

\[
(p,0)<(z_1,1)<(z_2,1)
\]

has boundary connecting the two inversion-edge generators.  This is an inter-core differential.  The three-chain profile `(1,0,0)` is the smallest example.

Thus the correct higher-dimensional object is not the exclusive graph alone but the hierarchy of chain-supported bicliques plus their available links.

## 9. Relation to the original bit-word model

The earlier split-completion relative complex was described by nonmonotone bit words.  The full-doubling model repackages the same obstruction more effectively:

- split states contribute no missing copy;
- 1-only states remove their lower copy;
- 0-only states remove their upper copy;
- a genuine obstruction occurs only when a chain needs both missing colours.

The binary descent is therefore equivalent to a two-colour missing-vertex interaction after the homotopy-neutral doubling.

# Literature and Priority Map -- Higher-Dimensional Inversion Gate

**Search horizon:** through 29 September 2026.  
**Method:** structural searches for poset fibers, induced-subcomplex vertex deletion, obstruction complexes, finite-space reductions, Horn closure systems, lattice order complexes, and total unimodularity.  Absence of the project terminology "carrier splitting" was not treated as novelty evidence.

## 1. Björner--Wachs--Welker: poset fiber decompositions

**Reference:** A. Björner, M. Wachs, V. Welker, *Poset fiber theorems*, Transactions of the AMS 357 (2005), 1877--1899.  Preprint: https://www.math.miami.edu/~wachs/papers/fibers.pdf

Their main theorem expresses the homotopy type of a poset in terms of the base and lower fibers under explicit connectivity hypotheses, subsuming Quillen/Baclawski/Babson fiber results.

**Overlap:** controlled-fiber decomposition and homotopy equivalence criteria.

**Difference:** the exclusive-inversion matching theorem gives exact integral cone homology from edge links without requiring those fiber-connectivity assumptions.  It is much narrower structurally.

## 2. Chachólski--Jin--Scolamiero--Tombari: vertex-cover obstruction complexes

**Reference:** W. Chachólski, A. Jin, M. Scolamiero, F. Tombari, *Homotopical decompositions of simplicial and Vietoris Rips complexes*, Journal of Applied and Computational Topology 5 (2021), 215--248. DOI: 10.1007/s41468-021-00066-2.  https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s41468-021-00066-2

They study inclusions induced by covers of a simplicial complex's vertex set, define obstruction complexes, and give homotopy-cofiber statements for one, two, and several outside vertices.  Their general theorem controls homotopy fibers of the inclusion by the obstruction complexes.

**Overlap:** this is the closest prior art to the full-doubling/missing-copy viewpoint.  In particular, the standard fact that deleting vertices produces cofiber/link obstructions is not new here.

**Candidate additional content:** in the observation-refinement product `Delta(Q x 2)`, the missing vertices have two special colours.  Their mixed simplices are exactly chain-supported bicliques of the exclusive inversion graph.  Matching of that graph forces a chain-level direct sum and yields the explicit coarse-edge-link formula.  I did not locate that exact specialization/formula in the searched source.

**Priority caution:** a specialist should still check whether this matching specialization is implicit in the authors' several-outside-points machinery.

## 3. Dey--Hirani--Krishnamoorthy: TU and torsion

**Reference:** T. K. Dey, A. N. Hirani, B. Krishnamoorthy, *Optimal Homologous Cycles, Total Unimodularity, and Linear Programming*, SIAM Journal on Computing 40(4) (2011), 1026--1044. DOI: 10.1137/100800245.  https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/100800245

They prove a topological characterization of total unimodularity of simplicial boundary matrices in terms of torsion-freeness of a family of pure relative subcomplex pairs.

**Consequence here:** torsion-free global cone homology is not enough to infer TU.  The matching realization transfers arbitrary torsion, so no blanket all-height TU theorem survives.

## 4. Stong; Barmak; Fernández--Minian

- R. E. Stong, *Finite topological spaces*, Trans. AMS 123 (1966), 325--340. DOI: 10.1090/S0002-9947-1966-0195042-2.
- J. A. Barmak, *On Quillen's Theorem A for posets*, JCTA 118 (2011), 2445--2453; arXiv:1005.0538.
- X. Fernández, E. G. Minian, *The cylinder of a relation and generalized versions of the Nerve Theorem*, arXiv:1801.07235.

**Overlap:** closure maps, beat-point reductions, simple-homotopy fiber criteria, mapping/relation cylinders.

**Difference:** these provide the standard finite-poset topology, not the specialized exclusive-inversion formula.

## 5. Horn / closure systems

Boolean relations closed componentwise under logical AND are exactly Horn-definable relations; this is standard Schaefer/Post-style Boolean relation theory.  A concise modern statement appears in the ICALP 2019 possibility-domain literature, and closure-system treatments identify Horn models with intersection-closed families.

**Overlap:** meet-closure itself is classical.

**Use here:** if the entire refined realized relation is meet-closed, it and its coordinate projection have minima, so the carrier cone is contractible.  This is a simple application, not a novelty claim about Horn logic.

## 6. Crosscut/shellability theory for distributive lattices

Modern crosscut-simplicial literature records that semidistributive lattices have interval order complexes that are contractible or spherical; distributive lattices are a special case.  See C. Defant and N. Williams, *Semidistrim Lattices*, Forum of Mathematics, Sigma 11 (2023), e50.

For the particular distributive lattice `J(R)`, the endpoint statement used here also follows directly from the classical crosscut theorem and the atom structure of `J(R)`: if `R` is not an antichain, the atom crosscut is a simplex; if `R` is an antichain, `J(R)` is Boolean and the crosscut is a sphere.

**Novelty status:** standard lattice topology applied as a corollary of the matching theorem.

## 7. 2026-current finite-poset work

A 2026 paper, *Discrete homotopy and homology theories for finite posets* (Advances in Applied Mathematics 177 (2026), 103074), develops discrete analogues of homotopy and homology for finite posets and relates the discrete homotopy groups to classical ones.

**Overlap:** finite-poset homotopy/homology environment.

**Difference:** no carrier-splitting, two-colour missing-copy, or matching edge-link classification was found there.

## 8. Priority table

| Result in this gate | Closest antecedent | Priority assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Full-doubling/missing-copy model | standard induced-subcomplex deletion; Chachólski et al. | **Not new topology; project-specific modeling reduction** |
| Two-colour shift `H_n(K,L) ~= H_{n+1}(K,U)` | LES/excision/Mayer--Vietoris | **Standard algebraic topology specialized here** |
| Biclique missing-core filtration | filtered relative chains + vertex deletion | **Potentially useful project-specific organization; do not make broad novelty claim yet** |
| Exclusive-inversion matching link formula | Chachólski obstruction complexes; link/cofiber theory | **Candidate substantive specialized theorem; exact statement not located** |
| Bounded-poset endpoint localization | elementary join/link argument | **Corollary** |
| Boolean/distributive sphere-or-zero rule | crosscut theorem | **Corollary; prior lattice topology** |
| Horn refined-relation neutrality | Horn meet closure + cone posets | **Application, not novelty** |
| Torsion universality inside matching | finite-poset realization + matching theorem | **Sharpness result specific to theorem** |

## 9. Recommended wording for a paper

Use wording such as:

> The underlying deletion and cofiber constructions are classical, and obstruction-complex methods for vertex covers are available in the literature.  Our contribution is the recognition that a Boolean observation split produces a two-colour deletion inside `Delta(Q x 2)`, for which the 1-only-to-0-only comparison graph controls interactions.  When this graph is a matching, the relative chain complex separates and yields an exact integral edge-link formula.

Avoid wording such as:

> We introduce a new general theory of vertex deletion or simplicial cofibers.

That would be inaccurate.

% Proposed insertion for Observation_Refinement_Descent_and_Cone_Draft_v0.3.tex
% Recommended location: after the general carrier-splitting factorization and
% before the cover-refinement section.  Bibliography additions are supplied in
% MANUSCRIPT_BIBLIOGRAPHY_ADDITIONS.tex.

\section{All-height carrier splitting under noninteracting exclusive inversions}
\label{sec:exclusive-matching}

The low-height rooted-incidence theorem gives a complete answer when the
weighted height is at most two.  In higher dimensions a universal rooted-forest
criterion is impossible: the same-carrier boundary case already supports
integral torsion and arbitrary finite-poset homotopy types.  Nevertheless, an
all-height exact classification survives when the genuinely incompatible
carrier outcomes do not interact.

Let
\[
A_a=\{s\in Q:(s,a)\in Q^\psi\},\qquad a\in\{0,1\},
\]
and put
\[
P=A_1\setminus A_0,\qquad Z=A_0\setminus A_1,\qquad
C=A_0\cap A_1.
\]
Thus $P$ consists of the $1$-only coarse states, $Z$ of the $0$-only coarse
states, and $C$ of the states that genuinely split.

\begin{definition}[Exclusive inversion graph]
\label{def:exclusive-inversion-graph}
The \emph{exclusive inversion graph} is the bipartite graph
\[
G_\psi=(P\sqcup Z,E_\psi),\qquad
E_\psi=\{(p,z)\in P\times Z:p<z\text{ in }Q\}.
\]
An edge records a coarse comparison whose earlier endpoint admits only the new
outcome $1$ while its later endpoint admits only $0$.
\end{definition}

\subsection{The full-doubling model}

Let
\[
D=Q\times\{0<1\},\qquad K=\Delta D,\qquad L=\Delta Q^\psi.
\]
The actual refined carrier is the induced subposet of $D$ obtained by deleting
exactly
\[
M_0=\{(p,0):p\in P\},\qquad
M_1=\{(z,1):z\in Z\}.
\]
Let $K_P$ be obtained by deleting $M_0$, let $K_Z$ be obtained by deleting
$M_1$, and put
\[
U=K_P\cup K_Z,\qquad L=K_P\cap K_Z.
\]
The complex $K_P$ closes upward to the full top row, while $K_Z$ closes
downward to the full bottom row.  Hence both $K_P\hookrightarrow K$ and
$K_Z\hookrightarrow K$ are homotopy equivalences.  The long exact sequences
of triples together with simplicial excision give
\begin{equation}
H_n(K,L;R)\cong H_{n+1}(K,U;R)
\label{eq:two-colour-shift}
\end{equation}
for every coefficient ring $R$.  Since $D\to Q$ is a homotopy equivalence,
$H_n(K,L;R)$ is the reduced homology of the homotopy cofiber of the refined
projection $\Delta\pi:\Delta Q^\psi\to\Delta Q$.

A simplex of $K\setminus U$ contains at least one missing lower copy $(p,0)$
and at least one missing upper copy $(z,1)$.  Because it is a product-order
chain, every such pair satisfies $p<z$.  Therefore the missing vertices of a
relative simplex project to a complete bipartite subgraph of $G_\psi$.  This
observation isolates the source of higher interaction: bicliques with more than
one edge couple otherwise local defects.

\begin{theorem}[Exclusive-Inversion Matching Theorem]
\label{thm:exclusive-matching}
Suppose that the exclusive inversion graph $G_\psi$ is a matching.  Then, for
every coefficient ring $R$ and every integer $n$,
\begin{equation}
\widetilde H_n\!\left(\Cone(\Delta\pi);R\right)
\cong
\bigoplus_{(p,z)\in E_\psi}
\widetilde H_{n-2}\!\left(
\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z];R
\right).
\label{eq:exclusive-matching}
\end{equation}
Consequently $\Delta\pi$ is an $R$-homology equivalence if and only if every
coarse edge link $\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z]$ indexed by an exclusive
inversion is $R$-acyclic.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
A relative simplex of $(K,U)$ contains at least one vertex of $M_0$ and one
vertex of $M_1$.  If it contained two missing lower vertices and one missing
upper vertex, the corresponding upper endpoint would have degree at least two
in $G_\psi$; the dual statement holds for two missing upper vertices.  The
matching hypothesis therefore forces every relative simplex to contain a unique
mixed pair
\[
e=((p,0)<(z,1)),\qquad (p,z)\in E_\psi.
\]
Deleting either endpoint of $e$ sends the simplex into $U$, while deleting any
other vertex preserves the same pair.  Hence the relative chain complex splits
as
\[
C_m(K,U;R)=\bigoplus_{e\in E_\psi}C_m^{(e)},
\qquad
C_m^{(e)}\cong
\widetilde C_{m-2}(\operatorname{lk}_K e;R).
\]
Thus
\[
H_m(K,U;R)\cong
\bigoplus_{e\in E_\psi}
\widetilde H_{m-2}(\operatorname{lk}_K e;R).
\]

It remains to identify the product-order link.  For
$e=((p,0)<(z,1))$, its link factors into the lower interval, the open middle
interval, and the upper interval.  The open middle interval is covered by two
contractible subposets: delete $(z,0)$ and close upward to the bit-$1$ row, or
delete $(p,1)$ and close downward to the bit-$0$ row.  Their intersection is
$(p,z)_Q\times\{0<1\}$, homotopy equivalent to $(p,z)_Q$.  Since $(p,1)$ and
$(z,0)$ are incomparable, every middle-chain lies in one of these two pieces;
therefore
\[
\Delta((p,0),(z,1))\simeq\Sigma\Delta(p,z)_Q.
\]
Joining with the lower and upper factors gives
\[
\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta(Q\times\mathbf2)}e
\simeq
\Sigma\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z].
\]
Combining this suspension shift with~\eqref{eq:two-colour-shift} yields
\eqref{eq:exclusive-matching}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bounded-poset localization]
\label{cor:bounded-localization}
Assume that $Q$ has a global minimum $\hat0$ and maximum $\hat1$, and that
$G_\psi$ is a matching.  Then every exclusive edge except possibly
$(\hat0,\hat1)$ has contractible coarse edge link.  Hence only the global
endpoint inversion can contribute to the cone homology.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
If $p\ne\hat0$, the lower factor $\Delta Q_{<p}$ has the minimum $\hat0$; if
$z\ne\hat1$, the upper factor $\Delta Q_{>z}$ has the maximum $\hat1$.  In
either case the edge link is a join with a nonempty contractible complex.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Distributive endpoint profile]
\label{cor:distributive-endpoint}
Let $Q=J(R)$ be the lattice of order ideals of a finite poset $R$.  Make the
bottom state $1$-only, the top state $0$-only, and every other state split.  If
$R$ is an $r$-element antichain, so that $Q=B_r$, then
\[
\widetilde H_r(\Cone(\Delta\pi);\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z
\]
and all other reduced cone homology vanishes.  If $R$ is not an antichain,
the cone is integrally acyclic.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Corollary~\ref{cor:bounded-localization} reduces the answer to the reduced
homology of the proper part of $J(R)$, shifted by two.  The atom crosscut is a
full simplex unless the atoms join to the top element.  In $J(R)$ the atoms
correspond to the minimal elements of $R$, and they join to the top exactly
when every element of $R$ is minimal, i.e. exactly when $R$ is an antichain.
In that case $J(R)=B_r$ and its proper part is homotopy equivalent to
$S^{r-2}$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Sharpness: interaction begins at the first shared endpoint}

The matching condition cannot be weakened merely to ``$G_\psi$ is a
forest.''  For the three-element chain $0<1<2$ with availability profile
\[
0:\{1\},\qquad 1:\{0\},\qquad 2:\{0\},
\]
the exclusive graph is the two-edge star $K_{1,2}$.  Direct integral Smith
normal form gives
\[
\widetilde H_1(\Cone(\Delta\pi);\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z,
\]
while the sum of the two individual coarse-edge-link contributions is zero.
The shared endpoint creates a three-vertex interaction core and a differential
between the two edge defects.

Nor does matching imply total unimodularity or torsion-freeness.  Given any
nonempty finite poset $R$, take
\[
Q=\hat0\oplus R\oplus\hat1
\]
and use the endpoint profile above.  There is exactly one exclusive inversion,
and Theorem~\ref{thm:exclusive-matching} gives
\[
\widetilde H_n(\Cone(\Delta\pi);\mathbb Z)
\cong
\widetilde H_{n-2}(\Delta R;\mathbb Z).
\]
Thus arbitrary finite-poset homology, including torsion, can occur even inside
the matching class.  In particular, total unimodularity must be controlled by
stronger conditions on the relevant links; global torsion-freeness alone is
not a TU criterion~\cite{DeyHiraniKrishnamoorthy2011}.

\subsection{Beyond matching: the interaction-core filtration}

For a relative simplex $\sigma\in K\setminus U$, define its missing core
\[
S(\sigma)=\sigma\cap(M_0\cup M_1).
\]
Filter $C_*(K,U)$ by $|S(\sigma)|$.  If $\mathcal C_r$ is the family of mixed
$r$-vertex missing cores that are simplices of $K$ and
\[
\Lambda_S=\operatorname{lk}_K(S)[V(L)],
\]
then the associated graded complex is
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{gr}_r C_m(K,U)
\cong
\bigoplus_{S\in\mathcal C_r}
\widetilde C_{m-r}(\Lambda_S).
\label{eq:interaction-graded}
\end{equation}
Indeed, deleting an available vertex preserves $S$, while deleting a missing
vertex lowers the filtration.  This produces a convergent interaction spectral
sequence whose first page is assembled from the homology of the
$\Lambda_S$.  The cores project to chain-supported bicliques of $G_\psi$.
Under the matching hypothesis only $r=2$ occurs, so the spectral sequence
collapses immediately and recovers Theorem~\ref{thm:exclusive-matching}.

This filtration is the natural next object beyond matching.  The smallest
nonmatching example above shows that shared endpoints already create higher
core differentials; therefore a higher-dimensional analogue of the low-height
rooted-forest theorem must control these interactions rather than only the
acyclicity of $G_\psi$.

\begin{remark}[Priority boundary]
The deletion/cofiber technology used here is classical.  In particular,
vertex-cover obstruction complexes already provide general homotopical tools
for comparing a complex with unions of induced subcomplexes
\cite{ChacholskiEtAl2021}, while poset-fiber decompositions give broad results
under fiber-connectivity hypotheses \cite{BjornerWachsWelker2005}.  The
candidate contribution of Theorem~\ref{thm:exclusive-matching} is the
observation-theoretic two-colour recognition and the resulting exact coarse
edge-link formula.  No claim is made that simplicial vertex deletion or
homotopy cofibers themselves are new.
\end{remark}

# Higher-Dimensional Inversion Complex Classification Gate

This package executes the requested research gate for the carrier-splitting inversion complex.

## Verdict

**Level A — Strong Success (mathematical), with conservative novelty language.**

The strongest result is the **Exclusive-Inversion Matching Theorem**.  If the bipartite graph from `1-only` coarse states to later `0-only` coarse states is a matching, then for every coefficient ring `R`

\[
\widetilde H_n(\operatorname{Cone}(\Delta\pi);R)
\cong
\bigoplus_{(p,z)\in E_\psi}
\widetilde H_{n-2}(\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z];R).
\]

This is an all-height exact classification and can contain torsion.  The first nonmatching shared endpoint already destroys naive edgewise additivity.

## Main files

- `HIGHER_DIMENSIONAL_INVERSION_GATE.md` — master report and answers to the ten gate questions.
- `EXACT_THEOREMS_AND_PROOFS.md` — theorem statements and proofs.
- `INVERSION_CHAIN_COMPLEX.md` — chain-level and interaction-core formulations.
- `STRUCTURAL_CLASS_COMPARISON.md` — comparison of requested structural programs.
- `COUNTEREXAMPLES_AND_OBSTRUCTIONS.md` — sharpness and minimal failures.
- `BOOLEAN_HORN_CASES.md` — Boolean, Horn, dual-Horn, distributive cases.
- `FIBER_TOPOLOGY_CASES.md` — comparison with controlled-fiber theory.
- `TU_AND_TORSION_AUDIT.md` — TU boundary and torsion audit.
- `COMPUTATIONAL_CLASSIFICATION.md` — finite-search methodology and results.
- `LITERATURE_PRIORITY_MAP.md` — theorem-level prior-art map through September 2026.
- `ADVERSARIAL_REVIEWS.md` — independent and hostile specialist attacks.
- `MANUSCRIPT_REVISION_SECTION.tex` — proposed new paper section (gate reached Level A).
- `MANUSCRIPT_BIBLIOGRAPHY_ADDITIONS.tex` — references needed by that section.
- `HANDOFF_TO_MASTER.md` — compact integration handoff.

- `verify_matching_inversion_theorem.py`

- `boolean_horn_verification.json`

Run the three verification scripts with Python 3 and SymPy installed.  The matching script performs exact integral Smith-normal-form calculations for the exhaustive small cases and additional deterministic finite-field checks at five coarse states.

# Structural Class Comparison

| Structural class | Exact result found | Nontrivial in dimension >2? | Torsion? | Priority assessment |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Exclusive inversion graph is a matching | Direct-sum coarse-edge-link formula for all integral cone homology | **Yes** | **Yes** | Strongest gate result; specialized exact theorem, close to standard vertex-deletion machinery |
| Bounded coarse poset + matching | Only global bottom-to-top inversion can contribute | Yes | Depends on proper part | Clean corollary |
| Finite distributive lattice + endpoint matching | Boolean `B_r` gives `H_r=Z`; non-Boolean distributive gives zero | **Yes** | No | Very clean structured example; crosscut theory is standard |
| Entire refined relation Horn / meet-closed | Both refined and projected posets have minima; cone contractible | No | No | Exact but topologically trivial |
| Entire refined relation dual-Horn / join-closed | Dual contractibility result | No | No | Exact but topologically trivial |
| Exclusive inversion graph empty | Isotone section; homotopy equivalence | No | No | Exact zeroth obstruction |
| Exclusive inversion graph a forest | No edgewise classification; 3-chain star is counterexample | Already fails in smallest star | N/A | **Rejected** |
| Coarse chain | Existing Ferrers/independence-complex trichotomy | No rich high homology | No | Mostly prior art / companion result |
| Weighted height <=2 | Existing rooted-incidence/TU classification | Dimension <=2 only | No | Previous exact theorem |
| Height 3 without further restriction | Torsion already possible | Yes | Yes | Too broad for clean coefficient-independent theorem |
| Controlled BWW lower fibers | Classical wedge/fiber results under connectivity hypotheses | Sometimes | Yes | Strong prior art; useful sufficient framework |
| Shellable/Cohen--Macaulay relevant edge links + matching | Matching formula specializes to concentrated/torsion-free homology as appropriate | Yes | Usually no over chosen coefficients | Corollary, not separate core theorem |
| General exclusive graph | Interaction-core spectral sequence indexed by chain-supported bicliques | Yes | Yes | Level-C general machinery; classification open |

## Main comparison

The strongest natural dividing line discovered is **interaction degree**, not height or graph acyclicity.

- `E_psi = empty`: no mixed interaction exists; a monotone section gives homotopy neutrality.
- `E_psi` a matching: every mixed relative simplex has one unique exclusive edge; exact link summation follows.
- first shared endpoint: three-vertex cores appear and generate differentials between edge defects.
- larger bicliques: higher interaction levels appear.

This explains both why the matching theorem is exact and why the forest generalization fails.

# Total Unimodularity and Torsion Audit

## 1. Low height

For weighted height at most two, the prior rooted-incidence theorem identifies the relative boundary map with a signed graph-incidence matrix.  That matrix is totally unimodular, so all relative integral homology is free and coefficient-independent.

## 2. What changes in high dimension

The all-height exclusive-inversion matching theorem gives

\[
H_n(Cone(Delta pi);Z)
\cong
\bigoplus_{(p,z)\in E_psi}
\widetilde H_{n-2}(lk_{Delta Q}[p,z];Z).
\]

Therefore torsion in an edge link is inherited directly by the cone.

The endpoint realization

\[
Q=0hat\oplus R\oplus1hat
\]

with only the endpoint inversion transfers

\[
\widetilde H_*(Delta R;Z)
\]

two degrees upward.  Choosing `R` with `Z/2` torsion gives torsion while `E_psi` remains a one-edge matching.

So:

\[
\boxed{\text{exclusive-inversion matching does not imply TU.}}
\]

## 3. Dey--Hirani--Krishnamoorthy benchmark

Dey, Hirani, and Krishnamoorthy prove that for a finite simplicial complex, a boundary matrix `partial_{p+1}` is totally unimodular iff all specified pure relative subcomplex pairs in dimensions `p,p+1` have torsion-free `H_p`.

This matters here because **global torsion-freeness of the carrier cone is weaker than TU**.  Even if every edge link in the matching theorem is torsion-free, that only controls the homology of the particular carrier-splitting pair; it does not automatically control every pure subpair required by the TU characterization.

## 4. Safe conclusions

1. If one relevant edge link has torsion, the carrier cone has torsion and the hoped-for blanket TU property fails.
2. If every relevant edge link has torsion-free integral homology, the carrier cone is torsion-free.
3. Statement 2 does **not** imply that every relative boundary matrix is TU.
4. The Boolean/distributive endpoint examples are torsion-free, but no new global TU theorem is claimed for them.

## 5. Small explicit torsion construction

Take a finite poset `R` whose order complex has `H_1 ~= Z/2`, for example a standard finite-poset model of `RP^2`.  Add global endpoints and use the one-edge matching profile.  Then

\[
H_3(Cone(Delta pi);Z)\cong Z/2.
\]

The companion paper cites a 13-point projective-plane model, giving a concrete small construction after adding the two endpoint states.  This is an explicit example, not a new minimality claim.

## 6. Forbidden-minor question

No finite forbidden-subconfiguration characterization of TU was obtained.  The matching realization shows why a graph-only obstruction list cannot work: a one-edge exclusive graph can already carry arbitrarily complicated torsion through its coarse edge link.

Any future TU classification must constrain the **link topology or link boundary matrices**, not only the exclusive inversion graph.

\section{Carrier splitting under a new Boolean observation}\label{sec:carrier-splitting}

We now treat the refinement regime left open in the previous draft: a new
observation is not constant on every current observational-equivalence class, so
one old $T_0$ state can split into two refined states.  This operation is not a
cover refinement and is not, on its face, a same-carrier order thinning.  It does,
however, admit a canonical factorization through one.

Let $W$ be the finite world set, let $\Phi$ be the current observation family,
and write
\[
 Q=o_\Phi(W)\subseteq\{0,1\}^{I}
\]
for the finite $T_0$ quotient ordered coordinatewise.  Add one Boolean
observation $\psi$.  The refined quotient is
\[
 Q^\psi=o_{\Phi\cup\{\psi\}}(W)
 \subseteq Q\times\{0,1\},
\]
with the product order.  Let
\[
 \pi:Q^\psi\longrightarrow Q,
 \qquad \pi(s,a)=s,
\]
be the coordinate-forgetting map.  For $a\in\{0,1\}$ put
\[
 A_a:=\{s\in Q:(s,a)\in Q^\psi\},
 \qquad C:=A_0\cap A_1.
\]
Thus $A_0\cup A_1=Q$, and $C$ is precisely the set of old observational
states that split.

\begin{definition}[Split completion]
On the same carrier as $Q^\psi$, define the split-completion order
$\widehat Q^\psi$ by
\[
 (s,a)\leq_{\widehat Q}(t,b)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \bigl(s<t\text{ in }Q\bigr)
 \ \text{or}\ 
 \bigl(s=t\text{ and }a\leq b\bigr).
\]
Equivalently, $\widehat Q^\psi$ is the lexicographic sum over $Q$ of the
nonempty fiber chains
\[
 F_s:=\{a\in\{0,1\}:(s,a)\in Q^\psi\}.
\]
Let $b(s,a)=a$ be the new-bit label on this expanded carrier.
\end{definition}

The distinction between $Q^\psi$ and $\widehat Q^\psi$ is exact.  The split
completion remembers every old comparison between coarse states, independently
of the new bit.  The actual refined order keeps only those comparisons along
which the new bit is nondecreasing.

\begin{theorem}[Carrier-splitting factorization]\label{thm:split-factorization}
With the notation above:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item the projection $p:\widehat Q^\psi\to Q$, $p(s,a)=s$, is a homotopy
  equivalence of finite posets; in fact $\widehat Q^\psi$ beat-reduces to a
  subposet isomorphic to $Q$;
\item the actual refined quotient is exactly the one-bit thinning of the split
  completion,
  \[
    Q^\psi=(\widehat Q^\psi)_b,
  \]
  meaning that a comparison $x<_{\widehat Q}y$ is retained precisely when
  $b(x)\leq b(y)$;
\item if $i:\Delta(Q^\psi)\hookrightarrow\Delta(\widehat Q^\psi)$ is the
  inclusion, then $\Delta(\pi)=\Delta(p)\circ i$, and there is a homotopy
  equivalence of homotopy cofibers
  \[
  \operatorname{Cof}(\Delta\pi)\simeq
  \operatorname{Cof}(i).
  \]
  Consequently, for every coefficient ring $R$,
  \[
  \widetilde H_n\!\left(\Cone(\Delta\pi);R\right)
  \cong
  H_n\!\left(\Delta(\widehat Q^\psi),\Delta(Q^\psi);R\right).
  \]
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
For every split state $s\in C$, the lower copy $(s,0)$ is an up-beat point of
$\widehat Q^\psi$: its strict upper set has the minimum $(s,1)$, because
$(s,1)$ lies below every copy over every $t>s$.  Remove these lower split
copies one at a time.  What remains has one representative over each $s\in Q$
and is order-isomorphic to $Q$.  Beat-point removal is a strong deformation
retraction for finite $T_0$ spaces, giving (i).

For distinct coarse states $s<t$, the split completion always contains
$(s,a)<(t,b)$ whenever those copies exist.  The product order on $Q^\psi$
retains exactly the cases $a\leq b$.  The same statement holds within a split
fiber, where $(s,0)<(s,1)$ is retained.  This proves (ii).  Part (iii) follows
from $\pi=p\circ i$ and homotopy invariance of the homotopy cofiber under
postcomposition by the homotopy equivalence $\Delta(p)$.  Since $i$ is a
simplicial inclusion, its homotopy cofiber computes the relative homology of
its simplicial pair.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[What is standard and what is specific]
Beat-point reduction is classical finite-space topology, and homotopy cofiber
invariance is standard.  The project-specific content is the observation-theoretic
factorization: an actual split of $T_0$ observational states is converted canonically
into a homotopy-neutral lexicographic expansion followed by the precise one-bit
monotonicity thinning already studied on a fixed carrier.  Thus carrier splitting
is not a fourth unrelated operation; it is a neutral blow-up plus an order defect.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The exact inversion-chain complex}

Theorem~\ref{thm:split-factorization} gives a chain-level classification without
any nerve hypothesis.

\begin{theorem}[Inversion-chain model]\label{thm:inversion-chain}
For any coefficient ring $R$, the relative group
\[
 C_k\!\left(\Delta(\widehat Q^\psi),\Delta(Q^\psi);R\right)
\]
is free on the strict chains
\[
 x_0<_{\widehat Q}x_1<_{\widehat Q}\cdots<_{\widehat Q}x_k
\]
whose bit word
\[
 b(x_0)b(x_1)\cdots b(x_k)
\]
is not weakly increasing.  Equivalently, a relative generator is exactly a
split-completion chain containing an inversion $1\cdots0$.  Its relative boundary
is the ordinary alternating simplicial boundary with every monotone-bit face set
to zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The two order complexes have the same vertex set.  A split-completion chain is a
simplex of $\Delta(Q^\psi)$ exactly when every comparison in the chain survives
the one-bit thinning, which is equivalent to the bit word being weakly increasing.
Quotienting the simplicial chain groups therefore leaves exactly the nonmonotone
chains, and the relative differential is the induced simplicial differential.
\end{proof}

This formulation is useful computationally: the defect depends only on the old
signature poset and the three-valued fiber profile
\[
 F_s\in\bigl\{\{0\},\{1\},\{0,1\}\bigr\},
\]
not on the number of worlds inside each old equivalence class.

\subsection{Immediate homotopy-neutrality criteria}

The factorization also reveals when splitting is automatically conservative.

\begin{proposition}[Monotone-section criterion]\label{prop:monotone-section}
If $A_1$ is an upward-closed subset of $Q$, then $\pi:Q^\psi\to Q$ is a
homotopy equivalence.  Dually, if $A_0$ is downward closed, then $\pi$ is a
homotopy equivalence.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Assume $A_1$ is upward closed.  Define
\[
 r_+(s)=
 \begin{cases}
 (s,1),&s\in A_1,\\
 (s,0),&s\notin A_1.
 \end{cases}
\]
The upset condition makes $r_+$ order preserving, and $\pi r_+=\mathrm{id}_Q$.
Moreover every $(s,a)\in Q^\psi$ satisfies $(s,a)\leq r_+(s)$, so
$\mathrm{id}_{Q^\psi}\leq r_+\pi$.  The order-homotopy lemma gives
$r_+\pi\simeq\mathrm{id}$ and hence $\pi$ is a homotopy equivalence.  The
$A_0$ statement is dual, using the minimum available bit in each fiber.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Common-outcome anchor]
If every old observational state has at least one refined world with $\psi=1$
($A_1=Q$), or every old state has at least one with $\psi=0$ ($A_0=Q$), then
carrier splitting is homotopy-neutral.  In particular, if every old state genuinely
splits, so $A_0=A_1=Q$, then $Q^\psi=Q\times\{0<1\}$ and the projection is a
homotopy equivalence.
\end{corollary}

Thus the act of duplicating a state is not itself the source of topological defect.
The defect is caused by incompatible outcome availability across comparable coarse
states: a lower state that can realize $1$ together with an upper state that can
realize $0$ creates a potentially deleted comparison.

\subsection{Localization by lower fibers}

For $s\in Q$ define the lower fiber
\[
 L_s:=\pi^{-1}(Q_{\leq s}).
\]
If $s\in A_1$, then $(s,1)$ is a maximum of $L_s$, hence $L_s$ is
contractible.  Therefore all lower-fiber obstructions to Quillen-type equivalence
localize to the $0$-only states $A_0\setminus A_1$.  Dually, all upper-fiber
obstructions localize to the $1$-only states $A_1\setminus A_0$.

This observation does not replace the exact relative complex above.  It does,
however, connect the carrier-splitting problem to the classical poset-fiber
framework.  Under the connectivity hypotheses of the Bj\"orner--Wachs--Welker
fiber theorem, the source $\Delta(Q^\psi)$ admits a wedge decomposition in terms
of the noncontractible lower fibers and upper links.  The important point here is
that the split fibers themselves disappear from that list whenever their top copy
is present.

\subsection{Exact low-height classification}

The general inversion complex can have arbitrarily high dimension.  In the first
nontrivial dimensional regime it collapses to graph incidence and admits a closed
integral classification.

\begin{definition}[Weighted split height]
Let $C=A_0\cap A_1$ be the split set.  Define
\[
 h_\psi(Q)
 :=\max_{s_0<\cdots<s_r\text{ in }Q}
 \left(r+\#\{j:s_j\in C\}\right).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:split-height}
$h_\psi(Q)=\dim\Delta(\widehat Q^\psi)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
A strict coarse chain contributes one vertex from every fiber, and a split fiber can
contribute both copies consecutively.  Taking both copies at every split state on the
chain attains the displayed number, and no split-completion chain can contain more.
\end{proof}

Suppose $h_\psi(Q)\leq2$.  An \emph{inversion edge} is a deleted order-complex edge
of $\Delta(\widehat Q^\psi)$, equivalently a pair
\[
 (s,1)<_{\widehat Q}(t,0),\qquad s<t,
\]
with $s\in A_1$ and $t\in A_0$.  A deleted triangle has one of the four nonmonotone
bit patterns
\[
 010,\qquad100,\qquad101,\qquad110.
\]
It therefore contains either one or two inversion edges.  Introduce one formal root
for each connected component of $Q$ (equivalently of $\widehat Q^\psi$).  The
\emph{carrier-split defect graph} $G_\psi(Q)$ has one vertex for every inversion edge;
a deleted triangle with two inversion edges joins their vertices, while a deleted
triangle with one inversion edge joins that vertex to the root of its component.
Parallel graph edges are allowed.

\begin{theorem}[Carrier-splitting cone classification in weighted height two]
\label{thm:carrier-graph}
Assume $h_\psi(Q)\leq2$.  Let $c_0(G_\psi)$ be the number of connected components
of $G_\psi(Q)$ containing no formal root.  Then
\[
 \widetilde H_n\!\left(\Cone(\Delta\pi);\mathbb Z\right)
 \cong
 \begin{cases}
   \mathbb Z^{\beta_1(G_\psi)},&n=2,\\
   \mathbb Z^{c_0(G_\psi)},&n=1,\\
   0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The relative boundary matrix is totally unimodular.  Hence the same Betti ranks hold
over every field.  Moreover the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item the carrier-splitting cone is acyclic over $\mathbb Z$;
\item it is acyclic over every field;
\item $G_\psi(Q)$ is a rooted forest;
\item $\Delta(\widehat Q^\psi)$ collapses onto $\Delta(Q^\psi)$ through deleted
edge--triangle pairs;
\item $\Delta\pi:\Delta(Q^\psi)\to\Delta(Q)$ is a homotopy equivalence.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:split-factorization}, the mapping-cone homology is the relative
homology of the one-bit thinning
$\Delta(Q^\psi)\subseteq\Delta(\widehat Q^\psi)$.  Lemma~\ref{lem:split-height}
places the split completion in dimension at most two.  The one-bit height-two
incidence theorem from the companion order-thinning analysis applies verbatim: the
relative $C_2\to C_1$ boundary is the oriented incidence matrix of the rooted defect
graph with root rows deleted.  Ordinary graph incidence gives the two displayed free
homology groups and total unimodularity; the rooted-forest condition is equivalent to
perfect relative cancellation and to an elementary collapse.  Finally
$\Delta(p)$ is already a homotopy equivalence, so two-out-of-three identifies
homotopy neutrality of the inclusion with homotopy neutrality of $\Delta\pi$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Status of the low-height theorem]
The graph-incidence algebra, total unimodularity, rooted forests, and beat-point
technology are standard.  The exact height-two theorem for one-bit thinning is proved
in the companion structural-computation manuscript.  The new point here is the
carrier-splitting reduction that makes that theorem applicable to a process which
changes the $T_0$ carrier.  Accordingly, this theorem should be positioned as an
exact transfer theorem, not as a new general theory of rooted forests.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Sharpness beyond weighted height two}

No coefficient-independent forest criterion can hold in unrestricted dimension.
The carrier-splitting family contains the no-split case $C=\varnothing$, which is
exactly arbitrary same-carrier one-bit thinning.  Companion results show that one-bit
thinning in height three can already have relative integral torsion, and in unrestricted
height can encode arbitrary finite-poset homotopy types inside a contractible coarse
cone.  If one insists that at least one old state genuinely split, a disjoint neutral
split component may be adjoined without changing positive-degree cone homology.
Thus the weighted-height-two hypothesis in Theorem~\ref{thm:carrier-graph} marks a
real boundary rather than a presentational convenience.

The appropriate all-height object is therefore the inversion-chain complex of
Theorem~\ref{thm:inversion-chain}, supplemented where useful by poset-fiber or
homotopy-colimit methods.  A realistic next target is not another universal forest
theorem, but a classification of higher-dimensional inversion complexes under
additional structural hypotheses on $Q$ and on the split profile $(A_0,A_1)$.

# Carrier-Splitting Research Gate

**Project:** Mathematical Reconstruction of Matte-Blanco's Unfolding Function and Mental Space  
**Date:** 29 September 2026  
**Status:** **Gate passed in a substantial restricted sense.** The carrier-splitting problem admits an exact reduction in all finite cases and a complete integral classification in weighted height at most two. A universal all-height rooted-forest classification is impossible.

## 1. Main structural result

Let `Q` be the current finite T0 quotient of realized observation signatures and add one Boolean observation `psi`. The refined quotient is

`Q^psi subseteq Q x {0,1}`

with product order, and `pi: Q^psi -> Q` forgets the new bit.

For each coarse state `s`, its refined fiber is one of `{0}`, `{1}`, or `{0,1}`. Define the **split completion** `Qhat^psi` on the same refined carrier by declaring all copies over a strictly smaller coarse state to lie below all copies over a larger coarse state, while keeping `0<1` inside a split fiber.

Then:

1. `Qhat^psi -> Q` is homotopy-neutral and in fact beat-reduces to a copy of `Q`.
2. `Q^psi` is exactly the one-bit monotonicity thinning of `Qhat^psi`: a split-completion comparison is retained iff its bit labels are nondecreasing.
3. The mapping cone of the actual carrier-splitting map has the same homology as the relative pair

   `H_*(Delta Qhat^psi, Delta Q^psi)`.

This is the crucial reduction. Carrier splitting is not an unrelated fourth mechanism: it is a **homotopy-neutral state blow-up followed by a same-carrier order defect**.

## 2. Exact all-height chain model

The relative chain complex is free on chains of `Qhat^psi` whose bit word contains a descent `1...0`.

Thus a relative k-cell is exactly a strict chain

`x_0 < ... < x_k`

whose bit word is not weakly increasing. Its boundary is the usual alternating simplicial boundary, with every face whose bit word becomes monotone set to zero in the relative quotient.

This gives a finite, explicit, coefficient-independent input model at every height. It depends only on:

- the old signature poset `Q`; and
- the three-valued fiber profile `{0}`, `{1}`, `{0,1}` at each coarse state.

The number of worlds inside an old observational class is irrelevant after that profile has been formed.

## 3. Homotopy-neutrality criteria

Write

- `A_1 = {s : a refined state (s,1) exists}`;
- `A_0 = {s : a refined state (s,0) exists}`.

If `A_1` is an upset in `Q`, choose the greatest available bit in each fiber. This gives a monotone section `r_+ : Q -> Q^psi` with `id <= r_+ pi`, proving `pi` is a homotopy equivalence.

Dually, if `A_0` is a downset, choosing the least available bit gives a monotone section and again `pi` is a homotopy equivalence.

Important corollaries:

- if every old class has at least one `psi=1` world, the split is homotopy-neutral;
- if every old class has at least one `psi=0` world, it is homotopy-neutral;
- if **every old class genuinely splits**, then `Q^psi = Q x {0<1}` and the projection is homotopy-neutral.

So duplication itself does not create the defect. The defect is generated by **incompatible outcome availability along old comparisons**.

## 4. Fiber localization

For a coarse state `s`, the lower fiber `pi^{-1}(Q_{<=s})` has maximum `(s,1)` whenever `s in A_1`. Therefore all possible lower-fiber obstructions localize to the 0-only coarse states `A_0 \ A_1`.

Dually, upper-fiber obstructions localize to the 1-only states `A_1 \ A_0`.

This places the exact chain model next to the classical Quillen/Bjorner-Wachs-Welker poset-fiber theory without reducing the result to a nerve argument.

## 5. Complete integral classification in weighted height <= 2

Let `C=A_0 cap A_1` be the set of genuinely split coarse states and define

`h_psi(Q) = max_chain (coarse chain dimension + number of split states on that chain)`.

This is exactly `dim Delta(Qhat^psi)`.

When `h_psi(Q) <= 2`, the relative complex has only deleted edges and triangles. A deleted edge is an inversion

`(s,1) < (t,0)` with `s<t`.

A deleted triangle has one of the four nonmonotone bit patterns

`010, 100, 101, 110`.

As in the companion one-bit thinning theorem, these data form a rooted incidence graph `G_psi(Q)`. Then

- `H_2(Cone Delta pi; Z) ~= Z^{beta_1(G_psi)}`;
- `H_1(Cone Delta pi; Z) ~= Z^{c_0(G_psi)}`;
- all other reduced integral cone homology vanishes;
- the boundary matrix is totally unimodular;
- the same Betti ranks therefore hold over every field;
- cone acyclicity is equivalent to `G_psi(Q)` being a rooted forest;
- equivalently the split-completion order complex collapses onto the actual refined order complex;
- equivalently `Delta pi` is a homotopy equivalence.

This is the nontrivial exact classification sought at this gate.

## 6. Sharpness: why there is no universal forest theorem

The unrestricted carrier-splitting problem contains same-carrier one-bit thinning as the special case with no genuinely split coarse state. The companion structural-computation work already proves that one-bit thinning in height three can have relative integral torsion and, in unrestricted height, can encode arbitrary finite-poset homotopy types inside a contractible coarse cone.

Therefore the weighted-height-two theorem marks a genuine mathematical boundary. Above it, no coefficient-independent rooted-forest criterion can classify the whole problem.

If one insists on examples with an actual split, a neutral split component can be adjoined without altering positive-degree cone homology, so the higher-dimensional obstruction is not an artifact of the no-split limit.

## 7. Exhaustive finite verification

`verify_carrier_splitting.py` exhaustively checked all naturally labelled finite posets on at most four coarse states (deduplicated after transitive closure) and every three-valued fiber profile `{0}`, `{1}`, `{0,1}`.

Results:

- 3,450 poset/profile cases tested;
- 2,744 contained at least one genuine split;
- 545 had nonzero cone homology;
- 305 of those nontrivial cases contained a genuine split;
- 2,172 lay in weighted height <= 2 and all matched the rooted-incidence formula;
- all 2,656 cases satisfying one of the monotone-section criteria were cone-acyclic;
- the direct normalized-chain mapping cone and the relative split-completion complex agreed in every case.

The computation is evidence for the formal proofs, not a substitute for them.

## 8. Literature/priority position

The following ingredients are standard and should be credited explicitly:

- beat-point reductions and strong deformation retracts of finite T0 spaces (Stong);
- Quillen-type fiber criteria and their simple-homotopy refinement (Barmak);
- homotopy decompositions from poset fibers (Bjorner-Wachs-Welker);
- non-Hausdorff mapping cylinders and relation cylinders in finite-poset topology (Fernandez-Minían).

The candidate project-specific contribution is narrower: **the exact observation-theoretic factorization of a T0 carrier split into a neutral lexicographic expansion plus one-bit thinning, and the transfer of the existing exact one-bit defect theorem to that changing-carrier process.** I did not find this exact formulation in the searched literature.

## 9. Recommendation

The research gate has succeeded. The carrier-splitting section is now mathematically strong enough to remain in the draft, and it is substantially more specific than generic cover-refinement or nerve theory.

The next theorem should not try to force a universal all-height forest rule. A better target is a higher-dimensional inversion-complex theorem under additional structure, for example:

- coarse intervals that are shellable or Cohen-Macaulay;
- bounded comparability/treewidth conditions;
- explicit lower-fiber connectivity conditions that make the Bjorner-Wachs-Welker decomposition computable;
- special classes of observation posets such as distributive subposets of Boolean cubes, Horn/dual-Horn signature sets, or the height-two/three regimes already arising in ProLT.

A second useful direction is to characterize exactly when the monotone-section criterion is not merely sufficient but necessary inside such restricted classes.
