# Exact local interaction models

All links below are available links Lambda_S unless explicitly called coarse links. Formulas use missing-first orientation and augmented chains. The coefficient ring is arbitrary.

## K1,2 and K2,1

For P-centre p with Z-leaves z1,z2, incomparable leaves give no triple core; the coarse-edge-link sum is exact. If z1<z2, let e_i=(p0,z_i1) and t=(p0,z1_1,z2_1). Then

    h:Ctilde(Lambda_t) -> Ctilde(Lambda_e1)+Ctilde(Lambda_e2)
      = (inclusion,-inclusion),
    H_n(cone) = H_(n-1)(Cone h).

The dual K2,1 case follows by reversing Q and swapping bits (or the same oriented-boundary calculation).

For the frozen three-chain (1-only,0-only,0-only), the first edge link and triple link are two points; the second edge link is an isolated point and an interval. Each has reduced H0=Z. The induced map is the primitive signed diagonal Z->Z². Thus d1 has rank one and H1(cone)=Z, with all other groups zero. The *coarse* edge links are contractible: this precisely explains why the old independent coarse-link formula fails.

## P4: three edges

Write edges ax,bx,by. The only possible triples are (b0,a0,x1) when b<a and (b0,y1,x1) when y<x. Their boundaries are ax-bx and by-bx. The two possible triple summands share the middle edge bx. Three edge-link summands and up to two triple-link summands form the exact mapping cone. There are no four-cores and no higher differential beyond d1.

## K2,2=C4

If both same-colour pairs are incomparable, four independent coarse-edge-link summands result. If exactly one pair is comparable, there are two triples and two independent star blocks. If both pairs are comparable, there are four edges, four triples, and one four-core, with the full integral three-column complex and d2 formula in MAX_DEGREE_TWO_CLASSIFICATION.md.

For the minimal chain with profile (1,1,0,0), all nine available links have reduced H0=Z. The horizontal complex has ranks 1->4->4, first map injective and second of rank three. It yields H1(cone)=Z, no other groups. An eight-state realization of the same graph instead has d2:Z->Z an isomorphism and acyclic cone; see C4_COUNTEREXAMPLE_PROOF.md. Thus graph type and maximum degree alone do not force E2 collapse.

## First chordal-bipartite non-Ferrers examples

Without connectedness, the smallest is 2K2, already a matching. With connectedness, it is P5 (four edges), not P4: P4 has nested neighbourhoods and is Ferrers. Write P5 edges ax,bx,by,cy. The only possible triples are bax if b<a and bcy if b<c; they have disjoint edge supports and give two independent star blocks.

## First even cycles

C4 is the first cycle and the only degree-two cycle allowing a four-core. For C6 and every longer even cycle, distinct same-colour vertices have distinct two-element neighbourhoods, so transitivity forbids comparable common-neighbour pairs. No triple core exists. The complete answer is the coarse-edge-link sum, with no interaction differential at all. In the minimal height-one realization of C6, all six coarse edge links are empty, so H1(cone)=Z^6.

## First demonstrated higher differential

The seven-state K1,3 witness in COUNTEREXAMPLES_AND_FAILURE_BOUNDARY.md has integral d1=0 but d2:Z->Z² primitive injective. It establishes E2 noncollapse on a tree/Ferrers/chordal-bipartite graph. It is minimal in its own induced-subposet search; global minimum state count is not claimed.

## Interaction-created torsion

The 32-state K1,31 construction in FERRERS_AND_CHORDAL_CASES.md has all available core links torsion-free (reduced H0=Z) and all coarse edge links torsion-free (reduced H1=Z). Its d1 creates Z/2 in H2(cone). This is a constructive existence result, not a smallest-example claim. The exact reduced interaction matrix and all links are verified integrally in interaction_torsion_star.json.

## Exact comparison with computation

The reproducible local-model and integral SNF records are supplied by verify_interaction.py and the supplemental audit scripts. A graph can admit different same-colour orders; each saved model specifies its coarse order and availability. No single small realization is claimed to classify all topologies carried by that graph.

% Candidate insertion after the unmerged higher-dimensional matching section.
% Frozen v0.3 and its existing revision section are not changed by this file.
% Requires the theorem environments and amsmath/amssymb used by the baseline.
\section{Interaction cores beyond matching}
\label{sec:interaction-cores}

Retain $K=\Delta(Q\times\mathbf 2)$, $L=\Delta Q^\psi$, the missing
sets $M_0=P\times\{0\}$ and $M_1=Z\times\{1\}$, and
$U=K_P\cup K_Z$.  Cone homology in this section is reduced homology
of the topological homotopy cofiber, equivalently homology of the algebraic
mapping cone.  The two-colour shift is
\[
 \widetilde H_n(\operatorname{Cone}(\Delta\pi);R)
 \cong H_{n+1}(K,U;R).
\]
For a mixed missing core $S$, put
$\Lambda_S=\operatorname{lk}_K(S)[V(L)]$.
All link chain complexes below are augmented, including degree $-1$.

\begin{proposition}[Interaction spectral sequence]
\label{prop:interaction-ss}
There is a finite convergent spectral sequence
\[
 E^1_{p,q}=\bigoplus_{|S|=p}\widetilde H_q(\Lambda_S;R)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad H_{p+q}(K,U;R),
\]
with $d^r$ of bidegree $(-r,r-1)$.  The first differential is the
signed sum of the inclusion maps obtained by deleting one missing vertex,
omitting nonmixed faces.  If all mixed cores have size at most $M\ge2$,
then $E^{M-1}=E^\infty$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Orient a relative simplex by listing its $p$ missing vertices first and
its available vertices second, with the corresponding shuffle sign.
Its boundary is
\[
 d(S\wedge T)=\sum_i(-1)^i(S\setminus\{s_i\})\wedge T
                 +(-1)^pS\wedge\partial T.
\]
Terms with nonmixed core vanish in the relative complex.  Filtering by
$p$ gives the displayed page and differential.  The filtration is finite.
Only columns $2,\ldots,M$ can occur, so every $d^r$ with $r\ge M-1$
has zero source or target.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact two-column interaction theorem]
\label{thm:two-column-interaction}
Suppose no mixed core has four or more vertices.  Define
\[
 A_\bullet=\bigoplus_{|S|=2}\widetilde C_\bullet(\Lambda_S;R),
 \qquad
 B_\bullet=\bigoplus_{|S|=3}\widetilde C_\bullet(\Lambda_S;R),
\]
and let $h:B_\bullet\to A_\bullet$ be the signed sum of core-deletion
inclusions.  Then
\[
 C_\bullet(K,U;R)\cong\operatorname{Cone}(h)[2],\qquad
 \widetilde H_n(\operatorname{Cone}(\Delta\pi);R)
 \cong H_{n-1}(\operatorname{Cone}(h)).
\]
The interaction spectral sequence collapses at $E^2$, and there is a
natural exact sequence
\[
 0\longrightarrow\operatorname{coker}H_{n-1}(h)
 \longrightarrow\widetilde H_n(\operatorname{Cone}(\Delta\pi);R)
 \longrightarrow\ker H_{n-2}(h)\longrightarrow0.
\]
In particular the cone is $R$-acyclic if and only if $h$ is a
quasi-isomorphism.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The degree-$m$ relative group is $A_{m-2}\oplus B_{m-3}$ and its
boundary is $(a,b)\mapsto(\partial a+hb,-\partial b)$.
This is the asserted shifted chain cone.  Apply the two-colour shift,
the mapping-cone long exact sequence, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:interaction-ss} with $M=3$.
\end{proof}

The exact sequence splits noncanonically over a field.  Over $\mathbb Z$
it splits when the right-hand kernel is free abelian; no splitting is
asserted in general.  Thus collapse alone does not replace the integral
answer by a direct sum of link-homology kernels and cokernels.  Signed
incidence coefficients on link chains likewise do not imply total
unimodularity of the induced maps on homology.

\begin{theorem}[Degree-two classification and its sharp page bound]
\label{thm:degree-two-interaction}
Suppose the exclusive graph has maximum degree at most two.
Every mixed core has size at most four, so $E^3=E^\infty$.
If no $C_4$ component has both its same-colour pairs comparable in $Q$,
Theorem~\ref{thm:two-column-interaction} applies and $E^2=E^\infty$.
In every cycle component of length at least six the cone contribution is
the coarse-edge-link direct sum of the matching theorem.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Transitivity gives $N(p')\subseteq N(p)$ when $p<p'$ in $P$, and
$N(z)\subseteq N(z')$ when $z<z'$ in $Z$.
A mixed core is a biclique with each colour class a chain.  Degree two
bounds both class sizes by two.  A four-core requires a whole $K_{2,2}$
component with both colour pairs comparable.  This proves the bounds.
On a longer cycle, two same-colour degree-two vertices have distinct
neighbourhoods of the same cardinality and cannot be comparable if they
share a neighbour.  Hence there are no triple cores.  No missing vertex
can then lie in a product-edge link, so the original matching proof
applies componentwise without change.
\end{proof}

More explicitly, a path with at least three edges supports triples only
on its first two or last two edges: a comparable common-neighbour pair
must include a leaf.  For a path of at least four edges these end triples
have disjoint edge supports, giving independent star blocks and interior
edge blocks.  A three-edge path has up to two triples sharing its middle
edge and is treated by one instance of $\operatorname{Cone}(h)$.
Every surviving relative face remains in the same exclusive graph
component, so the component decomposition is at chain level.  Links
must nevertheless be calculated in the whole coarse poset.

For a two-edge star with ordered leaves, $h$ is the signed pair of
inclusions from its triple link to its two edge links.  On the frozen
three-chain profile $(1,0,0)$, all three available links have reduced
$H_0=\mathbb Z$ and $h_0$ is the primitive signed diagonal
$\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z^2$.  This gives cone $H_1=\mathbb Z$,
although both coarse edge links are contractible.

\subsection{Higher differentials are necessary}
For a $C_4$ whose two pairs are comparable, write the core order
$a<b<x<y$.  Let $A,B,V$ be the sums of edge, triple, and four-core link
chains respectively.  Then
\[
 C_m(K,U)=A_{m-2}\oplus B_{m-3}\oplus V_{m-4},\qquad
 d(a,b,c)=(\partial a+hb,-\partial b+kc,\partial c),
\]
where $hk=0$.  The only possible higher differential is
\[
 d^2:E^2_{4,q}\longrightarrow E^2_{2,q+1}.
\]
If $\partial c=0$ and $\partial b=kc$, it is represented by $hb$.
Thus a differential lowering core size by at most one can still produce
a nonzero secondary differential.

An explicit eight-state example makes this bound sharp.  Take
$Q=A_2\oplus R\oplus A_2$, with bottom antichain $\{a,a'\}$,
top antichain $\{y,y'\}$, and
$R=\{v,b,w,x\}$ with relations $v<x$, $b<w$, $b<x$.
Make $a,b$ one-only and $x,y$ zero-only; split the other states.
The only nonzero first-page groups are
$E^1_{2,1}=\mathbb Z$ and $E^1_{4,0}=\mathbb Z$.
The four-core link consists of $b_1,x_0$; all triple links are
contractible; only the edge $ay$ has a nontrivial available link, a circle
up to homotopy.  The paths
\[
 x_0-v_0-v_1-a_1-b_1,\qquad
 x_0-y_0-w_0-w_1-b_1
\]
in the two relevant triple links fill the four-core difference.
Their difference generates the sole loop in the $ay$ link.  Therefore
$d^2$ is a unit $\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z$, and $E^3=0$.
The supplementary signed-chain certificate verifies these fillings and
the integral homology directly.

Nor do Ferrers or chordal-bipartite graphs force $E^2$ collapse.
The seven-state poset with covers
$0<1$, $0<2$, $1<3$, $2<3$, $2<5$, $3<4$, $3<6$, $5<6$,
and profile $(1,2,0,0,2,2,0)$ has exclusive graph $K_{1,3}$.
Its integral $E^1=E^2$ has $\mathbb Z^2$ in bidegree $(2,1)$
and $\mathbb Z$ in $(4,0)$; $d^2$ is a primitive injection.
Its only nonzero cone group is $H_2=\mathbb Z$.
These are explicit counterexamples, not global minimality claims.

\subsection{An unbounded interacting class and new torsion}
\begin{proposition}[All-exclusive star]
Let $R$ be a nonempty finite poset.  Take $Q=\{p\}\oplus R$, make
$p$ one-only and every state of $R$ zero-only.  Then $E^2=E^\infty$
integrally and
\[
 \widetilde H_n(\operatorname{Cone}(\Delta\pi);\mathbb Z)
 \cong H_{n-1}(\Delta R;\mathbb Z),
\]
where the right side is ordinary homology.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Every core is $\{p_0\}\cup\sigma_1$ for a nonempty chain $\sigma$
in $R$.  Its available link is the isolated vertex $p_1$ disjoint from
the cone $\Delta(R_{\le\min\sigma}\times\{0\})$.
The difference-of-components generators identify all nonzero link
homology with $\mathbb Z$ in degree zero and identify their inclusion
maps with the identity.  Consequently $d^1$ is, up to a uniform sign,
the ordinary simplicial boundary of $\Delta R$.  The single row
collapses on $E^2$ and has only one filtration grade in each total degree.
\end{proof}

For the nonempty-face poset of a triangulated projective plane, all these
available links have torsion-free homology, and every coarse edge link
is a vertex link in its barycentric subdivision, hence a circle.
Nevertheless the interaction differential creates $\mathbb Z/2$ in
cone degree two.  The explicit six-vertex triangulation in the
supplement gives a 32-state example, with every link and the reduced
interaction complex checked by integral Smith normal form.

\begin{remark}[Scope and priority]
Filtered-complex spectral sequences, link/cofiber recursions, and their
extension issues are classical.  The complexes $\Lambda_S$ are precisely
vertex-cover obstruction complexes in the sense of
Chach\'olski--Jin--Scolamiero--Tombari~\cite{ChacholskiEtAl2021}.
The results here explicitly identify which such complexes interact in
the observation product model, with positive class restrictions and
integral obstructions.  They do not introduce a new general obstruction
theory or supersede poset-fiber theorems.
\end{remark}

# Maximum-degree-two exclusive graphs

## Exact theorem

Let G_psi have maximum degree at most two. Suppose no C4 component has **both** its same-colour pairs comparable in Q. Then every mixed core has size at most three. With A, B, and h as in SPECTRAL_SEQUENCE_CONSTRUCTION.md,

    H_n(cone;R) = H_(n-1)(Cone(h:B->A)),
    E^2 = E^infinity,

over every coefficient ring. Acyclicity is equivalent to all H_q(h) being isomorphisms. Over fields, the kernel-plus-cokernel dimension formula is exact; integrally, use the chain cone or its natural short exact sequence, retaining extensions.

In particular this covers all disjoint unions of paths and even cycles of length at least six, with arbitrary available-link topology and arbitrary numbers of split states. It also covers C4 components with at least one incomparable colour pair. It is not a torsion-free or TU theorem.

## Proof of the structural restriction

For p,p' in P and z,z' in Z, transitivity gives

    p<p' implies N(p') subset N(p),
    z<z' implies N(z) subset N(z').

A mixed core is a biclique with both colour classes chains. Degree at most two bounds each class by two vertices, so cores have size at most four. A four-core requires K2,2, which in a degree-two graph is an entire C4 component, and it requires both same-colour pairs comparable. Conversely these comparisons in K2,2 form a four-core. Excluding this case leaves exactly two possible columns, and the exact chain-cone theorem applies.

## Stronger path and cycle classification

Two distinct same-colour degree-two vertices can be comparable only if they have identical neighbourhoods: inclusion plus equal cardinality forces equality. Such twins produce C4. It follows that:

* A C_(2k) component with k>=3 has no mixed 3-core. Its contribution is exactly the frozen coarse-edge-link sum, even though its graph is not a matching.
* In a path with at least three edges, a 3-core can occur only on the first two or last two edges. It consists of a leaf and its distance-two vertex, together with their common neighbour.
* For a P-coloured leaf a and degree-two P-vertex b, the only permitted comparison is b<a. For a Z-coloured leaf y and degree-two Z-vertex x, it is y<x. Reverse directions would force another exclusive edge.

Thus a path of at least four edges decomposes at chain level into at most two end-star blocks and individual interior edge blocks. The two end triples use disjoint edge sets. A path of three edges is exceptional only in that its two possible triples share the middle edge: use one three-edge/two-triple cone block. A two-edge path is the basic star block. These are exact decompositions, not just Betti-number identities.

The relative complex always splits over exclusive graph components, but the link attached to each block must still be computed in the full Q. Graph isomorphism type alone does not determine the answer.

## The remaining C4 case

If both sides are comparable, label the coarse chain a<b<x<y with a,b in P and x,y in Z. Put A=sum of four edge-link complexes, B=sum of four triple-link complexes, and V=Ctilde(Lambda_abxy). The exact complex is

    C_m(K,U) = A_(m-2) + B_(m-3) + V_(m-4),
    d(a,b,c) = (partial a+h b, -partial b+k c, partial c).

In triple order (abx,aby,axy,bxy), k has signs (-,+,-,+). The h maps are signed inclusions specified by

    h(abx)=bx-ax,   h(aby)=by-ay,
    h(axy)=ax-ay,   h(bxy)=bx-by.

Hence hk=0. The E2 columns are coker(Hh), ker(Hh)/im(Hk), and ker(Hk). The sole possible higher differential is

    d2:E2_(4,q) -> E2_(2,q+1).

For a cycle c in V_q with [kc]=0, choose b in B_(q+1) with partial b=kc; then d2[c]=[hb]. This is a complete chain-level computation and E3=E_infinity. It does not by itself prove E2 collapse.

The eight-state example in C4_COUNTEREXAMPLE_PROOF.md realizes d2 as an isomorphism Z->Z. Thus unrestricted maximum-degree-two E2-collapse is **false**, and the E3 bound is sharp even integrally.

There is nevertheless an exact acyclicity test for the full degree-two class: for every integer q, require the middle module ker(H_q h)/im(H_q k) to vanish and require the secondary map

    d2_q:ker(H_q k) -> coker(H_(q+1) h)

to be an isomorphism. Groups outside the supported degrees are zero. These conditions say exactly that all E3 groups vanish. A finite filtered module is zero exactly when its associated graded is zero, so they are necessary and sufficient for cone acyclicity. Apply this per component, together with the two-column and individual-edge blocks. For nonzero homology, the full chain complex retains the integral extension information that page groups alone omit.

## Status

The no-four-core theorem and its path/cycle classification are proved. The algebraic mechanism is classical. The contribution is an explicit recognition and block decomposition for this observation model. This meets Level B's exact interaction complex plus proved collapse criterion, with Level A-style acyclicity recognition on that restricted class; the conservative overall verdict is Level B. General integral cone homology cannot be advertised as the homology of abstract link-homology groups alone without the stated extension qualification.

# Interaction-core spectral sequence: exact conventions and theorems

Gate date: 29 September 2026. This is a new research artifact. The transferred package and manuscript v0.3 remain frozen.

## 1. Model and homology convention

Let Q be a finite poset, with each state available at bit 0 only (Z), bit 1 only (P), or both bits (C). Let D=Q x {0<1}, K=Delta D, and L=Delta Q^psi. The missing sets are M0=P x {0} and M1=Z x {1}. Put K_P=K[V(K)\M0], K_Z=K[V(K)\M1], and U=K_P union K_Z.

Throughout, H_n(cone) means the homology of the algebraic mapping cone, equivalently **reduced** homology of the topological homotopy cofiber. The frozen reduction gives

    H_n(cone;R) = H_n(K,L;R) = H_(n+1)(K,U;R).

The mixed-core filtration is on C_*(K,U), not directly on C_*(K,L). The latter also has single-colour relative simplices. Conflating the pairs would give an incorrect first page and degree shift.

## 2. Oriented chain identification

A relative simplex has a unique nonempty mixed core S (at least one vertex from each missing colour) and an available simplex T in

    Lambda_S = lk_K(S)[V(L)].

Include the empty available simplex in augmented chain degree -1. Write S=(s_0,...,s_(p-1)) and T=(t_0,...,t_q), in their inherited orders. Orient the full simplex by listing S first and T second. Its sign relative to the original increasing order is the sign of this shuffle. The resulting basis is denoted S wedge T.

The relative boundary is exactly

    d(S wedge T) = sum_i (-1)^i (S\{s_i}) wedge T
                  + (-1)^p S wedge partial(T),

where a term whose remaining core is not mixed is zero. Deleting a missing vertex induces the actual inclusion Lambda_S -> Lambda_(S\{s_i}). Thus d=v+h, where v preserves p, h lowers p by one, and v^2=h^2=vh+hv=0. The equality h^2=0 uses cancellation of the two orders of deletion, including the identical inclusion maps to the common target.

This is a finite double complex, with total degree m=p+q. It is also an explicit general interaction complex **of link chains**. Replacing chains by homology and keeping only h is not valid in general.

## 3. Pages and convergence

Filter increasingly by F_p=span{relative simplices with at most p missing vertices}. Then

    E^0_(p,q) = direct_sum_(|S|=p) Ctilde_q(Lambda_S;R),
    d^0 = (-1)^p partial,
    E^1_(p,q) = direct_sum_(|S|=p) Htilde_q(Lambda_S;R),
    d^1 = sum_i (-1)^i (Lambda_S -> Lambda_(S\{s_i}))_*.

In the general spectral-sequence convention,

    d^r: E^r_(p,q) -> E^r_(p-r,q+r-1).

It converges to gr_F H_(p+q)(K,U;R), hence the associated graded of cone homology in degree n=p+q-1. The filtration is finite and exhaustive, so there are no convergence or completion qualifications. Over a general ring the abutment retains extension data.

For a class represented by x in column p with vx=0, d^1[x]=[hx]. If hx=-vy can be solved in column p-1, the next differential is represented by hy. This zigzag explains why d^2 can be nonzero although the original chain boundary lowers the filtration by at most one. The seven-state star in COUNTEREXAMPLES_AND_FAILURE_BOUNDARY.md realizes this phenomenon integrally.

## 4. Bounded-core collapse theorem

If every mixed core has size at most M>=2, then

    E^(M-1) = E^infinity.

Proof: nonzero columns lie in 2,...,M. A differential with r>=M-1 cannot connect two such columns. This is sharper than the proposed E^M bound, and is standard finite-filtration support reasoning. If there are no mixed cores, the chain complex is zero and the frozen isotone-section theorem additionally gives a homotopy equivalence.

The bound is sharp for M=4: the explicit K_(1,3) example has nonzero d^2 and stabilizes only on E^3.

## 5. Exact two-column theorem

Assume there is no mixed core of cardinality at least four. Define augmented chain complexes

    A = direct_sum_(|S|=2) Ctilde_*(Lambda_S;R),
    B = direct_sum_(|S|=3) Ctilde_*(Lambda_S;R),

and let h:B->A be the signed sum of link inclusions obtained by deleting a core vertex, retaining mixed faces. Use Cone(h)_k=A_k direct_sum B_(k-1), with boundary (a,b)->(partial a+h b,-partial b). Then there is an actual chain isomorphism

    C_*(K,U;R) = Cone(h)[2],
    H_n(cone;R) = H_(n-1)(Cone(h)).

Here a shift [2] raises total degree by two. The two nonzero filtration columns force E^2 collapse. The exact integral conclusion is the natural short exact sequence

    0 -> coker H_(n-1)(h) -> H_n(cone)
      -> ker H_(n-2)(h) -> 0.

Consequently **cone acyclicity is equivalent to h being a quasi-isomorphism**, including augmented link degree -1. This is necessary and sufficient, not just a sufficient fibre criterion. It is a homology statement, and must not be upgraded to homotopy equivalence.

Over a field k, the sequence splits noncanonically and

    dim H_n(cone;k) = dim coker H_(n-1)(h) + dim ker H_(n-2)(h).

Over Z it splits if the right-hand kernel is free abelian. No general splitting is asserted. If all relevant link homology groups are free abelian, this freeness condition holds, but cokernels can still have torsion. Over arbitrary coefficient rings, use the chain cone or the exact sequence without assuming projectivity.

## 6. One-column extension of the matching theorem

The following condition is equivalent to having no mixed 3-core:

    any two exclusive vertices of the same colour sharing an exclusive
    neighbour are incomparable in Q.

Indeed a comparable such pair and their common neighbour are exactly a mixed 3-core; every larger core contains one. Under this condition, every available edge link is the full product-edge link: any missing vertex in that link would create a 3-core. Thus the frozen matching proof applies unchanged and yields

    H_n(cone;R) = direct_sum_(p,z in E_psi)
                    Htilde_(n-2)(lk_(Delta Q)[p,z];R).

This **extends the hypothesis**, rather than altering the frozen theorem. It covers, for example, every exclusive even cycle of length at least six in the maximum-degree-two class.

## 7. Components and exact recursion for larger cores

Every mixed core lies in one connected component of the exclusive graph. A surviving boundary face stays in that component. Therefore C_*(K,U) decomposes as a direct sum over its nontrivial exclusive graph components. The available links still use the whole Q.

For arbitrary core size, let G_p be the column complex with (G_p)_m=direct_sum_(|S|=p) Ctilde_(m-p)(Lambda_S) and vertical differential (-1)^p partial. The horizontal maps give a degree-zero chain map

    h_p:G_p[-1] -> F_(p-1).

Then

    F_p = Cone(h_p).

This is an exact integral iterative computation retaining chains and extensions. It is standard filtered-chain algebra specialized to this model; it is not a closed formula in abstract link homology groups and is not an independent novelty claim.

## 8. Status and prior-art boundary

The spectral-sequence construction, mapping-cone long exact sequence, and support-based collapse are standard. Lambda_S is precisely an available-vertex obstruction complex in the sense of Chacholski--Jin--Scolamiero--Tombari. The model-specific content is the two-colour product reduction, the recognition of chain-supported mixed cores, the graph/transitivity restrictions proved in MAX_DEGREE_TWO_CLASSIFICATION.md, and the exact positive/negative consequences for observation refinement. See LITERATURE_PRIORITY_MAP.md for theorem-level comparisons.

# Structural theorem notes: exact core interaction and degree two

Independent derivation, 2026-09-29. These notes prove the statements explicitly marked as theorems. The later exact eight-state example in `C4_COUNTEREXAMPLE_PROOF.md` resolves the C4 E2-collapse question negatively. No priority over standard filtered-complex theory is claimed.

## 1. Conventions and the exact chain complex

Use the frozen notation `K = Delta(Q x 2)`, `L = Delta Q^psi`, and `U = K_P union K_Z`. The mixed-core filtration belongs on `C_*(K,U)`, not directly on `C_*(K,L)`. The known two-colour shift is

`H_n(Cone(Delta pi);R) = H_{n+1}(K,U;R)`.

Here cone homology means reduced mapping-cone homology. Let a mixed core `S` have `r` missing vertices in their poset order, and let `T` be an available simplex in `Lambda_S = lk_K(S)[V(L)]`. Reorient the simplex by listing all vertices of `S` first and then all vertices of `T`; the shuffle sign from the original poset order is part of this basis change. The resulting differential is

`d(S wedge T) = sum_i (-1)^i (S minus s_i) wedge T + (-1)^r S wedge d(T)`,

where a term with a nonmixed remaining core is zero in `(K,U)`. The empty available simplex is included in augmented degree `-1`. Thus

`C_m(K,U) = direct_sum_{mixed S} Ctilde_{m-|S|}(Lambda_S)`

as modules, with the stated differential. All link inclusions from deleting a core vertex are actual inclusions: `Lambda_S subset Lambda_(S minus s_i)`.

With total relative degree `m=r+q`,

`E^0_(r,q) = direct_sum_|S|=r Ctilde_q(Lambda_S)`,

`d^0 = (-1)^r d_link`,

`E^1_(r,q) = direct_sum_|S|=r Htilde_q(Lambda_S)`,

and `d^1` is the signed sum of the homology maps of those link inclusions. The differential `d^k` has bidegree `(-k,k-1)`. Convergence is to the associated graded of `H_(r+q)(K,U)`, hence of cone homology in degree `r+q-1`.

**Bounded-core theorem.** If the maximum mixed-core cardinality is `R>=2`, then `E^(R-1)=E^infinity`. Indeed the only possibly nonzero columns are `2,...,R`, so every differential with `k>=R-1` has zero source or target. This includes `R=2 => E^1` collapse and `R=3 => E^2` collapse. It is a column-counting theorem and should not receive an independent novelty claim.

## 2. Exact two-column theorem and integral qualifications

Suppose there are no mixed cores of size four or more. Define ordinary augmented chain complexes

`A = direct_sum_|S|=2 Ctilde_*(Lambda_S)`,

`B = direct_sum_|S|=3 Ctilde_*(Lambda_S)`.

Let `h:B -> A` be the signed sum of link inclusions from deleting one missing vertex, retaining only mixed faces. In degree `m`, the relative differential is

`d(a,b) = (d a + h b, -d b)`

on `A_(m-2) plus B_(m-3)`. Therefore there is a literal chain isomorphism

`C_*(K,U) = Cone(h)[2]`.

Consequently, over any coefficient ring,

`H_n(Cone(Delta pi)) = H_(n-1)(Cone(h))`,

and the mapping-cone long exact sequence gives

`0 -> coker(H_(n-1)h) -> H_n(Cone(Delta pi)) -> ker(H_(n-2)h) -> 0`.

This is an exact necessary-and-sufficient acyclicity criterion: all reduced cone homology vanishes if and only if `H_q(h)` is an isomorphism for every augmented degree `q`.

Over a field the short exact sequence splits, noncanonically. Over `Z`, it also splits whenever the right-hand kernel is free abelian. In general, `E^2` collapse alone does not identify integral cone homology as the direct sum of kernel and cokernel. Nor do the abstract link homology groups, with no chain maps or extension information, automatically determine the integral result. The chain-level mapping cone remains exact without qualification.

The incidence coefficients `0,+1,-1` describe the maps between *link chain groups*. On link homology they are homomorphisms induced by inclusions; they are not automatically scalar incidence matrices in arbitrary homology bases. There is no resulting general total-unimodularity or torsion-freeness claim.

## 3. A stronger one-column criterion than graph matching

**Theorem (no comparable common-neighbour pair).** If every two exclusive vertices of one colour sharing an exclusive neighbour are incomparable in `Q`, then every mixed core has size exactly two, and the frozen matching formula holds unchanged:

`H_n(Cone(Delta pi);R) = direct_sum_(p,z)inE Htilde_(n-2)(lk_(Delta Q)[p,z];R)`.

**Proof.** A larger mixed core contains two missing vertices of the same colour that are comparable and have a common opposite-colour core vertex. Conversely such a pair and their common neighbour form a mixed 3-core. Under the hypothesis no missing vertex lies in the product link of any exclusive edge, because adjoining it would make a mixed 3-core. Thus each available edge link is its full product link. The chain direct sum and product-link suspension proof from the frozen matching theorem apply verbatim. This proves the assertion.

Graph matching is sufficient but not necessary. This theorem concerns the graph together with the order on each colour class; the graph alone does not record the needed comparabilities.

## 4. Universal component decomposition

**Theorem.** The relative chain complex is the direct sum of subcomplexes indexed by the nontrivial connected components of the exclusive graph.

**Proof.** The missing vertices of any mixed relative simplex form a complete bipartite graph, hence all belong to a single connected component. A surviving relative face still has at least one vertex of each colour and remains in that component. Therefore the basis and differential decompose as asserted. Available links in a component still depend on the entire coarse poset; this is not permission to replace `Q` by its induced exclusive-vertex subposet.

## 5. Transitivity restrictions in maximum degree two

For exclusive vertices,

`p<p' => N(p') subseteq N(p)`,

`z<z' => N(z) subseteq N(z')`.

These are immediate from transitivity of `Q`, and materially strengthen what follows from graph degree alone.

**Theorem.** If the exclusive graph has maximum degree at most two, then:

1. Every mixed core has cardinality at most four.
2. A four-core can occur only in a connected component `K_{2,2}=C_4`, and occurs there if and only if both colour classes are comparable pairs in `Q`.
3. In a cycle component `C_(2k)` with `k>=3`, there are no 3-cores. Consequently its homology contribution is the direct coarse-edge-link sum in Section 3.
4. In a path component with at least three edges, a 3-core can occur only on its first two or last two edges. In either case the leaf and the vertex at graph distance two must be comparable in the forced direction described below.

**Proof.** A mixed core is a biclique with each side a chain. Degree two bounds each biclique side by two. A 2-by-2 biclique in a degree-two graph is a whole `C_4` component. Two same-colour degree-two vertices can be comparable only if they have identical neighbourhoods, by the displayed inclusion and equal cardinalities. Identical two-element neighbourhoods give a `C_4` component. On a longer cycle there are no degree-one vertices and no twins, so no such comparable pair exists. In a path with at least three edges, a comparable same-colour common-neighbour pair therefore contains a degree-one leaf and its degree-two distance-two neighbour. These are exactly the pairs at the path ends.

For a `P`-coloured leaf `a` and degree-two `P`-vertex `b`, comparability must be `b<a`. For a `Z`-coloured leaf `y` and degree-two `Z`-vertex `x`, comparability must be `y<x`. The reverse directions would force an additional edge.

**Complete chain-level reduction outside the two-comparable-side C4 case.** Isolated edges contribute the frozen matching summands. A 2-edge path gives one star block if its endpoints are comparable, otherwise two independent edge blocks. A 3-edge path gives a 3-edge, at-most-2-triangle mapping-cone block. A path with at least four edges separates into two disjoint end blocks (each a star block if its endpoint comparability holds) and the remaining individual edge blocks. This last splitting is a literal direct sum because the two possible triples use disjoint edge sets. Longer even cycles consist entirely of individual edge blocks. Every such block has at most two columns, giving the exact cone and acyclicity theorem of Section 2.

In particular, the whole maximum-degree-two class has `E^3` collapse. The stronger `E^2` collapse is proved when no `C_4` component has both sides comparable. A general `E^2` theorem for the remaining C4 case is false: `C4_COUNTEREXAMPLE_PROOF.md` gives an eight-state example with integral `d^2=+/-1`, proving the E3 bound sharp.

## 6. Exact local models

### 6.1 K_(1,2), including the frozen obstruction

Let the centre be `p in P` and leaves `z_1,z_2 in Z`. If the leaves are incomparable there is no triangle and the one-column formula applies. If `z_1<z_2`, let `e_i=(p0,z_i1)` and `t=(p0,z_11,z_21)`. Then

`h: Ctilde(Lambda_t) -> Ctilde(Lambda_e1) plus Ctilde(Lambda_e2)`

is `(i_1,-i_2)` with the ordered orientations used above. The cone formula of Section 2 is the complete chain-level answer. The `K_(2,1)` answer follows by order duality and swapping colours, or directly from the corresponding oriented triangle.

For the minimal coarse chain `p<z_1<z_2` with availability `(1,0,0)`, the available vertices are `p1,z_10,z_20`. The first edge link is two points `p1,z_10`; the second is the disjoint union of `p1` and the segment `z_10<z_20`; the triangle link is two points `p1,z_10`. All have reduced `H_0=Z`. Both inclusion maps are isomorphisms, and `h_0` is the signed diagonal `Z -> Z^2`. Thus the relative cone has exactly `H_1=Z`, and the nonzero `d^1` has rank one. Both *coarse* edge links are contractible, so the independent coarse-link sum is zero. This recovers the frozen counterexample without suppressing it.

### 6.2 P4 (three exclusive edges)

Write edges as `ax,bx,by`, where `a` and `y` are the leaves. The only possible 3-cores are

`t_1=(b0,a0,x1)` if `b<a`,

`t_2=(b0,y1,x1)` if `y<x`.

Their signed boundaries are respectively `ax-bx` and `by-bx`, interpreted as the appropriate link inclusions. There is no four-core because `ay` is absent. Thus `A` has three edge-link summands and `B` has zero, one, or two triple-link summands. Section 2 gives the exact integral answer. When both triple cores exist, they interact through the shared middle edge `bx`; they cannot be treated as independent stars.

### 6.3 K_(2,2)=C4

Label the two `P` vertices `a,b` and the two `Z` vertices `x,y`.

* Neither colour pair comparable: four edge summands, no higher cores; one-column formula.
* Exactly one colour pair comparable: two triple cores and no four-core; two independent two-edge star blocks, hence the two-column theorem.
* Both pairs comparable: relabel so `a<b<x<y`. There are four edges, four triples, and one four-core.

In the last case set `A` to the sum of edge-link chains, `B` to the sum of triple-link chains, and `V=Ctilde(Lambda_abxy)`. Then

`C_m(K,U)=A_(m-2) plus B_(m-3) plus V_(m-4)`

with differential

`d(a,b,c)=(d a+h b, -d b+k c, d c)`.

In the triple order `abx,aby,axy,bxy`, the map `k` has signs `(-,+,-,+)`; every component is the natural link inclusion. The map `h` is determined by

`h(abx)=bx-ax`, `h(aby)=by-ay`,

`h(axy)=ax-ay`, `h(bxy)=bx-by`.

These formulas imply `h k=0`, including the actual inclusion maps. The second page has columns `coker(Hh)`, `ker(Hh)/im(Hk)`, and `ker(Hk)`. There is only one potentially nonzero higher differential:

`d^2: E^2_(4,q) -> E^2_(2,q+1)`.

It has the exact zigzag formula: represent a source class by `c in V_q` with `d c=0`; since `[k c]=0`, choose `b in B_(q+1)` with `d b=k c`. Then

`d^2[c]=[h b]` in `coker(H_(q+1)h)`.

The choice is immaterial on the stated page. There are no further differentials, so `E^3=E^infinity`. The eight-state example proved in `C4_COUNTEREXAMPLE_PROOF.md` has `E^2_(4,0)=E^2_(2,1)=Z` and `d^2=+/-1`, with all cone homology zero. Merely observing that the chain differential lowers core cardinality by at most one does not prove that `d^2=0`.

For the minimal four-chain with profile `(1,1,0,0)`, every available link above is homotopy equivalent to `S^0` and all component maps induce identity up to orientation. The horizontal complex has ranks `1 -> 4 -> 4`, with `k` injective and `h` rank three, so only one `Z` survives in the edge column. The cone has `H_1=Z` and no other reduced homology. This example does not test nonzero `d^2` because its possible source is already killed by `d^1`.

### 6.4 First chordal-bipartite non-Ferrers example

The smallest example without a connectedness requirement is `2K_2`, already a matching. The smallest connected example is `P5`, the four-edge path with edges `ax,bx,by,cy`. The only possible triangles are `bax` if `b<a` and `bcy` if `b<c`. These use disjoint edge sets and give two independent star blocks. Calling `P4` non-Ferrers would be incorrect: its neighbourhoods on each side are nested.

### 6.5 First longer even cycle

For `C6`, and indeed every `C_(2k)` with `k>=3`, same-colour neighbourhoods are distinct sets of size two. Transitivity therefore forbids comparability of a common-neighbour pair. No mixed 3-core exists. Its chain complex is exactly the edge-link direct sum, with no interaction differential at any page. Thus a graph cycle alone is not evidence of core interaction. C4 is the first cycle and the only degree-two cycle allowing a higher core.

## 7. Interaction torsion: updated exact star construction

The existing universality theorem supplies torsion inherited from coarse links in a one-edge matching. That must not be described as torsion created by interaction. A distinct realizable construction, independently checked with the root agent, does give torsion from d1: set `Q={p} ordinal-sum R`, `P={p}`, `Z=R`, and no split states. For each nonempty chain `sigma` of `R`, the mixed core is `p0 union sigma1`, with available link `{p1} disjoint-union Delta(R_<=min(sigma) at bit 0)`, homotopy equivalent to `S^0`. All links thus have torsion-free reduced homology, concentrated in degree zero. The horizontal complex is the negative ordinary, unaugmented chain complex of `Delta R` shifted one core degree. Therefore `H_n cone = H_(n-1)(Delta R)` with ordinary homology on the right. A face poset of a triangulation of `RP^2` gives `H_2 cone=Z/2` and `H_1 cone=Z`: torsion is produced by the d1 interaction complex, with no torsion in any available-link group. This is not a minimality claim. Extensions remain relevant in other integral examples.

## 8. Adversarial checkpoints

* The available links generally cannot be replaced by full coarse edge links outside the one-column case.
* The target shift is `H_n cone = H_(n+1)(K,U)`; omitting it shifts every spectral-sequence conclusion by one.
* Link homology includes degree `-1`, so empty links are retained.
* Spectral-sequence collapse computes associated graded modules, not canonical integral direct sums.
* A two-column bicomplex has no higher differential by support. A three-column one may have a nonzero zigzag differential despite having only vertical and horizontal chain components.
* Graph class alone does not determine homology or even the core poset; same-colour comparability and available links are essential.
* The first chordal-bipartite non-Ferrers connected example is P5, while disconnected 2K2 is smaller.
* All-degree-two E2 collapse is false by the exact eight-state C4 example. The correct unconditional bound is E3, and is sharp.

# Independent mathematical referee report: MIND unfolding v0.4

Review date: 29 September 2026. Target: `Observation_Refinement_Descent_and_Cone_Draft_v0.4.tex` and its 27-page PDF in `Manuscript Convergence 2026-09-29`.

**Recommended disposition: revise before submission.** The carrier-splitting, matching, interaction-complex, degree-two, and explicit torsion results in Sections 7–9 withstand this review. Their proofs, with the manuscript's augmented-chain conventions, support the stated conclusions over the stated coefficients. I found no fatal error in that mathematical core. This conclusion rests on the arguments below, not on passing enumerations.

The manuscript as a whole needs two precise repairs: make the admissibility assumptions on *every* nerve cover explicit in Theorem 11.2, and repair the fixed-arity definition and exceptional one-factor case of Theorem 2.4. The corrected distinction between descent on X and descent on Y is valid. Some further wording should distinguish homological detection from detection of all topological or support changes. Publication novelty is **not verified**. Much of the paper is standard machinery or a direct specialization; the potentially publishable core is the product-poset recognition, graph/transitivity restrictions, and sharp signed integral examples taken together.

This is a fresh AI mathematical review, not independent human peer review or formal proof certification. I read the entire v0.4 source and recorded an initial dependency map and concerns **before** reading earlier review verdicts. I then consulted the requested mathematical supplements and relevant companion claims, derived the arguments and witnesses, retrieved primary literature, and finally compared with internal reviews. No subagents were used. No manuscript, source archive, or earlier certificate was edited. All new files are in this separate directory.

## 1. Claim-by-claim assessment

“Verified” means the proof was checked or independently supplied in this report. Computation is additional evidence. Page numbers below are the manuscript's printed/PDF page numbers. “Valid with repair” distinguishes the intended result from an insufficiently specified literal formulation.

| Manuscript identifier | Status | Evidence and dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| Proposition 2.3, exact-one-false characterization | Verified | Pointwise evaluation of the disjoint Boolean disjuncts. |
| Definition 2.1 / Theorem 2.4, p. 4 | **False without an arity restriction; valid with the repair in §2 below** | For one factor, U(f)=not f is a Boolean-function operator. The printed proof compares tuples of different lengths despite the fixed-length definition. The non-congruence claim is true for each fixed length at least two. |
| Sections 3–4; Theorem 4.2 | Verified, with a minor proof-detail omission | XOR is a vector difference; tetrahedron and Hamming-layer claims follow directly. For the convex-hull equality, a slice vertex cannot have two fractional coordinates; its integral coordinate sum rules out exactly one fractional coordinate. This supplies the short missing argument in part (iii). The nontrivial layer has dimension m−1 and is a simplex exactly at weights 1 and m−1. |
| Theorem 5.2 and Corollary 5.3 | Verified | Relative skeleton chains occur only in degree r. Skeleton homology follows from exactness of simplex chains, Euler characteristic, and the top-dimensional cycle rank. |
| Section 6 refinement distinctions and nerve warning | Verified within the finite signature model | Forgetting coordinates coarsens equivalence; adding truth regions refines the generated topology. A tautological indexed region cones its nerve. No inference from arbitrary observation-list extension to cover refinement is justified or needed. |
| Theorem 7.2, p. 9 | Verified | Lower split copies are up-beat points; the remaining section is Q. The actual order is exactly the bit-monotone suborder. Cofiber invariance applies to the resulting factorization. |
| Theorem 7.4, p. 10 | Verified | Same vertices; retained chains are exactly weakly increasing bit words. The relative basis and boundary follow by quotient. |
| Proposition 7.5 / Corollary 7.6 | Verified | Available isotone section and pointwise comparison with the identity; dual argument for A0. |
| Lower-fiber discussion, §7.3 | Verified as a conditional statement | A top available copy is a maximum of its lower fiber. The Björner–Wachs–Welker conclusion requires the separately stated hypotheses; it is not automatic. |
| Lemma 7.8 / Theorem 7.9, pp. 11–12 | Verified | Weighted chain count; signed reduced graph incidence; leaf collapses. All five asserted equivalences hold. See §3. |

## 2. Prioritized findings and smallest repairs

### A. Missing cover admissibility in Theorem 11.2: substantive hypothesis clarification

The source at line 1226 says “Let V be a finite good cover of Y refining U|Y.” Definition 11.1 (lines 1213–1222) tests intersection contractibility, while the opening qualification refers to a pair for which a relative nerve theorem applies. Admissibility is a property of the covers and comparison maps, not just the pair of spaces. The proof needs a functorial nerve comparison for V as well as U and U|Y.

Under an intersection-only reading, take X=Y=[0,1], U={X}, and

    V1=[0,1/2),   V2=[1/2,1].

Both pieces are contractible, their intersection is empty, and they refine U. The pair and U are as well behaved as possible. Nevertheless N(V) is two points and N(U) is one point. The nerve map is not a homotopy equivalence; its chain cone has H1=Z, whereas H1(X,X)=0. Thus (b), (c), and (d) fail under that literal reading. This is not a counterexample if “the relative nerve theorem applies” is intended to quantify over **all** the displayed cover data; in that intended reading the problem is incomplete specification, not a failed nerve proof.

**Smallest repair:** require a finite simplicial pair with U and V covers by subcomplexes and all nonempty intersections, including restricted intersections, contractible. Alternatively explicitly require suitable numerable open covers and compatible natural nerve comparisons for U, U|Y, and V. A general version can specify a functorial span of homotopy equivalences from the covered spaces to the nerves. The finite-subcomplex version is sufficient and clean. No change to Sections 7–9 follows.

For (e–f), the new support distinction is correct. On an ordinary open-set site, a non-open Y is not automatically an object with a map F(X)→F(Y); either require Y to be admissible or explicitly use the restricted/inverse-image sheaf and its adjunction map. The existing admissibility clause takes the first route. Specify that covers are by inclusion morphisms, their intersections represent the relevant pullbacks, and the cosheaf target is, for example, abelian groups or another suitable cocomplete category. An arbitrary site cannot replace fiber products by set intersections without explanation. These are scope qualifications, not a recurrence of the v0.3 extension error.

### B. Theorem 2.4 has a false one-factor case and an invalid fixed-arity witness

Definition 2.1 fixes F=(f1,…,fm) with m=|A| (source line 143 onward). Theorem 2.4 then denies the existence of a Boolean-function operator for every factorization, but the printed proof uses F=(X,Y) and F′=(X,Y,X∨Z), of different lengths. More basically, for m=1, Π(f)=f and U_th(f)=¬f; the asserted nonexistence is false.

**Smallest repair:** state m≥2 and replace the witness by two m-tuples

    F=(0,1,1,…,1),   F′=(0,0,1,…,1).

Both conjunctions are zero; the unfolding outputs are respectively one and zero. Constants belong to the declared Boolean-function algebra. This proves the fixed-arity claim for every m≥2 without new assumptions. Alternatively allow arbitrary finite factorizations in the definition, but that changes the declared domain. No later topology theorem depends on the printed witness or on the m=1 assertion.

### C. Novelty and theorem hierarchy: publication-level issue, not a correctness failure

The abstract already acknowledges classical machinery and unresolved priority. That restraint is appropriate. It should be made equally clear that the two-column exact sequence is standard mapping-cone algebra, that filtration-width collapse is standard, and that the matching result combines a standard local deletion calculation with a product-link identification. Merely naming the obstruction links or the spectral sequence does not establish a new construction. The source comparison in §8 exhibits the actual parameter identifications.

**Smallest repair:** lead a submission with the observation-product calculation and sharp graph-class boundaries, and classify the general algebra as tools or lemmas. State exactly which specialized results are proposed as contributions. The broad historical/descent narrative may remain interpretive material, but does not strengthen the publication-priority claim. No optional new research theorem is required to make the existing core defensible.

### D. Exposition and proof portability

At source line 1291, the question “Did the underlying support or compatibility structure change?” is said to be answered by cone/relative homology. A proper inclusion {0}⊂[0,1] already changes support while having zero relative homology. Beyond the special low-height theorem, a homology equivalence need not be a homotopy equivalence. Replace the assertion by “Does the chosen map fail to be a homology equivalence?” or explicitly describe cone homology as one obstruction.

The seven-state link assertions are short in the manuscript; the paths in §6 below make the primitive differential reviewable without trusting the JSON. Incorporating that small argument or making a permanent, clearly indexed supplement available would improve proof completeness for external readers. This is not an unresolved mathematical gap after consulting the supplied supplement and performing the derivation.

The theorem's matching isomorphism is not explicitly claimed natural, which is appropriate. If naturality is added, specify at least compatible order embeddings preserving availability and the core labels; arbitrary maps may identify vertices or send missing copies to available copies, and may not induce the proposed link maps. The exact sequence in Theorem 9.2 is naturally functorial in commutative squares of chain maps h. That does not assert a natural splitting.

## 3. Carrier splitting, weighted height, and the five equivalences

For every split s, the strict upper set of (s,0) in the lexicographic completion has minimum (s,1). Removing a lower split copy leaves this property true for all remaining lower split copies. The resulting section takes the upper copy at split states and the unique copy otherwise; it is isomorphic to Q. The projection therefore is a finite-space homotopy equivalence and induces an order-complex homotopy equivalence. The original projection factors through the same-carrier thinning inclusion. All relative/cone statements follow by postcomposing with this equivalence, with reduced homology for the topological cofiber.

A chain of r+1 coarse states can contain an extra vertex precisely at each split state. This proves hψ(Q)=dim ΔQ-hat, not merely an upper bound.

When that dimension is at most two, relative C0=0 and the only possible boundary is d2:C2→C1. Orient triangles by their chain order. The inversion-edge parts of their boundaries are:

| Bit word on vertices 0,1,2 | Surviving terms |
|---|---|
| 010 | +[1,2] |
| 100 | −[0,2]+[0,1] |
| 101 | +[0,1] |
| 110 | +[1,2]−[0,2] |

These are exactly oriented graph columns, after supplying the omitted formal-root entry in a one-entry column. Reversing a graph edge orientation is harmless. A formal root is retained even when isolated. There is one per connected coarse component; a defect-graph component cannot acquire two roots because every contributing triangle stays in one coarse component. Parallel edges count in the graph cycle rank.

The complex is the graph's chain complex relative to its root set, shifted up by one. Thus H2 is free of rank β1 and H1 is free of rank the number of rootless components; all other cone groups vanish. Graph incidence and its row-deleted matrices are totally unimodular. Acyclicity over Z, over every field, or indeed over any one nonzero field is therefore equivalent to β1=c0=0.

If the graph is a rooted forest, every nontrivial component has a nonroot leaf. The corresponding deleted simplicial edge belongs to exactly one remaining triangle. It cannot belong to a retained triangle, because a retained subcomplex contains every face of each of its triangles; and there are no higher simplices. It is genuinely a free face, so leaf removal produces the stated elementary collapse. Repeat until no relative cells remain. A collapse implies a homotopy equivalence and acyclic relative chains. Conversely, if Δπ is a homotopy equivalence, two-out-of-three with the completion projection makes the inclusion a homotopy equivalence, hence its relative homology vanishes and the graph is a rooted forest. This checks every direction without using an invalid general “acyclic cofiber implies equivalence” principle.

The defect graph here has **inversion edges as vertices and deleted triangles as edges**. It is not the exclusive graph Gψ, whose vertices are exclusive coarse states. The distinction is indispensable.

For the higher-height boundary, the companion adjoins a greatest t to R and gives a chosen minimal z and t bit zero, all other states bit one. Internal comparisons survive; only z<t survives at t. The refined complex is ΔR with a collapsible whisker, while the coarse complex is a cone. This proves the claimed universality and homology shift. Taking the face poset of a triangulated RP² gives height-three torsion directly, without relying on the companion's smaller-model citation. A disjoint neutral split state preserves positive cone homology if actual splitting is desired.

## 4. Two-colour model and matching formula

Let K=Δ(Q×2), L=ΔQψ, and let K_P and K_Z delete the lower and upper missing sets respectively. The map (s,a)↦(s,1) retracts K_P to the top row and the dual retracts K_Z to the bottom row. These retractions are compatible with the projection to Q, so the inclusions into K are homotopy equivalences. The triple and excision isomorphisms are

    H_n(K,L) ← H_n(K_P,L) = H_n(U,K_Z) ← H_(n+1)(K,U).

The arrows displayed are isomorphisms, including in degree zero; ordinary negative-degree relative groups are zero. The projection K→ΔQ gives H_n(cone π)=H_n(K,L). This proves the single downward shift from mixed relative degree to cone degree.

In a matching, any relative simplex has exactly two missing vertices, e=(p0,z1). Any further missing vertex in lk_K(e) would form a triple core and give degree at least two at an exclusive endpoint. Thus the **full** product-edge link equals the available link. The differential cannot mix different e-summands. Orienting e first gives

    C_m(K,U)= ⊕_e C-tilde_(m−2)(lk_K e).

In the open product interval between p0 and z1, remove z0 for the first piece and p1 for the second. The first closes to a top row with minimum p1; the second closes to a bottom row with maximum z0. The two endpoints are incomparable, so these order complexes really cover all chains. Their intersection is Δ((p,z)×2), equivalent to Δ(p,z). The union is therefore a suspension. If the coarse interval is empty, the two pieces are points with empty intersection and the union is S0, exactly the augmented suspension convention. The lower and upper link factors are ΔQ_<p and ΔQ_>z, so their joins give lk_K(e)≃Σ lk_ΔQ[p,z]. No Künneth freeness assumption is used.

Consequently, putting m=n+1 gives

    H_n(cone π;R) = ⊕_(p,z) H-tilde_(n−2)(lk_ΔQ[p,z];R).

This holds over every commutative coefficient ring as stated. A two-state chain with profile (1,0) has empty coarse edge link and cone H1=R; a direct calculation confirms the degree. Two disjoint such chains give R² in degree one. Negative cone degrees and degree zero vanish. The empty exclusive graph yields zero mixed complex, and the separate explicit section proves homotopy neutrality. Disconnected links are correctly handled by reduced H0; disconnected Q is handled componentwise by ordinary relative chains.

Bounded-poset localization follows because any nonglobal endpoint supplies a nonempty contractible outside factor. In J(R), the atoms are its minimal singleton ideals. Their join is top exactly when R is an antichain; otherwise the atom crosscut is a full simplex. For r=1, the proper part of B1 is empty and the answer is correctly H1=Z. This also checks the smallest distributive example.

## 5. Interaction filtration, two columns, and degree two

A relative simplex is uniquely S∪T, with p=|S| missing vertices of both colours and an available face T of dimension q, allowing T=∅ and q=−1. Its dimension is p+q. With missing vertices first,

    d(S∧T)=Σ_i (−1)^i (S−s_i)∧T + (−1)^p S∧∂T,

discarding a core face that loses mixedness. Deleting an available vertex preserves p; deleting a missing vertex lowers p by one and induces the actual inclusion of available links. Thus v²=h²=vh+hv=0. Independent signed enumeration checked this identity against every surviving ordinary boundary term in the ten test systems listed in §7.

The increasing filtration F_p is on **C(K,U)**, with E0_(p,q)=⊕ C-tilde_q(ΛS) and vertical sign (−1)^p. Therefore E1_(p,q)=⊕ H-tilde_q(ΛS), d1 is signed core deletion, and d^r has degree (−r,r−1). Cone degree is p+q−1. The filtration is finite and exhaustive over any coefficient ring. Its limit is gr_F H_(p+q)(K,U). Columns 2,…,M imply E^(M−1)=E∞; for M=2 this already means E1. The empty-core case is the zero complex. Augmentation is part of the construction, even where an actual product-model link happens to be nonempty.

With only columns two and three, the degree-m group is A_(m−2)⊕B_(m−3), and its boundary is (a,b)↦(∂a+hb,−∂b). This is exactly Cone(h)[2], with the paper's shift convention. The mapping-cone long exact sequence yields

    0 → coker H_(n−1)(h) → H_n(cone π) → ker H_(n−2)(h) → 0.

Vanishing in every degree is equivalent to h being a quasi-isomorphism, including its augmented degree. Over a field the sequence splits noncanonically. Over Z it splits if the kernel on the right is free; it need not split otherwise. The chain-cone formula determines actual homology; the spectral-sequence page alone generally determines only its associated graded. E∞=0 does determine actual vanishing because the filtration is finite. No missing extension can rescue a nonzero group with zero associated graded.

For degree-two exclusive graphs, p<p′ implies N(p′)⊆N(p); z<z′ implies N(z)⊆N(z′). A mixed core is a biclique whose two colour classes are chains. Each class has at most two elements, and a four-core is a whole K2,2 component with both colour pairs comparable. Conversely those hypotheses produce the four-core. This proves E3 stabilization and the stated conditional E2 result.

Two comparable same-colour vertices of degree two must have identical neighborhoods. In a path of at least three edges, a supported triple consequently contains a leaf and its distance-two neighbor. For P-coloured leaf a and internal b, only b<a is possible; for Z-coloured leaf y and internal x, only y<x is possible. End triples have disjoint edge supports for paths of at least four edges. On a three-edge path they can share the middle edge and must be included in the same cone block. On a cycle of length at least six there are no such twins, hence no triple core; the matching chain argument applies to that component.

Boundary faces preserve the exclusive component, which gives the chain-level direct sum. The links must still be calculated in the **entire** Q. Even for p<c<z with c split and p,z exclusive, the whole-poset coarse edge link is a point, whereas restricting to the exclusive vertices makes it empty and incorrectly predicts H1=Z. The manuscript correctly retains this distinction.

For an ordered C4 core a<b<x<y, direct deletion gives k=(-,+,−,+) in triple order (abx,aby,axy,bxy), and h=(bx−ax, by−ay, ax−ay, bx−by). Substitution gives hk=0. If ∂c=0 and ∂b=kc, the total differential of (0,b,c) is (hb,0,0), proving the stated d² formula. This shows precisely why a double-complex boundary can have a nonzero higher differential.

## 6. Reconstruction of the witnesses

All homology in this section is integral; cone homology is reduced topological-cofiber homology.

**Three-chain (1,0,0).** The refined complex is an isolated point and an edge, while Q is contractible, so H1(cone)=Z. The missing vertices are 0_0,1_1,2_1. The first edge link and the triple link are two points; the second edge link is a point disjoint from an interval. In component-difference bases, deletion gives h0:Z→Z², 1↦(1,−1). Its cokernel is Z. Both coarse edge links are points, so their independent coarse-link contributions vanish. This refutes the forest extension of the coarse-link formula; it does not refute the correct two-column theorem.

**Seven-state star.** Use the covers and profile in the manuscript. Write A=023, B=026, C=036 for the three missing triple cores (each includes 0_0 and the indicated upper missing copies). The four-core link is {0_1,2_0}. The triple links and paths, oriented from 2_0 to 0_1, are:

| Core | Available link / chosen path |
|---|---|
| 023 | 2_0—4_1—0_1 |
| 026 | 2_0—5_1—0_1 |
| 036 | 2_0—3_0—1_0—1_1—0_1 |

All are contractible. The 02 edge link is the four-edge cycle with bipartition {0_1,2_0} and {4_1,5_1}. The 03 edge link is a cone with apex 4_1. The 06 edge link has maximal faces

    [0_1,1_1], [0_1,5_1], [1_0,1_1],
    [1_0,3_0,6_0], [2_0,3_0,6_0],
    [2_0,5_0,5_1], [2_0,5_0,6_0].

It collapses to a cycle: eliminate each triangle through an outer edge, then remove the resulting dangling edges; the remaining cycle passes through 0_1,1_1,1_0,3_0,2_0,5_1. These descriptions establish E1=E2 with Z² at (2,1) and Z at (4,0), and no other groups.

For c=[0_1]−[2_0], the triple corrections in order (023,026,036) have signs (−,+,−). Their horizontal boundary has components B−A at edge 02, A−C at edge 03, and C−B at edge 06. In particular B−A traverses the square 02 once. Thus d² is nonzero and primitive, without deducing primitivity merely from rational rank. The independent code checks the path boundaries and verifies that attaching the target cycle kills H1 without introducing torsion in each noncontractible target link.

For an independent abutment argument, put T=Q−{0}, C_split={1,4,5}. The two lower ideals of the maximal elements of T are cones, with their contractible intersection T_≤3; thus ΔT is contractible. ΔC_split is an edge and an isolated point. The refined complex is the union of a piece retracting to ΔT and a cone on ΔC_split, glued along ΔC_split. Hence H_n(cone)=H_(n−1)(ΔT,ΔC_split), which is Z in degree n=2 only. This confirms the primitive injection Z→Z² and disproves unconditional E2 collapse for forests, Ferrers graphs and chordal-bipartite graphs.

**Eight-state C4.** Use a,a′,v,b,w,x,y,y′ and the profile in §9.1. Its exclusive core is a0<b0<x1<y1. The four-core link is {b1,x0}. Triple links abx and bxy are the two-edge paths through y′1 and a′0 respectively; aby and axy are

    x0—y0—w0—w1—b1,
    x0—v0—v1—a1—b1.

The edge links ax, by and bx are cones with the manuscript's stated apices. The remaining ay link has triangles [a1,b1,w1] and [v0,x0,y0], and edges [a1,v1], [v0,v1], [w0,w1], [w0,y0]. Collapse the two triangle ears to obtain a cycle. Every one of the nine links is thereby identified, not just its Euler characteristic.

Let P_t denote the four paths from x0 to b1. The triple correction is (−P_abx,P_aby,−P_axy,P_bxy). Its ay component is P_axy−P_aby, which goes once around the remaining cycle. The other components lie in contractible links. Thus d²:Z→Z is a unit, E3=0, and the cone is acyclic. This is a sharp E3 bound for maximum degree two, not a proof that every such C4 has nonzero d². The independent full calculations used 108 mixed cells and 340 direct-pair cells; the star used 79 and 205 respectively.

**All-exclusive star and RP².** For Q={p}⊕R, the refined complex is the disjoint union of a point and ΔR. Since Q is contractible, the cofiber long exact sequence already gives H_n(cone)=H_(n−1)(ΔR), with **ordinary H0**. This includes disconnected R: two isolated R states give cone H1=Z². There is no cone H0.

For the filtration proof, every mixed core is p0 followed by a nonempty R1-chain σ. Its available link is isolated p1 disjoint from the cone on R_≤min σ at bit zero. Taking the isolated component minus the lower component gives a consistent H-tilde_0 generator. Core deletion preserves it and gives minus the ordinary simplicial differential of ΔR. Only q=0 survives, so E2=E∞ and there is only one surviving filtration position in each total degree: no extension remains unresolved here.

The ten facets 012,013,024,035,045,125,134,145,234,235 have face vector (6,15,10), every edge in two triangles, and connected cyclic vertex links. This is a connected closed surface with Euler characteristic 1, hence RP². Independently cancelling integer unit chain entries on the original triangulation leaves one degree-zero generator and a differential [2] from degree two to degree one. Thus H0=Z, H1=Z/2. Its nonempty-face poset has 31 states, and adding p gives 32. Every coarse [p,z] link is the vertex link of z in the barycentric subdivision, hence a circle. Every available core link has only free reduced H0=Z. The star formula therefore gives cone H1=Z and H2=Z/2. This verifies precisely torsion created by interaction relative to those local links; it does not say that the chosen underlying R itself is torsion-free.

Neither explicit d² witness establishes global minimality. The RP² example is an existence construction, not a minimum-size result. None of these examples refutes the positive hypotheses actually stated in Theorems 8.3, 9.2 or 9.3.

The 87 coarse types, 16,761 profiles and 70 exclusive graph types are postprocessing, not additional independent experiments. Integral conclusions in this report come from integral arguments or the explicitly named integer computations.

## 8. Prior art, exact overlap, and contribution

Primary sources were retrieved during this review. The following comparison is deliberately narrower than a certification that no equivalent theorem exists elsewhere.

**Chachólski–Jin–Scolamiero–Tombari.** Their published Definition 5.1, Corollary 7.2(2a) and Theorem 8.6 identify the direct antecedents. In the available v1 preprint these are Definition 4.1, Corollary 6.2 (p. 10) and Theorem 7.5 (p. 12). Set X=V(K)−M0, Y=V(K)−M1, A=V(L). Then X∪Y=V(K), K_X∪K_Y=U, and their obstructing simplices are exactly mixed missing cores. Since S∩A=∅, St(S,A)=ΛS after adding the empty face. For matching, put K_e=e*lk_K(e). Its deletion union is ∂e*lk_K(e)=U∩K_e; distinct blocks intersect only in U. Applying their corollary with σ=e and n=1 gives the local double-suspension relative homology. Summing blocks and applying the independently verified product-link suspension and two-colour shift gives Theorem 8.3. Thus its deletion mechanism is a **direct specialization**, with the product identification the specialized content. Theorem 8.6 is a fiber bound, not the paper's exact kernel/cokernel computation. [Published primary text](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s41468-021-00066-2), [numbering cross-check in the primary preprint](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.03409).

**Björner–Wachs–Welker.** Theorem 1.1 (author PDF p. 2) requires each lower fiber to be ℓ(f^−1(Q_<q))-connected; Theorem 2.5 (p. 7) instead requires nonempty fibers and null-homotopic lower-fiber attachments. The identification here is f=π and the lower fibers are the manuscript's L_q. Matching does not force either hypothesis: take p<z and c<z, p one-only, z zero-only, c split. At z, the lower fiber has isolated p1 and the component c0<c1, c0<z0; the preimage below z meets both components. Its inclusion cannot be null-homotopic, and the fiber is not even connected. Consequently those theorems are not blanket corollaries yielding the matching formula by this f. The conditional invocation in §7 is accurate. [Author-hosted primary paper](https://www.math.miami.edu/~wachs/papers/fibers.pdf), Theorems 1.1 and 2.5; [published DOI](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9947-04-03496-8).

**Dey–Hirani–Krishnamoorthy.** Theorem 5.2, preprint p. 11, characterizes TU of ∂_(p+1) by torsion-freeness of H_p(L,L0) for **all** nested pure subcomplex pairs of dimensions p+1 and p. It is not a criterion using only global homology or only this manuscript's single relative pair. In Theorem 7.9, TU follows more directly from the actual reduced incidence matrix. The RP² examples correctly block a universal TU inference. This is **standard machinery/direct specialization**, not a new TU theorem. [Primary preprint](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1001.0338), [published source](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/100800245).

**Filtered-complex algebra.** Weibel's Construction Theorem 5.4.1 (p. 132) and Classical Convergence Theorem 5.5.1 (p. 135) apply with C=C(K,U) and F_p defined above: boundary preservation and finite exhaustion have been checked explicitly. Exercises 5.1.1–5.1.2 (p. 121) already express the two-column extension and secondary zigzag. Proposition 9.1 and the algebra in Theorem 9.2 are therefore **standard machinery**, specialized through the identified link complexes and inclusions. [Primary book chapter](https://math.mit.edu/~hrm/palestine/weibel/05-spectral_sequences.pdf).

**Functorial nerves.** Bauer–Kerber–Roll–Rolle, Theorem 4.8 (retrieved preprint p. 28), gives natural homotopy-equivalence spans for good covers by subcomplexes. Apply it to (X,U), (Y,U|Y), and (Y,V); inclusion and refinement induce maps of covers. Good intersections and subcomplex inclusions verify its hypotheses, and the long exact sequences of pairs give Theorem 11.2(c). Theorem 5.9 (pp. 32–33) supplies the appropriate open/numerable or closed/cofibration alternatives. These are **direct specializations** once the cover hypotheses are made explicit. [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2203.03571), [published DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.exmath.2023.04.005). Ramras's Definition 2.8 and Theorem 2.13 likewise impose actual cover-category conditions and give natural comparison zigzags; they do not remove that requirement. [Published primary source](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00454-025-00809-3). Leitão's cited 2026 cover-refinement paper exists; its detailed stability results were not audited here. [Primary record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22784).

| Candidate contribution | Referee classification |
|---|---|
| Beat-point reduction and cofiber invariance | Standard machinery; split-completion recognition is a direct, useful specialization. |
| Weighted-height-two classification | Direct transfer of the companion's incidence result, now with a self-contained proof. |
| Matching coarse-edge-link formula | Direct deletion specialization plus a model-specific product-link identification; useful exact result, modest standalone novelty. |
| Interaction E1 page, page-width bound, two-column exact sequence | Standard filtered-chain and cone algebra after explicit identification. |
| Transitivity recognition of supported cores; path blocks and long cycles | Substantive specialized combinatorial result in this model, though short; exact priority unresolved. |
| Sharp degree-two E3 bound with eight-state unit d²; seven-state star primitive d² | Substantive specialized examples/class boundaries; potential contribution, priority unresolved. |
| Star realization and RP² torsion with free local links | Elementary realization and explicit specialized failure boundary; potential supporting result, not new general torsion machinery. |
| Cover/descent theorem, Boolean/Hamming and skeleton sections | Standard constructions and interpretations; not a new general descent or topology theorem. |

This is a stronger qualification of the matching theorem's standalone novelty than merely saying “deletion is classical.” It is not a disagreement with its proof. Conversely, the explicit failure of the BWW hypotheses above is a reason not to dismiss the whole matching statement by a slogan about fiber theorems. No failed search is used as positive evidence of novelty.

## 9. Comparison with earlier internal assessments and disposition

The internal reviews' sign, grading, extension, degree-two and torsion conclusions agree with the independent derivations and computations here. Their certificate-annotation explanation is reproduced exactly. Their correction of gluing on a proper support is valid and necessary. I do not treat those agreements as additional independent experiments.

The additional findings in this review are the explicit fixed-arity/one-factor defect, the precise admissibility issue for the refining cover with a concrete counterexample to an intersection-only reading, a concrete matching system where the BWW null-attachment hypothesis fails, and the explicit local identification showing how the matching deletion step follows from the established cofiber result. The cover issue is mainly a statement-scope problem under the intended interpretation; the one-factor case is an actual false literal assertion. Neither invalidates the central Sections 7–9 mathematics.

**Disposition: revise before submission, rather than reconsider the mathematical core.** The strongest defensible article would center on Boolean product-poset relative homology: neutral completion; matching coarse links; exact interaction chains; degree-two support classification and sharp E3 behavior; and the two explicit mechanisms of inherited versus interaction-created torsion. Retain the integral qualifications and negative examples. Required mathematical revisions are the arity repair, explicit cover/site hypotheses, and narrower homological-detection wording. Required positioning work is a precise contribution statement acknowledging direct specializations. A permanent, readable signed-witness supplement is advisable; no further search or conjecture is needed to support the established claims.

For publication, obtain independent human expert judgment on novelty and presentation after those repairs. The review request itself is complete. Any manuscript repair needs a new instruction, since this request expressly excludes implementing repairs. Keep that closely related work in this task to reuse the findings and file/version boundaries; gpt-6-sol with high reasoning is the least costly available model tier I would recommend for these bounded theorem-statement repairs, with no claim of measured pricing savings. Defer unrelated research. No further model run is required to complete this review.

# Initial independent pass (before internal reviews)

Read the complete v0.4 TeX, sections 1-20 and appendix, on 2026-09-29 before consulting earlier verdicts.

Dependency map: 7.2 split completion -> 7.4 inversion chains -> 7.9 weighted-height incidence; full doubling and triple exact sequences -> two-colour shift -> 8.3 matching and coarse-link suspension -> endpoint corollaries. Missing-core filtration -> 9.1 spectral sequence -> 9.2 two-column cone -> 9.3 degree-two bounds; explicit four-core zigzags prove sharpness. All-exclusive star reduces to ordinary chains of R. Cover contiguity + functorial relative nerve hypotheses -> 11.2(a-d); sheaf/cosheaf axioms independently -> 11.2(e-f).

Initial findings/concerns to test:
- Split-completion beat reduction and incidence signs appear correct; distinguish formal-root graph from exclusive graph.
- Two-colour degree shift agrees with the triple sequences; missing-core degree is p+q, cone degree p+q-1.
- Matching link suspension includes the empty-middle case (two incomparable vertices). Need check full link has no further missing vertices.
- Two-column mapping cone signs and degrees appear consistent; integral extensions cannot be dropped.
- Four-cycle and star d2 claims need explicit oriented fillings and primitive integer certificates, not rank calculations.
- Degree-two component decomposition must keep links in the entire poset; manuscript explicitly says this.
- Section 11 must require the nerve hypotheses on V as well as U, and specify site intersections as pullbacks / inclusions, with a cocomplete cosheaf target. Good intersection homotopy types alone are insufficient.
- Section 2 defines fixed length m=|A| but its non-congruence proof compares lengths two and three: repair with equal-length factors or allow arbitrary finite tuples.
- Naturality of the matching direct sum is not automatic for arbitrary poset maps; state a category preserving the availability/core decomposition before strengthening it.
- All-exclusive-star H0 term must be ordinary; verify empty-link, disconnected-R and low-degree behavior.
- Prior-art classification and exact corollary claims remain entirely open at this initial pass.

These are preliminary concerns, not final verdicts or evidence imported from previous reviews.
