Carrier Splitting, Interaction-Core Homology, and Descent
Brian Droncheff
Convergence draft v0.4 — 29 September 2026
Abstract
A 2015 proposal for concept unfolding combined Boolean distinction, simplicial boundary, and
local-to-global reconstruction. We separate these operations and study one precise refinement
model: a new Boolean observation splits the states of a finite observational posetQ, producing
an induced subposetQψ⊆Q×{ 0< 1} with projectionπ.
Carrier splitting factors through a homotopy-neutral split completion followed by order
thinning. In weighted height at most two its cone has a complete integral rooted-incidence
classification. At arbitrary height, a two-colour missing-copy model identifies the obstruction. If
the exclusive inversion graph is a matching, cone homology is the direct sum of coarse edge-link
reduced homology shifted by two, with no torsion-freeness assumption.
Beyond matching, a filtration by mixed-core size has first page given by available-link
homology. When cores have at most three vertices, an explicit chain mapping cone computes the
defect and the spectral sequence collapses atE2, with integral extensions retained. Maximum-
degree-two exclusive graphs stabilize atE3; an eight-stateK2,2 example proves this bound
sharp. A seven-state star rules out unconditionalE2 collapse for forests, Ferrers graphs, and
chordal-bipartite graphs. An all-exclusive star family further shows that interaction can create
torsion even when all local links have torsion-free homology.
The Boolean historical reconstruction and cover/descent framework are retained as separate
interpretations. The general cofiber, obstruction-complex, spectral-sequence, nerve, and sheaf
machinery is classical. The contribution claimed here is the explicit observation-product special-
ization and its positive classifications and integral failure boundaries; publication priority for the
exact specialization remains subject to review.

6 Observation systems and three kinds of refinement
The word “refinement” is overloaded. Three operations should be distinguished.
Definition 6.1(Signature refinement). An observation map isqk :X→Ok. We sayqk+1 refines
qk when there isrk :Ok+1→Ok with qk =rk◦qk+1. Equivalently, everyqk+1-fiber lies in aqk-fiber.
For finite propositional observation families, adding observables refines the generated topology,
can split observational equivalence classes, thins the specialization preorder, and can increase
signature distance. This is an observation-theoretic notion of differentiation.
A second regime occurs when a new observation is constant on every currentT0 equivalence class.
Then the carrier does not split; only order relations can be removed. This becomes a same-carrier
order-thinning problem, which is treated separately in companion work. If the new observation
separates previously identified worlds, the refined carrier gains points and a different construction is
required.
A third notion, used in the main theorem below, is acover refinement. It concerns local pieces
representing a support, not merely enlargement of an observation vocabulary.
Remark 6.2 (Presentation-dependent nerve warning). For an indexed family of truth regions
{ς(φi)}, the observation-side nerve records joint satisfiability, but it is presentation-dependent.
Adding a tautological observation can cone the nerve without changing the generated observation
topology. Therefore arbitrary extension of an observation list should not be identified with a
topologically meaningful nerve filtration. The main theorem uses actual refinement of covers with
explicit containment data.

9.3 Whole-relation Horn closure is neutral
Proposition 9.5. If the nonempty refined Boolean relation is closed under coordinatewise meet,

Proof. Finiteness and meet closure give a minimum in the refined relation. Its coordinate projection

Join closure gives maxima.
The hypothesis concerns the whole realized refined relation; it is not merely a closure assumption
on a selected subset of observations. This is an elementary application of closure-system topology,
not a new Horn theorem.

their extension issues are classical. The complexesΛS are precisely vertex-cover obstruction complexes
in the sense of Chachólski–Jin–Scolamiero–Tombari [23]. The results here explicitly identify which

obstructions. They do not introduce a new general obstruction theory or supersede poset-fiber

11 Observation–Refinement Descent and Cone Theorem
We now state the central structural result in a form adapted to successive concept differentiation.
Definition 11.1(Pair-good cover). LetY ⊆X. A finite coverU ={Ui}i∈I of X is good relative
to Y if, for every nonempty finiteσ⊆I,
Uσ̸= ∅ =⇒ Uσ is contractible,

Theorem 11.2(Observation–Refinement Descent and Cone Theorem). LetY ⊆X be a pair of
spaces for which the relative nerve theorem applies (for example, a finite simplicial pair covered by
suitable subcomplexes, or a paracompact pair with numerable good covers). LetU be a finite cover of
X good relative toY. LetV be a finite good cover ofY refiningU|Y. Choose any refinement map
ρ :V−→U| Y
and let

be the induced simplicial map. Then:
(a) the homotopy class up to contiguity, and hence the induced homology mapu∗, is independent
of the refinement choice;
(b) N(ρ) : Nrv(V)→ Nrv(U|Y ) is a homotopy equivalence;
(c) for any coefficient ringR,
Hn(Cone(C∗(u;R)))∼=Hn(X,Y ;R)
naturally up to the standard nerve identifications;
(d) in the conservative caseY =X, the cone is acyclic, equivalentlyu is a quasi-isomorphism;
(e) assume additionally thatX, Y, the cover members, and their intersections are admissible
objects of the chosen site, and the displayed families are covers in that site. For a sheaf
F, compatible data onU reconstructF(X); compatible data onU|Y orV reconstructF(Y ).
Refinement between the latter two covers preserves that section onY. No unique extension
fromY to X is asserted;
(f) under the same site hypothesis, a cosheafG is assembled as the colimit of the intersection
diagram on each covered support: the colimits areG(X) andG(Y ), respectively. Refinement
on Y preserves its colimit; inclusion induces the comparisonG(Y )→G (X), which need not be
an isomorphism.
Proof. Part (a) is Lemma 10.3. For (b), bothV andU|Y are good covers ofY. The functorial/relative
form of the nerve theorem [27, 15] identifies their nerves withY and identifies the refinement map
with the identity ofY up to homotopy. HenceN(ρ) is a homotopy equivalence.
Let j : Nrv(U|Y ) ↪→ Nrv(U). Since N(ρ) is a homotopy equivalence, the mapping cones of
j◦N(ρ) and j have isomorphic homology; this follows, for example, by comparing the long exact
sequences of the two cones and applying the five lemma. The mapping cone of the chain inclusion
C∗(j) computes
Hn(Nrv(U), Nrv(U|Y );R).
The relative nerve theorem identifies this withHn(X,Y ;R), proving (c). IfY =X, the relative
groups vanish, giving (d).
For (e), apply the sheaf axiom [9] separately on each support: compatible families on a cover of

11.1 What the theorem means for unfolding
The theorem separates two questions that were previously mixed:

A finer description can therefore be topologically conservative while still providing more local
information. Conversely, one may have perfect local gluing on a support whose topology has
genuinely changed.

16 Relation to observation topologies and order thinning
The observation-topology program provides a natural semantic base for the present construction.
An indexed familyΦ = (φi) defines signatures and an observation-generated topology. ExtendingΦ
by new coordinates makes the topology finer, refines observational equivalence, and thins the special-
ization preorder. These facts supply a mathematically clean interpretation of “more differentiated
observation.”
However, the passage from observation topology to complex must be chosen explicitly. The
nerve of the indexed truth regions records joint satisfiability but is not an invariant of the generated
topology. This is why the present paper uses a cover-refinement contract when applying the nerve
theorem.
There is also an important same-carrier subcase. If a new Boolean observation factors through the
currentT0 quotient, it does not split observational states; it only removes comparisons incompatible
with the new bit. Companion work shows that, for a height-two current signature poset and one
new bit, homotopy neutrality can be recognized exactly by a rooted-forest criterion and certified by
simplicial collapse. That result complements the present theorem: the present paper treats changing
carriers, matching and interacting cone defects, and cover-level descent, while the companion
order-thinning paper develops the same-carrier incidence theorem and its separate sharpness results.
17 Persistence and zigzags
A monotone sequence of inclusions of concept complexes
K0↪→K1↪→···
produces an ordinary persistence module on homology. If differentiation alternates between additions,
deletions, support restrictions, or reinterpretations, the natural object is instead a zigzag
K0→K1←K2→K3←··· .
23

PDF PAGE 24
This is preferable to forcing every cognitive or observational change into a monotone filtration.
Cover-level persistence is already an active theory. In particular, Leitão develops persistent
homology directly from cover refinements and proves stability statements that propagate through
nerve and co-nerve functors. Therefore any novelty claim here must be made at the level of the
specific observation semantics, relative defect interpretation, or descent coupling, not at the level of
cover-refinement persistence itself.
18 Priority and novelty position
The standard ingredients include Boolean/Hamming and hypersimplex geometry, chain cones, beat-
point reductions, relative nerve theorems, sheaf descent, poset-fiber methods, and filtered-complex
spectral sequences. For the coverX0 =V (K)\M0, X1 =V (K)\M1, withA =X0∩X1 =V (L),
each ΛS is precisely the available-vertex obstruction complexSt(S,A ) of Chachólski–Jin–Scolamiero–
Tombari [23], with our augmented empty-face convention. Their published Corollary 7.2 treats
several outside vertices and Theorem 8.6 controls the homotopy fibers of the vertex-cover inclusion
through these obstruction complexes.
The Björner–Wachs–Welker fiber theorem [21] gives decompositions under explicit fiber-
connectivity or null-attachment hypotheses. Here the attachment maps are retained and may
produce torsion or higher differentials. This is a narrower exact computation, not a replacement
for general fiber theory. Likewise, Ferrers graph resolutions, graph independence complexes, and
unweighted biclique complexes do not by themselves identify the available-link diagram used here.
The candidate contribution is the explicit observation-product recognition, the coarse-edge-link
matching formula, the transitivity restrictions on interacting cores, and the sharp integral positive
and negative examples. The historical audit and descent framework provide interpretation rather
than priority for classical machinery. No claim of first discovery of the exact specialization is
made solely from its absence in a targeted search. The separate convergence report records the
primary-source comparison and the remaining publication-level judgment.
19 Next theorem target
The matching case, the two-column interaction case, and the degree-twoE3 bound are now
established. Unrestricted E2 collapse in the proposed graph classes is false, so it is no longer an
open target.
Question 19.1(Integral secondary maps in a four-cycle). For each integerk≥ 2, can an exclusive
K2,2 profile with torsion-free available-link homology realized2 : Z→ Z as multiplication byk?
Alternatively, what restrictions does the product-poset geometry impose on the possible integral
secondary maps?
This isolates interaction-created torsion at the smallest exclusive graph that supports a four-
core. The unit example above does not resolve it. The smallest possible higher-differential or
interaction-torsion realization also remains open globally; induced-restriction minimality is weaker.
20 Conclusion
Observation refinement is a transformation between representations, not a chain boundary. Carrier
splitting has a neutral-completion factorization, an exact low-height incidence description, and
24

an all-height matching edge-link formula. Beyond matching, available-link inclusions form the
interaction complex. Two core columns give an exact chain cone andE2 collapse; degree two permits
a genuined2 and only the sharpE3 bound in general. Interaction can create integral torsion even
from torsion-free local links.
Cover refinement and descent answer a separate question on the support actually covered. The
historical Boolean reconstruction, local-to-global data, and structural homology therefore remain
distinct. The mathematical claims of this draft are the stated specialized formulas and failure
boundaries; general topological machinery and publication priority are not silently strengthened.

Successive Concept Differentiation as Observation
Refinement
Carrier Splitting, Interaction-Core Homology, and Descent
Brian Droncheff
Convergence draft v0.4 — 29 September 2026
Abstract
A 2015 proposal for concept unfolding combined Boolean distinction, simplicial boundary, and
local-to-global reconstruction. We separate these operations and study one precise refinement
model: a new Boolean observation splits the states of a finite observational posetQ, producing
an induced subposetQψ⊆Q×{0< 1}with projectionπ.
Carrier splitting factors through a homotopy-neutral split completion followed by order
thinning. In weighted height at most two its cone has a complete integral rooted-incidence
classification. At arbitrary height, a two-colour missing-copy model identifies the obstruction. If
the exclusive inversion graph is a matching, cone homology is the direct sum of coarse edge-link
reduced homology shifted by two, with no torsion-freeness assumption.
Beyond matching, a filtration by mixed-core size has first page given by available-link
homology. When cores have at most three vertices, an explicit chain mapping cone computes the
defect and the spectral sequence collapses atE2, with integral extensions retained. Maximum-
degree-two exclusive graphs stabilize atE3; an eight-stateK2,2 example proves this bound
sharp. A seven-state star rules out unconditionalE2 collapse for forests, Ferrers graphs, and
chordal-bipartite graphs. An all-exclusive star family further shows that interaction can create
torsion even when all local links have torsion-free homology.
The Boolean historical reconstruction and cover/descent framework are retained as separate
interpretations. The general cofiber, obstruction-complex, spectral-sequence, nerve, and sheaf
machinery is classical. The contribution claimed here is the explicit observation-product special-
ization and its positive classifications and integral failure boundaries; publication priority for the
exact specialization remains subject to review.

1 Purpose and scope
The motivating question is
Can successive differentiation of a concept be represented rigorously as a
transformation between complexes?
The answer developed here is yes, provided that four levels are not conflated:
(i) a semantic state space and its attributes;
(ii) an observation or distinction process;
(iii) a combinatorial/topological representation of the observed structure;
(iv) a genuine chain differential on that representation.
The historical thesis is used only as a source of ideas. The mathematical claims below stand on
newly stated definitions.
The resulting architecture has two primary operators:
d :Cn(Kk;R)−→Cn−1(Kk;R), d 2 = 0,
and
Uk :C•(Kk;R)−→C•(Kk+1;R),
where d is the ordinary chain differential andUk is induced by an unfolding/refinement map. When
Uk is a chain map, it induces homology maps; when the represented support changes,H∗(Cone(Uk))
measures the change relative to the chosen representation.
1.1 Conventions and result hierarchy
Finite observational posets are assumed nonempty. An order complex includes the empty face. Its
augmented chain complex is denoted˜C∗; in particular ˜H−1(∆ ∅;R) = R. Joins and suspensions
of empty links use this simplicial convention; the formal(−1)-sphere has no vertices. Ordinary
homology is zero in negative degrees. A coefficient ring is commutative with identity.
For a chain mapf : A∗→B∗, use Cone(f)n = Bn⊕An−1 and d(b,a) = (dBb +f(a),−dAa).
For a map of spaces or simplicial complexes,Cone(f) denotes its homotopy cofiber and its homology
is explicitly reduced. For nonempty source and target these conventions agree under the usual chain
comparison. A simplicial map that repeats an image vertex sends that oriented simplex to zero on
normalized chains. A shiftC[k]n =Cn−k has differential(−1)kdC.
The main mathematical results are organized as follows.
(1) Theorem 7.2 converts a changing observational carrier into a neutral split completion followed
by order thinning.
(2) Theorem 7.9 gives the exact integral low-height result; Theorem 8.3 gives the all-height
coarse-edge-link formula.
(3) Theorems 9.2 and 9.3 describe controlled overlap, including the sharp distinction betweenE2
and E3 collapse.

to new general Boolean, polyhedral, or sheaf theory.

6 Observation systems and three kinds of refinement
The word “refinement” is overloaded. Three operations should be distinguished.
Definition 6.1(Signature refinement). An observation map isqk :X→Ok. We sayqk+1 refines
qk when there isrk :Ok+1→Ok with qk =rk◦qk+1. Equivalently, everyqk+1-fiber lies in aqk-fiber.
For finite propositional observation families, adding observables refines the generated topology,
can split observational equivalence classes, thins the specialization preorder, and can increase
signature distance. This is an observation-theoretic notion of differentiation.
A second regime occurs when a new observation is constant on every currentT0 equivalence class.
Then the carrier does not split; only order relations can be removed. This becomes a same-carrier
order-thinning problem, which is treated separately in companion work. If the new observation
separates previously identified worlds, the refined carrier gains points and a different construction is
required.
A third notion, used in the main theorem below, is acover refinement. It concerns local pieces
representing a support, not merely enlargement of an observation vocabulary.
Remark 6.2 (Presentation-dependent nerve warning). For an indexed family of truth regions
{ς(φi)}, the observation-side nerve records joint satisfiability, but it is presentation-dependent.
Adding a tautological observation can cone the nerve without changing the generated observation
topology. Therefore arbitrary extension of an observation list should not be identified with a
topologically meaningful nerve filtration. The main theorem uses actual refinement of covers with
explicit containment data.

No coefficient-independent forest criterion can hold in unrestricted dimension. The carrier-splitting

torsion, and in unrestricted height can encode arbitrary finite-poset homotopy types inside a
contractible coarse cone. If one insists that at least one old state genuinely split, a disjoint neutral
split component may be adjoined without changing positive-degree cone homology. Thus the
weighted-height-two hypothesis in Theorem 7.9 marks a real boundary rather than a presentational
convenience.

supplemented where useful by poset-fiber or homotopy-colimit methods. The next two sections give
all-height results under matching and interaction-core hypotheses, together with explicit obstructions
to stronger graph-class conclusions.

The theorem separates two questions that were previously mixed:
(i) Did the underlying support or compatibility structure change?This is answered by cone/relative
homology.
(ii) Can compatible local descriptions be reconstructed globally?This is answered by descent or
colimit conditions.
A finer description can therefore be topologically conservative while still providing more local
information. Conversely, one may have perfect local gluing on a support whose topology has
genuinely changed.
12 Descent defects for data that are not already a sheaf
If one assumes a sheaf from the beginning, reconstruction is built into the axioms. For modeling it
is useful to measure how a candidate local-data system fails to be a sheaf.
LetF be a presheaf of abelian groups andU ={Ui}a finite cover. Define
C0(U;F) =
∏
i
F(Ui), C 1(U;F) =
∏
i<j
F(Ui∩Uj),
and
(δ0s)ij =sj|Ui∩Uj−si|Ui∩Uj.
Let Z0 = kerδ0 be the compatible local families and let
res :F(X)→Z0(U;F)
be global restriction.
Definition 12.1(Descent defects). Define
Duniq(U;F) = ker(res), D exist(U;F) = coker(res).
Proposition 12.2 (Exact reconstruction criterion). Compatible local data reconstruct a unique
global element if and only if
Duniq = 0 =Dexist.
In particular both defects vanish for a sheaf.
This motivates a two-axis defect signature for an unfolding stepu:
D(u;F) = (H∗(ConeC∗(u)), Duniq, Dexist).
The first entry is structural; the latter two are semantic/local-to-global. They should not be collapsed
into one number.
21

PAGE 22
13 Exact simplicial gluing and the no-filler warning
Proposition 13.1(Exact gluing as a colimit). If a simplicial complexK is covered by subcomplexes
{Ki}i∈I, thenK is the colimit of the full diagram consisting of theKi and all their finite intersections,
with the evident inclusion maps.
This is the rigorous combinatorial version of rebuilding an object from pieces with overlap
provenance.
Proposition 13.2 (Bare proper faces do not determine a filler). The proper-face data of an
n-simplex do not by themselves determine whether then-simplex is present.
Proof. The boundary complex∂∆ n and the filled simplex∆ n have exactly the same proper faces,
but only the latter contains the top-dimensional simplex.
Therefore the historical idea of an “integrator” requires a filler rule, provenance, a flag/clique
convention, a colimit diagram containing the intended top cell, or semantic descent data. Conjunction
of face-formulas is not a general simplicial gluing operation.
14 Finite prototypes
14.1 Three attributes: vertices, cycle, filler
The cumulative distinction filtration form = 3 is
K0 ={1,2,3}↪→K1 =∂∆ 2↪→K2 = ∆ 2.
Over F2:
H0(K0)∼= F3
2, H 1(K1)∼= F2, H >0(K2) = 0.
The first step adds three edges and has
H1(K1,K0)∼= F3
2.
The second adds one triangle and has
H2(K2,K1)∼= F2.
The one-dimensional cycle at the middle stage is therefore not a symmetry invariant; it is the
obstruction created by having all pairwise compatibilities without the triple filler.
14.2 Four attributes: a tetrahedral history complex
Form = 4:
K0⊂K1⊂K2⊂K3 = ∆ 3,
where K1 is the complete graphK4 and K2 is the tetrahedral boundary. The nonzero reduced
homology is
˜H0(K0)∼=R3, H 1(K1)∼=R3, H 2(K2)∼=R.
The next stage fills the tetrahedron and kills the2-cycle.
At the exact-state level, however, thek = 2 Hamming layer has six points and convex hull an
octahedron. This illustrates why the state-layer geometry and the distinction-history complex are
related but not identical constructions.
22

PAGE 23
15 Symmetry, indistinguishability, and homology are different
invariants
Let Aut(K) be the simplicial automorphism group. Let an observation mapq : X→O define
indistinguishability by equal fibers. Neither is determined by homology.
A filled triangle has automorphism groupS3 but trivial positive-dimensional homology. Con-
versely, an asymmetric unicyclic graph can haveH1∼= Z and trivial automorphism group. Thus
cycles cannot generally be identified with symmetry.
There is nevertheless a rigorous symmetry-breaking statement at the observational level. If a
group G acts onX, define
Gq ={g∈G :q(gx) =q(x)∀x∈X}.
If qk+1 refinesqk, then
Gqk+1≤Gqk.
Finer observation can therefore break observational symmetry by shrinking the subgroup that
preserves all observations. This is separate from the homology of the chosen complex.
16 Relation to observation topologies and order thinning
The observation-topology program provides a natural semantic base for the present construction.
An indexed familyΦ = (φi) defines signatures and an observation-generated topology. ExtendingΦ
by new coordinates makes the topology finer, refines observational equivalence, and thins the special-
ization preorder. These facts supply a mathematically clean interpretation of “more differentiated
observation.”
However, the passage from observation topology to complex must be chosen explicitly. The
nerve of the indexed truth regions records joint satisfiability but is not an invariant of the generated
topology. This is why the present paper uses a cover-refinement contract when applying the nerve
theorem.
There is also an important same-carrier subcase. If a new Boolean observation factors through the
currentT0 quotient, it does not split observational states; it only removes comparisons incompatible
with the new bit. Companion work shows that, for a height-two current signature poset and one
new bit, homotopy neutrality can be recognized exactly by a rooted-forest criterion and certified by
simplicial collapse. That result complements the present theorem: the present paper treats changing
carriers, matching and interacting cone defects, and cover-level descent, while the companion
order-thinning paper develops the same-carrier incidence theorem and its separate sharpness results.
17 Persistence and zigzags
A monotone sequence of inclusions of concept complexes
K0↪→K1↪→···
produces an ordinary persistence module on homology. If differentiation alternates between additions,
deletions, support restrictions, or reinterpretations, the natural object is instead a zigzag
K0→K1←K2→K3←···.
23

PAGE 24
This is preferable to forcing every cognitive or observational change into a monotone filtration.
Cover-level persistence is already an active theory. In particular, Leitão develops persistent
homology directly from cover refinements and proves stability statements that propagate through
nerve and co-nerve functors. Therefore any novelty claim here must be made at the level of the
specific observation semantics, relative defect interpretation, or descent coupling, not at the level of
cover-refinement persistence itself.
18 Priority and novelty position
The standard ingredients include Boolean/Hamming and hypersimplex geometry, chain cones, beat-
point reductions, relative nerve theorems, sheaf descent, poset-fiber methods, and filtered-complex
spectral sequences. For the coverX0 =V (K)\M0, X1 =V (K)\M1, withA =X0∩X1 =V (L),
each ΛS is precisely the available-vertex obstruction complexSt(S,A) of Chachólski–Jin–Scolamiero–
Tombari [23], with our augmented empty-face convention. Their published Corollary 7.2 treats
several outside vertices and Theorem 8.6 controls the homotopy fibers of the vertex-cover inclusion
through these obstruction complexes.
The Björner–Wachs–Welker fiber theorem [21] gives decompositions under explicit fiber-
connectivity or null-attachment hypotheses. Here the attachment maps are retained and may
produce torsion or higher differentials. This is a narrower exact computation, not a replacement
for general fiber theory. Likewise, Ferrers graph resolutions, graph independence complexes, and
unweighted biclique complexes do not by themselves identify the available-link diagram used here.
The candidate contribution is the explicit observation-product recognition, the coarse-edge-link
matching formula, the transitivity restrictions on interacting cores, and the sharp integral positive
and negative examples. The historical audit and descent framework provide interpretation rather
than priority for classical machinery. No claim of first discovery of the exact specialization is
made solely from its absence in a targeted search. The separate convergence report records the
primary-source comparison and the remaining publication-level judgment.
19 Next theorem target
The matching case, the two-column interaction case, and the degree-twoE3 bound are now
established. UnrestrictedE2 collapse in the proposed graph classes is false, so it is no longer an
open target.
Question 19.1(Integral secondary maps in a four-cycle). For each integerk≥2, can an exclusive
K2,2 profile with torsion-free available-link homology realized2 : Z→Z as multiplication byk?
Alternatively, what restrictions does the product-poset geometry impose on the possible integral
secondary maps?
This isolates interaction-created torsion at the smallest exclusive graph that supports a four-
core. The unit example above does not resolve it. The smallest possible higher-differential or
interaction-torsion realization also remains open globally; induced-restriction minimality is weaker.
20 Conclusion
Observation refinement is a transformation between representations, not a chain boundary. Carrier
splitting has a neutral-completion factorization, an exact low-height incidence description, and
24

PAGE 25
an all-height matching edge-link formula. Beyond matching, available-link inclusions form the
interaction complex. Two core columns give an exact chain cone andE2 collapse; degree two permits
a genuined2 and only the sharpE3 bound in general. Interaction can create integral torsion even
from torsion-free local links.
Cover refinement and descent answer a separate question on the support actually covered. The
historical Boolean reconstruction, local-to-global data, and structural homology therefore remain
distinct. The mathematical claims of this draft are the stated specialized formulas and failure
boundaries; general topological machinery and publication priority are not silently strengthened.
A Reproducibility
The accompanying scriptverify_unfolding_complexes.py checks the following finite claims over
F2 for 2≤m≤8:
• affine independence of the parent plus all one-flip children;
• exact-layer cardinalities and constant Hamming weights;
• Betti numbers of the cumulative simplex skeletons;
• the relative/mapping-cone rank formula of Theorem 5.2;
• the three-variableG,D,E,Fcalculation extracted from the attached logical-complex notes.
The earlier audit scripts separately verify the non-congruence counterexample, the gated Boolean
derivative identity, the characteristic-two incidence differential, and the failure of the thesis’s printed
gluing identity.
A.1 Carrier-splitting and interaction verification
The transferred matching gate records 3,242 integral matching cases through four coarse states,
1,707 product-link checks overF2, and 639 additional nonempty matching five-state checks overF2.
The interaction gate enumerates 90,201 naturally labelled poset/profile cases through five states
over F2, plus 5,000 seeded six-state trials. Coarse-poset isomorphism postprocessing yields 87 poset
types and 16,761 profiles; exclusive graphs give 70 colour-preserving types with isolated exclusive
vertices retained. These are different counts of the same bounded exhaustive evidence, not additional
independent cases.
The main interaction run makes 435 selected integral comparisons, supplemented by nine exact
local models, signed integer certificates for bothd2 witnesses, and a separate 32-state torsion
construction. The latter checks 181 available links, 31 coarse edge links, and the proved reduced
interaction matrix by Smith normal form, not the whole doubled pair. The projective-plane
triangulation has facets
012,013,024,035,045,125,134,145,234,235.
An additional 20,000 targetedK2,2 trials locate the sharp secondary differential; these trials are not
an exhaustive or uniform isomorphism sample. All coefficients, seeds, scripts, and integer certificates
are recorded in the accompanying interaction-gate reports. Computations support the proofs and
do not establish global minimality or publication priority.

# Manuscript convergence review — 29 September 2026

**Decision:** integrate the transferred matching section and the completed interaction-core gate into a separate v0.4 research draft. The frozen v0.3, original archive, and previous gate records remain unchanged. This is an internal proof/editorial review, not independent peer review or a certification of priority.

## Substantive correction to the frozen baseline

The original Observation–Refinement Descent and Cone Theorem, clauses (e) and (f), conflated reconstruction on a cover of X with reconstruction on a cover of a possibly proper subset Y. Good-cover hypotheses do not make sections on Y uniquely extend to X.

The revised Theorem 11.2 applies the sheaf and cosheaf axioms separately on the support actually covered. Compatible sheaf data on U reconstruct F(X); data on U restricted to Y or on V reconstruct F(Y). Refinement between covers of Y preserves the latter section. The restriction F(X) → F(Y) need not be bijective. For a cosheaf the comparison is G(Y) → G(X), with no isomorphism claimed. The admissible-site hypotheses are stated explicitly.

Example 11.3 records the obstruction: X={a,b} is discrete, Y={a}, and F is the sheaf of integer-valued functions. Singleton covers satisfy the good-cover conditions, but F(X)=Z² → F(Y)=Z is projection; every section on Y has many extensions. The nerve/cone assertions (a)–(d) do not rely on the invalid extension claim and are retained under their stated nerve-theorem hypotheses.

This is a correction of an established manuscript statement, not a new result of the interaction gate. It is deliberately visible in both the paper and this review.

## Theorem hierarchy after integration

| Layer | Retained statement and boundary |
|---|---|
| Observation model | Refinement is not a chain differential; structural homology and semantic descent remain separate. |
| Split completion | The completion is homotopy-neutral; actual refinement is order thinning. |
| Weighted height ≤2 | Rooted-incidence classification, total unimodularity, and the equivalence between acyclicity, rooted forest, relative collapse, and homotopy equivalence. A self-contained signed-incidence and leaf-collapse proof replaces reliance on an external companion. |
| Exclusive matching | Over the stated coefficient ring, cone homology is the sum of coarse edge-link reduced homology shifted by two. Empty links use augmented homology. Matching does not imply torsion-freeness or TU. |
| General mixed cores | Filter C(K,U) by missing-core size. E¹[p,q] is the sum of reduced H_q of the available links; cone degree is p+q−1. Differentials have bidegree (−r,r−1); maximal core size M gives E^(M−1)=E∞. |
| Cores of size ≤3 | C(K,U)=Cone(h)[2]. The cone groups fit the exact kernel/cokernel sequence, with integral extension data retained. Acyclicity is equivalent to h being a quasi-isomorphism. |
| Maximum exclusive degree 2 | E³ collapse is sharp. Excluding a C4 component with both same-colour pairs comparable gives E². Cycles of length ≥6 have no triple cores and admit the edge-link sum. Path endpoint interactions and the shared-middle-edge case are distinguished. |
| All-exclusive stars | E² collapse with cone H_n equal to ordinary H_(n−1)(ΔR), including ordinary H_0. The projective-plane face-poset example creates integral torsion from torsion-free local homology. |
| Whole-relation Horn closure | A nonempty finite meet-closed or join-closed relation and its projection have extrema, hence contractible order complexes. This elementary criterion concerns the whole relation. |

The rooted incidence graph is now denoted D_ψ to distinguish it from the exclusive inversion graph. Augmented links, coefficient conventions, normalized induced simplicial maps, chain-cone convention, and grading shifts are stated near the beginning.

## Negative results explicitly preserved

- Higher-dimensional order thinning can have arbitrary homotopy and torsion phenomena; the low-height graph theorem does not extend universally.
- The three-chain profile (1,0,0) has two contractible coarse edge links but cone H₁=Z. Its available-link interaction map is a primitive signed diagonal Z→Z².
- The seven-state K1,3 example has nonzero primitive d²: Z→Z². Forest, Ferrers, and chordal-bipartite hypotheses alone do not force E² collapse.
- The eight-state C4 example has a unit d²: Z→Z, proving the degree-two E³ bound sharp. The manuscript now lists the relevant links and gives the path-filling argument, in addition to the supplementary integer certificate.
- The 32-state all-exclusive star has cone H₁=Z and H₂=Z/2, although all 181 available links and all 31 coarse edge links have torsion-free homology.
- Spectral-sequence collapse does not determine integral extensions. Signed chain incidences do not imply that induced homology maps are totally unimodular.
- No witness is claimed globally minimal. Induced-restriction minimality and a bounded search are weaker statements.
- The new proper-support descent counterexample is retained alongside the historical negative results.

## Priority and reference audit

The audit positions claims against primary sources; it cannot establish absence of every prior equivalent theorem.

1. **Obstruction complexes:** Λ_S is the induced available-vertex part of the link of S, precisely the vertex-cover obstruction complex used by Chachólski, Jin, Scolamiero, and Tombari. Their general gluing and obstruction machinery is prior art. See the [published paper](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s41468-021-00066-2), including Corollary 7.2 and Theorem 8.6. Candidate distinctiveness lies in the observation-product identification, exact class restrictions, and explicit integral failures.
2. **Poset fibers:** Björner–Wachs–Welker's fiber theorem requires its connectivity hypotheses. The manuscript invokes that framework conditionally and does not claim a blanket wedge decomposition. See the [authors' paper](https://www.math.miami.edu/~wachs/papers/fibers.pdf), Theorem 1.1.
3. **Total unimodularity:** Torsion of the relevant relative groups is central to Dey–Hirani–Krishnamoorthy's TU criterion; torsion-free global homology alone is insufficient. See the [published article](https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/100800245). The draft confines the unconditional incidence/TU conclusion to weighted height at most two.
4. **Nerves and refinement:** Contiguity of refinement choices and functorial nerve comparisons are classical. The draft cites [Bauer–Kerber–Roll–Rolle](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.03571), [Ramras](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00454-025-00809-3), and [Leitão](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22784). These are attribution sources, not evidence that the observation-specific classification is already known or new.
5. **Other standard tools:** Chain cones, relative homology, spectral sequences, crosscut methods, and sheaf descent receive standard references. The Fernández–Minian bibliographic record was completed to DCG 63 (2020), 549–559, consistent with the [author's publication list](https://mate.dm.uba.ar/~gminian/publications.html).

The exact specialization remains a candidate contribution. This draft should not be described as publication-priority certified.

## Computation and verification scope

The manuscript distinguishes the transferred matching checks from the interaction-gate evidence: 90,201 exhaustive naturally labelled cases through five coarse states over F₂, 5,000 seeded six-state trials, 435 selected integral comparisons, nine local models, and a separate targeted C4 search. Canonical counts (87 coarse poset types, 16,761 profiles, 70 colour-preserving graph types) are postprocessing of bounded evidence, not new independent trials.

For this convergence phase, `verify_convergence.py` reruns only the two signed integral d² certificates and the torsion-star construction, directing all new outputs to `build/certificates/`. Every mathematical field is compared with the earlier certificates. The first comparison detected differences only in historical minimality annotations: the scripts/input records were updated after the earlier certificates, with revised wording and induced-subset counts. These metadata differences are explicitly preserved in the verification receipt; no mathematical discrepancy was found and no global minimality is inferred. The torsion-star calculation checks the reduced interaction model and all specified links, not a direct Smith reduction of the entire doubled pair. No large exhaustive enumeration was repeated.

The same script verifies the source ZIP hash, all 83 entries in the transferred SHA256 manifest, unchanged prior-gate files, and the integration input/output hashes. `VERIFICATION_RECEIPT.json` records actual results. `PDF_QA_RECEIPT.json` records compilation, page count, and visual inspection. The source builder asserts unique labels, resolved references, and existing bibliography keys.

The earlier gate's statement that LaTeX tooling was unavailable remains historical. The installed MiKTeX works when granted normal access to its existing per-user configuration and cache; sandbox access, not the manuscript source, caused the initial failure. Compilation uses `--disable-installer` and `--disable-write18`; no packages were installed and no shell escape was enabled.

## Editorial disposition and remaining boundaries

v0.4 is an integrated research draft, not a submission-ready article. The broad historical and semantic framework is retained so that integration does not silently discard the transferred project's scope. A focused paper led by the carrier-splitting and interaction theorems may be more suitable for submission, but that is a separate editorial decision.

The archived companion has the title-page author name **Brian Theory**, while the main paper uses **Brian Droncheff**. The bibliography records the archived name transparently; the intended public attribution should be confirmed before submission. The independent mathematical proof supplied here removes a dependency on accessing that companion for the low-height theorem.

No further mathematical theorem is required to finish this convergence phase. Before publication, obtain an independent expert review of the exact specialization and priority positioning, resolve author attribution and venue scope, and prepare a journal-specific version. The optional subsequent research question is whether a degree-two C4 interaction can realize a nonunit d² while all local link homology is free; it was not pursued here.

Before publication, resolve the companion's title-page name Brian Theory versus the main paper's Brian Droncheff, decide manuscript scope/venue, and obtain independent expert review. No additional theorem is needed for this phase.

# Independent mathematical review of the MIND unfolding manuscript v0.4

You are an independent referee with expertise in finite-poset topology, simplicial and relative homology, filtered chain complexes, spectral sequences, and integral algebra. Review this research draft for correctness, precise scope, and prior-art positioning. Your task is to test the claims, not to endorse the project's existing assessments or develop its next conjecture.

This is a review request. Do not rewrite the manuscript, start a new research gate, contact anyone, publish, or modify the source archive. If you use computational tools, keep new scripts and outputs in a separate review directory. Do not overwrite existing certificates. A human reviewer may simply return the requested report.

## Materials and versions

For a reviewer in the same Windows workspace, the project root is:

`C:\Users\brian\Documents\Math Latex etc\Papers for Publication\The MIND`

Use these three directories relative to that root:

- **Current manuscript:** `Manuscript Convergence 2026-09-29`
- **Interaction supplement:** `Interaction Core Gate 2026-09-29`
- **Transferred archive:** `Transferred Research\MIND_Unfolding_Project_Consolidated_Handoff_2026-09-29`

For a reviewer outside this workspace, the requester must supply the corresponding files. Local path strings do not grant access. Identify any unavailable material and limit your conclusions accordingly; do not imply that you inspected missing files.

The review target is `Observation_Refinement_Descent_and_Cone_Draft_v0.4.tex` and its matching 27-page PDF in the current-manuscript directory. The transferred `01_CURRENT_MANUSCRIPT/Observation_Refinement_Descent_and_Cone_Draft_v0.3` is the frozen historical baseline. Two formerly unmerged sections have been integrated into v0.4 only. The incoming archive and baseline are provenance records, not proof that their statements are correct.

## Reading order and independence

First read v0.4 itself and make your own theorem/dependency map. Prioritize Sections 7–11; assess the surrounding framework for unsupported claims and inconsistencies as well. Record initial concerns before reading earlier review verdicts.

Then consult the interaction supplement's mathematical evidence:

- `SPECTRAL_SEQUENCE_CONSTRUCTION.md`
- `MAX_DEGREE_TWO_CLASSIFICATION.md`
- `C4_COUNTEREXAMPLE_PROOF.md`
- `FERRERS_AND_CHORDAL_CASES.md`
- `LOCAL_INTERACTION_MODELS.md`
- `COUNTEREXAMPLES_AND_FAILURE_BOUNDARY.md`
- `COMPUTATIONAL_INTERACTION_AUDIT.md`
- The Python verifiers and their JSON certificates, especially `verify_d2_certificate.py`, `verify_torsion_star.py`, and the corresponding outputs.

Consult the transferred `02_LATEST_HIGHER_DIMENSIONAL_GATE/EXACT_THEOREMS_AND_PROOFS.md` and `COUNTEREXAMPLES_AND_OBSTRUCTIONS.md` for the matching results. Consult the archived companion in `07_RELATED_THEORY/` only for claims that depend on it.

Finally compare your findings with the current `CONVERGENCE_REVIEW.md`, `INTEGRATION_RECEIPT.json`, `VERIFICATION_RECEIPT.json`, the interaction `LITERATURE_PRIORITY_MAP.md`, and its adversarial review files. Treat these as earlier internal assessments, not independent validation. Distinguish disagreement with a proof from disagreement with wording or novelty positioning.

## Questions requiring explicit answers

1. **Carrier splitting and low height.** Verify the neutral split-completion factorization and its relationship to order thinning. Check the weighted-height-two incidence matrix, boundary signs, root convention, total unimodularity, and every direction in the claimed equivalence between acyclicity, rooted forest, elementary collapse, and homotopy equivalence. Distinguish the incidence graph from the exclusive inversion graph.

2. **Matching theorem and grading.** Independently derive the two-colour relative model with K=Δ(Q×2), L=ΔQ^ψ, and U=K_P∪K_Z. Check the identification of cone H_n with H_(n+1)(K,U), the edge-link suspension, and the final shift by two. Test empty links, disconnected complexes, empty exclusive graphs, low degrees, and the stated coefficient generality. Determine whether any naturality claim needs qualification.

3. **Interaction spectral sequence.** Verify that the filtration is on C(K,U), that E¹_(p,q) is the sum of reduced H_q(Λ_S) for |S|=p with Λ_S=lk_K(S)[V(L)], and that cone degree is p+q−1. Check the missing-first orientation, d=v+h, augmented degree −1, d^r bidegree (−r,r−1), convergence, and page bound. Establish which statements determine actual homology and which determine only associated graded groups.

4. **Exact two-column theorem.** Verify C(K,U)≅Cone(h)[2] when no mixed core has size ≥4. Derive the short exact kernel/cokernel sequence with its stated degrees. Audit the quasi-isomorphism criterion and integral splitting caveat. Do not infer a direct-sum decomposition solely from E² collapse.

5. **Maximum degree two.** Check the same-colour neighbourhood inclusions imposed by transitivity, the characterization of four-cores, the E³ bound, the conditional E² result, path endpoint blocks, the shared-middle-edge case, and the length ≥6 cycle decomposition. Check that componentwise splitting does not incorrectly replace links in the whole poset by links in a component.

6. **Counterexamples and torsion.** Reconstruct the three-chain profile (1,0,0), the seven-state K1,3 primitive d²: Z→Z², and the eight-state C4 unit d²: Z→Z. Check the explicit link descriptions and path fillings rather than accepting a nonzero-rank output alone. Verify the all-exclusive-star formula using ordinary H_(n−1)(ΔR), and the 32-state projective-plane example with cone H₁=Z and H₂=Z/2 despite torsion-free local links. Test whether these witnesses establish exactly the advertised failures of stronger hypotheses. Do not infer global minimality.

7. **Descent correction and other claims.** v0.3 conflated gluing on X with gluing on a proper subset Y. Verify v0.4 Theorem 11.2 and Example 11.3 independently, including the precise site, cover, nerve, relative-homology, sheaf, and cosheaf hypotheses. Check whether additional qualifications are needed. Audit whole-relation meet/join neutrality and the separation between observation refinement, genuine chain differential, and semantic descent.

8. **Prior art and contribution.** Compare exact statements and hypotheses with Chachólski–Jin–Scolamiero–Tombari obstruction complexes, Björner–Wachs–Welker fiber theorems, Dey–Hirani–Krishnamoorthy's TU criterion, and standard filtered-complex and functorial-nerve results. Retrieve primary sources; give theorem/page identifiers and stable links. Classify contributions as standard machinery, direct specialization, substantive specialized result, or unresolved priority. A failed search is not evidence of novelty. If a claim is an immediate corollary, exhibit the parameter identification and verify every hypothesis.

## Computation standards

Separate hand proofs from computation, field calculations from integral calculations, and exhaustive ranges from random/targeted samples. The earlier 90,201 small cases are over F₂; they cannot certify integral conclusions. Canonical/isomorphism counts are postprocessing, not independent experiments. The torsion-star verification uses the reduced interaction complex and local links, not a direct Smith reduction of the full doubled pair.

Read code before running it. Prefer a few independent discriminating checks to repeating the entire enumeration. Inspect integer signs and Smith-normal-form logic. Record exactly what you ran, software versions, outputs, and what you did not check. The convergence receipt records historical annotation differences between regenerated and archived certificates; determine whether these affect any mathematical claim. Report uncertainty rather than manufacturing a definite result.

## Required report

Return a self-contained referee report containing:

1. A concise verdict distinguishing mathematical correctness, proof completeness, and novelty/publication readiness. Use “not verified” where appropriate.
2. A claim-by-claim table: manuscript identifier, status (verified / valid with repair / false / not verified), evidence, and dependencies. Do not mark a theorem verified merely because its tests passed.
3. Prioritized findings. For each serious issue, quote or locate the exact claim, explain the gap, provide a counterexample or missing argument if available, and state the smallest repair and its downstream effects. Clearly separate fatal errors, substantive gaps, missing hypotheses, and exposition.
4. A reproducibility record and an explicit list of unreviewed material.
5. A prior-art comparison with precise citations and a defensible description of what, if anything, remains potentially publishable.
6. A recommended disposition: ready for external submission review, revise before submission, or reconsider the central claim. Identify the strongest defensible mathematical core and only the changes necessary to support it.

If working locally, write a new `INDEPENDENT_EXPERT_REPORT.md` and any supporting files under a separate `Independent Expert Review` directory in the project root; use a distinct directory if one already exists. Preserve v0.3, v0.4, the archive, and all prior evidence. Do not implement repairs or explore the optional nonunit-C4-d² research question during this review.

A fresh AI review can provide another critical pass but is not a substitute for independent human peer review. State the review method and its limitations honestly.

\documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}

\newcommand{\Cone}{\operatorname{Cone}}
\newcommand{\Nrv}{\operatorname{Nrv}}
