(4) Theorem 11.2 treats cover refinement and descent separately. It reconstructs data on the
support actually covered; restriction fromX to a proper subspaceY need not preserve or
uniquely extend global sections.
The historical Boolean and simplex-skeleton constructions motivate the model; they are not a claim
to new general Boolean, polyhedral, or sheaf theory.

Proof. The jth disjunct requiresfj(x) = 0 and every other factor to be1. Distinct disjuncts are

For the positive conjunctionX1∧···∧Xm, the one-step output is therefore the Hamming layer

2.2 Representation dependence
Theorem 2.4(Non-congruence of factorized unfolding). Fix the aritym =|A|≥2. There is no
Boolean-function operatorU : B(A)→B(A) satisfying

Thus the failure of semantic descent begins at arity two. Form≥2, either internal factoriza-
tion/provenance is part of the concept, a canonical normal form must be chosen, or the historical
rule must be replaced by a semantic operator.

6 Observation systems and three kinds of refinement
The word “refinement” is overloaded. Three operations should be distinguished.
Definition 6.1(Signature refinement). An observation map isqk :X→Ok. We sayqk+1 refines
qk when there isrk :Ok+1→Ok with qk =rk◦qk+1. Equivalently, everyqk+1-fiber lies in aqk-fiber.
For finite propositional observation families, adding observables refines the generated topology,
can split observational equivalence classes, thins the specialization preorder, and can increase
signature distance. This is an observation-theoretic notion of differentiation.
A second regime occurs when a new observation is constant on every currentT0 equivalence class.
Then the carrier does not split; only order relations can be removed. This becomes a same-carrier
order-thinning problem, which is treated separately in companion work. If the new observation
separates previously identified worlds, the refined carrier gains points and a different construction is
required.
A third notion, used in the main theorem below, is acover refinement. It concerns local pieces
representing a support, not merely enlargement of an observation vocabulary.
Remark 6.2 (Presentation-dependent nerve warning). For an indexed family of truth regions
{ς(φi)}, the observation-side nerve records joint satisfiability, but it is presentation-dependent.
Adding a tautological observation can cone the nerve without changing the generated observation
topology. Therefore arbitrary extension of an observation list should not be identified with a
topologically meaningful nerve filtration. The main theorem uses actual refinement of covers with
explicit containment data.

The observation-topology program provides a natural semantic base for the present construction.
An indexed familyΦ = (φi) defines signatures and an observation-generated topology. ExtendingΦ

17 Persistence and zigzags
A monotone sequence of inclusions of concept complexes
K0↪→K1↪→···
produces an ordinary persistence module on homology. If differentiation alternates between additions,
deletions, support restrictions, or reinterpretations, the natural object is instead a zigzag

The current integrated reading draft is `Observation_Refinement_Descent_and_Cone_Draft_v0.5.pdf` with its matching `.tex` in this directory. It was generated from v0.4 by `build_v05.py`; `REPAIR_RECEIPT.json` records source/output hashes and ten bounded transformations. v0.5 repairs the independent referee's two material theorem-statement findings: Theorem 2.4 now has fixed arity `m≥2` and an explicit `m=1` negation exception; Theorem 11.2 requires a finite simplicial pair and good covers **by subcomplexes** for all three displayed covers. Its descent clauses specify an inclusion site, intersection pullbacks, and target limits/colimits. Section 11.1 now limits what cone homology detects. Theorem 4.2 gets the missing vertex proof, Section 18 states direct prior-art specializations, and Section 9.1 includes explicit signed seven-state paths.

None of the established negative results, coefficient conventions, integral extension cautions, or global-minimality limitations has been dropped.

The archived companion title page uses Brian Theory while the main manuscript uses Brian Droncheff; resolve intended public attribution before submission. No external publication, message, commit, push, or frozen-file overwrite was performed. Further work on this manuscript should start from v0.5 and retain the previous versions for provenance.
