# Literature and Priority Map -- Higher-Dimensional Inversion Gate

**Search horizon:** through 29 September 2026.  
**Method:** structural searches for poset fibers, induced-subcomplex vertex deletion, obstruction complexes, finite-space reductions, Horn closure systems, lattice order complexes, and total unimodularity.  Absence of the project terminology "carrier splitting" was not treated as novelty evidence.

## 1. Björner--Wachs--Welker: poset fiber decompositions

**Reference:** A. Björner, M. Wachs, V. Welker, *Poset fiber theorems*, Transactions of the AMS 357 (2005), 1877--1899.  Preprint: https://www.math.miami.edu/~wachs/papers/fibers.pdf

Their main theorem expresses the homotopy type of a poset in terms of the base and lower fibers under explicit connectivity hypotheses, subsuming Quillen/Baclawski/Babson fiber results.

**Overlap:** controlled-fiber decomposition and homotopy equivalence criteria.

**Difference:** the exclusive-inversion matching theorem gives exact integral cone homology from edge links without requiring those fiber-connectivity assumptions.  It is much narrower structurally.

## 2. Chachólski--Jin--Scolamiero--Tombari: vertex-cover obstruction complexes

**Reference:** W. Chachólski, A. Jin, M. Scolamiero, F. Tombari, *Homotopical decompositions of simplicial and Vietoris Rips complexes*, Journal of Applied and Computational Topology 5 (2021), 215--248. DOI: 10.1007/s41468-021-00066-2.  https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s41468-021-00066-2

They study inclusions induced by covers of a simplicial complex's vertex set, define obstruction complexes, and give homotopy-cofiber statements for one, two, and several outside vertices.  Their general theorem controls homotopy fibers of the inclusion by the obstruction complexes.

**Overlap:** this is the closest prior art to the full-doubling/missing-copy viewpoint.  In particular, the standard fact that deleting vertices produces cofiber/link obstructions is not new here.

**Candidate additional content:** in the observation-refinement product `Delta(Q x 2)`, the missing vertices have two special colours.  Their mixed simplices are exactly chain-supported bicliques of the exclusive inversion graph.  Matching of that graph forces a chain-level direct sum and yields the explicit coarse-edge-link formula.  I did not locate that exact specialization/formula in the searched source.

**Priority caution:** a specialist should still check whether this matching specialization is implicit in the authors' several-outside-points machinery.

## 3. Dey--Hirani--Krishnamoorthy: TU and torsion

**Reference:** T. K. Dey, A. N. Hirani, B. Krishnamoorthy, *Optimal Homologous Cycles, Total Unimodularity, and Linear Programming*, SIAM Journal on Computing 40(4) (2011), 1026--1044. DOI: 10.1137/100800245.  https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/100800245

They prove a topological characterization of total unimodularity of simplicial boundary matrices in terms of torsion-freeness of a family of pure relative subcomplex pairs.

**Consequence here:** torsion-free global cone homology is not enough to infer TU.  The matching realization transfers arbitrary torsion, so no blanket all-height TU theorem survives.

## 4. Stong; Barmak; Fernández--Minian

- R. E. Stong, *Finite topological spaces*, Trans. AMS 123 (1966), 325--340. DOI: 10.1090/S0002-9947-1966-0195042-2.
- J. A. Barmak, *On Quillen's Theorem A for posets*, JCTA 118 (2011), 2445--2453; arXiv:1005.0538.
- X. Fernández, E. G. Minian, *The cylinder of a relation and generalized versions of the Nerve Theorem*, arXiv:1801.07235.

**Overlap:** closure maps, beat-point reductions, simple-homotopy fiber criteria, mapping/relation cylinders.

**Difference:** these provide the standard finite-poset topology, not the specialized exclusive-inversion formula.

## 5. Horn / closure systems

Boolean relations closed componentwise under logical AND are exactly Horn-definable relations; this is standard Schaefer/Post-style Boolean relation theory.  A concise modern statement appears in the ICALP 2019 possibility-domain literature, and closure-system treatments identify Horn models with intersection-closed families.

**Overlap:** meet-closure itself is classical.

**Use here:** if the entire refined realized relation is meet-closed, it and its coordinate projection have minima, so the carrier cone is contractible.  This is a simple application, not a novelty claim about Horn logic.

## 6. Crosscut/shellability theory for distributive lattices

Modern crosscut-simplicial literature records that semidistributive lattices have interval order complexes that are contractible or spherical; distributive lattices are a special case.  See C. Defant and N. Williams, *Semidistrim Lattices*, Forum of Mathematics, Sigma 11 (2023), e50.

For the particular distributive lattice `J(R)`, the endpoint statement used here also follows directly from the classical crosscut theorem and the atom structure of `J(R)`: if `R` is not an antichain, the atom crosscut is a simplex; if `R` is an antichain, `J(R)` is Boolean and the crosscut is a sphere.

**Novelty status:** standard lattice topology applied as a corollary of the matching theorem.

## 7. 2026-current finite-poset work

A 2026 paper, *Discrete homotopy and homology theories for finite posets* (Advances in Applied Mathematics 177 (2026), 103074), develops discrete analogues of homotopy and homology for finite posets and relates the discrete homotopy groups to classical ones.

**Overlap:** finite-poset homotopy/homology environment.

**Difference:** no carrier-splitting, two-colour missing-copy, or matching edge-link classification was found there.

## 8. Priority table

| Result in this gate | Closest antecedent | Priority assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Full-doubling/missing-copy model | standard induced-subcomplex deletion; Chachólski et al. | **Not new topology; project-specific modeling reduction** |
| Two-colour shift `H_n(K,L) ~= H_{n+1}(K,U)` | LES/excision/Mayer--Vietoris | **Standard algebraic topology specialized here** |
| Biclique missing-core filtration | filtered relative chains + vertex deletion | **Potentially useful project-specific organization; do not make broad novelty claim yet** |
| Exclusive-inversion matching link formula | Chachólski obstruction complexes; link/cofiber theory | **Candidate substantive specialized theorem; exact statement not located** |
| Bounded-poset endpoint localization | elementary join/link argument | **Corollary** |
| Boolean/distributive sphere-or-zero rule | crosscut theorem | **Corollary; prior lattice topology** |
| Horn refined-relation neutrality | Horn meet closure + cone posets | **Application, not novelty** |
| Torsion universality inside matching | finite-poset realization + matching theorem | **Sharpness result specific to theorem** |

## 9. Recommended wording for a paper

Use wording such as:

> The underlying deletion and cofiber constructions are classical, and obstruction-complex methods for vertex covers are available in the literature.  Our contribution is the recognition that a Boolean observation split produces a two-colour deletion inside `Delta(Q x 2)`, for which the 1-only-to-0-only comparison graph controls interactions.  When this graph is a matching, the relative chain complex separates and yields an exact integral edge-link formula.

Avoid wording such as:

> We introduce a new general theory of vertex deletion or simplicial cofibers.

That would be inaccurate.

# Computational Classification

## Scripts

- `verify_matching_inversion_theorem.py`
- `verify_boolean_horn_cases.py`
- `verify_distributive_corollary.py`

All were run in the supplied package.

## 1. Exact integral matching verification

The matching verifier represents the changing-carrier problem directly as the pair

\[
(\Delta(Q\times2),\Delta Q^\psi)
\]

and computes integral homology using Smith normal form.  For each boundary `d_n`, a full Smith decomposition is used to obtain a primitive integer basis of `ker d_n`; the image of `d_{n+1}` is then expressed in that kernel basis and Smith-reduced again.  Thus the comparison records both free rank and torsion invariants.

Results for all naturally labelled finite coarse posets with at most four states and all three-valued availability profiles:

| Quantity | Count |
|---|---:|
| total poset/profile cases | 3,450 |
| matching cases checked integrally by SNF | 3,242 |
| matching cases with at least one exclusive inversion | 566 |
| failures of exact integral link formula | **0** |
| profiles with empty exclusive graph and nonzero F2 cone homology | **0** |

## 2. Product-edge-link suspension

For every comparable pair in every naturally labelled coarse poset through five states, the verifier compared

\[
\widetilde H_*(lk_{Delta(Qx2)}((p,0)<(z,1));F_2)
\]

with the one-degree shift of

\[
\widetilde H_*(lk_{Delta Q}[p,z];F_2).
\]

Checks: **1,707**.  Failures: **0**.

## 3. Five-state targeted search

The verifier ran 3,000 deterministic random poset/profile trials over the complete family of naturally labelled five-state transitive closures.  Among them, 639 cases had a nonempty exclusive matching and were checked directly over `F2` against the link formula.

Failures: **0**.

## 4. Boolean high-dimensional examples

Endpoint matching profiles gave:

- `B_2`: direct integral pair homology `H_2 = Z`;
- `B_3`: direct integral pair homology `H_3 = Z`;
- `B_4`: theorem/link computation predicts `H_4 = Z`.

This confirms that the theorem is genuinely higher-dimensional and not merely a reformulation of the height-two graph result.

## 5. Minimal nonmatching counterexample

For the coarse chain `0<1<2` and profile `(1-only,0-only,0-only)`:

- exclusive graph: two-edge star;
- direct integral relative homology: `H_1 = Z`;
- false independent-edge formula: zero.

The verifier asserts this discrepancy, so a future accidental weakening from `matching` to `forest` will fail the regression suite.

## 6. Horn / dual-Horn enumeration

Every nonempty Boolean relation through four coordinates was enumerated.

| Refined dimension | nonempty relations | meet-closed | join-closed | minimum/maximum failures |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| 2 | 15 | 13 | 13 | 0 |
| 3 | 255 | 121 | 121 | 0 |
| 4 | 65,535 | 4,959 | 4,959 | 0 |

Projection preserved the relevant meet/join closure in every case, as expected algebraically.

## 7. Distributive-lattice endpoint verification

For every order-ideal lattice `J(R)` generated by a naturally labelled poset `R` with at most three elements (10 cases):

- the Boolean-versus-non-Boolean crosscut classification

all agreed.  Failures: **0**.

# Total Unimodularity and Torsion Audit

## 1. Low height

For weighted height at most two, the prior rooted-incidence theorem identifies the relative boundary map with a signed graph-incidence matrix.  That matrix is totally unimodular, so all relative integral homology is free and coefficient-independent.

## 2. What changes in high dimension

The all-height exclusive-inversion matching theorem gives

\[
H_n(Cone(Delta pi);Z)
\cong
\bigoplus_{(p,z)\in E_psi}
\widetilde H_{n-2}(lk_{Delta Q}[p,z];Z).
\]

Therefore torsion in an edge link is inherited directly by the cone.

The endpoint realization

\[
Q=0hat\oplus R\oplus1hat
\]

with only the endpoint inversion transfers

\[
\widetilde H_*(Delta R;Z)
\]

two degrees upward.  Choosing `R` with `Z/2` torsion gives torsion while `E_psi` remains a one-edge matching.

So:

\[
\boxed{\text{exclusive-inversion matching does not imply TU.}}
\]

## 3. Dey--Hirani--Krishnamoorthy benchmark

Dey, Hirani, and Krishnamoorthy prove that for a finite simplicial complex, a boundary matrix `partial_{p+1}` is totally unimodular iff all specified pure relative subcomplex pairs in dimensions `p,p+1` have torsion-free `H_p`.

This matters here because **global torsion-freeness of the carrier cone is weaker than TU**.  Even if every edge link in the matching theorem is torsion-free, that only controls the homology of the particular carrier-splitting pair; it does not automatically control every pure subpair required by the TU characterization.

## 4. Safe conclusions

1. If one relevant edge link has torsion, the carrier cone has torsion and the hoped-for blanket TU property fails.
2. If every relevant edge link has torsion-free integral homology, the carrier cone is torsion-free.
3. Statement 2 does **not** imply that every relative boundary matrix is TU.
4. The Boolean/distributive endpoint examples are torsion-free, but no new global TU theorem is claimed for them.

## 5. Small explicit torsion construction

Take a finite poset `R` whose order complex has `H_1 ~= Z/2`, for example a standard finite-poset model of `RP^2`.  Add global endpoints and use the one-edge matching profile.  Then

\[
H_3(Cone(Delta pi);Z)\cong Z/2.
\]

The companion paper cites a 13-point projective-plane model, giving a concrete small construction after adding the two endpoint states.  This is an explicit example, not a new minimality claim.

## 6. Forbidden-minor question

No finite forbidden-subconfiguration characterization of TU was obtained.  The matching realization shows why a graph-only obstruction list cannot work: a one-edge exclusive graph can already carry arbitrarily complicated torsion through its coarse edge link.

Any future TU classification must constrain the **link topology or link boundary matrices**, not only the exclusive inversion graph.

# Handoff to Master -- Higher-Dimensional Inversion Gate

**Status:** Gate reaches **Level A mathematically**, with conservative novelty language required.

## Strongest theorem

Let `P` be the 1-only coarse states and `Z` the 0-only coarse states after a Boolean carrier split.  Form the exclusive inversion graph

\[
E_psi=\{(p,z)\in P\times Z:p<z\}.
\]

If `E_psi` is a matching, then for all `n`

\[
H_n(Cone(Delta pi);Z)
\cong
\bigoplus_{(p,z)\in E_psi}
\widetilde H_{n-2}(lk_{Delta Q}[p,z];Z).
\]

This holds over arbitrary coefficients and is all-dimensional.

## Why it works

Replace the split completion by the full doubled product `D=Q x 2`.  The refined carrier is the induced subposet obtained by deleting `(p,0)` for 1-only states and `(z,1)` for 0-only states.  Separately deleting each colour is homotopy-neutral.  Mixed relative simplices correspond to chain-supported bicliques of the exclusive inversion graph.  A matching allows only one-edge mixed cores, forcing a chain-level direct sum.

## High-dimensional canonical example

For `Q=B_m`, bottom 1-only, top 0-only, all other states split:

\[
H_m(Cone)=Z.
\]

Direct SNF check: `B_3` gives `H_3=Z`.

## Sharp counterexample

Do **not** weaken matching to forest.  The 3-chain profile `(1,0,0)` has a two-edge star exclusive graph and actual `H_1=Z`, while independent edge-link summation gives zero.

## Torsion warning

Matching does not imply TU or torsion-freeness.  With `Q=0hat + R + 1hat` and endpoint-only inversion,

\[
H_n(Cone)=\widetilde H_{n-2}(Delta R),
\]

so arbitrary finite-poset torsion transfers.

## Boolean/Horn conclusions

- whole refined relation meet-closed (Horn) -> refined and projected posets have minima -> homotopy-neutral;
- dual-Horn is dual;
- finite distributive lattice endpoint profile is neutral unless the lattice is Boolean, in which case `B_r` gives a single `Z` in degree `r`.

## Computation

- 3,242 matching cases through 4 coarse states checked integrally by SNF: 0 failures;
- 1,707 product-link suspension checks through 5 states: 0 failures;
- 639 nonempty matching five-state random cases checked over F2: 0 failures;
- Horn relations exhaustively checked through 4 refined coordinates;
- 10 small distributive lattices checked integrally.

## Literature boundary

Closest prior art is Chachólski--Jin--Scolamiero--Tombari (2021) on vertex-cover obstruction complexes and cofiber decompositions.  Generic deletion/cofiber machinery is not new.  The candidate project-specific result is the exact observation-theoretic two-colour matching reduction and coarse-edge-link formula.

## Recommended manuscript action

Add a new theorem section after the general carrier-splitting factorization.  Do not replace the general theorem.  Insert the matching theorem, Boolean/distributive corollaries, forest counterexample, and torsion sharpness.

## Next research target

Build the **exclusive-inversion interaction spectral sequence** beyond matching.  First attack exclusive graphs of maximum degree 2 / chordal or Ferrers biclique structure, and characterize when the core-size spectral sequence collapses at `E^2`.

# Structural Class Comparison

| Structural class | Exact result found | Nontrivial in dimension >2? | Torsion? | Priority assessment |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Exclusive inversion graph is a matching | Direct-sum coarse-edge-link formula for all integral cone homology | **Yes** | **Yes** | Strongest gate result; specialized exact theorem, close to standard vertex-deletion machinery |
| Bounded coarse poset + matching | Only global bottom-to-top inversion can contribute | Yes | Depends on proper part | Clean corollary |
| Finite distributive lattice + endpoint matching | Boolean `B_r` gives `H_r=Z`; non-Boolean distributive gives zero | **Yes** | No | Very clean structured example; crosscut theory is standard |
| Entire refined relation Horn / meet-closed | Both refined and projected posets have minima; cone contractible | No | No | Exact but topologically trivial |
| Entire refined relation dual-Horn / join-closed | Dual contractibility result | No | No | Exact but topologically trivial |
| Exclusive inversion graph empty | Isotone section; homotopy equivalence | No | No | Exact zeroth obstruction |
| Exclusive inversion graph a forest | No edgewise classification; 3-chain star is counterexample | Already fails in smallest star | N/A | **Rejected** |
| Coarse chain | Existing Ferrers/independence-complex trichotomy | No rich high homology | No | Mostly prior art / companion result |
| Weighted height <=2 | Existing rooted-incidence/TU classification | Dimension <=2 only | No | Previous exact theorem |
| Height 3 without further restriction | Torsion already possible | Yes | Yes | Too broad for clean coefficient-independent theorem |
| Controlled BWW lower fibers | Classical wedge/fiber results under connectivity hypotheses | Sometimes | Yes | Strong prior art; useful sufficient framework |
| Shellable/Cohen--Macaulay relevant edge links + matching | Matching formula specializes to concentrated/torsion-free homology as appropriate | Yes | Usually no over chosen coefficients | Corollary, not separate core theorem |
| General exclusive graph | Interaction-core spectral sequence indexed by chain-supported bicliques | Yes | Yes | Level-C general machinery; classification open |

## Main comparison

The strongest natural dividing line discovered is **interaction degree**, not height or graph acyclicity.

- `E_psi = empty`: no mixed interaction exists; a monotone section gives homotopy neutrality.
- `E_psi` a matching: every mixed relative simplex has one unique exclusive edge; exact link summation follows.
- first shared endpoint: three-vertex cores appear and generate differentials between edge defects.
- larger bicliques: higher interaction levels appear.

This explains both why the matching theorem is exact and why the forest generalization fails.

# Algebra of the Higher-Dimensional Inversion Chain Complex

## 1. Product model

Let `Q` be a finite poset and `Q^psi subseteq Q x {0,1}` the realized refined signatures.  Put

\[
D=Q\times\mathbf2,\quad K=\Delta D,\quad L=\Delta Q^\psi.
\]

Let

\[
P=A_1\setminus A_0,\qquad Z=A_0\setminus A_1.
\]

The vertices missing from `L` are

\[
M_0=P\times\{0\},\qquad M_1=Z\times\{1\}.
\]

This realizes the changing-carrier problem as an induced-subcomplex deletion from one fixed order complex.

## 2. Two-colour deletion pair

Define

\[
K_P=K[V\setminus M_0],\qquad K_Z=K[V\setminus M_1],
\]

\[
L=K_P\cap K_Z,\qquad U=K_P\cup K_Z.
\]

Both `K_P -> K` and `K_Z -> K` are homotopy equivalences by the top-row and bottom-row closure maps.  Consequently

\[
H_n(K,L;R)\cong H_{n+1}(K,U;R).
\]

The relative complex `C_*(K,U)` is free on chains containing at least one vertex of each missing colour.

## 3. Exclusive inversion graph

Let

\[
E_\psi=\{(p,z)\in P\times Z:p<z\}.
\]

For a relative simplex `sigma`, put

\[
P(\sigma)=\{p:(p,0)\in\sigma\},\qquad
Z(\sigma)=\{z:(z,1)\in\sigma\}.
\]

Then `P(sigma) x Z(sigma)` is a complete bipartite subgraph of `E_psi`.  Hence higher relative cells are controlled not by arbitrary subsets of inversions but by **chain-supported bicliques**.

This gives a sharper description than simply saying that the bit word has a descent.

## 4. Core-size filtration

Define the missing core

\[
S(\sigma)=\sigma\cap(M_0\cup M_1).
\]

Every relative simplex has `|S(sigma)| >= 2`.  Filter by

\[
F_r C_m(K,U)=\langle\sigma:|S(\sigma)|\le r\rangle.
\]

Since taking a face cannot increase the number of missing vertices, this is a chain filtration.

Let `C_r` be the family of `r`-vertex mixed missing cores that are themselves simplices of `K`.  For `S in C_r`, define

\[
\Lambda_S=\operatorname{lk}_K(S)[V(L)].
\]

In the associated graded complex, deleting a missing vertex lowers the filtration and disappears, while deleting an available vertex preserves the core.  Therefore

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{gr}_r C_m(K,U)
\cong
\bigoplus_{S\in\mathcal C_r}
\widetilde C_{m-r}(\Lambda_S).
}
\]

A standard filtered-complex spectral sequence follows, with first-page terms built from

\[
\widetilde H_*(\Lambda_S).
\]

The first inter-core differentials delete one missing vertex and hence measure interactions among overlapping exclusive inversions.

## 5. Matching collapse

If `E_psi` is a matching, no relative simplex can contain more than two missing vertices.  Hence all mixed cores have exactly two vertices and are exactly the edges

\[
e=((p,0)<(z,1)),\qquad (p,z)\in E_\psi.
\]

Moreover every vertex in `lk_K(e)` is available: a missing vertex in the link would create another exclusive edge sharing `p` or `z`.

Thus the filtration has only one nonzero mixed-core level and collapses immediately:

\[
C_m(K,U)
\cong
\bigoplus_{e\in E_\psi}
\widetilde C_{m-2}(\operatorname{lk}_K e).
\]

This is a literal chain-level direct sum, not merely an equality of Betti numbers.

## 6. Product link versus coarse link

For `e=((p,0)<(z,1))`,

\[
\operatorname{lk}_K e
=
\Delta(Q_{<p})*\Delta M_{p,z}*\Delta(Q_{>z}),
\]

where `M_{p,z}=((p,0),(z,1))` in `Q x 2`.

Writing `R=(p,z)_Q`, cover `Delta M_{p,z}` by

- `M_{p,z} \ {(z,0)}`, which closes upward to a cone with minimum `(p,1)`;
- `M_{p,z} \ {(p,1)}`, which closes downward to a cone with maximum `(z,0)`.

Their intersection is `R x 2`, homotopy equivalent to `R`.  Hence

\[
\Delta M_{p,z}\simeq\Sigma\Delta R,
\]

and therefore

\[
\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta(Q\times2)}e
\simeq
\Sigma\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z].
\]

## 7. Exact integral formula

Combining the direct sum, the product-link suspension, and

\[
H_n(K,L)\cong H_{n+1}(K,U),
\]

gives

\[
H_n(K,L;\mathbb Z)
\cong
\bigoplus_{(p,z)\in E_\psi}
\widetilde H_{n-2}(\operatorname{lk}_{\Delta Q}[p,z];\mathbb Z).
\]

The same argument works over arbitrary coefficients.

## 8. Why forests fail

A forest can contain a star.  If `p` is adjacent to two comparable `z_1<z_2`, then the relative triangle

\[
(p,0)<(z_1,1)<(z_2,1)
\]

has boundary connecting the two inversion-edge generators.  This is an inter-core differential.  The three-chain profile `(1,0,0)` is the smallest example.

Thus the correct higher-dimensional object is not the exclusive graph alone but the hierarchy of chain-supported bicliques plus their available links.

## 9. Relation to the original bit-word model

The earlier split-completion relative complex was described by nonmonotone bit words.  The full-doubling model repackages the same obstruction more effectively:

- split states contribute no missing copy;
- 1-only states remove their lower copy;
- 0-only states remove their upper copy;
- a genuine obstruction occurs only when a chain needs both missing colours.

The binary descent is therefore equivalent to a two-colour missing-vertex interaction after the homotopy-neutral doubling.

# Adversarial Specialist Reviews

## Referee A — finite-poset topology

**Attack.** The proposed classification is only Quillen/Björner–Wachs–Welker fiber theory in different notation.

**Finding.** Generic fiber criteria and wedge decompositions are indeed prior art.  The matching theorem is narrower but computes the complete integral cofiber homology directly from coarse edge links without assuming the connectivity conditions used in the standard fiber formula.  The defensible claim is therefore a specialized exact recognition theorem for the observation-refinement model, not a new general fiber theorem.

## Referee B — combinatorial topology / vertex deletion

**Attack.** The full-doubling argument is generic induced-subcomplex vertex deletion.

**Finding.** Substantially correct as a priority warning.  Chachólski–Jin–Scolamiero–Tombari develop obstruction complexes and homotopical decompositions associated with vertex covers, including multiple outside vertices.  What remains project-specific is the two-colour missing-copy structure forced by a Boolean observation, the exclusive inversion graph, the biclique interaction filtration, and the matching reduction to coarse edge links.

## Referee C — integral homology and total unimodularity

**Attack.** A matching interaction graph should force torsion-free homology and probably total unimodularity.

**Finding.** False.  The endpoint construction `Q = 0hat + R + 1hat` transfers `H~_*(Delta R; Z)` two degrees upward while the exclusive graph consists of one edge.  Thus arbitrary torsion occurs inside the matching class.  Dey–Hirani–Krishnamoorthy also show that TU is controlled by torsion-freeness of an entire family of pure relative subpairs, not by the global homology of one pair.

## Referee D — Horn/closure systems

**Attack.** Horn structure should yield the sought rich higher-dimensional classification.

**Finding.** Not in the strongest natural formulation.  A nonempty meet-closed refined relation has a minimum, and its coordinate projection is again meet-closed with a minimum.  Both order complexes are therefore contractible and the refinement is homotopy-neutral.  Dual-Horn is dual.  Horn is an exact neutral regime, not the source of rich higher homology.

## Hostile minimal-counterexample attack

**Target.** Relax “matching” to “forest”.

**Counterexample.** Take the coarse chain `0<1<2` and the availability profile `(1-only,0-only,0-only)`.  The exclusive graph is the two-edge star `K_{1,2}`, hence a forest.  Direct integral Smith normal form yields `H~_1(Cone)=Z`, whereas the independent sum of the two edge-link contributions is zero.

**Consequence.** Acyclicity of the exclusive inversion graph is insufficient.  The first shared endpoint creates a genuine three-vertex interaction core, so any theorem beyond matching must track higher cores/differentials.

## Referee consensus

Correctness confidence is high for the matching formula and its corollaries, given the chain-level proof and exhaustive/targeted computation.  Priority confidence is medium: the exact two-colour matching specialization was not located in the searched literature, but it sits close to established obstruction-complex and vertex-deletion machinery.  Publication wording should emphasize the observation-theoretic specialization and explicit link formula.

# Exact Theorems and Proofs

## T1. Missing-copy cofiber model

**Theorem.** Let `Q^psi subseteq Q x 2` be the refined signature poset and let `pi:Q^psi -> Q` be projection.  Put `K=Delta(Q x 2)` and regard `L=Delta Q^psi` as the induced subcomplex on the realized copies.  Then the mapping cone of `Delta pi` has the same reduced homology as the pair `(K,L)` over arbitrary coefficients.

**Proof.** The projection `Q x 2 -> Q` is a homotopy equivalence, with a closure section to either constant-bit row.  The map `Delta pi` is the composite `L -> K -> Delta Q`.  Homotopy cofibers are invariant under homotopy equivalence of the target, and the cofiber of a simplicial inclusion has reduced homology `H_*(K,L)`.  QED.

## T2. Two-colour shift

Let `P` be the 1-only states and `Z` the 0-only states.  Delete `P x {0}` and `Z x {1}` separately to get `K_P` and `K_Z`, and put `U=K_P union K_Z`, `L=K_P intersect K_Z`.

**Theorem.** For every `n` and every coefficient ring `R`,

\[
H_n(K,L;R)\cong H_{n+1}(K,U;R).
\]

**Proof.** `K_P` closes upward to the top row and `K_Z` closes downward to the bottom row, so `H_*(K,K_P)=H_*(K,K_Z)=0`.  The triple `(K,K_P,L)` gives `H_n(K,L) ~= H_n(K_P,L)`.  Excision for the union `U=K_P union K_Z` gives `H_n(K_P,L) ~= H_n(U,K_Z)`.  The triple `(K,U,K_Z)` gives `H_n(U,K_Z) ~= H_{n+1}(K,U)`.  Compose.  QED.

## T3. Empty-exclusive-graph neutrality

Define

\[
E_\psi=\{(p,z):p\in P,z\in Z,p<z\}.
\]

**Theorem.** If `E_psi` is empty, then `Delta pi` is a homotopy equivalence.

**Proof.** Define `b(s)=1` iff some `p in P` satisfies `p<=s`; otherwise set `b(s)=0`.  No `z in Z` can receive label `1`, because that would give an exclusive edge.  Thus `(s,b(s))` is an available refined state for every `s`, and `b` is isotone.  The section `r(s)=(s,b(s))` satisfies `pi r=id`.  On `Q^psi`, let `c_+(s,a)=(s,max(a,b(s)))`.  Then `id <= c_+ >= r pi`.  Comparable poset maps induce homotopic order-complex maps, so `r` is a homotopy inverse.  QED.

## T4. Interaction-core filtration

**Theorem.** The relative complex `C_*(K,U)` has a filtration by the number of missing vertices.  If `C_r` is the family of mixed `r`-vertex missing cores that form simplices of `K`, and

\[
\Lambda_S=lk_K(S)[V(L)],
\]

then

\[
gr_r C_m(K,U)
\cong
\bigoplus_{S\in C_r}\widetilde C_{m-r}(\Lambda_S).
\]

**Proof.** Every relative simplex has a unique missing core `S`.  Its remaining vertices are available and form a simplex in the indicated link.  A boundary face obtained by deleting an available vertex preserves `S`; deleting a missing vertex strictly lowers the filtration.  Therefore only the former survives in the associated graded differential, giving the augmented link complex with the stated degree shift.  QED.

**Corollary.** There is a convergent interaction spectral sequence whose first page is the direct sum of the reduced homologies of these available-link complexes.  The mixed cores are chain-supported bicliques of the exclusive inversion graph.

## T5. Exclusive-Inversion Matching Theorem

**Theorem.** If `E_psi` is a matching, then for every coefficient ring `R`,

\[
H_n(Cone(Delta pi);R)
\cong
\bigoplus_{(p,z)\in E_\psi}
\widetilde H_{n-2}(lk_{Delta Q}[p,z];R).
\]

**Proof.** Under matching, a relative simplex in `K\U` contains exactly one missing lower copy and exactly one missing upper copy; otherwise some exclusive vertex would have degree at least two.  Hence the chain complex splits directly over exclusive edges `e=((p,0)<(z,1))`.  The `e`-summand is the augmented chain complex of `lk_K e`, shifted by two.  T2 adds one further relative-degree shift.

It remains to identify the product link.  The link of `e` factors as

\[
Delta Q_{<p} * Delta((p,0),(z,1))_{Qx2} * Delta Q_{>z}.
\]

The middle interval is the union of two contractible induced subposets obtained by deleting `(z,0)` and `(p,1)` respectively; their intersection is `(p,z)_Q x 2`, homotopy equivalent to `(p,z)_Q`.  Therefore the middle interval has order complex homotopy equivalent to `Sigma Delta(p,z)_Q`.  Joining with the lower and upper factors gives

\[
lk_{Delta(Qx2)}e \simeq Sigma lk_{Delta Q}[p,z].
\]

Apply reduced homology.  QED.

## T6. Bounded-poset localization

**Theorem.** Assume `Q` has global minimum `0hat` and maximum `1hat`, and `E_psi` is a matching.  Then every exclusive edge other than `(0hat,1hat)` has contractible coarse edge link.  Hence only the global endpoint inversion can contribute to cone homology.

**Proof.** If `p != 0hat`, the lower-link factor `Delta Q_{<p}` has minimum `0hat` and is contractible.  If `z != 1hat`, the upper-link factor `Delta Q_{>z}` has maximum `1hat` and is contractible.  The edge link is their join with the open-interval factor.  A join with a nonempty contractible complex is contractible.  QED.

## T7. Distributive-lattice endpoint theorem

Let `L=J(R)` be a finite distributive lattice and use the endpoint matching profile: bottom is 1-only, top is 0-only, every other state splits.

**Theorem.** If `R` is an `r`-element antichain, so `L=B_r`, then

\[
H_r(Cone(Delta pi);Z) ~= Z
\]

and all other reduced cone homology vanishes.  If `R` is not an antichain, the cone is integrally acyclic.

**Proof.** T6 reduces the answer to the reduced homology of the proper part of `L`, shifted by two.  The atoms of `J(R)` are the singleton ideals generated by the minimal elements of `R`.  If `R` has a nonminimal element, the join of all atoms is still below the top element, so the atom crosscut complex is a full simplex and hence contractible.  If every element of `R` is minimal, `R` is an antichain, `J(R)=B_r`, and the atom crosscut complex is the boundary of an `(r-1)`-simplex, namely `S^{r-2}`.  Apply the crosscut theorem and shift by two.  QED.

## T8. Matching universality

**Theorem.** For every nonempty finite poset `R`, there is a carrier-splitting system with a one-edge exclusive matching such that

\[
H_n(Cone(Delta pi);Z)
\cong
\widetilde H_{n-2}(Delta R;Z).
\]

**Proof.** Take `Q=0hat ordinal-sum R ordinal-sum 1hat`.  Make `0hat` 1-only, `1hat` 0-only, and every `R` state split.  The exclusive graph has exactly the endpoint edge and its coarse edge link is `Delta R`.  Apply T5.  QED.

This theorem transfers arbitrary finite-poset torsion into the matching class and rules out a universal TU or wedge-of-spheres theorem there.

# Audit of the attached `Logical Complexes.tex` notes

## Bottom line

The notes are useful. They contain two ideas that survive almost exactly after the ambient algebra is clarified:

1. Boolean valuation vectors naturally live in an affine/vector geometry over \(\mathbf F_2\), where XOR is vector difference.
2. The observation that signs can disappear and a second boundary can cancel is correct for **formal simplicial chains over \(\mathbf F_2\)**.

The notes also reveal a stronger geometric structure not stated there: exact unfolding layers are **hypersimplices**, and the parent plus all one-coordinate distinctions is an affine simplex.

## What is correct or salvageable

### 1. XOR of Boolean points

For \(x,y\in\mathbf F_2^m\),
\[
x\Updownarrow y=x+y
\]
is the coordinatewise difference vector. Its Hamming weight is the scalar Hamming distance:
\[
d_H(x,y)=\mathrm{wt}(x\Updownarrow y).
\]
So the notes' repeated use of XOR as a geometric difference is sound after this wording change.

### 2. The points \(G,D,E,F\)

The notes use
\[
G=111,\quad D=110,\quad E=101,\quad F=011.
\]
Relative to \(G\), the three differences are
\[
G\Updownarrow D=001,\quad G\Updownarrow E=010,\quad G\Updownarrow F=100.
\]
They are a basis. Therefore the **four** points \(G,D,E,F\) are affinely independent and form a genuine tetrahedron.

This corrects the note's suggestion that three such points might already make a 3-simplex. Any three points in \(\mathbb R^3\) are coplanar; a tetrahedron needs four affinely independent points.

### 3. The special relation \(D\Updownarrow E=F\)

This is correct for the three-variable example:
\[
110\Updownarrow101=011.
\]
Indeed \(\{000,110,101,011\}\) is the even-parity two-dimensional subspace of \(\mathbf F_2^3\).

It is a low-arity coincidence, not a general law of one-flip layers. For \(m>3\), XOR of two one-flip children of \(1^m\) has Hamming weight two and normally leaves the one-flip layer.

### 4. The \(\partial^2=0\) intuition

The notes' cancellation intuition is valid after moving to a formal chain group. Over \(\mathbf F_2\), the simplicial boundary is
\[
d[v_0,\ldots,v_n]=\sum_i[v_0,\ldots,\widehat v_i,\ldots,v_n],
\]
with no visible signs because \(-1=+1\). Every codimension-two face occurs twice in \(d^2\), so it cancels.

The necessary correction is conceptual: the XOR/addition here is **addition of formal simplices in the chain group**, not XOR of the vertex labels themselves. The two additions may both be over \(\mathbf F_2\), but they act in different vector spaces.

## Stronger structure recovered from the notes

### Exact layers are hypersimplices

Starting from \(1^m\), the states reached by switching exactly \(k\) coordinates are
\[
L_k^{(m)}=\{x\in\{0,1\}^m:\mathrm{wt}(x)=m-k\}.
\]
Their convex hull is the hypersimplex
\[
\Delta(m,m-k)=\left\{x\in[0,1]^m:\sum_i x_i=m-k\right\}.
\]
Only the first and last nontrivial layers are simplices in general.

For \(m=4\) the layer geometry is:

**point -> tetrahedron -> octahedron -> tetrahedron -> point.**

This is a clean modern replacement for the notes' questions about planes, simplices, and apparently redundant Boolean points.

### Distinction histories form a simplex skeleton filtration

If a state is labeled by the subset \(S\subseteq[m]\) of coordinates that have been distinguished, then allowing all distinction sets of size at most \(r+1\) gives
\[
K_r=\operatorname{sk}_r\Delta^{m-1}.
\]
Thus successive differentiation has a canonical simplicial filtration even though each exact state layer is generally a hypersimplex rather than a simplex.

For the step \(K_{r-1}\hookrightarrow K_r\),
\[
H_q(K_r,K_{r-1};R)\cong
\begin{cases}
R^{\binom{m}{r+1}},&q=r,\\
0,&q\ne r.
\end{cases}
\]
The same groups are the homology of the mapping cone of the inclusion.

## What should not be carried forward literally

- Do not call the XOR vector itself a scalar distance; use its Hamming weight.
- Do not use a determinant of three position vectors to decide affine independence of four points. Use differences from one base point.
- Do not identify Boolean valuation vectors with simplicial chains.
- Do not treat conjunction of logical labels as the simplicial boundary.
- Do not infer that a collection of proper faces contains its filler.
- Do not infer symmetry from the existence of a homology cycle.

## Recommendation

The useful material from the notes should be retained as a short section in the new paper, but in the following repaired form:

1. valuation space \(\mathbf F_2^m\);
2. XOR as difference vector and Hamming weight as distance;
3. one-flip affine simplex theorem;
4. exact layers as hypersimplices;
5. chain complex over \(\mathbf F_2\) as a separate formal object;
6. cumulative distinction skeletons and their cone defects.

That is stronger, cleaner, and more general than the original notes while preserving the intuition that motivated them.

# Research handoff: Observation–Refinement Descent and Cone project

**Status:** Draft v0.2 created. Core mathematics checked. Not yet a submission manuscript.

## Main advance in this round

The proposed Observation–Refinement Descent and Cone theorem has been formalized in a relative good-cover setting:

- cover refinement induces a nerve map;
- different refinement choices are contiguous;
- under good-cover hypotheses the fine-to-coarse nerve map on the same support is a homotopy equivalence;
- for a changing support \(Y\subseteq X\), the mapping cone computes \(H_*(X,Y)\) up to the standard relative nerve identifications;
- for a sheaf/cosheaf, local-to-global reconstruction is handled by descent/colimits rather than by a Boolean conjunction formula.

## Important priority correction

A 2026 preprint by António Leitão, *It's All About Covers: Persistent Homology of Cover Refinements* (arXiv:2602.22784), explicitly develops cover refinements, contiguity of refinement maps, and propagation through nerve/co-nerve functors. Therefore the **contiguity/canonical-homology-map component is not a novelty claim** for this project.

The draft now says this explicitly.

## New structure extracted from the attached `Logical Complexes.tex`

The notes were useful. They led to two clean results:

1. **Boolean unfolding simplex theorem.** For parent \(1^m\), the parent plus all one-coordinate-flip children is an affine \(m\)-simplex.
2. **Exact-layer hypersimplex theorem.** The exact depth-\(k\) states form the vertices of the hypersimplex \(\Delta(m,m-k)\).

The notes' three-variable points \(111,110,101,011\) really do form a tetrahedron. The notes were wrong only in the suggestion that three points could form a 3-simplex or that XOR itself is a scalar distance.

## New exact finite model

The cumulative distinction-history complex
\[
K_r^{(m)}=\operatorname{sk}_r\Delta^{m-1}
\]
has a closed-form step defect:
\[
H_q(K_r,K_{r-1};R)
\cong H_q(\operatorname{Cone}(i_r))
\cong
\begin{cases}
R^{\binom{m}{r+1}},&q=r,\\
0,&q\ne r.
\end{cases}
\]

For \(m=4\):

- \(K_0\): four vertices;
- \(K_1\): \(K_4\), with \(\beta_1=3\);
- \(K_2\): tetrahedral boundary, with \(\beta_2=1\);
- \(K_3\): filled tetrahedron, contractible.

This is a much cleaner prototype of successive differentiation than the older ad hoc path-cycle-disk example.

## Interaction with the existing ProLT program

The draft distinguishes three operations that had previously risked being conflated:

1. **Observation vocabulary extension**: add formulas; topology becomes finer and observational equivalence can split.
2. **Same-carrier order thinning**: a new observation factors through the current \(T_0\) quotient; points do not split, only order relations are removed. The companion height-two rooted-forest theorem applies here.
3. **Cover refinement**: local pieces of a support refine other local pieces; the nerve/refinement theorem applies here.

This separation should remain explicit in all future drafts.

## Strongest next theorem

The strongest next target is now more specific than the original cover-refinement theorem:

### Carrier-Splitting Cone Theorem

When a new observation separates worlds that were previously a single point in the current \(T_0\) quotient, construct a canonical span/correspondence between the old and new order complexes and classify the mapping-cone homology in terms of the split fibers.

This target sits exactly between:

- the existing **same-carrier one-bit order-thinning** theorem, and
- the current **cover-refinement relative-cone** theorem.

A successful theorem here would be much more project-specific and less vulnerable to being only a repackaging of standard nerve theory.

## Secondary next target

Characterize when an observation-generated concept cover is **pair-good** directly from finite observation/incidence data. A finite combinatorial criterion would strengthen the main theorem by making its hypotheses checkable from the logical model itself.

- `Observation_Refinement_Descent_and_Cone_Draft_v0.2.tex`

- `LOGICAL_COMPLEXES_NOTES_AUDIT.md`
- `verify_unfolding_complexes.py`
- `verification_results.json`

\newcommand{\Ftwo}{\mathbb F_2}
\newcommand{\Cone}{\operatorname{Cone}}
\newcommand{\Nrv}{\operatorname{Nrv}}
