# Literature and priority audit

Audit date: 2026-09-29. This is a targeted primary-source search conducted during the transfer gate, with no asserted exhaustive coverage through 2026 and no proof of absence of earlier work. Source publication dates below come from the papers or publisher records; search-engine crawl dates are not publication dates. All claims of contribution remain provisional.

## Verdict

The adaptive formalism is a restricted decision tree with a support-dependent legal-action map. That formalism, its minimax recursion, and ordinary binary information bounds are established mathematics. The project cannot claim a new general adaptive-identification framework on that basis. The useful specialized content is the exact logical-to-incidence translation, its behavior under support restriction, and rigorously delimited consequences for supplied observation libraries.

The most defensible package is an exact repair-restriction theorem with explicit activation/deactivation mechanisms, together with examples and gap theorems showing what the topological legal-action predicate changes. Even that package has only low-to-moderate novelty confidence: much of its algebra is a short specialization of standard matrix and graphic-matroid facts. No publication-ready priority verdict has been established.

## Verified primary sources and what they do establish

| Source | Exact relevance checked | Boundary of the comparison |
|---|---|---|
| [Hyafil and Rivest, Constructing Optimal Binary Decision Trees is NP-Complete (1976)](https://people.csail.mit.edu/rivest/pubs/HR76.pdf) | Explicit finite objects, fixed Boolean tests, identification trees; principal cost is total external path length. | Do not quote its main result as if it proved minimum worst-case height. |
| [Laber and Nogueira, On the hardness of the minimum height decision tree problem (2004)](https://www2.ic.uff.br/~loana/decisiontree.pdf) | Explicitly minimizes worst-case test count; Theorem 1 gives a set-cover-based approximation-hardness reduction. | Appropriate source for the ordinary depth problem, not RF-IDENT feasibility hardness. |
| [Karbasi and Zadimoghaddam, Constrained Binary Identification Problem (STACS 2013)](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.STACS.2013.550) | Constrained Twenty Questions with graph, cost, and submodular query restrictions; adaptive identification and approximation bounds. | Different concrete restrictions and principally expected-cost objectives; no checked repair-forest predicate. |
| [Hoffmann and Brafman, Contingent Planning via Heuristic Forward Search with Implicit Belief States (ICAPS 2005)](https://cdn.aaai.org/ICAPS/2005/ICAPS05-008.pdf) | Belief states are sets of worlds; sensing actions split them; action applicability and AND/OR search are explicit. | Its universal pointwise preconditions are hereditary under pure support restriction; that special mechanism cannot produce repair-safety deactivation without changing the model. |
| [Kohler, Akrour, and Preux, Interpretable Decision Tree Search as a Markov Decision Process, v3 (2024), Sec. 5.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2309.12701v3#S5.SS1) | Explicit map phi:S->P(F) specifies a state-dependent admissible-test set, and dynamic programming solves the resulting state graph. | This is a classification/regularized-loss setting using heuristic test generation, not the same topological predicate. The generic state-dependent decision-tree architecture nevertheless predates this project. |
| [The later version, Breiman meets Bellman: Non-Greedy Decision Trees with MDPs (KDD 2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2309.12701v5) | Confirms the same work's later title and publication version. | Distinguish the 2024 version title from the 2025 publication title. |
| [Cheraghchi, Karbasi, Mohajer, and Saligrama, Graph-Constrained Group Testing (2010 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.1445) | Pools satisfy graph connectivity restrictions; nonadaptive multi-defective identification is studied. | Connectivity of a queried pool is different from preserving an order complex before conditioning. |
| [Golovin and Krause, Adaptive Submodular Optimization under Matroid Constraints (2011)](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~dgolovin/papers/1101.4450v1%20adapt_matroids.pdf) | Adaptive selection under fixed matroid/independence constraints has established approximation theory. | A repair matrix has a matroid on triangle columns, not automatically on supplied observations. No adaptive-submodularity or greedy-approximation theorem is transferred here. |
| [Bernardi and Klivans, Directed Rooted Forests in Higher Dimension (2016)](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/view/v23i4p35), [author manuscript](https://www.dam.brown.edu/people/cklivans/Forests.pdf) | Lemma 14 identifies rooted forests with square nonsingular boundary submatrices; fitting orientations and homological weights are already developed. | General rooted cellular-forest and determinant terminology is prior art, as v0.5 already acknowledges. |
| [Duval, Klivans, and Martin, Simplicial and Cellular Trees (2015 preprint; 2016 chapter)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.06819) | Cellular-matroid, higher-tree, and torsion background. | Supports the standard framework, not a new fixed-library adaptive theorem. |
| [Barmak and Minian, Simple Homotopy Types and Finite Spaces (2006 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0611158) | Finite-space collapses and their correspondence with simplicial collapses. | Finite posets and order-complex/simple-homotopy methods are established foundations. |

The source comparisons above are verified from primary documents or their primary records. Statements about how the ProLT model embeds or fails to embed into them are deductions of this audit, not claims made by those authors.

## Corrections already recorded in the transferred audit

The local `03_PROLT_PRIMARY_SOURCES/CLAIM_AUDIT_TABLE.csv` must accompany the source papers. Its V5-06 already marks the asserted total-order relative observation dimension / classical 2-dimension equality `FALSE/COUNTEREXAMPLE`; V5-07 marks its inherited complexity claim `NEEDS_MAJOR_REPAIR`. The two-chain check in the independent complexity audit confirms this known correction and is not a new discovery.

V5-09 already marks the block-to-rooted-forest translation `NEEDS_MINOR_REPAIR`: generating the auxiliary complex only from deleted triangles may omit unsupported deleted edges and their zero boundary rows. Use G=K^(1) union the deleted triangles, with retained edges as the root, or explicitly retain and handle the omitted rows. The present one-bit matrix/repair graph construction includes every descent edge, including isolated graph vertices.

V3-13 classifies the chain trichotomy as `PRIOR_ART_EQUIVALENT` and calls for disclosure of the unlocated Ehrenborg-Kitaev proof cited by the transferred audit. This audit has not located or independently checked that cited proof. The later hostile-audit theorem A1 remains preserved with its narrower ProLT-specific adaptive statement and moderate novelty assessment; it does not make the underlying chain classification new.

## The hostile reduction test

For fixed P0 and Q define A(S) to be the nonconstant supplied tests whose one-bit refinements are repair-safe on P0[S]. Branch cancellation implies that S is a complete state for future decisions. The resulting task is exactly deterministic identification with state-dependent available actions. A test has two successor supports, and a successful policy is an AND/OR solution tree ending in singletons.

This reduces the planning aspect to established decision-tree/belief-state ideas. It does not make the legal-action geometry vacuous: a general support-dependent map can be arbitrary, whereas here it comes from deleted chains and a particularly sparse relative boundary. The contribution must be a theorem exploiting that restriction, not renamed dynamic programming.

Standard contingent planning with preconditions holding in every possible world permits activation as the belief set shrinks. Such applicability is hereditary: once all surviving worlds satisfy a precondition, all subsets do too. Repair-safety can deactivate. This separates the concrete predicate from that particular simple sensing model; it does not establish priority over all epistemic planning or all state-dependent action models.

## Claim-by-claim novelty classification

| Proposed result | Classification | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Branch cancellation | Definition-level specialization | Every previously observed coordinate is constant on the conditioned support. |
| Support-only DP and exact feasibility recursion | Standard algorithmic specialization | Ordinary Bellman / AND-OR recursion with a computable legal-action predicate. |
| RF-SAFE polynomial time | Direct source-theorem algorithm | Build the existing one-bit repair graph and test the forest condition. |
| RF-DEPTH NP-complete | Standard hardness transfer | Antichains recover unrestricted fixed-library depth; no repair geometry is needed. |
| Height-one polynomial RF-IDENT | Generic hereditary-action lemma plus ProLT specialization | Safety becomes isotonicity; a legal split cannot destroy feasibility. |
| Root splitting and exact retained-cell boundary formula | Useful ProLT structural synthesis | The graph representation must track support of every edge/triangle and coarse component. |
| Column-matroid deletion under conditioning | Elementary but important exact fact | Every retained triangle retains every incident descent row, so removed rows are zero on retained columns. |
| Minimal activation/deactivation examples | Concrete separating examples | Value lies in correctness and minimality, not in the word “activation.” |
| Sharp finite gap n-1-ceil(log2 n) | Elementary ProLT-specific extremal corollary | Star examples already realize it at height one with oriented libraries. |
| Exact complement-closed parity-family depth D_k=2^(k-1)+k-1 | Stronger structured-family result; provisional contribution candidate | Gives exact penalty n/2-1 even with complements supplied. It still occurs at height one. |
| A1 from the transferred audit | Preserved, no new claim | Arbitrary Boolean query profiles on chains differ from a fixed supplied library. |

The classifications are judgments, not bibliographic proofs. A correct elementary result may still be useful, but should not be described as a new general theory merely because its application vocabulary differs.

## Exact matroid boundary of novelty

Fix one observation r. Let B_S have rows E_r(S) (descent edges) and columns F_r(S) (deleted triangles). For T subset S,

    B_T = B_S[E_r(T), F_r(T)].

Every triangle in F_r(T) has all three vertices in T, hence every descent in its column lies in E_r(T). Therefore the removed rows in B_S[:,F_r(T)] are zero. All column dependences are unchanged, giving

    M(B_T) = M(B_S) restricted to F_r(T).

Thus the represented matroid evolves by deletion. A blanket claim of “no clean matroid-minor operation” is false. Graphically the formal roots may split, but identifying all formal roots gives an ordinary graphic representation with exactly this column matroid. Safety additionally demands spanning all remaining descent rows; matroid independence alone omits this condition. If B_S is invertible, B_T is injective and safety is equivalent to |F_r(T)|=|E_r(T)|. Conditioning cannot create a new column cycle; loss of anchoring/full row rank explains deactivation.

This argument is an elementary consequence of standard represented-matroid restriction. Its value here is preventing incorrect claims about rank updates, root changes, and newly created cycles.

## Depth-gap caveats and a stronger family

The extremal oriented-library gap supplied elsewhere in the gate is mathematically useful, but it does not require height-two triangles. A height-one star already suffices. Moreover, complementing its antitone code queries makes them isotone, eliminating that family's penalty. That dependence must be stated.

Complement closure does **not** eliminate all gaps. The independently audited family in `COMPLEXITY_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md`, C6, uses all k-bit words, with every even-parity word below every odd-parity word. Supply coordinates and singleton indicators, including all complements. For k>=2, coordinate safety forces deletion of a whole layer/bit cell of n/4 vertices. The untouched opposite bit half is a smaller instance; charging any earlier deletions in that half gives the exact recurrence D_k=n/4+1+D_(k-1), with D_1=1. Consequently d_RF=n/2+k-1, d_ad=k, and the exact penalty is n/2-1. This structured-family theorem is stronger than a mere unbounded-gap example. It remains a height-one construction and leaves the special value of height-two deactivation to be justified separately. Its exact statement has not received an exhaustive priority audit.

## Search coverage and unresolved priority

Queries covered restricted Twenty Questions, minimum-height decision trees, constrained binary identification, state-dependent test sets, contingent sensing, graph-constrained group testing, adaptive matroid constraints, rooted cellular forests, and finite-space simple homotopy. Strong exact matches were found for the general decision process and for the rooted-boundary algebra. No exact fixed-library ProLT repair-safety theorem was located in this targeted search.

That last observation is not an originality certificate. Detailed citation chasing for adaptive test cover, epistemic action preconditions beyond universal pointwise conditions, and poset-search variants remains incomplete. A public “first” claim or high-confidence priority claim would exceed the evidence.

## Recommended publication gate

Keep the focus on the exact restriction theorem and a structural result that needs nonhereditary legality at height two. General RF-IDENT complexity, or an efficient complete algorithm on a natural height-two class, would add more substance than another decision-tree restatement. The complement-closed gap is a useful supporting theorem. Before drafting a principal novelty claim, perform a targeted second audit against those precise statements and have an independent referee reconstruct their proofs.

## Final narrow priority check: exact parity-family theorem

After the exact recurrence was proved, five additional targeted web searches were run on 2026-09-29. These are the exact query strings:

1. `"decision tree" "poset" "parity" "monotone"`
2. `"decision tree" "complete bipartite" "coordinate" "singleton"`
3. `"identification" "isotone" "queries"`
4. `"decision tree" "2^{k-1}" "k-1" "parity"`
5. `"search" "posets" "queries" "two-level" monotone`

The target was the conjunction of a two-level complete bipartite order defined by Boolean parity classes, a supplied coordinate-plus-singleton library with complements, support-relative isotone admissibility, and exact depth 2^(k-1)+k-1. No returned source inspected in this narrow pass gave that construction, recurrence, or exact theorem.

The principal apparent matches were different problems, checked at their primary sources:

- [Besselman et al., Direct Sums for Parity Decision Trees (CCC 2025)](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol339-ccc2025/html/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.16/LIPIcs.CCC.2025.16.html) permits linear parity queries to compute functions and proves direct-sum results. Here parity defines the two poset layers; parity queries are not part of the supplied library. The models must not be conflated.
- [Blanc et al., Decision Tree Heuristics Can Fail, Even in the Smoothed Setting (2021)](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol207-approx-random2021/LIPIcs.APPROX-RANDOM.2021.45/LIPIcs.APPROX-RANDOM.2021.45.pdf) studies failure of greedy learning heuristics. It does not provide the checked support-relative isotone identification model or the exact parity-family depth formula.
- [Canonne et al., Testing k-Monotonicity: The Rise and Fall of Boolean Functions (2019)](https://theoryofcomputing.org/articles/v015a001/) concerns property testing of an unknown Boolean function on a poset. In the present theorem the functions are supplied and monotonicity restricts which test may be asked on the surviving support. This is a different role for monotonicity.

**Result and limitation.** The exact theorem survives this small targeted search in the limited sense that no direct prior theorem was located. Five search strings and inspection of the apparent primary-source matches do not exhaust differently named models, unpublished work, or citation networks. The audit therefore retains provisional low-to-moderate novelty confidence and does not make a “first” claim. Mathematical verification of the recurrence is substantially stronger than the present evidence about priority.

# Main result: restriction controls repair-safe adaptive identification

## H8: support restriction theorem and adaptive consequences

Let P be a finite post-T0 poset of height at most two, Q a fixed library of oriented Boolean tests, and r in Q. For a support S write D_r(S) for descent pairs, A_r(S) for deleted three-chains, and B_r(S) for the F2 relative boundary.

1. At every history h the branch poset is canonically P|S_h. Hence the current support alone determines the future unit-cost subproblem.
2. For T subseteq S,

     B_r(T)=B_r(S)[D_r(T),A_r(T)],

   and all entries of retained columns in removed rows are zero.
3. Therefore the actual triangle-column matroid is obtained by deletion, and relative H2 cannot increase. After adjoining artificial root-edge unit columns, restriction is exactly contraction of removed artificial edges plus deletion of removed actual triangle columns.
4. If r is safe on S, it is safe on T iff |D_r(T)|=|A_r(T)|. Any failure is precisely a rootless repair component, with relative H1 dimension |D_r(T)|-|A_r(T)|. It cannot arise by creation of a new triangle-column dependence.
5. Safety is not hereditary: a legal restriction can activate or deactivate an informative test on three states, and three is minimal.
6. The safe identification depth is given exactly by the support min-max recurrence. A legal choice need not preserve future feasibility at height two, unlike the hereditary height-one regime.

### Proof

Part 1 is coordinate cancellation on an answer fiber (BRANCH_CANCELLATION.md). Parts 2-4 follow from induced-chain restriction, reduced graph incidence, and extension of kernel vectors by zero (REPAIR_GRAPH_DYNAMICS.md and MATROID_INTERPRETATION.md). Part 5 is witnessed by the connected fork activation and chain anchor-loss examples (QUERY_ACTIVATION_DEACTIVATION.md). Part 6 follows by induction on support size; the library {010,011} on a three-chain disproves arbitrary-safe-first feasibility preservation (FIXED_LIBRARY_IDENTIFICATION.md).

## Sharp consequences for fixed libraries

For every n>=3 there is a connected poset of actual height two and a fixed library with

  d_ad=ceil(log2 n),  d_RF=n-1.

This attains the universal largest finite additive gap. For complement-closed libraries, a connected height-one family with n=2^k has the exact depths

  d_ad=k,  d_RF=n/2+k-1,  gap=n/2-1,

for k>=1. Both families have unbounded depth ratios. Complete proofs, including polarity limitations and the recurrence proving the second formula, are in ADAPTIVE_DEPTH_THEORY.md.

## Correctness versus novelty

These are proved statements, with bounded computation used as an independent check rather than a substitute for proof. The inherited v0.4 repair-forest theorem is the essential topological input.

The support recurrence, graph-incidence algebra, matroid minors, information bounds and generic query-restriction penalties are established mathematical tools. The best candidate contribution is the precise support-restriction/anchor-loss theorem for this ProLT legality rule and its consequences for activation and feasibility. The extremal examples are useful exact corollaries, but do not by themselves establish a new height-two decision-tree theory.

Novelty confidence is moderate-to-low pending a focused comparison of this specific theorem with prior work. No claim of priority or publication readiness is made from the bounded search.

# Matroid interpretation

Use the notation D,A,B from REPAIR_GRAPH_DYNAMICS.md.

## The actual column matroid

Identify all formal roots to a distinguished root *. Since distinct coarse components have no shared nonroot vertices, this identification introduces no new cycle. The reduced incidence matrix remains B. Its column matroid M(B), on deleted triangles A, is a standard graphic matroid.

For induced T, every retained column is zero in every removed row. Therefore

  M(B_T)=M(B)|A_T.

This is exactly a matroid restriction (deletion of the missing triangle elements), not merely a conjectured analogy. No contraction is needed for this statement. Dependencies cannot be created under conditioning.

However, safety is not just "the actual triangles form a basis of their own column matroid." That statement misses full row rank: a rootless tree has independent columns spanning its column space but leaves a nonzero relative H1 defect.

## Full-rank augmentation and an exact minor

Adjoin one artificial edge s_e from * to each deleted-edge vertex e. The augmented reduced incidence matrix is

  [B | I_D].

This is still a graphic matroid and has rank |D|. The actual triangle set A is a basis of this augmented matroid iff B is square invertible, exactly repair safety.

Let J=D\D_T. Contract the artificial edges s_e for e in J and delete the actual triangle columns A\A_T. The unit columns being contracted are independent; contraction quotients out their coordinate directions. In the remaining representation the contracted rows disappear, leaving

  [B_T | I_(D_T)].

Thus conditioning IS an exact standard graphic-matroid minor in this augmented, provenance-aware representation. Retained actual columns were zero in the contracted rows, so the construction agrees with the direct restriction theorem.

The abstract column matroid alone forgets world/triangle provenance and the row target. It cannot by itself say which support deletions are permitted or detect lost anchors. One must carry the support labels and augmented root data.

## Priority

Incidence representations, graphic bases, deletion and contraction are standard. The relevant derived result is their exact fit to this particular support-restriction operation, together with the obstruction interpretation. A claim that conditioning has "no matroid-minor description" is too strong and is rejected.

# Open problems after this gate

## Highest priority: genuine height-two feasibility

Classify RF-IDENT for explicit post-T0 height-at-most-two posets and a fixed supplied query table. It is in NP, has an exact support DP, and is polynomial at height at most one. The three-chain library {010,011} defeats arbitrary-safe-first greedy feasibility at height two. Either a separate NP-hardness reduction or a complete polynomial algorithm would settle a real remaining question.

A tightly specified natural height-two class with a complete feasibility algorithm would also be valuable. Do not treat an optimization hardness result or an exponential DP as a feasibility classification.

## Priority review of exact statements

Before a publication claim, audit the precise restriction/anchor-loss theorem and exact parity-bipartite recurrence against primary work on hereditary and nonhereditary test admissibility. The present search establishes broad overlap, not exhaustive absence of equivalents.

## Lower priority, conditional on the main gate

* Characterize deactivation-free reachable libraries beyond globally isotone tests; universal induced-support safety is already solved.
* Investigate complexity or algorithms exploiting bounded width/treewidth only after specifying which graph (Hasse, comparability or repair) is bounded.
* Distinguish adaptive query choice from a fixed schedule that conditions on each outcome. Existing examples separate full-carrier safety benchmarks, not every possible scheduled-conditioning model.
* Weighted costs, succinct formula representations and logical-fragment-specific algorithms need separate precise inputs and proofs.

The maximal finite gap and complement-closed unbounded-gap questions are resolved here; do not reopen them as conjectures. The exact parity formula is proved, not merely suggested by n=4,8,16.

No return to consciousness interpretations, broad category theory, physical quantum claims or higher-dimensional generalization is needed for these questions.

# H3: activation, deactivation and their minimal witnesses

Queries are tested before conditioning. "Informative transition" means the target query remains nonconstant on the child support. A reachable witness additionally specifies a legal conditioning query.

## Activation: three states, connected height one

Take P with a<b and a<c, and query r=(1,0,1) in the order (a,b,c). Its only descent is a<b, with no repair triangle, so its relative matrix is 1-by-0 and it is unsafe.

The isotone query q=(0,1,1) is legal. On q=1 the support is {b,c}, an antichain; r=(0,1) is nonconstant and safe with a 0-by-0 matrix. Thus the fixed library {q,r} identifies all three states safely in depth two, although its initially safe subset {q} does not separate b from c.

This shows a real use of initially unavailable tests. Activation is not merely a query becoming constant.

## Deactivation: three-state chain, actual height two

Take x<y<z, r=010 and q=011. Initially r has the sole descent yz and sole deleted triangle xyz of word 010. Its matrix is [1], and the repair graph is a rooted one-edge tree.

The isotone q is safe. Conditioning on q=1 leaves y<z, where r=10. The matrix becomes 1-by-0: the descent vertex survives, its anchor triangle does not. Hence r becomes unsafe.

This also disproves an arbitrary-legal-query greedy feasibility strategy at height two. The library {010,011} is feasible by asking 010 first and then 011 on its {x,z} branch. Asking legal query 011 first strands the {y,z} branch.

## Minimality and hereditary safety

Fewer than three states cannot give a useful transition under proper restriction, since the child has at most one state. Both witnesses above have three states and are therefore vertex-minimal among informative transitions, even with legal one-step reachability required.

If one allows a constant target query on the child, unsafe 10 on a two-chain becomes trivially safe on a singleton. This is a different, uninformative minimum and should not be confused with query activation useful for identification.

For any finite poset, an observation is safe on EVERY induced support iff it is isotone:

* If isotone, it deletes no comparisons on any support.
* If not, there is a descent x<y. Restrict to {x,y}; refinement deletes the sole edge, separating a connected interval into two points.

Thus universal hereditary safety is exactly redundancy. This does not say a fixed library can reach every offending two-point support.

On height at most one, safety at a given support already means isotonicity there and is hereditary below that support. At height two, safe nonredundant queries introduce the first deactivation phenomenon.

## Nonadaptive comparisons, defined explicitly

The activation example separates the adaptive conditioning model from three full-carrier benchmarks:

1. An initially individually safe separating sublibrary does not exist.
2. A sequence that refines the full carrier without conditioning, requiring each prefix inclusion safe, cannot identify using {q,r}: q is redundant and leaves r unsafe.
3. A jointly safe separating block does not exist in this library: every separating block contains r and deletes the sole descending edge a<b without any triangles.

These are the coordinatewise, sequential-prefix and simultaneous notions distinguished in v0.5. They are not interchangeable. This example does NOT separate adaptive query choice from a predetermined schedule that is allowed to condition after every answer and omit constant tests: the schedule q then r works in that latter model. No broader adaptivity advantage is claimed.

# H2: exact repair-graph and boundary restriction

All coefficients below are F2. P is finite, post-T0, of height at most two; r is ONE oriented Boolean test. Write K=Delta(P), L=Delta(P_r).

## Source theorem reconstructed

Let D be all comparable pairs x<y with r(x)=1,r(y)=0. These are all deleted edges, including transitive comparisons, not just Hasse edges. Let A be all three-chains x<y<z with a nonmonotone bit word. The relative chain complex is

  0 -> F2[A] --B--> F2[D] -> 0.

There are no relative vertices and no cells above dimension two. A matrix column has a 1 exactly at each deleted edge that is a face of its triangle.

| Word | Deleted edges | Repair graph edge |
|---|---|---|
| 010 | yz | formal root to yz |
| 101 | xy | formal root to xy |
| 100 | xy,xz | xy to xz |
| 110 | xz,yz | xz to yz |

The other four words 000,001,011,111 retain the triangle. Introduce one formal root for EVERY coarse comparability component, including components with no deleted cells, and one graph vertex per deleted edge. Keep parallel graph edges. Each deleted triangle contributes the graph edge shown in the table. B is precisely its incidence matrix with root rows removed.

The v0.4 theorem equates: homotopy equivalence of L->K; simple homotopy equivalence; collapse using only deleted edge-triangle pairs; F2 homology equivalence; B invertible; and the repair graph a forest with exactly one root per graph component. A 0-by-0 matrix is invertible. Isolated formal roots are harmless. An isolated descent vertex is not.

Proof checkpoint: relative acyclicity is matrix bijectivity. An invertible reduced incidence matrix excludes cycles and rootless components. Conversely, repeatedly remove a nonroot leaf of the rooted forest. Its deleted edge belongs to exactly one remaining triangle; no retained triangle contains a deleted edge, and height excludes higher cofaces. Hence it is a free edge-triangle collapse. This establishes the full equivalence without assuming that homology generally determines homotopy.

## Exact restriction theorem

For T subseteq P define

  D_T={e in D: both vertices of e lie in T},
  A_T={tau in A: all three vertices of tau lie in T}.

Then, in the inherited cell orders,

  B_r(P|T)=B_r(P)[D_T,A_T].

Moreover B_r(P)[D\D_T,A_T]=0: every face of a retained triangle remains in T.

Proof: induced orders retain exactly those chains whose vertices survive. The r-values and simplicial incidence coefficients are unchanged. This proves both assertions.

At graph level the exact operation is:

1. Remove descent vertices whose underlying pairs do not survive.
2. Remove triangle edges whose underlying triples do not survive, EVEN IF both graph endpoints survive.
3. Recompute the coarse components of P|T. Replace an old formal root by one root for each surviving coarse component and attach each surviving anchor to its new component root.
4. Keep the endpoints of surviving dependency edges. Add isolated roots where required; omit empty coarse components.

This is generally not an induced graph subgraph. In the chain 010, deleting the first state removes the anchor triangle while retaining its descent vertex. Triangle provenance is essential; an abstract unlabeled repair graph alone is insufficient input to the restriction operation.

## Exact defects and all safety transitions

Let c0(T) be the number of graph components with no root and let beta(T) be the ordinary graph cycle rank (parallel edges count). No graph component can contain two formal roots: every graph edge stays inside one coarse component, which has only one root. Standard incidence rank gives

  rank B_T = |D_T|-c0(T),
  dim H1(K_T,L_T;F2)=c0(T),
  dim H2(K_T,L_T;F2)=beta(T)=|A_T|-|D_T|+c0(T).

Thus safety is exactly c0(T)=beta(T)=0.

Extension of a vector by zero gives an injection ker(B_T) -> ker(B). Indeed the retained columns have zero entries in every removed row. Consequently restriction CANNOT create a new column dependence or increase relative H2. This is stronger and more precise than a visual analogy about graph deletion.

| Parent -> child | Exact criterion |
|---|---|
| safe -> safe | c0(T)=0; beta(T)=0 is automatic |
| safe -> unsafe | c0(T)>0; the failure is lost anchoring, never a newly created cycle |
| unsafe -> safe | all parent dependencies on retained triangles disappear, and every residual descent component is rooted |
| unsafe -> unsafe | a retained cycle or a rootless component remains |

In particular, if r was safe on P, then

  r safe on P|T iff |D_T|=|A_T|,
  dim H1(K_T,L_T)=|D_T|-|A_T| >= 0,
  H2(K_T,L_T)=0.

This count shortcut is valid only with the prior safety/column-independence certificate. Equal counts alone do not prove safety in general.

## Incremental implementation

Precompute each query's deleted pairs and triples with their vertex provenance. Deleting a state removes only incident pairs/triples. The boundary update is exact row/column selection, never a numerical approximation. Coarse-root recomputation is needed for a literal graph certificate, but not to obtain B_T from its stored columns.

A full one-query test costs O(n^3) to enumerate chains from an explicit order matrix and O(n+|D|+|A|) graph traversal once cells/components are known. After a safe ancestor, maintain deleted-pair and deleted-triple counts; each vertex deletion costs the number of still-active incident stored cells, and count equality decides safety on every descendant. This does not claim an output-independent constant-time dynamic connectivity algorithm.

# Independent structural audit: height-two fixed-library gate

Date: 2026-09-29. This file contains independently checked deductions from the supplied source conventions. Proofs are mathematical proofs; no computation or priority search is claimed here. Novelty remains unassessed except where the construction plainly uses standard linear algebra or graphic matroids.

## 1. Source theorem and conventions

The authoritative one-bit construction is ProLT v0.4, section “Height two: from a boundary matrix to a repair forest.” Height at most two means no strict chain has more than three vertices. A finite post-T0 signature poset is identified with its states, using injectivity of the old signature map.

For a Boolean observation r, the refined order is

    x <=_r y iff x <=_P y and r(x) <= r(y).

Write K=Delta(P), L=Delta(P_r). Vertices are unchanged. Deleted edges D are all strict comparisons (not merely Hasse edges) with bit pattern 10. Deleted triangles A are all three-chains whose word is not nondecreasing:

| Word on x<y<z | Deleted edges | Repair edge |
|---|---|---|
| 010 | yz | root--v_yz |
| 101 | xy | root--v_xy |
| 100 | xy, xz | v_xy--v_xz |
| 110 | xz, yz | v_xz--v_yz |

There is one formal root for every connected component of the coarse poset, including a root with no incident repair edges if needed. Distinct triangles remain distinct graph edges; parallel anchor edges are possible and count as a cycle of length two. Every repair-graph component has at most one root, because no repair edge crosses coarse components and each coarse component has only one root. Rootless repair components can occur.

Over F2, the relative complex is

    0 -> F2^A --B--> F2^D -> 0,

where B is the repair incidence matrix with root rows removed. A 0-by-0 matrix is invertible. The source theorem equates the following for the *inclusion* L -> K:

1. homotopy equivalence;
2. simple homotopy equivalence;
3. a collapse K onto L using deleted edge--triangle pairs;
4. F2 homology equivalence;
5. invertibility of B;
6. repair graph a forest with one root in every component.

The proof is sound: invertibility excludes cycles and rootless components. Conversely, a rooted tree has a nonroot leaf unless it is an isolated root; pair its descent edge with its unique incident deleted triangle. A retained triangle cannot contain a deleted edge, and there are no higher-dimensional cells. Therefore the edge is free, and repeated pruning gives the claimed collapse. The statement is about the specific inclusion, not merely an abstract coincidence of homotopy types.

## 2. Branch cancellation and sufficient state

**Theorem BC.** At every history h of an adaptive protocol beginning with a post-T0 state (S0,P0), the current branch poset is canonically P0 restricted to its surviving support S_h. In particular it remains T0 and has height at most that of P0.

**Proof.** Old coordinates are retained when a query q is appended. On the outcome support T={x in S_h:q(x)=b}, the new coordinate takes the same value b everywhere. Thus for x,y in T,

    x <=_(Phi_h+q) y iff x <=_(Phi_h) y and b<=b
                         iff x <=_(Phi_h) y.

The signature embedding with one constant coordinate appended is a canonical order isomorphism. Iteration gives P0|S_h. Injectivity of the initial signature map persists because its coordinates remain. Restriction also preserves injectivity. QED.

This does not claim that the unconditioned refinement leaves order unchanged. Legality must be tested before the outcome is imposed.

With Q fixed globally, support S is sufficient for a dynamic program. Previously queried tests are constant on S and cannot separate it; retaining them in the global library while excluding currently constant tests yields the same recursion as explicitly removing used tests. No independent accumulated-coordinate state is necessary.

## 3. Exact support restriction theorem

Fix r and T subset P. Let

    D_T = {e in D: both endpoints of e lie in T},
    A_T = {tau in A: all three vertices of tau lie in T}.

**Theorem SR.** The repair graph on P|T is obtained as follows:

1. Keep precisely the descent vertices D_T.
2. Keep precisely the triangle edges A_T.
3. For each old coarse component C, replace its formal root by one formal root for each component C' of P|T contained in C. Attach a retained anchor edge to the root of the unique C' containing its triangle.

No new descent or triangle edge appears. A dependency edge survives exactly when both its descent vertices survive, because those two original comparisons together use all three triangle vertices. An anchor edge additionally requires its third, witness vertex to survive. Thus merely inducing on surviving descent vertices and the old roots is wrong: an anchor witness can disappear while the descent remains, and coarse roots can split.

For the relative matrices,

    B_T = B[D_T,A_T].                                      (1)

Moreover,

    B[D\D_T,A_T] = 0.                                     (2)

**Proof.** A comparison or three-chain survives support restriction exactly when all its vertices do. Its bit values and deleted/retained classification do not change. The incidence entries in a surviving triangle are therefore unchanged. Every edge of a surviving triangle has both endpoints in T, proving (2). Coarse-component containment gives the root rule. QED.

This gives a direct incremental implementation: cache descent endpoints and triangle vertex masks once per query; filter these masks at a support; retain the corresponding rows and columns. Root splitting is needed for graph display, but not for boundary construction or rank. Union-find on retained repair edges and roots gives a linear check in retained cell counts after the masks have been filtered. Across a library of m queries, naive first construction costs O(m n^3); no subcubic global update bound is asserted.

## 4. Exact homological defects and all safety transitions

For a repair graph G, let f(G) be the number of components without a root, and c(G) its ordinary cycle rank, counting multiedges. If d=|D| and a=|A|, then

    rank(B)=d-f(G),
    dim H1(K,L;F2)=f(G),
    dim H2(K,L;F2)=c(G)=a-d+f(G).                          (3)

**Proof.** In a rooted connected component the reduced incidence matrix has full row rank. In a rootless component the incidence rank is one less than the number of vertices. Summing gives the first equation; the relative complex gives the second and third. Equivalently the usual graph formula uses total vertices d+r and components f+r, where r is the number of formal roots. QED.

**Theorem CD.** Support restriction cannot create a triangle-column dependence or a relative H2 class: extension by zero gives an injection

    ker B_T -> ker B.

Consequently c(G_T)<=c(G).

**Proof.** Extend a vector indexed by A_T by zeros on A\A_T. Equation (2) guarantees that B kills it whenever B_T does. This map is injective. QED.

This is stronger than saying root splitting cannot create graph cycles. Cycle creation is impossible under arbitrary induced support restriction, even from an unsafe parent. Existing cycles can survive or disappear; they cannot be newly created.

**Corollary SS.** If r is safe on P, then every retained column is independent, so

    rank(B_T)=|A_T|,
    f(G_T)=|D_T|-|A_T| >= 0,
    r is safe on P|T iff |D_T|=|A_T|.                     (4)

Thus deactivation occurs precisely by losing anchors or dependencies in such a way that a surviving descent cluster is no longer attached to any root. It never occurs through cycle creation. Its relative-H1 defect equals the number of rootless components, and also equals

    (number of deleted parent triangles) -
    (number of deleted parent descent edges).

Here “deleted parent” means lost during support restriction, rather than deleted during observation refinement.

All four safety transitions are now exact:

| Parent -> child | Exact criterion |
|---|---|
| safe -> safe | f(G_T)=0; cycles are automatically absent |
| safe -> unsafe | f(G_T)>0; no new cycle obstruction is possible |
| unsafe -> safe | all surviving cycle dependencies are eliminated and f(G_T)=0 |
| unsafe -> unsafe | a surviving cycle or rootless component remains |

The last two rows do not promise that breaking every cycle is sufficient: support loss can simultaneously destroy needed anchors.

## 5. Hereditary safety and minimal transition examples

**Theorem HS.** A Boolean observation is safe on every induced subposet of a height-at-most-two P if and only if it is isotone on P.

**Proof.** An isotone observation deletes no comparison on any restriction. Conversely, any descent x<y gives an induced two-state chain on which the query deletes the sole edge and has no triangle to repair it. QED.

This is universality over *all* supports. It does not say that every such support is reachable in an arbitrary supplied library, or that every nonisotone safe query must deactivate along every protocol.

Minimal deactivation on a legal branch uses three states. Let P be x<y<z, r=010 and q=011. Both queries are safe initially: r has one anchor triangle and q is isotone. Conditioning q=1 leaves {y,z}; r restricts to 10 and is unsafe. The repair triangle disappears with x, leaving its descent vertex unanchored. No two-state example exists, because a safe query on a two-state chain must be isotone, and all queries on an antichain remain safe.

For the fixed library {r,q}, asking q first therefore dead-ends on its one branch. Asking r first succeeds: the one branch is singleton {y}, while the zero branch {x,z} has q=01 and is safely identified. Thus choosing an initially safe query greedily can destroy feasibility, even when all library tests were initially safe.

Minimal activation including constant outcome restrictions uses two states: x<y, r=10 unsafe, q=01 safe, and either q-outcome is a singleton on which r is safe but constant. This is a formally valid, uninformative activation.

Minimal **nonconstant** activation uses three states if disconnected posets are allowed. Take a<b with c isolated; r(a,b,c)=(1,0,0) is unsafe. The isotone legal query q=(0,1,0) has outcome-zero support {a,c}, an antichain on which r=(1,0) is safe and informative. No two-state nonconstant example is possible because every proper nonempty branch is a singleton.

Connected posets also admit nonconstant activation at three states: take a<b,a<c, r=101, q=011. Here r is unsafe because a<b descends, while q is isotone; the q=1 branch {b,c} is an antichain with r=01, safe and informative. The three-chain itself cannot realize informative activation: its only unsafe words are 100 and 110, and every nonconstant two-state restriction remains a descending comparable pair. Thus chain-only reconnaissance would miss the smallest connected example.

## 6. Matroid interpretation: restriction and an augmented minor

Let M(B) be the represented matroid on actual triangle columns A.

**Theorem MR.** The actual column matroid under conditioning is exactly ordinary restriction:

    M(B_T)=M(B)|A_T.                                      (5)

**Proof.** First restrict columns to A_T. All rows subsequently removed are zero by (2), so their removal changes no column dependencies. QED.

Calling the complete actual triangle set “a basis of its repair matroid” is insufficient for safety. Any rootless tree has independent actual columns, hence its entire edge set is a basis of its own graphic matroid, but its reduced incidence matrix is not surjective onto descent rows. Rootless rows must be represented in the full target dimension.

For correct ambient bookkeeping, append one artificial anchor column s_e for every descent e:

    Bhat=[ B | I_D ].

This is still a graphic representation: add an artificial edge from each descent vertex to its coarse-component root. Its rank is exactly |D|, whether or not actual triangles have roots or cycles.

**Theorem AM.** A query is safe if and only if its actual triangle set A is a basis of M(Bhat). Under support restriction, the augmented matroid is the standard minor

    M(Bhat_T) = ( M(Bhat) / {s_e:e in D\D_T} )
                         \ (A\A_T).                     (6)

Ground labels on retained columns and artificial anchors are identified canonically.

**Proof.** The basis statement is precisely square invertibility of B in a full-rank ambient representation. Contracting a collection of independent unit columns is represented by deleting their coordinate rows and deleting those unit columns. Deleting the absent actual triangle columns leaves [B_T|I_DT]. QED.

Thus two compatible descriptions are available: actual triangle dependencies undergo deletion alone, while a full-rank ambient rooted graphic matroid undergoes contraction of absent artificial anchors and deletion of absent actual triangles. Formal-root splitting changes the graph realization but does not invalidate either represented-matroid equality. This is standard graphic-matroid machinery specialized to the support geometry, not evidence of a new kind of matroid.

## 7. Exact natural-family feasibility: a height-one star

Let P consist of a greatest state z and incomparable leaves X with x<z for every x. Q is an arbitrary fixed Boolean library.

Every height-one query is safe iff it is isotone, because there are no triangles and therefore no way to repair a descent. On a nonsingleton support A union {z}, an informative safe query necessarily has q(z)=1 and nonempty zero set

    Z_q(A)={x in A:q(x)=0}.

The zero outcome is an antichain. The one outcome remains a star containing z.

**Theorem SF.** Repair-safe identification on this star is feasible if and only if:

1. Q distinguishes every two leaves;
2. for every leaf x there exists q in Q with q(x)=0 and q(z)=1.

**Proof.** Identical complete library signatures cannot be distinguished by any protocol. On the z outcome path, x can be eliminated only by an informative safe query of the displayed orientation; this proves necessity of condition 2. Conversely, ask such oriented queries along the z path until their zero sets cover all leaves. Each peeled zero branch is an antichain and can be identified by remaining library tests because condition 1 holds. Earlier queries are constant on that branch, so they cannot be the sole distinguishers of any surviving leaf pair. QED.

This is polynomial-time feasibility by signature comparisons and coverage, though it does not imply polynomial-time optimal depth.

Write O(Z) for ordinary fixed-library optimal depth on leaf subset Z (all queries are safe because Z is an antichain). Then the exact star depth satisfies

    F(empty)=0,
    F(A)=1+min_{q:q(z)=1, Z_q(A) nonempty}
               max( O(Z_q(A)), F(A\Z_q(A)) ),             (7)

with infinity when the feasible set is empty or a necessary branch is unidentifiable. Previously used queries are constant on the support, so the full fixed Q may remain in this formula. The minimum size of an oriented zero-set cover is a lower bound on the z-path length; (7) also accounts for identifying the groups peeled along that path.

## 8. Independent audit of the maximal-gap family

The parent investigation proposed the following family; every step has been checked independently here.

For n>=3 let P_n have a least state a, a greatest state z, and n-2 incomparable intermediate states x_i, with a<x_i<z. This is connected and has height exactly two. Let k=ceil(log2 n). Assign distinct k-bit labels with label(a)=11...1, label(z)=00...0, and distinct other labels to the intermediate states. Let Q contain:

- all k coordinate tests of these labels;
- each peeling test p_v, v != z, equal to zero exactly at v and one elsewhere.

If an identical test appears twice, treat the library as a set; the argument is unaffected.

**Theorem MG.**

    d_ad(P_n,Q)=ceil(log2 n),
    d_RF(P_n,Q)=n-1,
    Delta_RF=n-1-ceil(log2 n).                            (8)

**Proof.** All states have distinct code labels, so querying code coordinates identifies them in k steps; the binary information bound gives equality.

Each code bit is antitone on P_n. On every nonsingleton support containing z that arises by peeling other states, the induced poset remains connected (every surviving state lies below z). A nonconstant antitone bit removes every comparison between its nonempty zero and one sets. Its refinement therefore disconnects a formerly connected complex and is unsafe. A code bit that is constant is uninformative.

Every informative peeling test is safe on these z-containing supports. The test p_a is isotone. For an intermediate v=x_i, if a survives then the sole descent is a<x_i and its sole repairing triangle is a<x_i<z with word 101, giving a one-by-one invertible matrix. If a is absent, p_x_i is isotone. A peeling test whose exceptional state is absent is constant.

Consequently every informative safe query on the z path removes exactly one other state. This requires n-1 queries. Asking the peeling tests successively attains that bound, with every zero branch a singleton. QED.

The penalty is maximal among *finite* penalties on n states. Every finite identifying binary tree with nonconstant tests has depth at most n-1 after irrelevant nodes are removed, because each queried branch strictly reduces candidate-set size. Meanwhile ordinary depth is at least ceil(log2 n). Thus (8) attains the universal upper bound, and the gap is unbounded as n grows.

This family uses fixed query orientation. Automatically adding complements would change the supplied library and invalidate the claimed example: complements of the antitone code bits are isotone and would identify efficiently. Complement closure is an additional hypothesis, not part of the stated primary problem.

The height-one star version, with z assigned the zero code and leaves assigned distinct nonzero codes, has the same exact maximal gap. The height-two version is preferable for this gate because it explicitly uses the 101 repair triangle to certify intermediate peeling tests.

### Complement-closed unbounded-gap family

The parent investigation subsequently supplied a family that removes the polarity caveat for *unboundedness*, although it does not claim the exact maximal gap. Let n=2^k, k>=2, with states all k-bit strings. Put every even-parity string below every odd-parity string, with no other strict comparisons. This is a connected height-one complete bipartite poset. The fixed library contains every coordinate and its complement, and every singleton indicator and its complement.

**Theorem CG.** For this complement-closed library,

    d_ad=k,
    n/4+k <= d_RF <= n-1,
    Delta_RF >= n/4.                                     (9)

For k=2, d_RF=3 and d_ad=2 exactly.

**Proof.** The k coordinates identify all states, and the binary lower bound gives ordinary depth k. For any coordinate polarity, exactly n/4 lower states have value one and exactly n/4 upper states have value zero. Height-one safety is isotonicity, so that polarity can be safe on a support only after all states in at least one of these two forbidden sets have disappeared. Until n/4 states have been removed, no coordinate polarity is legal.

The only remaining available informative queries are singleton indicators or their complements; each isolates exactly one state. An adversary follows the nonsingleton branch of the first n/4 queries. These queries must all be singleton tests, since before the last such query fewer than n/4 states have disappeared. The remaining support has size 3n/4, requiring at least ceil(log2(3n/4))=k more queries even with no safety constraint. This proves the lower bound.

Every remaining vertex has a safe singleton polarity: the singleton indicator is isotone for an upper vertex, and its complement is isotone for a lower vertex. Successive peeling therefore identifies all states in at most n-1 queries, proving finiteness and the upper bound. For n=4 both bounds are three. QED.

The argument establishes linear unbounded penalties even under complement closure, so orientation alone does not explain the phenomenon. The construction is nevertheless already height one; it is an appropriate boundary/control theorem for a height-at-most-two investigation, not evidence that the gap itself needs the nontrivial repair mechanism.

### Exact depth of the complement-closed parity family

The parent investigation subsequently strengthened (9) to an exact recurrence. The proof below was independently hostile-audited, including the residual-library identification and the first-coordinate lower bound.

Let D_k be repair-safe depth for the parity bipartite family on all k-bit strings, with all coordinate polarities and singleton polarities. Include k=1 as the two-state-chain base instance, where D_1=1. Then

    D_k = 2^(k-2)+1+D_(k-1),                  k>=2,
    D_k = 2^(k-1)+k-1,                        k>=1,
    Delta_RF = 2^(k-1)-1 = n/2-1.                        (10)

**Upper bound.** Fix a coordinate q. Peel all n/4 lower vertices for which q=1, using their isotone singleton complements. Query q. It is now safe, since no lower state has q=1. Its q=0 branch is the canonical parity bipartite instance on k-1 free coordinates and n/2 states. The restricted library contains exactly that canonical smaller library, together with constants and duplicates. Its q=1 branch consists of the n/4 upper states with q=1, an antichain. Their k-1 remaining coordinates satisfy one parity equation, so k-2 coordinate tests identify them. Since D_(k-1)>=k-2, the resulting depth is at most n/4+1+D_(k-1).

**Lower bound.** Consider any safe identifying tree, removing constant queries. Follow nonsingleton branches of its singleton queries until the first coordinate query (of either polarity). Suppose t singleton peels occur first. If no coordinate query ever occurs on this path, its length is n-1, which is at least n/2+k-1 because k<=2^(k-1).

Otherwise denote the first coordinate polarity by q. Originally each of its two forbidden sets, lower states with q=1 and upper states with q=0, has n/4 elements. Safety requires at least one forbidden set to have been completely removed. Let E be the coordinate half containing such a removed set, and H the opposite half. If t_H states were removed from H, then

    t >= n/4+t_H.                                       (11)

Before any deletions H is a canonical parity bipartite instance on k-1 coordinates, possibly with the two parity classes interchanged. That interchange is removed by flipping one free coordinate, which preserves the complemented coordinate/singleton library. Let R be the t_H removed states and D(H\R) the optimal depth of the residual instance. Every singleton can be safely peeled from any induced subposet of H by choosing its appropriate polarity. Prepending these t_H safe singleton peels to an optimal protocol for H\R therefore gives

    D_(k-1) <= t_H+D(H\R).                              (12)

The actual tree's q-outcome in H must take at least D(H\R) further queries. Previous singleton queries and q itself are constant on this outcome, so excluding already used tests changes no residual identification capability. Because q is informative, both coordinate outcomes, including H\R, are nonempty. Combining (11)--(12), the tree has depth at least

    t+1+D(H\R) >= n/4+1+D_(k-1).

Together with the upper construction this proves the recurrence. Its solution is (10), and ordinary depth remains exactly k. QED.

For k=2,3,4 this yields exact safe depths 3,6,11. The proof, rather than any finite computation, establishes the full family. Complement closure therefore permits a sharp linear safety penalty in this supplied family. The exact recurrence still relies only on height-one isotonicity and structured library geometry.

## 9. Independently confirmed existing source corrections

The supplied `03_PROLT_PRIMARY_SOURCES/CLAIM_AUDIT_TABLE.csv` already flags v0.5 claim V5-06 as `FALSE/COUNTEREXAMPLE` and V5-07 as `NEEDS_MAJOR_REPAIR`. The check performed in this investigation independently confirms those existing corrections; it is not a newly discovered source defect.

Specifically, v0.5's raw TeX claims odim_P(Q)=dim_2(Q) whenever P is a total order extending Q. As written this is false: take Q=P a two-state chain. The source definition gives odim_P(P)=0, while the classical Boolean order-embedding dimension of a two-state chain is 1. The proposed proof incorrectly treats the biconditional imposed only on P-comparable forward pairs as if it were imposed on every ordered pair. The complexity corollary justified by that equality is therefore unsupported by that argument. The existing audit withdraws the inherited total-order hardness claim and records a separate repaired general-case result; the raw TeX must not override those later corrections.

The same claim-audit table flags V5-09 as `NEEDS_MINOR_REPAIR`: generating the ambient complex only from deleted triangles can omit deleted edges unsupported by any triangle, thereby omitting zero rows of the relative boundary matrix. The recorded repair is to take G=K^(1) union the deleted triangles and R=the retained edges, so every deleted edge remains represented. This correction is consistent with the full-descent-row and ambient-matroid bookkeeping in the present audit.

These inherited corrections do not affect the v0.4 repair theorem, branch cancellation, restriction dynamics, or the current fixed-library model. They are preserved here for source provenance; repairing observation dimension theory is outside this gate.

## 10. Hostile verdict and priority limits

The dynamic program is an ordinary restricted decision tree with a support-dependent legal action set. Its recursion alone is not a contribution. The useful structural content proved above is the exact restriction law, the one-sided cycle monotonicity and rootless-component deactivation formula, the explicit augmented graphic-matroid minor, and the exact maximal-gap family on a connected height-two class. All follow with short proofs from the source representation; none should be called novel without a theorem-level literature audit.

An especially useful adversarial check is to keep three notions distinct: one-bit safety on the current conditioned support, sequential safety of unconditioned accumulated refinements, and simultaneous block safety. The branch-cancellation theorem only concerns the first adaptive model and does not transfer v0.4 graph conclusions to arbitrary multi-bit block refinements.

# H6: structured posets and libraries

## Exact solved families

The strongest exact depth family obtained here is the connected complete-bipartite parity order on n=2^k states, with coordinate tests and singleton tests, all supplied with both polarities. Its depths are

  d_ad=k, d_RF=2^(k-1)+k-1.

The recurrence D_1=1, D_k=2^(k-2)+1+D_(k-1) is proved in ADAPTIVE_DEPTH_THEORY.md. This is an exact result for a natural complete-bipartite height-one family with a precisely specified library. The genuinely height-two family with one bottom, n-2 middle states and one top attains the maximal finite gap with its oriented code-and-peeling library.

## Arbitrary libraries on a height-one star

Let P consist of incomparable leaves X below a top z. Safe identification is possible iff:

1. Q separates every two leaves;
2. for every leaf x there is a supplied oriented query q with q(x)=0,q(z)=1.

Necessity: leaf pairs must be distinguishable, and the first query separating x from z on the z path must have the safe orientation 0<1.

Sufficiency: along the z branch, successively ask useful supplied queries with q(z)=1. They are isotone and remove their zero-set leaves. Condition 2 eventually leaves only z. Every zero branch is an antichain and condition 1 supplies ordinary identification there.

For A subseteq X let A_qb={x in A:q(x)=b}. If F(A) is the star depth on A union {z}, and d_ad(B) the ordinary fixed-library depth on the leaf antichain B, then

  F(empty)=0,
  F(A)=1+min_(q(z)=1, A_q0 nonempty)
                 max(d_ad(A_q0), F(A_q1)).

The fixed query table, not arbitrary new tests, is used in both terms. This gives an exact feasibility characterization and exact recurrence; it is not a claim of polynomial optimal-depth computation.

## General height-one feasibility

RF-SAFE equals isotonicity, so it is hereditary. The generic hereditary-action proof in FIXED_LIBRARY_IDENTIFICATION.md yields polynomial RF-IDENT on all height-one posets, including crowns and fences with no three-chain. Actual height two is the first place where the proof fails because legal tests can deactivate.

## Which syntactic restrictions actually imply something

| Supplied class | Established conclusion | Limitation |
|---|---|---|
| Isotone tests on P0 | All remain safe; d_RF=d_ad, including infinity | Optimizing ordinary depth need not be easy |
| Old positive signature coordinates / monotone formulas in them | Isotone, hence preceding row | Their outcomes must still be acquired under the model |
| Literals with both polarities | Positive polarity isotone if it is an old coordinate | General supplied attribute coordinates need not be isotone |
| Complement-closed arbitrary library | Penalties persist, including exact linear family above | Complement closure is not unrestricted Boolean synthesis |
| Horn / dual-Horn | v0.4 sufficient repair certificates require its semilattice and cofinality hypotheses | No unrestricted Horn safety claim; restriction can lose hypotheses |
| Affine / XOR | No general safety guarantee | XOR safe on the full Boolean diamond can be unsafe after restriction |
| Bounded formula size | Defines a finite candidate pool once syntax and variables are fixed | Complexity depends on representation; no new bound proved here |
| CM/LM-supported tests | No extra theorem claimed | A precise compiler/allowed-class definition is still needed |

For a concrete XOR boundary, on diamond states 00<01,10<11 the XOR query has profile 0110 and is safe. Restrict to {01,11}; XOR is 10 on a two-chain and is unsafe. This support is obtained by conditioning the isotone old Y coordinate to 1 (with the conventional second-bit Y). Hence even a familiar formula class does not replace branch-relative safety checks.

The external bit codes used in the gap constructions are supplied attributes; they are not asserted to be the old order-embedding signature coordinates.

# Independent mathematical referee report: MIND unfolding v0.4

Review date: 29 September 2026. Target: `Observation_Refinement_Descent_and_Cone_Draft_v0.4.tex` and its 27-page PDF in `Manuscript Convergence 2026-09-29`.

**Recommended disposition: revise before submission.** The carrier-splitting, matching, interaction-complex, degree-two, and explicit torsion results in Sections 7–9 withstand this review. Their proofs, with the manuscript's augmented-chain conventions, support the stated conclusions over the stated coefficients. I found no fatal error in that mathematical core. This conclusion rests on the arguments below, not on passing enumerations.

The manuscript as a whole needs two precise repairs: make the admissibility assumptions on *every* nerve cover explicit in Theorem 11.2, and repair the fixed-arity definition and exceptional one-factor case of Theorem 2.4. The corrected distinction between descent on X and descent on Y is valid. Some further wording should distinguish homological detection from detection of all topological or support changes. Publication novelty is **not verified**. Much of the paper is standard machinery or a direct specialization; the potentially publishable core is the product-poset recognition, graph/transitivity restrictions, and sharp signed integral examples taken together.

This is a fresh AI mathematical review, not independent human peer review or formal proof certification. I read the entire v0.4 source and recorded an initial dependency map and concerns **before** reading earlier review verdicts. I then consulted the requested mathematical supplements and relevant companion claims, derived the arguments and witnesses, retrieved primary literature, and finally compared with internal reviews. No subagents were used. No manuscript, source archive, or earlier certificate was edited. All new files are in this separate directory.

## 1. Claim-by-claim assessment

“Verified” means the proof was checked or independently supplied in this report. Computation is additional evidence. Page numbers below are the manuscript's printed/PDF page numbers. “Valid with repair” distinguishes the intended result from an insufficiently specified literal formulation.

| Manuscript identifier | Status | Evidence and dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| Proposition 2.3, exact-one-false characterization | Verified | Pointwise evaluation of the disjoint Boolean disjuncts. |
| Definition 2.1 / Theorem 2.4, p. 4 | **False without an arity restriction; valid with the repair in §2 below** | For one factor, U(f)=not f is a Boolean-function operator. The printed proof compares tuples of different lengths despite the fixed-length definition. The non-congruence claim is true for each fixed length at least two. |
| Sections 3–4; Theorem 4.2 | Verified, with a minor proof-detail omission | XOR is a vector difference; tetrahedron and Hamming-layer claims follow directly. For the convex-hull equality, a slice vertex cannot have two fractional coordinates; its integral coordinate sum rules out exactly one fractional coordinate. This supplies the short missing argument in part (iii). The nontrivial layer has dimension m−1 and is a simplex exactly at weights 1 and m−1. |
| Theorem 5.2 and Corollary 5.3 | Verified | Relative skeleton chains occur only in degree r. Skeleton homology follows from exactness of simplex chains, Euler characteristic, and the top-dimensional cycle rank. |
| Section 6 refinement distinctions and nerve warning | Verified within the finite signature model | Forgetting coordinates coarsens equivalence; adding truth regions refines the generated topology. A tautological indexed region cones its nerve. No inference from arbitrary observation-list extension to cover refinement is justified or needed. |
| Theorem 7.2, p. 9 | Verified | Lower split copies are up-beat points; the remaining section is Q. The actual order is exactly the bit-monotone suborder. Cofiber invariance applies to the resulting factorization. |
| Theorem 7.4, p. 10 | Verified | Same vertices; retained chains are exactly weakly increasing bit words. The relative basis and boundary follow by quotient. |
| Proposition 7.5 / Corollary 7.6 | Verified | Available isotone section and pointwise comparison with the identity; dual argument for A0. |
| Lower-fiber discussion, §7.3 | Verified as a conditional statement | A top available copy is a maximum of its lower fiber. The Björner–Wachs–Welker conclusion requires the separately stated hypotheses; it is not automatic. |
| Lemma 7.8 / Theorem 7.9, pp. 11–12 | Verified | Weighted chain count; signed reduced graph incidence; leaf collapses. All five asserted equivalences hold. See §3. |
| §7.5 higher-height sharpness | Verified for existence and unrestricted realization | Companion cone–whisker argument checked independently. A face-poset model of RP² suffices for height-three torsion. The companion's particular 13-point/14-state economy was not independently verified and is unnecessary here. |
| Equation (1), §8.1, p. 13 | Verified over every stated coefficient ring | Two relative-acyclic inclusions, two triple sequences, and simplicial excision. See §4. |
| Proposition 8.2, p. 14 | Verified | Explicit isotone available-bit section and comparison map. This proves homotopy equivalence, beyond merely homology equivalence. |
| Theorem 8.3, p. 14 | Verified | Unique mixed pair, actual chain direct sum, product-edge-link suspension, and the two-colour shift. Empty/disconnected cases checked. Naturality needs a specified category if asserted beyond the present statement. |
| Corollaries 8.4–8.5, pp. 14–15 | Verified | Contractible outside factors; atom crosscut. The hypothesis that the generating poset is nonempty handles the singleton-lattice exception. |
| §8.2 three-chain and matching-torsion boundaries | Verified | Three-chain hand calculation; endpoint realization transfers arbitrary reduced link homology. It refutes universal torsion-freeness/TU, not just a field formula. |
| Proposition 9.1, p. 16 | Verified | Explicit filtered chains, signs, augmented degree, bidegree and finite convergence; only associated graded homology is determined by E∞ in general. |
| Theorem 9.2, p. 16 | Verified | Actual isomorphism to Cone(h)[2]; long exact sequence gives the stated kernel/cokernel degrees and quasi-isomorphism criterion. Integral extension warning is correct. |
| Theorem 9.3 and path blocks, p. 17 | Verified | Transitivity forces neighborhood inclusions; four-cores are exactly the specified C4 components; longer cycles have no triple cores. Full-poset links remain essential. |
| §9.1 eight-state C4, pp. 17–18 | Verified | All nine links reconstructed; oriented paths give a unit d²; independent full-pair and mixed-complex integral checks agree. |
| §9.1 seven-state K1,3, p. 18 | Verified | All seven links reconstructed; explicit triple-link paths give a primitive d²; star-pair topology independently gives cone H2=Z. |
| Proposition 9.4, p. 18 | Verified | Every available link has two contractible components; inclusions preserve component-difference generators. The horizontal row is the ordinary chain complex of ΔR, with a sign change. |

| Theorem 11.2(e–f), p. 20 | Verified on the intended inclusion site; general-site wording needs clarification | Separate sheaf/cosheaf descent on X and Y is correct. Use actual site morphisms and fiber-product/intersection diagrams, and a category admitting the requisite limits/colimits. |

| §11.1 claim that cone homology answers whether support/structure changed | Valid only after narrowing the wording | Cone homology detects failure of homology equivalence, not every change of support or homotopy type. |
