## 3. Source details and stable links

### Matrix and vector logic

**August Stern (1988), _Matrix Logic: Theory and Applications_.**  
Elsevier / ScienceDirect: https://www.sciencedirect.com/book/9780444704320/matrix-logic  
The publisher describes a formulation of logic using matrices and vector spaces and explicitly discusses a connection with Dirac quantum formalism.

**Eduardo Mizraji (1992), "Vector logics: The matrix-vector representation of logical calculus," _Fuzzy Sets and Systems_ 50(2), 179-185.**  
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/0165-0114(92)90216-Q  
The abstract states that binary operations such as conjunction, disjunction, implication, and Sheffer's connective are represented by matrices acting on Kronecker products of vectors.

**Eduardo Mizraji (1996), "The Operators of Vector Logic," _Mathematical Logic Quarterly_ 42(1), 27-40.**  
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1002/malq.19960420104

**William Bricken (internally dated March 1997), "Notes on Matrix Techniques for Logic."**  
https://wbricken.com/pdfs/01bm/01math/03math-supporting/math-tangential/04matrix-tech.pdf  
The current website establishes access to the note and the document itself carries the March 1997 date. It does **not** by itself establish when the note first became publicly available or peer-reviewed; that chronology should remain qualified.

### Semi-tensor-product and Boolean matrix calculus

**Daizhan Cheng, Hongsheng Qi, Zhiqiang Li, _Analysis and Control of Boolean Networks: A Semi-tensor Product Approach_.**  
Springer: https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-85729-097-7  
The book contains chapters on propositional logic, semi-tensor products, and matrix expression of logic.

**Daizhan Cheng, Yin Zhao, Xiangru Xu (2011), "Matrix Approach to Boolean Calculus."**  
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1109/CDC.2011.6160289

### Projective/spectral logic

Original arXiv posting: 21 Dec 2015: https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.06632  
Published in _Logica Universalis_ 14 (2020), 175-207. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/s11787-020-00252-3  
Key construction: logical operators as commuting projection operators, truth values as eigenvalues, interpretations as eigenvectors.

**Francois Dubois, Zeno Toffano (2016), "Eigenlogic: a Quantum View for Multiple-Valued and Fuzzy Systems."**  
https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.03509

**Francois Dubois, Zeno Toffano (2025), "Eigenlogic and Probabilistic Inference; when Bayes meets Born."**  
https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10045  
Relevant as a recent development of the projector/Born-rule line, not as historical prior art to the thesis.

### Modal quantum theory and contextuality

**Benjamin Schumacher, Michael D. Westmoreland (2010), "Modal quantum theory."**  
https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.2929  
Finite-field theory using possibility and necessity in place of quantitative probability.

**Samson Abramsky, Adam Brandenburger (2011), "The Sheaf-Theoretic Structure of Non-Locality and Contextuality."**  
https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.0264  
Contextuality/nonlocality are formulated as obstructions to global sections over measurement covers.

### Effect algebras and sequential measurement

**Stan Gudder, Richard Greechie (2002), "Sequential products on effect algebras," _Reports on Mathematical Physics_ 49(1), 87-111.**  
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/S0034-4877(02)80007-6

### General probabilistic theories

ArXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.07469  
Published in _Physics Reports_ 1033 (2023), 1-64. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physrep.2023.09.001  
The framework explicitly distinguishes states, effects, measurements, channels, and instruments.

### Quantum cognition and p-adic mental space

**Andrei Khrennikov (2003), "Quantum-like formalism for cognitive measurements," _Biosystems_ 70(3), 211-233.**  
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/S0303-2647(03)00041-8

The abstract explicitly describes Hilbert-space cognitive measurement, consciousness as a self-measuring quantum-like system, and p-adic hierarchical trees as a mathematical model of mental space. This is the strongest pre-2015 conceptual overlap found with the thesis's measurement/consciousness/p-adic program.

DOI: https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-psych-033020-123501

## 4. What can still plausibly be claimed as contribution

The evidence supports a contribution framed around **integration and precise separation of roles**, not first invention of projective logic.

A defensible current contribution would be:

- a canonical typed map from compact CM truth data to valuation-space sharp effects;
- a complete finite classification showing how compact-CM idempotence depends on the multiplication law;
- a proof that the natural diagonal measurement algebra is classical/commutative;
- an exact separation between observation refinement and selective outcome update, linked to the current ProLT formalism;
- a theorem showing the thesis's context-relative "purity" is cylinder extension;
- explicit counterexamples showing symmetry-stabilizer decrease is not equivalent to increased distinguishability;
- a clean boundary specifying what additional axioms are needed before modal/contextual/quantum measurement claims are meaningful.

This combination appears substantially more precise than the 2015 formulation even where its individual ingredients are classical or have prior art.

## 5. Priority cautions for a future manuscript

Do not claim:

- invention of matrix logic;
- first vector/matrix representation of Boolean connectives;
- first bra-ket representation of logic;
- first logical projectors or truth-eigenvalue observables;
- first quantum-like model of cognitive measurement;
- first p-adic mental-space model;
- contextuality from ambient-variable dependence alone.

A future paper should instead say exactly which theorem or typed bridge is proved and compare it directly with the constructions above.

# Symmetry Reduction and Logical Differentiation

## 1. Two symmetry notions must be separated

The 2015 thesis calls a binary CM symmetric when `A=A^T`. For a truth-table matrix this is exactly the condition

`Theta(x,y)=Theta(y,x)`,

so it is simply **commutativity under operand exchange**. Exhaustive enumeration gives 8 transpose-symmetric and 8 transpose-asymmetric binary connectives.

A broader natural frame-symmetry group is the order-eight group generated by:

- swapping `X` and `Y`;
- negating `X`;
- negating `Y`.

On the square of four valuations this is `D_4`. The audit therefore also computed each truth support's `D_4` stabilizer and orbit.

## 2. Restriction does not monotonically break symmetry

For a support state `S` and a true-outcome effect `E`, the canonical update is

`M_E(S)=S intersect E`.

Among all 16x16 binary state/effect pairs, restricting to nonempty proper updates produced:

- **30** stabilizer decreases;
- **8** stabilizer increases;
- **72** stabilizer-preserving updates.

Hence the proposed criterion

`|Stab(M_E(S))| < |Stab(S)|`

cannot define or characterize measurement-induced distinguishability.

### Counterexample: restriction can increase symmetry

`S = X_IMPLIES_Y` has three valuations and `|Stab_D4(S)|=2`.

Restrict by `E=XNOR`. The result is `XNOR`, which has two valuations but stabilizer size 4. The state has become more selective while also becoming more symmetric.

### Example: restriction can decrease symmetry

`S=XOR` has stabilizer size 4. Restrict by `X_AND_NOT_Y`; the singleton result has stabilizer size 2.

### Example: support can shrink with no stabilizer change

`S=X` restricted by AND becomes AND, reducing support size 2 to 1 while the `D_4` stabilizer remains 2.

## 3. Structural reason

If `M` is equivariant under a group `G`, then every symmetry of `x` remains a symmetry of `M(x)`:

`Stab_G(x) subseteq Stab_G(M(x))`.

Therefore a stabilizer decrease requires the observation context/effect itself to break part of the original symmetry, or requires changing the acting group. A fixed effect `E` is generally equivariant only under its own stabilizer subgroup.

This shows that "measurement breaks symmetry" is not an intrinsic theorem of measurement. It is a statement about the combined system **state + chosen effect/context**.

## 4. Better notions of differentiation

### Observational differentiation

Given an observation family `Phi`, use the signature partition

`v ~_Phi w <=> o_Phi(v)=o_Phi(w)`.

Adding `psi` strictly increases distinguishability iff it splits an existing signature block.

### Selective information gain

Given support `S`, a possible true outcome gives

`S' = S intersect E`.

Under a uniform prior the Hartley information gain is

`log2(|S|/|S'|)`.

This measures uncertainty reduction, not symmetry.

### Symmetry reduction

If symmetry itself matters, record stabilizers separately. A useful triplet is therefore

`(number of observation blocks, support uncertainty, symmetry stabilizer)`.

No single one of these should be treated as a proxy for the other two.

## 5. Complete differentiation example

The path

`TRUE -> XOR -> X_AND_NOT_Y`

uses only valid restrictions. Support size decreases `4 -> 2 -> 1`. Under operand swap, TRUE and XOR remain symmetric, whereas the final singleton is asymmetric. Thus differentiation begins before thesis-style symmetry breaking occurs.

## 6. Reproducibility

See:

- `SYMMETRY_TABLE.csv` for every binary truth support;
- `RESTRICTION_SYMMETRY_TRANSITIONS.csv` for all 256 restrictions;
- `verify_cm_measurement_independent.py` for independent enumeration.

# Quantum Status Audit

## Executive finding

The **core CM/LM calculus is not quantum mechanics and is not, by itself, a nonclassical measurement theory**. It is an exact Boolean/F2 operator representation with useful quantum-inspired notation. A canonical projector semantics exists on valuation space, but it is a commuting Boolean event algebra and is therefore classical. Genuinely modal/contextual behavior requires extra state/effect/context/tensor postulates of the sort stated separately in finite-field or chain-ring models.

## 1. Axiom-by-axiom comparison

| Feature | Core compact CM/LM | Canonical diagonal CM effects | Modal finite-field/chain-ring extension | Ordinary quantum theory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| State carrier | Boolean/formula states; one-hot valued selectors; truth tensors | subsets/support vectors on finite valuation space; optional classical distributions | nonzero/admissible vectors or module elements under an explicit contract | rays/density operators on complex Hilbert space |
| Scalars | Boolean algebra / `F_2` where declared | `R/C/F_2` can encode the same diagonal 0/1 effects | finite field or finite ring | `C` |
| Superposition | thesis OR-superposition; modern pointwise Boolean operator superposition | set union / vector support; no amplitude phase | linear combinations over finite scalar system can be genuine modal superposition after state axioms | complex linear superposition |
| Inner product | no Hilbert inner product in core | standard Euclidean inner product can be added for diagonal representation, but is not needed for Boolean semantics | usually effect-state pairing / contraction, model-dependent | complex inner product |
| Norm/positivity | absent | optional classical probability simplex | generally no real norm/probability in purely modal version | positive norm; positive density/effects |
| Born rule | absent | absent unless an external classical probability distribution is supplied | absent in possibility-only modal semantics | fundamental |
| Observable | compact CM is a truth-table operator, not generally spectral | `D_f` is a commuting sharp truth effect/projector | context families of declared effects | self-adjoint operator / POVM effects |
| Measurement update | not intrinsically defined in core | support restriction or classical conditioning | possibility branches under model-specific effects/instruments | instrument/Luders or general CP map |
| Sequential order effects | compact matrix products can be noncommutative but lack measurement semantics | none: all `D_f` commute | possible if the declared contexts/process semantics are nonclassical | possible for incompatible measurements |
| Tensor composition | truth tensors / declared flattenings | classical product valuation spaces | must specify balanced/literal tensor and admissibility | Hilbert tensor product |
| Interference | no amplitude interference in core | none | modal cancellation can occur depending on scalar arithmetic but has no Born probabilities | complex-amplitude interference |
| Contextuality | not implied by CMs | none for the full commuting event algebra | can be genuine support-level contextuality when measurement contexts/global-section obstruction are present | contextuality possible |

## 2. Bra-ket notation does not decide the issue

The current CM foundations manuscript explicitly defines one-hot Boolean states and uses bra-ket notation as compact row/map/column notation without assuming Hilbert-space physics. That is the correct stance.

The historical thesis went further rhetorically. Its `|X>` notation and matrix formulas are mathematically useful, but the notation alone establishes neither:

- complex amplitudes;
- normalization;
- phase;
- a Born probability rule;
- self-adjoint observable axioms;
- unitary dynamics;
- physical tensor composition;
- a measurement instrument.

## 3. The historical OR "superposition"

The thesis defines a logic wave as the OR of true and false possibilities and logical superposition as OR of logical states. This is cleanly interpreted as **support union**. It can be written as a 0/1 support vector, but it is not Hilbert superposition.

One could construct a modal vector-space theory over `F_2`, but doing so requires a new state/effect interpretation. The 2015 definitions do not by themselves supply that complete operational contract.

## 4. Compact-CM projectors do not form a quantum observable family

Under XOR-AND multiplication over `F_2`, 8 of the 16 compact CMs are idempotent. Only four are also symmetric: FALSE, AND, NOR, and XNOR. OR has no eigenvalue in `F_2`; XOR is involutory but does not have the truth values of the connective as its spectral data. Therefore the compact CM spectrum is an algebraic invariant, not a truth-observable spectrum.

The current CM manuscript correctly identifies a different representation:

`D_Theta=diag(Theta_11,Theta_10,Theta_01,Theta_00)`.

There the truth values are eigenvalues and valuation basis vectors are eigenvectors. This is a direct bridge to Eigenlogic-style logical observables.

## 5. Why the diagonal projector theory is classical

All `D_f` are diagonal in the same global valuation basis. Consequently

`D_fD_g=D_gD_f=D_(f and g)`.

The sharp effects form a Boolean algebra isomorphic to the power set of the finite valuation space. There is one global assignment space and no incompatibility among these effects. This is a classical event algebra written in projection-operator form.

It is therefore accurate to call it **projective logical measurement**, provided "projective" is understood algebraically. It would be misleading to present it as specifically quantum measurement.

## 6. Relation to effect algebras

The diagonal 0/1 effects are sharp effects. With complement and partial sum on disjoint events they form a finite Boolean effect algebra. Sequential product reduces to meet/intersection because all sharp effects commute.

This is exactly the classical corner of the broader effect-algebra/sequential-effect literature. Non-Boolean finite sequential effect algebras require additional structure; compact CM noncommutativity does not automatically provide it.

## 7. Relation to generalized probabilistic theories

A GPT specifies at least a convex state space, affine effects into `[0,1]`, measurements as compatible collections of effects, and transformations/instruments. The CM truth-effect algebra can be embedded into the ordinary classical simplex GPT on `Omega_n`:

- states = probability vectors on valuations;
- effects = indicator functions or general `[0,1]` functions;
- measurement probabilities = expectation of effects;
- posteriors = classical conditioning/instruments.

Nothing in the core CM calculus forces a nonclassical GPT state space.

## 8. Relation to modal quantum theory

Schumacher-Westmoreland-style modal quantum theory replaces quantitative probabilities by possibility/necessity over finite fields while retaining linear state/effect structure. The supplied chain-ring manuscript goes further to finite local/chain rings and explicitly declares:

- scalar ring;
- admissible state/resource class;
- local basis effects;
- nonzero contraction as possibility;
- complete measurement contexts;
- tensor and correction contracts for information tasks.

Those declarations are exactly what is missing from a bare CM truth-table calculus. If the attached chain-ring theorems survive their own independent review, they represent a serious genuinely modal extension of the broader research program, but they should remain a separate layer from the classical CM measurement formalism.

## 9. Relation to contextuality

Context dependence is not the same as contextuality.

- The thesis's fact that `X` is singleton-supported in one variable but not after adjoining an unconstrained `Y` is cylinder extension.
- ProLT observation families are context-dependent interfaces, but a family of commuting Boolean truth effects still has a global valuation model.
- Abramsky-Brandenburger contextuality requires an obstruction to a compatible global assignment across a measurement cover.

Thus "contextual" should be reserved for the latter kind of theorem when that measurement scenario is actually specified.

## 10. Relation to quantum cognition

Quantum cognition uses quantum probability as a mathematical model for empirical phenomena such as order effects, interference-like probability patterns, and context dependence; it need not claim physical quantum coherence in the brain. This is a more demanding standard than using quantum vocabulary.

A future CM-consciousness model would earn a nonclassical/quantum-cognitive interpretation only if it produces operationally testable deviations from the classical commuting model, for example:

- question-order effects that cannot be represented by one common Boolean event algebra;
- contextuality/global-section obstruction;
- probability interference requiring a non-Kolmogorov model;
- incompatible instruments with empirically distinct sequential predictions.

Until such evidence or axioms are supplied, the most defensible description is **a finite mathematical model of observation, refinement, and logical differentiation**.

## 11. Bottom line

- **Core CM/LM:** Boolean/F2 operator calculus; quantum-inspired notation, not quantum mechanics.
- **Diagonal CM truth effects:** rigorous projectors, but commuting/classical.
- **ProLT refinement/update:** rigorous theory of observational differentiation and conditioning.
- **Finite-field/chain-ring measurement contexts:** candidate genuinely modal/nonclassical extension, requiring separate theorem-level validation.
- **Consciousness application:** mathematically serious as an information/observation model; scientifically quantum only if additional operational axioms and empirical signatures justify that label.

# CM Measurement Audit

**Project:** Correspondence-Matrix Measurement as a Model of Logical Differentiation  
**Audit date:** 28 September 2026  
**Status:** independent reconstruction, finite verification, formal repair, and bounded literature/priority audit.

## Executive conclusion

There **is** a clean and rigorous measurement theory naturally associated with Correspondence Matrices (CMs), but it is not the thesis's unrestricted rule that every outer product `|alpha><beta|` is a projector, and it is not obtained by treating every compact 2x2 CM as a quantum observable.

The mathematically clean core is this:

1. A Boolean formula/operator `Theta` determines a truth region `E_Theta` in the finite valuation space `Omega_n={0,1}^n`.
2. The same truth data determines a diagonal sharp effect/projector

   `D_Theta = diag(1[v models Theta])`

   on the free module/vector space with valuation basis `|v>`.
3. A **selective measurement outcome** is support restriction/conditioning:

   `M_Theta(S) = S intersect E_Theta`, equivalently `s -> D_Theta s` for a support vector.
4. A **measurement question** distinguishes worlds by its two outcomes. A family of questions `Phi` determines an observation signature and hence an observational partition/topology. Adding an observation is **refinement**; learning an outcome is **update/restriction**. These are different operations.

This repaired formalism preserves the strongest mathematical intuition of the 2015 thesis: observation can convert an undifferentiated possibility set into a progressively differentiated one. It also makes precise where the quantum analogy stops. In the canonical diagonal representation all Boolean effects commute, sequential measurement is simply intersection, and there is no Born rule, amplitude interference, or specifically quantum collapse. The framework becomes genuinely modal/contextual only after adding further state/effect/context structure, such as the separately specified finite-field/chain-ring measurement scenarios; that extra structure is not entailed by the compact CMs themselves.

The most useful conceptual correction is therefore:

> **Unfolding exposes distinctions; measurement selects/conditions relative to distinctions.**

The thesis often mixes these two roles. Separating them produces a substantially cleaner theory of logical differentiation.

---

## 1. Source basis and audit method

The audit used the following supplied sources rather than assuming the historical thesis or current CM work to be correct:

- **2015 thesis:** *On the Ultrametric Unconscious, Quantum Consciousness, and Mental Spaces*, especially pp. 34-48 (CMs, bra-kets, projection, logic waves, purity), pp. 56-63 (unfolding/distinguishing), and pp. 67-72 (collapse, symmetry/asymmetry, measurement analogies).
- **Current CM/LM foundations manuscript:** `CM_LM_Boolean_Operator_Calculus_Revised.tex`, especially its explicit separation of XOR-AND matrix product, pointwise Boolean superposition, and Boolean-function superposition; its frame interpretation of literal CM rotation; and its spectral-boundary section.
- **Current ProLT observation manuscript:** `ProLT_Observation_Topologies_Submission_v0.9_FINAL.tex`, especially the observation-signature formalism and the distinction between observation refinement and premise update.
- **Current modal/chain-ring manuscript:** `Chain Ring.tex`, used only to identify what *additional* contracts are required for a genuinely modal support-level measurement theory. Its global classification theorems are not prerequisites for the core CM conclusions here.
- **Binary order-thinning manuscript:** `binary_order_thinning_finite_posets_reviewed_v3.tex`, used as a boundary on when an added observation can be modeled as same-carrier order thinning and when refinement instead changes the Kolmogorov quotient itself.

The 16 binary CMs were independently regenerated from their four truth values in true-first order `(11,10,01,00)`. Idempotence, sequential products, commutators, state actions, diagonal effects, symmetry stabilizers, and three-variable cylinder embeddings were then exhaustively enumerated. A second implementation, `verify_cm_measurement_independent.py`, does not import the main computation and passed **553 assertions**.

---

## 2. Reconstruction of the thesis measurement system

### 2.1 Classification of the historical constructions

| Thesis construction | What it actually is | Audit class | Status after reconstruction |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 binary Correspondence Matrices | A bijective 2x2 arrangement of the four truth values of a binary Boolean function | ordinary Boolean algebra + finite matrix representation | **Sound after typing the multiplication law.** The representation itself is exact, not quantum-specific. |
| `|X>=[X,not X]^T`, `<X|=[X,not X]` | Formula/Boolean-valued row and column notation; after valuation, one-hot vectors | finite linear/semilinear algebra + quantum-inspired notation | **Sound as notation.** It is not a Hilbert-space ket unless extra scalar, inner-product, and state axioms are supplied. |
| Bra-CM-ket evaluation | One-hot selection of a truth-table entry in the numeric CM; formula pairing in the modern LM layer | Boolean/F2 operator calculus | **Sound.** Modern CM work correctly treats it as matrix-element semantics, not spectral measurement. |
| "Logical superposition" by OR | Union of alternative supports/possibilities | ordinary Boolean algebra + quantum-inspired terminology | **Mathematically usable as support union, but not Hilbert superposition.** |
| "Logic wave" = true possibility OR false possibility | A two-alternative support description | Boolean support semantics + quantum-inspired terminology | **Usable after reinterpretation.** It has no amplitudes, phase, norm, or Born probabilities. |
| `[P]=|alpha><beta|` called a projection operator | General rank-one outer product | finite linear algebra + quantum-inspired notation | **Too broad / incorrect as stated.** A general outer product is not idempotent. |
| Projective measurement = `[P]|psi>` | Action of a purported projector | underdefined | **Repair required.** Restrict `P` to an actual idempotent effect/projector and specify outcome semantics. |
| `|1><1|` and `|0><0|` as true/false measurement matrices | Coordinate projectors | finite linear algebra | **Sound special cases.** These are genuine idempotents. |
| "Pure logic state" = exactly one satisfying valuation | Singleton truth support/minterm relative to the declared ambient variables | ordinary Boolean semantics | **Sound as a definition, but not quantum purity.** It is context-relative. |
| Historical "logical distinguishability" definitions using truth of OR/AND | Satisfiability conditions, not a robust equivalence/metric of distinguishability | ordinary Boolean algebra but conceptually underdefined | **Replace.** Use observation signatures/equivalence classes from ProLT. |
| Symmetric CM = `A=A^T` | Invariance under swapping the two operands; exactly commutativity of the binary Boolean function | finite matrix/group action | **Sound but narrow.** It is not a general physical symmetry criterion. |
| Quarter-turn matrix rotation | Signed reindexing of the truth-table frame | finite group action | **Sound in modern form.** `rot(Theta)(x,y)=Theta(not y,x)`; not physical phase by itself. |
| Collapse | Usually a change from a broad Boolean support to a selected sub-support, but sometimes a change to a disjoint formula | quantum-inspired terminology; partly underdefined | **Split into restriction versus unfolding.** Only the former is measurement/conditioning. |
| Distinguishing/unfolding operator `partial` | A custom Boolean face-decomposition transform that negates one omitted coordinate | Boolean/simplicial-inspired construction | **Not a standard simplicial boundary and not measurement in general.** It can create alternatives outside the original truth support. |
| Chain-ring/modal support measurement (later work) | Nonzero-contraction possibility semantics with context families of effects | module/finite-ring mathematics; genuinely modal when the full contract is used | **A separate extension.** It must not be retroactively identified with the thesis's compact-CM measurement. |

### 2.2 The most important historical correction: an outer product is not automatically a projector

The thesis defines a projection operator by

`P = |alpha><beta|`.

In ordinary rank-one operator algebra,

`P^2 = |alpha><beta|alpha><beta| = <beta|alpha> P`.

Therefore `P` is idempotent only when the overlap scalar satisfies `<beta|alpha>=1` (or in a degenerate zero case). A concrete counterexample from the thesis's own Boolean basis is

`|1><0| = [[0,1],[0,0]]`,

which is nonzero but squares to zero under both ordinary matrix multiplication and XOR-AND multiplication over `F_2`. The independent verifier checks this explicitly. Thus the historical definition must be replaced by either `|alpha><alpha|` for normalized orthogonal basis states, or, more generally, by an operator explicitly required to satisfy `P^2=P` (and, for an ordinary orthogonal projector, `P=P*`).

### 2.3 What survives from the historical true/false measurements

The thesis's matrices

`|1><1| = [[1,0],[0,0]]` and `|0><0| = [[0,0],[0,1]]`

are genuine coordinate projections. In the compact CM atlas they coincide as arrays with AND and NOR respectively. This is a valid algebraic observation, but the *type* matters: the same 2x2 array can be read as a binary truth table or as a unary coordinate endomorphism. The modern theory should state which role is active instead of identifying them silently.

---

## 3. Rebuilding measurement in a modern CM framework

### 3.1 Valuation-space state model

For `n` propositional variables let

`Omega_n = {0,1}^n`.

A Boolean formula `f` determines its truth region

`E_f = {v in Omega_n : v models f}`.

A coarse logical state can be represented as a possibility support `S subseteq Omega_n`. If probabilities are desired, replace `S` by a distribution `p` on `Omega_n`; no probability is assumed by the core theory.

### 3.2 Canonical CM-associated truth effect

Let `V_n` be the free module/vector space with basis `{|v> : v in Omega_n}`. Define

`D_f = sum_{v in E_f} |v><v|`.

For a binary CM in true-first order,

`[Theta] = [[Theta_11,Theta_10],[Theta_01,Theta_00]]`,

this is simply

`D_Theta = diag(Theta_11,Theta_10,Theta_01,Theta_00)`.

This construction is canonical once the valuation order is fixed. It is also exactly the bridge isolated in the current CM manuscript's spectral-boundary section. It should not be confused with the compact 2x2 CM itself.

Every `D_f` satisfies

- `D_f^2=D_f`;
- over ordinary real/complex scalars, `D_f` is self-adjoint and hence an orthogonal projector;
- `im(D_f)=span{|v>:v in E_f}`;
- `ker(D_f)=span{|v>:v notin E_f}`;
- `rank(D_f)=|E_f|`;
- `D_f D_g = D_g D_f = D_{f and g}`.

For the 16 binary connectives, **all 16** therefore become sharp commuting projectors in the four-dimensional interpretation space.

### 3.3 Selective and nonselective measurement

The clean selective true-outcome update is

`M_f(S)=S intersect E_f`.

The false outcome is

`M_not_f(S)=S intersect (Omega_n \ E_f)`.

Equivalently, a support indicator vector `s` updates to `D_f s`. The complete yes/no measurement is the pair of branches `{D_f,D_not_f}`. If the outcome is ignored, the two classical support branches reunite to the original support. If a prior probability `p` is explicitly added, the selective update is ordinary conditioning

`p(v | f) = p(v) 1[v in E_f] / p(E_f)`.

Thus the core CM-associated measurement has a precise interpretation, but it is a **classical sharp event measurement**.

### 3.4 Why this is the cleanest notion of "distinguishing"

Measurement has two logically different components:

- **a question/effect**, which can separate states into outcome classes;
- **an outcome update**, which removes states incompatible with the recorded outcome.

The current ProLT framework supplies the right language for the first component. For an observation family `Phi=(phi_1,...,phi_m)`, define

`o_Phi(v)=(1[v models phi_1],...,1[v models phi_m])`.

Two valuations are observationally indistinguishable exactly when they have the same signature. Adding a new observation `psi` strictly increases distinguishability on a carrier `S` precisely when there are `v,w in S` such that

`o_Phi(v)=o_Phi(w)` but `psi(v) != psi(w)`.

This is stronger and cleaner than the thesis's satisfiability-based definitions of distinguishability.

---

## 4. Exhaustive projector classification of the 16 compact CMs

The same 16 binary arrays behave differently under different multiplication laws. The audit therefore kept four algebras separate.

| Multiplication law on compact 2x2 CMs | Idempotent CMs | Count | Ordered idempotent pairs | Commuting pairs | Noncommuting pairs | Products still idempotent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| XOR-AND matrix product over `F_2` | FALSE, AND, NOR, X, Y, XNOR, NOT_Y, NOT_X | 8 | 64 | 40 | 24 | 58 |
| OR-AND Boolean-semiring matrix product | previous 8 + X_IMPLIES_Y, Y_IMPLIES_X, TRUE | 11 | 121 | 65 | 56 | 115 |
| ordinary integer matrix product | same 8 as `F_2` | 8 | 64 | 36 | 28 | 54 |
| cyclic convolution over `F_2` on the four rotation coordinates | FALSE, AND | 2 | 4 | 4 | 0 | 4 |

The full row-by-row data, state actions, finite images/kernels, and ranks are in `PROJECTOR_CLASSIFICATION.csv`; all ordered products are in `SEQUENTIAL_MEASUREMENTS.csv`.

Two conclusions matter for measurement theory.

First, **compact-CM idempotence is representation- and multiplication-dependent**. One cannot call a 2x2 truth-table array a projector without saying which multiplication is being used.

Second, even when compact idempotents fail to commute, this alone does **not** create quantum measurement. For example, some products of compact idempotents cease to be idempotent, and ordinary integer products can even leave the 0/1 matrix set. No Born probabilities, positive effects, state-update axiom, or operational measurement context follows from this noncommutativity.

The cyclic-convolution result is especially sharp. The separate coefficient algebra is `F_2[C_4] ~= F_2[u]/(u^4)`, a local ring, so it has only the trivial idempotents 0 and 1. In the chosen coefficient basis these are FALSE and AND. Therefore the phase/convolution algebra does **not** supply a rich internal projector lattice for the 16 CMs.

By contrast, the valuation-space diagonal representation has 16/16 projectors, all commuting. It is therefore the right representation if the goal is logical event measurement.

---

## 5. Sequential measurements and compatibility

For the canonical diagonal effects,

`D_f D_g = D_{f and g} = D_g D_f`.

Hence every pair is compatible in the commutation sense and a sequence of recorded true outcomes is simply accumulated Boolean restriction:

`S -> S intersect E_f -> S intersect E_f intersect E_g`.

Order cannot matter in this core theory. This is the decisive reason the repaired CM measurement is classical rather than quantum-like in the operational sense.

A useful distinction is:

- **compact-CM product noncommutativity** = an algebraic property of one representation;
- **measurement incompatibility/order effect** = an operational property of effects/instruments acting on states.

The first does not imply the second.

---

## 6. Symmetry breaking: the proposed stabilizer criterion fails as a general test

The thesis uses transpose symmetry, which for a binary CM is exactly invariance under exchanging the two operands. Exhaustive enumeration confirms that 8 of the 16 binary connectives are transpose-symmetric and 8 are not.

To test a broader symmetry criterion, the audit used the natural signed-input square group `D_4`, generated by swapping `X,Y` and independently negating the two coordinates. For a truth support `S`, let `Stab(S)` be its stabilizer under this group.

The proposed condition

`|Stab(M(S))| < |Stab(S)|`

is **not** a reliable definition of increased distinguishability. Among nonempty strict restrictions `S -> S intersect E`, exhaustive enumeration found:

- 30 cases in which the stabilizer decreased;
- 8 cases in which it **increased**;
- 72 cases in which it stayed the same.

For example,

`X_IMPLIES_Y -> XNOR`

under restriction by XNOR shrinks the support from 3 valuations to 2 while the `D_4` stabilizer grows from 2 to 4. The selected subset is *more symmetric* even though uncertainty has decreased. Conversely,

`XOR -> X_AND_NOT_Y`

shrinks support from 2 valuations to 1 and the stabilizer decreases from 4 to 2.

There is a conceptual reason. If a map `M` were fully `G`-equivariant, then `Stab_G(x) subseteq Stab_G(M(x))`; an equivariant map cannot reduce the stabilizer. Symmetry reduction occurs because a chosen effect/context itself breaks part of the original group action. Stabilizer size therefore measures symmetry, not distinguishability.

The exact criterion for **new distinguishability** is instead partition refinement: a new observation must split at least one existing observation-signature fiber.

See `SYMMETRY_REDUCTION.md`, `SYMMETRY_TABLE.csv`, and `RESTRICTION_SYMMETRY_TRANSITIONS.csv`.

---

## 7. Context dependence and the thesis's "pure" states

The thesis defines a pure logic state as one having exactly one satisfying truth assignment. This is a well-defined combinatorial notion, but it depends on the ambient variable universe.

Let a formula `f` depend on `n` variables and embed it canonically into `n+m` variables by ignoring the new variables. Its truth region becomes the cylinder

`E_f x {0,1}^m`.

Therefore

`|E_f^(n+m)| = 2^m |E_f^(n)|`.

Consequently, any satisfiable singleton support ceases to be singleton as soon as at least one unconstrained variable is adjoined. The audit reproduced the thesis's phenomenon explicitly:

- `X` has support size 1 in one variable and size 4 in a three-variable universe;
- `X and not Y` has support size 1 in two variables and size 2 in three variables;
- `X XOR Y` has support size 2 in two variables and size 4 in three variables.

This is ordinary **cylinder-set extension**, not contextuality in the sheaf/global-section sense. A deeper contextual theory requires incompatible measurement contexts or the failure of a global assignment. The separate modal chain-ring program supplies that kind of additional structure; the cylinder phenomenon alone does not.

The diagonal projector rank tracks this exactly: under an `m`-variable cylinder extension, `rank(D_f)` is multiplied by `2^m`. Compact 2x2/F2 rank should not be used as a purity measure because it is a different invariant of a different representation.

---

## 8. Measurement versus unfolding

The thesis's distinguishing operator `partial` is best understood as an **unfolding/refinement transform**, not generally as measurement.

The decisive finite example is the thesis's own two-variable intuition:

`partial(X and Y) = X XOR Y`.

As truth supports,

- `E_(X and Y) = {11}`;
- `E_(X XOR Y) = {10,01}`.

These are disjoint. Therefore `X and Y -> X XOR Y` cannot be a selective conditioning/restriction of the original state. It creates/exposes alternatives rather than selecting a surviving alternative.

This suggests a clean typed split:

- `U` (**unfolding/refinement**) enlarges the observation description or expands a coarse representation so that previously hidden alternatives become separately expressible;
- `M` (**measurement/update**) conditions the current possibility state on a recorded outcome.

The current ProLT manuscript already has the exact analogue: enlarging the observation family is refinement on a fixed carrier, whereas learning a premise restricts the carrier. If `U` merely adds observations on the same carrier and the measurement effect `E` is defined independently of that refinement, the natural restriction/refinement square commutes. If unfolding changes the carrier, introduces latent coordinates, or makes the measurement effect definable only after expansion, `MU` and `UM` need not agree and may not even have the same type.

This separation is one of the strongest recoveries from the thesis. It preserves both intuitions without forcing one operator to do incompatible jobs.

---

## 9. A complete finite path from a coarse state to a differentiated state

Take `Omega_2={11,10,01,00}` and begin with the totally coarse possibility state

`S_0 = TRUE = {11,10,01,00}`.

A valid two-stage selective measurement path is

`TRUE --(XOR=true)--> XOR={10,01} --(X=true)--> X_AND_NOT_Y={10}`.

In diagonal form,

`D_XOR = diag(0,1,1,0)`,

and the second true outcome applies `D_X=diag(1,1,0,0)`, leaving

`D_X D_XOR = diag(0,1,0,0) = D_(X_AND_NOT_Y)`.

The possibility count falls `4 -> 2 -> 1`. Under a uniform prior, the two recorded outcomes yield 1 bit and then 1 further bit of Hartley/Shannon information. The last state is a singleton minterm and therefore maximally differentiated with respect to the two declared Boolean coordinates.

This example also separates **differentiation** from **symmetry breaking**. TRUE and XOR are both invariant under operand swap; the first restriction decreases uncertainty without breaking that symmetry. The second branch to `X_AND_NOT_Y` breaks operand-swap symmetry. Thus the two notions should not be identified.

---

## 10. Quantum-status audit in one paragraph

The core CM/LM calculus is Boolean/F2 mathematics with one-hot selection, truth tensors, signed frame actions, and formula-valued operator structure. Its bra-ket notation is representational; its OR-based "superposition" is support union; and its native compact-CM semantics supplies neither Born probabilities nor state collapse. The canonical diagonal truth effects are projectors, but they all commute and therefore form a classical Boolean sharp-effect algebra. A generalized probabilistic theory would additionally require a convex state space and probabilistic effects/instruments. A genuinely modal theory can be built by adding a finite-field/ring module, admissible states/effects, tensor composition, measurement contexts, and a nonzero-contraction possibility rule; that is an enrichment, not a hidden property of the 2x2 CMs. See `QUANTUM_STATUS_AUDIT.md` for the full axiom-by-axiom comparison.

---

## 11. Literature and priority result

A 2026-current literature search does **not** support priority for the broad ideas "logic by matrices," "logical bra-matrix-ket evaluation," or "logical propositions as projectors." Strong antecedents include Stern's *Matrix Logic* (1988), Mizraji's vector logic (1992/1996), Bricken's internally dated 1997 matrix-logic notes, semi-tensor-product Boolean logic, Cheng-Zhao-Xu's Boolean matrix calculus (2011), and Eigenlogic's explicit treatment of logical propositions as commuting projectors with truth values as eigenvalues (2015/2016 preprints; 2020 publication). Quantum-like cognitive measurement on p-adic mental spaces also predates the thesis in Khrennikov's 2001 preprint / 2003 paper.

The modern CM/LM manuscript already draws the correct priority boundary: the strongest defensible contribution lies in its **typed formula-valued LM architecture, frame coherence, pairing, and integration**, not in matrix logic or physical measurement firstness. The measurement formalism developed in this audit should likewise be presented as a rigorous integration/repair of CM truth operators with standard finite event/projector semantics and the newer ProLT distinction between observation refinement and update.

See `LITERATURE_PRIORITY_MAP.md` for construction-level comparisons and URLs/DOIs.

---

## 12. Proposed theorem program

The clean paper-sized mathematical development is summarized in `THEOREM_SEQUENCE.md`. The central sequence is:

1. CM/event/diagonal-projector equivalence on finite valuation space.
2. Exact image/kernel/rank and selective-measurement theorem.
3. Sequential-measurement/intersection theorem and commutativity/classicality corollary.
4. Complete 16-CM compact idempotent classification under each multiplication law.
5. Failure of stabilizer monotonicity under restriction.
6. Exact observation-refinement criterion for increased distinguishability.
7. Cylinder-extension theorem for context-relative purity.
8. Refinement/update commutative square.
9. Classicality boundary for the core CM measurement algebra.
10. Optional modal-extension theorem schema stating exactly which additional contracts are required before contextual measurement claims are meaningful.

---

## 13. Answers to the five required questions

### 1. What is the cleanest CM notion of measurement?

A CM represents a Boolean event/effect; lift its truth vector to the valuation-space diagonal projector `D_Theta`. A recorded outcome acts by `S -> S intersect E_Theta` (or `s -> D_Theta s`). The measurement question itself is represented by the two complementary effects. This is mathematically exact, typed, and compatible with the modern CM framework.

### 2. Does it give anything beyond ordinary Boolean restriction?

At the **core measurement level, no**: the canonical sharp CM measurement is ordinary finite Boolean event restriction/conditioning written in operator form. The genuinely useful extra structure is organizational: CM/LM typing, frame actions, tensorization, and the ProLT observation architecture make it possible to distinguish *what can be observed* from *which possibilities survive*. Nonclassical behavior requires extra modal/probabilistic/contextual postulates not present in the compact CM calculus.

### 3. When does it increase distinguishability?

Adding an observation `psi` increases distinguishability exactly when it splits an existing observation-signature class: there exist `v,w` with the same old signature but different `psi` values. A recorded outcome may reduce uncertainty whenever it is a proper nonempty restriction, but that is not the same as increasing pairwise distinguishability among survivors. Stabilizer decrease is neither necessary nor the right definition.

### 4. How does it differ from unfolding?

Unfolding/refinement exposes or creates a finer description of alternatives; measurement/conditioning selects the alternatives compatible with an outcome. The thesis's `AND -> XOR` example proves they cannot be identified because XOR is disjoint from the AND truth support. Under fixed-carrier observation refinement, unfolding and measurement satisfy a natural commuting restriction square; under carrier-expanding unfolding they need not commute.

### 5. Is there a serious mathematical route from this theory to the thesis's intended notion of conscious differentiation?

**Yes as a rigorous mathematical model of logical/observational differentiation, not yet as a theory of phenomenal consciousness.** A defensible route is to model an informational state by `(S,Phi)`: `S` is the current possibility support and `Phi` the currently available observation family. Differentiation has two independent monotone directions: refine `Phi` to split observational equivalence classes, and condition `S` on recorded outcomes to reduce uncertainty. This gives exact finite invariants, commuting diagrams, information measures, and testable order/context extensions. To make a scientific claim about consciousness, the model would still need an operational mapping from cognitive/neural experiments to states, observations, and updates, plus empirical predictions that distinguish it from ordinary classical conditioning. If noncommutative/quantum-cognitive behavior is claimed, order effects, contextuality, or probability-interference data would have to justify the extra structure rather than the words "superposition" or "collapse" doing so by analogy.

---

## Reproducibility files

- `cm_measurement_compute.py` — exhaustive primary enumeration.
- `verify_cm_measurement_independent.py` — separate implementation and cross-check.
- `verification_report.json` — 553-predicate PASS record.
- `PROJECTOR_CLASSIFICATION.csv` — all 16 compact CMs under four multiplication laws.
- `DIAGONAL_EFFECT_PROJECTORS.csv` — all 16 canonical valuation-space projectors.
- `SEQUENTIAL_MEASUREMENTS.csv` — compact algebraic sequences plus all 256 diagonal-effect sequences.
- `SYMMETRY_TABLE.csv`, `RESTRICTION_SYMMETRY_TRANSITIONS.csv` — symmetry audit.
- `THREE_VARIABLE_EMBEDDING.csv` — explicit context/cylinder examples.

This directory contains the deliverables for **Correspondence-Matrix Measurement as a Model of Logical Differentiation**.

- `CM_MEASUREMENT_AUDIT.md` — full audit, reconstruction, corrections, computations, and final answers.

The cleanest CM measurement is not "any outer product" and not the spectrum of every compact 2x2 CM. A Boolean CM defines a truth event, which canonically defines a **diagonal sharp effect on valuation space**. Selective measurement is event restriction/conditioning. **Observation refinement** is the separate operation that increases distinguishability. The core effect algebra is commuting/classical; genuinely modal or contextual measurement requires additional state/effect/context axioms.

# Proposed Theorem Sequence for a CM Measurement Paper

A short, coherent paper can be built without making claims about physical consciousness or quantum mechanics. The natural title would be something like **"Boolean Observation and Measurement from Correspondence Matrices"** or **"Correspondence-Matrix Effects, Observation Refinement, and Logical Differentiation."**

## T1. CM-event-projector equivalence

Let `Omega_2={11,10,01,00}`. The following are canonically bijective once the true-first frame is fixed:

1. binary Boolean functions `Theta`;
2. compact CMs `[Theta] in {0,1}^{2x2}`;
3. subsets `E_Theta subseteq Omega_2`;
4. diagonal 0/1 projectors `D_Theta` on `K^{Omega_2}`.

The bijection preserves Boolean complement and meet at the event/projector level.

**Purpose:** establishes the exact measurement bridge without identifying the compact CM with the projector.

## T2. Sharp selective measurement theorem

For support states `S subseteq Omega_n`, define `M_f(S)=S intersect E_f`. Then `M_f` is idempotent. In valuation-space form `D_f` has

`im D_f = span(E_f)`, `ker D_f=span(E_f^c)`, and `rank D_f=|E_f|`.

**Purpose:** gives the rigorous replacement for the thesis's projection/measurement definition.

## T3. Sequential-measurement theorem

For Boolean effects `f,g`,

`D_fD_g=D_gD_f=D_(f and g)`

and

`M_g M_f = M_f M_g = M_(f and g)`.

Corollary: the canonical CM sharp-effect theory has no intrinsic order effects and is a classical Boolean measurement algebra.

## T4. Complete compact-CM idempotent classification

Among the 16 compact binary CMs:

- XOR-AND over `F_2`: exactly 8 idempotents;
- OR-AND Boolean-semiring product: exactly 11;
- ordinary integer/real matrix product: exactly 8;
- cyclic `F_2` convolution on quarter-turn coordinates: exactly 2.

Give the explicit lists and characterize the four compact `F_2` idempotents that are also symmetric.

**Purpose:** closes the natural finite classification while emphasizing type dependence.

## T5. Outer-product projector criterion

For rank-one `P=|alpha><beta|` in any scalar setting where the contraction is defined,

`P^2=<beta|alpha>P`.

Hence a nonzero `P` is idempotent iff `<beta|alpha>=1`. In particular `|1><0|` is nilpotent rather than projective.

**Purpose:** repairs the central historical definition transparently.

## T6. Stabilizer non-monotonicity under logical restriction

Under the signed-input `D_4` action on binary truth supports, strict nonempty restriction `S -> S intersect E` does not monotonically change stabilizer size. Exhibit both an increase and a decrease; optionally state the full finite count `8/30/72` for increase/decrease/same.

Add the general lemma: if `M` is `G`-equivariant then `Stab_G(x) subseteq Stab_G(M(x))`.

**Purpose:** proves that symmetry breaking and distinguishability are distinct notions.

## T7. Observation-refinement criterion

For an observation family `Phi` and new observation `psi`, refinement is strict on a carrier `S` iff `psi` is nonconstant on at least one `Phi`-signature class in `S`.

**Purpose:** supplies the exact notion of increased distinguishability.

## T8. Cylinder-context theorem

If a formula `f` is embedded from `n` variables into `n+m` by ignoring the new variables, then

`E_iota(f)=E_f x {0,1}^m`,

so `|E_iota(f)|=2^m|E_f|` and `rank D_iota(f)=2^m rank D_f`.

Corollary: singleton-support "purity" is not preserved by adjoining an unconstrained variable.

**Purpose:** resolves the thesis's context-dependence observation as ordinary cylinder extension.

## T9. Refinement-update commutative square

At fixed carrier, adding an observation and then restricting to an independently defined event gives the same restricted observation system as restricting first and then adding the restricted observation.

**Purpose:** gives the precise relationship between unfolding/refinement `U` and measurement/update `M` and identifies the hypotheses under which `MU=UM`.

## T10. Classicality boundary

The canonical CM truth effects form a commuting Boolean algebra of sharp projectors. Consequently no sheaf-theoretic contextuality or noncommutative measurement order effect can arise from this full effect algebra alone.

**Purpose:** prevents overclaiming and cleanly motivates a separate modal extension.

## T11. Optional modal-extension schema

State as a *schema*, not as a consequence of T1-T10: a nonclassical extension must specify

- scalar semiring/ring/field;
- admissible states;
- effects and measurement contexts;
- composite-system tensor product;
- possibility/probability rule;
- post-measurement/process semantics.

Only after these are fixed should contextuality, interference, teleportation, or noncommuting measurement theorems be formulated.

**Purpose:** creates a principled bridge to the separate finite-field/chain-ring program without contaminating the core Boolean measurement results.

## Suggested paper narrative

Start from the historical projector mistake, repair it by the valuation-space diagonal effect, prove the classical measurement algebra, then use ProLT to show that **distinguishing** is properly a refinement property rather than a collapse property. The compact-CM idempotent classification and stabilizer counterexamples make strong finite sections. End with the exact boundary between classical CM observation and genuinely modal contextual extensions.

# Measurement Formalism for Correspondence Matrices

## 1. Design goal

The goal is to give a mathematically typed meaning to "observation" and "measurement" that preserves the useful truth-operator structure of Correspondence Matrices without importing Hilbert-space physics by terminology alone.

The formalism separates four objects:

1. **worlds/valuations** — what may be the case;
2. **effects/observations** — yes/no predicates on those worlds;
3. **observation interfaces** — which predicates are available for distinguishing worlds;
4. **outcome updates** — which worlds remain possible after an outcome is recorded.

This distinction is the main repair of the 2015 system.

---

## 2. Valuation space, events, and CM truth data

Let `P={X_1,...,X_n}` and

`Omega_P={0,1}^P`.

For a formula `f`, define

`E_f = {v in Omega_P : v models f}`

and its characteristic function

`chi_f(v)=1[v in E_f]`.

For a binary connective `Theta`, the compact CM is

`[Theta]=[[Theta_11,Theta_10],[Theta_01,Theta_00]]`,

where the four entries are exactly `chi_Theta(11),chi_Theta(10),chi_Theta(01),chi_Theta(00)`.

Thus there are three equivalent *data* presentations:

- truth table / truth region `E_Theta`;
- four-bit truth vector `(Theta_11,Theta_10,Theta_01,Theta_00)`;
- compact 2x2 CM `[Theta]`.

They are equivalent as encodings of a binary Boolean function. Their available algebraic operations are not automatically the same.

---

## 3. Canonical truth-effect projector

Let `K` be `R`, `C`, or `F_2` as appropriate and let

`V_P = K^{Omega_P}`

with valuation basis `{|v>}`. Define

`D_f := sum_{v in E_f} |v><v|`.

For two variables in true-first order,

`D_Theta = diag(Theta_11,Theta_10,Theta_01,Theta_00)`.

### Proposition 3.1 — sharp-effect properties

For every Boolean formula `f`:

`D_f^2=D_f`.

Moreover:

- `im D_f = span{|v>:v in E_f}`;
- `ker D_f = span{|v>:v notin E_f}`;
- `rank D_f = |E_f|`;
- over `R` or `C`, `D_f=D_f^*`, so it is an orthogonal projector;
- `D_f D_g = D_{f and g} = D_g D_f`.

**Proof.** Each diagonal entry is 0 or 1, so its square equals itself. Products multiply characteristic functions pointwise. Image, kernel, and rank follow directly from the selected valuation basis coordinates.

This is the canonical projector representation associated with CM truth data. It is distinct from the compact 2x2 CM.

---

## 4. State types

Three state levels should be kept separate.

### 4.1 Possibility support

A state is `S subseteq Omega_P`. This is the minimal, probability-free model.

A Boolean vector `s in {0,1}^{Omega_P}` can encode it by `s_v=1[v in S]`.

### 4.2 Probability state

A probability state is a distribution `p:Omega_P->[0,1]` with total mass 1. This is an optional classical enrichment.

### 4.3 Modal/module state

A modal theory may instead use a nonzero vector/module element together with an explicitly stated effect pairing and possibility rule, e.g. "outcome possible iff contraction is nonzero." This is **not** supplied automatically by the compact CM representation; scalar ring, admissibility, composition, and measurement contexts must be separately declared.

---

## 5. Selective measurement and conditioning

For the true outcome of `f`, define

`M_f(S)=S intersect E_f`.

For the false outcome,

`M_not_f(S)=S intersect E_not_f`.

In support-vector form,

`s -> D_f s`.

For a probability distribution and `p(E_f)>0`,

`p_f(v) = p(v) chi_f(v) / sum_w p(w) chi_f(w)`.

### Proposition 5.1 — repeated measurement

`M_f(M_f(S))=M_f(S)`.

This is ordinary idempotence of set intersection and is the support-level counterpart of `D_f^2=D_f`.

### Proposition 5.2 — sequential sharp measurement

`M_g(M_f(S))=S intersect E_f intersect E_g=M_f(M_g(S))`.

Hence the core sharp CM effects exhibit no order effect.

---

## 6. Complete measurements versus selected branches

The complete yes/no measurement associated with `f` is the pair

`{E_f,E_not_f}`

or equivalently `{D_f,D_not_f}`.

It partitions any support `S` into

`S_f=S intersect E_f`,  `S_not_f=S intersect E_not_f`.

If both branches are retained together with their labels, no valuation has been lost. A *selective* branch discards the incompatible part. If the outcome label is ignored and the support branches are reunited, one recovers `S`.

This distinction prevents "measurement" from being confused with unconditional destruction.

---

## 7. Observation families and distinguishability

Let

`Phi=(phi_1,...,phi_m)`.

Define the observation signature

`o_Phi(v)=(chi_phi1(v),...,chi_phim(v))`.

Define observational equivalence

`v ~_Phi w  iff  o_Phi(v)=o_Phi(w)`.

This gives a partition `Pi_Phi` of the valuation carrier.

### Theorem 7.1 — exact strict-refinement criterion

Let `Psi=Phi union {psi}`. Then `Psi` strictly increases distinguishability on a support `S` iff there exist `v,w in S` such that

`o_Phi(v)=o_Phi(w)` and `chi_psi(v) != chi_psi(w)`.

Equivalently, the new test splits at least one old signature block.

**Proof.** The new signature is `(o_Phi(v),chi_psi(v))`; two worlds that were previously in one block split exactly when their new coordinate differs.

This is the preferred mathematical definition of "observation increases distinguishability."

---

## 8. Distinguishability and uncertainty are two different axes

A useful state of logical differentiation is the pair

`(S,Pi_Phi)`.

Two operations act on different components:

- **refinement/unfolding** `U_psi`: `(S,Pi_Phi) -> (S,Pi_{Phi union {psi}})`;
- **measurement update** `M_f`: `(S,Pi_Phi) -> (S intersect E_f, Pi_Phi restricted to S intersect E_f)`.

This produces two independent finite measures.

### 8.1 Observational resolution

A simple unweighted resolution is the number of realized signature blocks

`R(Phi,S)=|{o_Phi(v):v in S}|`.

It is monotone nondecreasing under observation refinement.

With a probability distribution, one can instead use entropy of the induced signature random variable.

### 8.2 Residual uncertainty

For uniform support,

`H_0(S)=log_2 |S|`

is Hartley uncertainty. A possible selective outcome satisfies

`H_0(S intersect E_f) <= H_0(S)`.

If `0<|S intersect E_f|<|S|`, the recorded outcome yields positive information

`I_f = log_2(|S|/|S intersect E_f|)`.

These are not the same quantity: one can reduce uncertainty without adding a new discriminating coordinate, or add a discriminating coordinate before learning its outcome.

---

## 9. Unfolding as observation refinement

The thesis's `partial` operator should not be identified with `M_f`. Its motivating examples often change a formula into a family/union of alternatives not contained in the original truth support.

A clean modern interpretation is:

`U : observation description -> finer observation description`.

At fixed carrier, this is exactly ProLT observation refinement.

### Theorem 9.1 — refinement/update naturality

Suppose `U_psi` only enlarges the observation family on the same carrier and `M_f` conditions by a truth region defined independently of that enlargement. Then

`M_f U_psi = U_(psi|E_f) M_f`

in the sense that both routes yield the carrier `S intersect E_f` equipped with the restricted enlarged observation family.

Diagrammatically:

```text
(S, Phi) ----------------U_psi----------------> (S, Phi union {psi})
   |                                              |
  M_f                                            M_f
   |                                              |
   v                                              v
(S intersect E_f, Phi|E_f) --U_(psi|E_f)--> (S intersect E_f, (Phi union {psi})|E_f)
```

If unfolding changes the carrier or introduces new latent coordinates, a different typed diagram is required; commutation is then an additional theorem, not an assumption.

---

## 10. Context embedding and purity

Let `f` be a formula on `n` variables. Its canonical extension to `n+m` variables ignores the added variables:

`iota(f)(x_1,...,x_n,z_1,...,z_m)=f(x_1,...,x_n)`.

### Theorem 10.1 — cylinder-extension law

`E_iota(f)=E_f x {0,1}^m`, hence

`|E_iota(f)|=2^m |E_f|`

and

`rank D_iota(f)=2^m rank D_f`.

Therefore the thesis's singleton-support notion of "pure logic state" is not preserved by adjoining an unconstrained variable. This is ordinary cylinder extension.

A stronger contextuality notion requires a family of measurement contexts for which compatible local outcome data fail to admit a global assignment; cylinder replication does not provide that obstruction.

---

## 11. Compact-CM idempotents: algebraic projectors, not automatically effects

Let `A` be a 2x2 compact CM. Four products were audited separately.

### 11.1 XOR-AND over `F_2`

Exactly eight of the 16 satisfy `A^2=A`:

`FALSE, AND, NOR, X, Y, XNOR, NOT_Y, NOT_X`.

The symmetric/self-transpose members are exactly

`FALSE, AND, NOR, XNOR`.

Over ordinary real scalars these four are orthogonal coordinate projectors. The other four real idempotents are oblique rather than orthogonal projectors.

### 11.2 Boolean-semiring product

Exactly eleven are idempotent: the previous eight plus

`X_IMPLIES_Y, Y_IMPLIES_X, TRUE`.

### 11.3 Ordinary integer/real multiplication

Among the 16 zero-one arrays, the same eight as the `F_2` case are idempotent.

### 11.4 Cyclic convolution on rotation coordinates

Only FALSE and AND are idempotent. In the coefficient-ring identification `F_2[C_4] ~= F_2[u]/(u^4)`, they are 0 and 1. This algebra is local, so it has no nontrivial idempotents.

These facts are useful structural classifications. They do not replace the valuation-space effect representation, where all 16 Boolean events are projectors.

---

## 12. Symmetry is not distinguishability

Let a group `G` act on a state object. A smaller stabilizer can be a meaningful notion of lower symmetry, but it is not a general information criterion.

### Proposition 12.1 — equivariant maps cannot decrease stabilizers

If `M` is `G`-equivariant, then

`Stab_G(x) subseteq Stab_G(M(x))`.

**Proof.** If `gx=x`, then `gM(x)=M(gx)=M(x)`.

Thus any genuine stabilizer decrease must come from a context/effect that is not invariant under the full symmetry group, or from changing the group being considered.

For fixed-effect restriction `S -> S intersect E`, exhaustive `D_4` computation confirms that stabilizer size can increase, decrease, or remain unchanged. Therefore use signature partition refinement for distinguishability and reserve stabilizers for symmetry analysis.

---

## 13. Finite worked differentiation path

Start with no restriction:

`S_0=TRUE={11,10,01,00}`.

Ask the XOR question and record TRUE:

`S_1=S_0 intersect XOR={10,01}`.

Then ask X and record TRUE:

`S_2=S_1 intersect X={10}=X AND NOT Y`.

The associated projectors satisfy

`D_X D_XOR D_TRUE = D_(X AND NOT Y)`.

Support sizes are `4 -> 2 -> 1`. This is a valid finite model of progressive differentiation.

By contrast,

`AND -> XOR`

cannot be a conditioning step because `AND intersect XOR=FALSE`. If retained as a thesis idea, it belongs to unfolding/re-description rather than measurement.

---

## 14. Optional probabilistic and modal enrichments

### Classical probabilistic extension

Add a prior `p` and use ordinary conditioning. This immediately yields expected information gain and allows empirical estimation.

### Generalized probabilistic extension

A GPT requires a convex state space, an effect space of affine maps to `[0,1]`, measurements whose effects sum to the unit effect, and instruments/channels for post-measurement states. The core CM event algebra embeds into the classical simplex GPT but is not by itself a general GPT specification.

### Modal extension

A finite-field/ring model can instead use possibility/necessity: states are admissible module vectors; effects are covectors; an outcome is possible when the contraction is nonzero; measurements are declared context families of effects. Contextuality then becomes a global-section/support question. These axioms are additional to CM truth-table representation.

---

## 15. Recommended terminology

For a future paper, use:

- **CM** for compact truth-table operator `[Theta]`;
- **truth effect** or **valuation projector** for `D_Theta`;
- **observation refinement** for adding tests;
- **selective measurement/update** for support restriction;
- **conditioning** only when a probability state is present;
- **unfolding** for a representation/refinement transform that exposes latent alternatives;
- **modal measurement** only after a complete modal state/effect/context contract has been stated.

Avoid using "collapse," "pure," "superposition," "observable," or "entanglement" without defining the exact mathematical sense each time.

# U1 — Preorder refinement by intersection

## Verdict

**VALID AS STATED.** The result is exact, but it is essentially definitional once the observation preorder is defined coordinatewise. It should be retained as the foundational bookkeeping lemma, not advertised as a new theorem.

Let `S` be a finite support and let every observation `phi` take values in a preorder `A_phi`. Define

\[
x\preceq_{\Phi,S}y
\iff
x,y\in S\ \text{and}\ \phi(x)\le_{A_\phi}\phi(y)\quad\forall\phi\in\Phi.
\]

Boolean values are not essential. Any preordered codomains work.

For observation families `Phi,Theta`,

\[
\preceq_{\Phi\cup\Theta,S}
=
\preceq_{\Phi,S}\cap\preceq_{\Theta,S}.
\]

For `T subseteq S`,

\[
\preceq_{\Phi,T}
=
\preceq_{\Phi,S}\cap(T\times T).
\]

The second identity is simultaneously the restriction of a relation, the induced subpreorder, and—under the finite Alexandrov correspondence—the specialization preorder of the induced subspace.

## Hidden hypotheses

1. Each observation must be a total map on the carrier under consideration. Partial observations require either restricting their domains or adding an explicit undefined value/order.
2. The observation codomain must carry a preorder if the coordinatewise order definition is to make sense.
3. Duplicated/indexed observations do not change the induced relation unless later weights/costs use multiplicity.

## Novelty classification

Finite topological spaces are classically equivalent to finite preorders, and `T0` is exactly antisymmetry. The intersection identity adds no independent novelty. Its value is architectural: it puts refinement and support restriction in one relation calculus.

# Literature and priority audit through September 2026

This audit is conservative: absence of an exact phrase is not evidence of novelty.

## U1/U2 — finite topologies and preorders

Finite topology/preorder equivalence and the fact that `T0` corresponds to antisymmetry are classical. A recent accessible statement is:

- Mrozek et al., *Conley Index for Multivalued Maps on Finite Topological Spaces*, Foundations of Computational Mathematics (2024/2025 online context), https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10208-024-09685-4
- Jonathan Barmak, *Algebraic Topology of Finite Topological Spaces and Applications*, Springer, 2011, DOI 10.1007/978-3-642-22003-6.

**Priority effect:** U1 is standard. U2's repaired fiber/cross-fiber interpretation is a synthesis, not a claim to the quotient-order foundations.

## U3 — lexicographic sums

The intermediate `F=sum_p B_p` matches the standard lexicographic sum/substitution of posets: within a fiber use its order; when index `p<q`, every point of the `p`-fiber is below every point of the `q`-fiber.

- Sage/Stanford finite-poset documentation: https://sporadic.stanford.edu/reference/combinat/sage/combinat/posets/posets.html

**Priority effect:** lexicographic sum is standard. The potentially useful project-specific step is identifying it canonically from ProLT fiber profiles and then separating its expansion map from descent thinning.

## U4 — mapping cones and the octahedral axiom

The cone of a map gives the standard distinguished triangle, and composable maps fit the octahedral pattern connecting `Cone(f)`, `Cone(gf)`, and `Cone(g)`.

- Stacks Project, *Cones and distinguished triangles*: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09P1
- Stacks Project, *Distinguished triangles in the homotopy category*: https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/014P

**Priority effect:** the octahedral LES is standard homological algebra. Do not claim it. The application to the U3 refinement factorization is the only project-specific content.

## U5/U6 — pullbacks, saturation, and measurement availability

Pullbacks are fiber products; in sets and concrete ordered settings the relevant square selects exactly the elements lying over the surviving base. Saturated subsets of a quotient are unions of whole quotient fibers. U5/U6 are therefore close to standard fiber/saturation mathematics.

- nLab pullback overview: https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/pullback

The epistemic-update interpretation also has established neighbors. Public Announcement Logic updates a model by deleting worlds at which the announced formula is false:

- Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, *Dynamic Epistemic Logic*: https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/dynamic-epistemic/
- SEP, *Logic and Information*: https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/logic-information/

**Priority effect:** U5 is a standard pullback criterion in project notation. U6 is a useful synthesis identifying non-cartesianity with “newly enabled measurement” under a fine-measurability hypothesis.

## Observation design — 2-dimension and Test Cover

Bit-vector encodings of a poset into a Boolean lattice, minimizing the number of coordinates, are the classical 2-dimension problem:

- Habib et al., *Computational aspects of the 2-dimension of partially ordered sets*, Theoretical Computer Science 312 (2004) 401–431, DOI 10.1016/j.tcs.2003.10.029, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304397503005747

Pair separation from a prescribed test pool is classical Test Cover:

- Gutin, Muciaccia, Yeo, *(Non-)existence of polynomial kernels for the Test Cover problem*, Information Processing Letters 113 (2013) 123–126, DOI 10.1016/j.ipl.2012.12.008, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0020019012003183

**Priority effect:** unrestricted U-design is standard territory. Novelty, if any, must come from ProLT-specific admissibility/cost/topological constraints.

## Adaptive identification and restricted query languages

Decision-tree optimization and constrained query families are deeply established:

- Hyafil & Rivest, *Constructing optimal binary decision trees is NP-complete*, Information Processing Letters 5 (1976) 15–17, DOI 10.1016/0020-0190(76)90095-8.
- Karbasi & Zadimoghaddam, *Constrained Binary Identification Problem*, STACS 2013, https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.STACS.2013.550
- Dagan, Filmus, Gabizon, Moran, *Twenty (Simple) Questions*, STOC 2017, DOI 10.1145/3055399.3055422, arXiv:1611.01655. This explicitly studies restricted sets of yes/no questions while trying to retain optimal information performance.
- Nowak, *The Geometry of Generalized Binary Search*, IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 57 (2011); arXiv:0910.4397. It studies adaptively chosen near-balanced queries and logarithmic query complexity under geometric conditions.
- Cicalese et al./related poset-search literature: *On the complexity of searching in trees and partially ordered structures*, Theoretical Computer Science 412 (2011) 6879–6896, DOI 10.1016/j.tcs.2011.08.042.
- Eisel, McMullen, Muth, *An efficient search strategy for hidden ideals in pointed partially ordered sets* (2025/2026 publication cycle), DOI 10.61091/jcmcc128-11, arXiv:2505.07604.

**Priority effect on A1:** the general topic “adaptive identification under restricted queries” is emphatically not new. The potentially new item is only the exact query language induced by the ProLT chain homotopy classification and the resulting “exactly one redundant query is necessary/sufficient” corollary. This should be presented as a narrow ProLT theorem unless a deeper priority audit finds a direct equivalent.

## Bottom line

- U1: standard.
- U2: repaired useful synthesis.
- U3: standard lexicographic construction + useful ProLT factorization.
- U4: standard octahedral machinery + useful application.
- U5: standard pullback/fiber criterion in ProLT form.
- U6: useful saturation/measurement-availability synthesis.
- A1: correct and nontrivial as a ProLT consequence; novelty plausible but modest and should remain explicitly provisional.

# Counterexamples and repaired overstatements

## C1 — quotient refinement can expose a new strict order inside a split coarse point

**False stronger statement:** “No new strict quotient comparabilities ever appear under refinement.”

Carrier `S={a,b}`; no coarse observations; add `theta(a)=0, theta(b)=1`.

- coarse quotient: one point;
- fine quotient: two-point chain `0<1`.

**Repair:** no fine comparability can connect descendants of two distinct coarse-incomparable points. New strict relations may appear **inside the fiber of one split coarse point**.

## C2 — cartesianity does not imply coarse measurability without fine measurability

Coarse cell `{a,b,c}`; fine cells `{a,b}` and `{c}`; event `E={a,c}`.

`E` cuts a fine cell. Thus it is not fine-measurable and not coarse-measurable, even though the coarser label-profile condition can be cartesian.

**Repair:** U6 must assume `E` is a union of fine signature classes.

## C3 — U4 is not a direct-sum decomposition theorem

The octahedral axiom yields a distinguished triangle and long exact sequence. Without vanishing connecting morphisms and further splitting data, one cannot conclude

\[
D^{\rm total}\cong D^{\rm thin}\oplus D^{\rm exp}.
\]

**Repair:** call U4 an “octahedral defect sequence” or “cone factorization sequence,” not an unconditional direct decomposition.

## C4 — homotopy-neutral query restrictions alone do not make adaptive identification hard

If arbitrary Boolean queries are available on a finite T0 poset, choose a linear extension. Any suffix of a linear extension is an upset and therefore defines an isotone/topologically redundant query. A suffix can be chosen to split the current support as evenly as possible. Repeating yields depth `ceil(log2 n)`.

**Repair of research target:** to obtain nontrivial adaptive complexity, impose a fixed query library, syntactic/cost restriction, or require nonredundant safe queries.

# Unified Differentiation Calculus Investigation

**Project:** Refinement, conditioning, constrained observation design, and adaptive protocols  
**Date:** 29 September 2026  
**Status:** exploratory theorem program with bounded exhaustive verification; novelty not claimed without a dedicated priority audit.

## 1. Executive finding

There is a clean unification, and it is stronger than treating pre-\(T_0\) splitting and post-\(T_0\) thinning as separate regimes.

The correct carrier-level object is the **observation specialization preorder** on the surviving worlds:

\[
x\preceq_{\Phi,S} y
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x,y\in S\ \text{and}\ \phi(x)\le \phi(y)\ \text{for every }\phi\in\Phi.
\]

Equivalently, if \(o_\Phi(x)\in\{0,1\}^{\Phi}\) is the observation signature,

\[
x\preceq_{\Phi,S}y
\iff
o_\Phi(x)\le o_\Phi(y)
\]

coordinatewise.

Adding an observation never performs two fundamentally different operations at this level. It simply **thins the preorder**:

\[
\preceq_{\Phi\cup\Theta,S}
=
\preceq_{\Phi,S}\cap \preceq_{\Theta,S}.
\]

Conditioning to \(T\subseteq S\) simply takes the induced subpreorder:

\[
\preceq_{\Phi,T}
=
\preceq_{\Phi,S}\cap(T\times T).
\]

Hence fixed refinement and fixed conditioning commute strictly on the world-level preorder.

The familiar phase transition at \(T_0\) appears only after quotienting the preorder by observational equivalence:

\[
x\equiv_\Phi y
\iff
x\preceq_\Phi y\ \text{and}\ y\preceq_\Phi x
\iff
o_\Phi(x)=o_\Phi(y).
\]

Before \(T_0\), thinning may delete one or both directions between two equivalent worlds and thereby **split a quotient point**. After \(T_0\), no nontrivial symmetric pair remains, so further refinement can only delete strict comparabilities: **order thinning**.

This gives one mechanism with two quotient-level manifestations.

The strongest structural extension found in this investigation is a canonical factorization of every finite refinement into:

1. **fiber expansion** of coarse observational states; followed by
2. **descent thinning** of the resulting order.

Support conditioning fits into a commuting refinement--conditioning prism. The only non-cartesian face is the fiber-expansion face, and its failure is exactly a saturation/measurement-availability obstruction. After relative \(T_0\), that obstruction vanishes automatically, recovering the existing post-\(T_0\) bifiltration.
