### 4.2 v0.2 — correct general classification machinery

The profile normal form Q={(p,a):a in B_p}, with product order, is correct. It precisely distinguishes splitting from non-splitting. Redundancy is the singleton-isotone case. After identifying vertices in a non-splitting refinement,

    x <=_Q y iff x <=_P y and a(x) <= a(y).

The relative chain basis consists of deleted chains; its differential simply discards faces retained in L. The mapping cone is equivalent at homology level to the ordinary pair (K,L) in this regime.

The adjoint criteria are correct. Taking the union of all new profiles below p produces the greatest principal lower fiber exactly when that union itself occurs at p; the dual intersection criterion handles least upper fibers. The possible/forced one-bit formulation is a direct specialization. The principal-fiber theorems are correctly about r^{-1}(down p) or r^{-1}(up p), **not** point fibers. Contractible and acyclic versions do different jobs, and neither becomes necessary merely because small tests pass [R02].

The cone criterion is exact for homology neutrality. Betti and Euler checks are only necessary shortcuts; equality of endpoint Betti numbers alone does not certify the map. The component criterion is exact because the refinement is surjective on vertices and therefore on coarse components.

The examples separate redundancy, section adjoints, principal-fiber tests, homotopy neutrality, and homology neutrality. Adding X to no observations shows that splitting need not be topologically destructive. XOR on the Boolean square is neutral without a section adjoint. The alternating chain profile shows that both principal-fiber orientations may fail although the actual map is neutral. Acyclic noncontractible complexes give the final homology-versus-homotopy separation.

Universality via minterm realization and principal ideals is correct for **nonempty** targets on a nonempty point-coarse carrier. Add that qualification. The contractibility-undecidability reduction is valid: start with a nonempty finite complex, take its face poset, realize it as a fine signature poset over a point, and ask whether Delta(r) is a homotopy equivalence. The high-dimensional classical theorem suffices [R05, Appendix A, Theorem 11, d>=5]. This is an effective encoding argument; it does not need or supply polynomial formula-size bounds. Homology neutrality remains decidable by finite matrix computation.

**Verdict:** correct standard/adapted framework, with two minor nonempty qualifications. A6 below strengthens its limitation theorem to a single bit after T0.

### 4.3 v0.3 — correct controlled results; chain novelty substantially reduced

The positive and anti-positive normal forms are correct. Post-T0 section-adjoint rigidity is also correct: a section of the same-vertex identity map is forced to be the identity, and monotonicity in both directions then forces the two orders to agree. This explains why adjoints cease to certify interesting proper thinnings in this regime.

An antitone label retains only comparisons between equal label values. If a coarse connected component contains multiple values, it splits; neutrality is therefore equivalent to constant profile on each coarse component. Adding all old-coordinate negations makes the quotient discrete.

Height-one homology rigidity has a particularly short proof: the relative chain complex has only C1=Z^(deleted edges), with C0=0 and no C2. Every deleted edge creates a nonzero relative class. At height two, the whole relative problem is the two-term boundary B:C2->C1. Invertibility is an exact field-homology criterion, and unequal edge/triangle counts obstruct neutrality. This is standard relative-chain algebra, not yet the special one-bit theorem.

**Independent chain proof.** Let b_1...b_n label an n-chain. A nondecreasing word changes no comparisons. A nonconstant nonincreasing word 1^a0^(n-a) gives two disjoint chains. In every other case, first bit 0 gives a global minimum, or last bit 1 gives a global maximum. In the remaining mixed case, delete each initial 1 as an up-beat point, using the first later 1 as its least strict upper element; the remaining initial 0 is a minimum. This proves the trichotomy without a Betti-number inference. Counting gives n+1, n-1, and 2^n-2n. Applying the same classification to every prefix/suffix proves the exact Quillen visibility tests and the count 2^(n-2)-(n-1) for n>=2.

**Prior-art consequence.** The incomparability graph of this refined chain is the bipartite inversion/Ferrers graph, and Delta(Q) is its independence complex. The introduction of Claesson-Kitaev-Ragnarsson-Tenner explicitly announces the corresponding point-versus-two-points simple-homotopy classification, citing an Ehrenborg-Kitaev work listed in preparation [R09]. The underlying proof was not located. Therefore the chain homotopy classification has strong prior-art overlap, while the direct beat proof and exact test-coverage counts remain useful exposition. It should not be advertised as an independently new classification without resolving that bibliographic history.

Block universality over a coarse chain and the refinement/update bifiltration are correct. They are elementary representation and diagram constructions. All eighteen named statements survive. Restore the empty TeX source before freezing the manuscript.

### 4.4 v0.4 — the strongest exact specialization

The repair-map, floor/ceiling, anchor, and semilattice arguments are correct applications of comparable monotone maps and closure/interior ideas. Horn truth sets supply meet closure; dual-Horn falsity sets supply join closure. The realized semilattice and upper/lower cofinality assumptions are indispensable. The full Boolean-lattice endpoint test correctly certifies XOR/XNOR, while NOR can isolate the bottom and change H0. These are useful sufficient conditions, not a general classification of logical fragments [R02,R20].

**The repair-forest proof survives every listed local concern.** Orient a triangle x<y<z by its order. Its boundary is [y,z]-[x,z]+[x,y]. The deleted bit patterns are exactly 010, 101, 100, and 110. The first two give one deleted edge; the last two give two, with opposite integral signs. No deleted triangle has three deleted edges. Attach singleton columns to a formal root in their coarse component, and interpret two-entry columns as graph edges. This gives a reduced integral incidence matrix.

On a rooted tree, a nonroot leaf corresponds to a deleted edge in exactly one remaining deleted triangle. A retained triangle cannot contain a deleted edge, because L is a subcomplex. Height<=2 excludes higher cofaces. Thus the leaf pair is genuinely free in the current complex. Repeating the operation collapses K to L. Disconnected coarse components, isolated roots, parallel edges, and empty deleted-cell sets cause no gap: parallel edges create cycles; isolated roots contribute nothing; the empty matching/collapse is valid.

Conversely, homotopy equivalence implies F2 homology equivalence, so B is invertible. Reduced graph incidence is invertible precisely when every graph component is a tree with exactly one root. The complete equivalence is therefore proved, not computationally guessed.

**Integral strengthening A1.** The matrix is totally unimodular. If c0 counts rootless repair-graph components and beta1 its graph cycle rank, then

    H1(K,L;Z) = Z^c0,     H2(K,L;Z) = Z^beta1,

and all other relative groups vanish. In particular, no one-bit height-two refinement can have relative torsion, and neutrality over any one field already implies integral neutrality and direct collapse.

**Novelty assessment:** the graph-incidence theorem and collapse machinery are established [R03-R04,R19]. The specific binary-order-thinning recognition is the narrow candidate contribution. I did not locate an exact earlier statement with all these hypotheses and equivalences; that supports `NOVELTY_UNCLEAR`, not “new.” The theorem is coherent and useful enough to anchor a tightly scoped manuscript, but its proof should openly reveal how little genuinely new machinery is required.

### 4.5 v0.5 — valuable limits, one major branch correction

The coordinatewise order-thinning description, joint-complex intersection theorem, and sufficiency of sequential neutrality are correct. “Every coordinate safe relative to the original P” is different from “every step safe relative to the current intermediate order.” This distinction explains why destructive interaction is possible without contradicting composition of equivalences.

Universality of same-vertex suborders is correct: label v by its principal Q-ideal. The basic dimension bound survives. The equality with classical 2-dimension does not.

**Two minimal counterexamples.** For P=Q a two-chain, odim=0 but dim2=1. For P a two-chain and Q an antichain, a single label word 10 deletes the only forward relation, so odim=1, while dim2(Q)=2. The coarse order handles reverse noncomparisons for free; an ordinary Boolean embedding cannot. The original inherited-hardness proof must be removed rather than cosmetically adjusted.

**Replacement A2.** Make each deleted comparison a demand. Two demands (x,y),(u,v) conflict iff x<=_Q v or u<=_Q y. A valid bit is a Q-upset. One bit can satisfy a collection of demands exactly when that collection is independent in the conflict graph: take the upward closure of their first endpoints. Therefore odim is exactly the graph's chromatic number. Equivalently, it is generalized Boolean rank of a 0/1/? matrix. This is an established covering framework [R07-R08], specialized to nested orders.

The explicit graph-to-height-one-poset reduction proves general NP-completeness. The total-coarse-order restriction remains unproved here. An additional exact easy case is target Q antichain: odim=ceil(log2 h), where h is the maximum number of elements in a P-chain. Distinct labels are necessary along a chain, and reverse Boolean-lattice linear-extension labels assigned by chain rank suffice.

The coefficient-sensitive boundary criterion is correct. A square integer matrix is rationally invertible iff its determinant is nonzero; integral neutrality requires determinant +/-1; mod-p neutrality requires p not dividing the determinant. Rectangular or singular cases require kernel/cokernel, not a scalar weight. The Bernardi-Klivans translation needs all deleted-edge rows present; a deleted edge lying in no triangle is omitted by the original triangle-generated setup. C03 repairs this. The nonsingular examples are unaffected [R03].

**Named examples.** The 010/101 example is correct and minimal for that three-chain mechanism. The five-state example has the stated compensation and a unimodular 3x3 matrix with a unique matching. The eight-state three-bit example has a unimodular 11x11 matrix and exactly three perfect matchings, each cyclic. Both endpoint posets are beat-contractible, so the inclusion is a homotopy equivalence, but no direct relative collapse exists. This refutes the block extension of the one-bit collapse equivalence. No global minimality claim follows from the small enumeration.

**Matching strengthening A4.** In this height-two two-layer incidence setting, a perfect matching is acyclic exactly when it is unique: a directed cycle is an alternating cycle, and the symmetric difference of two perfect matchings consists of alternating cycles. Thus unique fitting orientation is not merely sufficient; it is equivalent to direct relative collapse. This is a standard matching/Morse observation, and it explains the eight-state failure without redefining rooted-forest theory.

## 5. Interaction and coefficient-sensitive constructions

### 5.1 What Mayer-Vietoris actually contributes

For coordinate subcomplexes A,B of K, let I=A intersection B and U=A union B. There is a natural short exact sequence

    0 -> C(K,I) -> C(K,A) direct_sum C(K,B) -> C(K,U) -> 0,

with diagonal and difference maps. Its long exact sequence gives, when both individual inclusions are homology equivalences,

    H_n(K,I) is naturally isomorphic to H_(n+1)(K,U).

For 010/101, U is the boundary of the coarse triangle and I is an edge plus an isolated point. The connecting morphism identifies the union's relative two-class with the joint relative one-class. This supplies a meaningful explanation of interaction, but it is standard relative Mayer-Vietoris, not a newly discovered homology theory [R18]. Higher Cech-type bookkeeping is available; it should not be developed merely because it can be written down.

### 5.2 Torsion exists, and F2 can miss it completely

A5 realizes a connected two-dimensional finite complex X by its face poset P and retains a spanning-tree suborder Q containing all vertices. Then H_k(Delta(P),Delta(Q);Z)=reduced H_k(X;Z) for k>=1. Principal-Q-ideal labels realize Q as a block refinement. This gives arbitrary finite abelian relative H1 torsion by standard Moore-space constructions.

The audit supplies two complete examples. A 13-state regular-CW face-poset model of RP2 yields a 24x24 relative matrix with Smith diagonal (1 repeated 23 times,2). Its relative H1 is Z/2. A 79-state degree-three Moore model yields a 162x162 matrix with Smith diagonal (1 repeated 161 times,3). Its relative H1 is Z/3; its F2 relative homology vanishes, but its integral homology does not. The latter is an explicit F2-neutral observation block that is not homotopy-neutral.

A final conflict-coloring check compresses the thirteen-state torsion witness to **exactly two observations**, without changing its order or boundary matrix. Its labels are supplied explicitly. This already refutes a two-bit extension based on rational homology neutrality; it does not refute the proposed F2-neutrality question because its determinant is even. The same check proves the eight-state noncollapse pair genuinely needs three bits: three specified deleted-comparison demands form a conflict triangle. The five-state compensating pair's final order can, separately, be realized by one bit.

The underlying small projective-plane model is established finite-space topology [R15]. These witnesses are clean, reproducible realizations, not globally minimal relative-pair claims. The original notes' general matrix framework already predicts coefficient sensitivity; the audit makes it concrete.

### 5.3 One bit in higher height is already universal

A6 gives a simple sharpness construction. Start with any nonempty finite poset R and minimal element z. Add a greatest element t. Give z and t bit0, and every other vertex bit1. Every old R-comparison survives; among comparisons into t only z<t survives. Thus the coarse order complex is a cone on Delta(R), while the fine complex is Delta(R) with a whisker attached at z.

The whisker collapses, so the refined complex has exactly the homotopy type of Delta(R). Consequently one-bit, non-splitting refinement over a coarse cone already realizes arbitrary finite-complex homotopy types in unrestricted height. The order-complex neutrality decision is undecidable even under those restrictions. Relative homology is shifted reduced homology of R.

Choosing the 13-state projective-plane model for R gives a **14-state, height-three, one-bit** refinement with relative H2=Z/2. The analogous Z/3 construction uses 80 states and is F2-neutral but not integrally neutral. This makes the height restriction essential and rules out an unrestricted first-descent/last-descent collapse algorithm. Further positive higher-height theorems need genuine extra hypotheses, not just a contractible coarse endpoint.

## 6. Reproducibility findings and limits

All original scripts passed, but pass/fail alone was insufficient. The independent audit checked actual maps through relative chains, reconstructed all named examples from orders and labels, and used integer Smith forms rather than numerical determinant approximations.

Completed coverage includes: 8,190 chain words through n=12 with actual beat checks; 274,738 height<=2 one-bit profiles through n=6, including all 184,088 exact-height-two profiles in the supplied table; the original 10,468 two-bit cases with 4,459 neutral and 100 destructive; and an extension of 337,920 five-vertex two-bit profiles with 103,562 neutral and 4,514 destructive. No two-bit neutral/noncollapse witness was found in the completed range. The same neutrality decisions held over F2,F3,F5 in that extension.

The natural-label convention represents every isomorphism type but may represent a type more than once. Counts are not uniform statistics on isomorphism classes. Some original “homotopy” checks only calculate homology. The last one-bit CSV forest column excludes redundant cases. The early 255-profile generator was rerun but not independently reimplemented exactly. A six-vertex **two-bit** extension timed out and produced no completed result; no coverage is claimed for it.

No formal proof assistant, independent human panel, or complete automated homotopy oracle was used. Full code, exact scope, unsuccessful-run disclosure, and certificates are in the reproducibility report. These limits do not weaken the explicit mathematical proofs, but they constrain computational and novelty claims.

## 8. Publication assessment and terminology

The package's breadth currently obscures its best theorem. Most definitions are useful names for standard constructions, but a journal referee will ask what survives after the observation notation is removed. The answer should be the binary-labelled finite-poset characterization and its sharp boundaries, not “a new homological foundation for logic.”

The preferred manuscript is **Binary order thinning of finite posets: homology, collapses, and sharp limits**. Put the signed forest theorem, algorithm, and carefully chosen limitations at its center. Explain propositional realization as an application. Move the long foundations dictionary to an expository technical report. The alternative is separate one-bit and block papers, but only after the block paper gains a substantial structural theorem. The dimension branch is presently a corrected technical note, not a third research article.

Keep “repair graph” and “destructive interaction” only as explicitly defined descriptive terms. Use established language for mapping cones, relative homology, rooted forests, fitting orientations, and acyclic matchings. Explain odim immediately as a minimum Q-upset separation number and generalized covering problem. R22's recent “relative dimension” is a different invariant; avoid an unqualified name collision.

Real connections include information-system signatures, Dowker/formal-context relations, closure operators, graph incidence, and Boolean rectangle covering. Rough-set fixed-attribute reducts, SAT theta complexes, abstract interpretation, and contextuality cohomology are useful comparisons but not interchangeable models. Cognitive/mental-space claims remain speculative and should not support a mathematical significance claim.

A dedicated name for this restricted family was not verified. A theorem exploiting a prescribed coarse chain or another meaningful structural restriction is needed for a standalone paper.

### 9. Are there torsion/coefficient-sensitive examples?

Yes. The audit gives a 13-state height-two **two-bit** block with relative Z/2 and a 79-state block with relative Z/3. The latter is F2-neutral but not integrally neutral. Height-three one-bit examples on 14 and 80 states show that the one-bit field-independent conclusion also depends essentially on height<=2. All have exact certificates; global minimality is not claimed.

### 10. What should happen to the foundations?

A citable expository technical report is the best current form. Its value is a correct dictionary and well-chosen examples, not a new homology theory. The focused research paper needs only a few pages of this background.

### 11. How many papers, with which theorems?

Prepare one focused research manuscript: V4-11..15 and integral A1 as the core, selected V3 preliminaries, V5-14..15/A4 as the block boundary, and A6 as the higher-height boundary. Use small interaction/torsion examples selectively. Put V1, general V2, compatibility/cochains/persistence, and explanatory material into one foundations report. A second block paper and a dimension note are conditional, not current commitments.

### 12. What should be frozen?

Freeze the base quotient, profile normal form, standard fiber hierarchy, positive DNF, chain classification/counts, and foundations constructions. Freeze all existing examples with their certificates. Do not continue expanding cohomology, SR, persistence, or cognitive branches in parallel. Replace the false dimension claim in the ledger and keep deferred directions visible but inactive.

### 13. What is the single highest-value next theorem?

Determine whether every **two-bit height-two F2-neutral thinning collapses directly**. One bit is proved, three bits fail, and completed two-bit checks through five vertices find no exception. A proof or a compact counterexample would establish a meaningful bit-complexity boundary. Do not promote the finite evidence to a theorem.

### 14. What are the largest novelty risks?

The forest theorem may be regarded as an immediate incidence/Morse corollary; the chain theorem has Ferrers antecedents; dimension is generalized Boolean covering; closure/Horn criteria are standard operator arguments; and most foundations/persistence material is existing topology in a new vocabulary. These risks require a narrow contribution statement and precise citations, not a larger manuscript.

### 15. What would prevent acceptance today?

For Paper A: unresolved narrow novelty positioning, excessive standard-background volume, missing source reproducibility, and ambiguity between finite-space and order-complex homotopy. For proposed Paper B: examples and standard MV/rooted-forest machinery without an independent structural theorem. For proposed Paper C: a false central identification, a failed restricted-hardness proof, and insufficient separation from existing covering theory. For the foundations as a journal research paper: no demonstrated new theorem beyond a useful synthesis. These are repairable scope/evidence problems, not a reason to abandon the validated central mathematics.

## 10. Final decision

**Do not submit the package unchanged. Do not discard it.** Preserve the correct binary order-thinning theorem, its algorithm, and its sharp limits; correct the dimension branch openly; publish the foundational dictionary as exposition; and keep exactly one next theorem active. The result should be a smaller, more defensible research program with a clear mathematical object and verifiable claims.

# Audit additions and independent proofs

**Issued:** 24 September 2026. **Status:** additions produced during the audit, not claims that were already in v0.1-v0.5. These are mathematical proofs and reproducible constructions, not a novelty certification. Source identifiers R01-R22 refer to `LITERATURE_SOURCES.md`.

## A1. Integral one-bit incidence theorem and complete relative homology

Let P be a finite poset of height at most two, where height counts strict inequalities. Let b:P -> {0,1}, and put

\[
x\le_Qy\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\le_Py\text{ and }b(x)\le b(y),
\qquad K=\Delta P,\quad L=\Delta Q.
\]

All vertices survive. Write E and T for the deleted edges and triangles. With the order orientation, the only possibly nonzero relative boundary is

\[
B:C_2(K,L;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^T\longrightarrow
C_1(K,L;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^E.
\]

For a triangle x<y<z, the boundary is [y,z]-[x,z]+[x,y]. The four deleted binary patterns have the following columns:

| Pattern | Deleted edges | Integral coefficients |
|---|---|---|
| 010 | yz | +1 |
| 101 | xy | +1 |
| 100 | xy, xz | +1, -1 |
| 110 | xz, yz | -1, +1 |

Every other binary pattern retains the triangle. In particular, a deleted triangle never has zero or three deleted edges.

Construct the graph G with vertex set E together with one formal root for every connected component of P. A two-entry column is an oriented edge between its two deleted-edge vertices. A one-entry column is an oriented edge between that vertex and its component root. Then B is an oriented incidence matrix with all root rows removed. This observation strengthens v0.4 Proposition `prop:incidence` from F2 to Z.

**Theorem.** B is totally unimodular. Let c0 be the number of connected components of G containing no root, and let beta1(G)=|T|-|V(G)|+c(G). Then

\[
H_2(K,L;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^{\beta_1(G)},\qquad
H_1(K,L;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^{c_0},\qquad H_0(K,L;\mathbb Z)=0.
\]

Thus every integral relative homology group is free, and its ranks are independent of the coefficient field.

**Proof.** The oriented incidence matrix of a graph is totally unimodular: in any square submatrix, a column with at most one nonzero allows determinant induction; if every column has two entries, their opposite signs make the row sum zero. Deleting rows preserves this property. Each graph component has at most one root, since its vertices and edges stay inside one coarse component and there is just one root there. On a component with a root, reduced incidence has full row rank and cokernel zero. On one without a root, ordinary incidence has cokernel Z. In either case, the kernel is its integral cycle space. Direct sums give the formula. Isolated roots contribute neither a row nor a homology generator. Empty E and T give the zero complex, as required. QED.

**Collapse consequence.** All six equivalences in v0.4's repair-forest theorem remain correct. They can now include integral homology equivalence and homology equivalence over any one field. If the graph is a rooted forest, choose a nonroot leaf. It is a deleted edge with exactly one current deleted triangle above it. No retained triangle contains a deleted edge because L is a subcomplex. There are no higher cells. Consequently this is an actual free-face collapse, not merely algebraic cancellation. Repetition ends precisely at L. Multi-edges, when present, produce graph cycles and do not invalidate this argument.

**Prior-art assessment:** graph incidence and total unimodularity are standard; relative torsion interpretations are established [R03,R04]. The binary-labelled-poset recognition step is the specific adaptation. This is not a new matrix-tree theorem.

## A2. Exact observation-design parameter as coloring and generalized Boolean rank

Let P and Q be partial orders on the same finite set V, with Q contained in P. The package defines odim_P(Q) as the least k for which there is a map a:V -> {0,1}^k satisfying

\[
x\le_Qy\iff \bigl(x\le_Py\text{ and }a(x)\le a(y)\bigr).
\]

No injectivity is imposed on a, and a is not an order embedding of Q in general.

Let D={(x,y):x<_P y and x not<=_Q y}. Define a simple conflict graph Gamma(P,Q) on D by declaring two distinct demands (x,y),(u,v) adjacent when

\[
x\le_Qv\quad\text{or}\quad u\le_Qy.
\]

**Theorem.** With chromatic number zero for the empty graph,

\[
\operatorname{odim}_P(Q)=\chi(\Gamma(P,Q)).
\]

**Proof.** Each coordinate must be isotone on Q, so its truth set U is a Q-upset. It deletes exactly those demands (x,y) with x in U and y not in U. Two conflicting demands cannot both be deleted by this bit: for example x<=_Q v would force v into U whenever x is in U.

Conversely, let S be an independent set of demands. Take U to be the Q-upward closure of all first entries of demands in S. No second entry of a demand in S belongs to U: such membership would say that a first entry lies below that second entry, giving either a conflict or a forbidden self-demand. Therefore this one bit deletes all demands in S and preserves every Q-comparison. A coloring supplies one bit per color class. Conversely, assign each demand to any coordinate deleting it; each resulting color class is independent. QED.

**Exact established optimization framework.** Form a generalized binary matrix indexed by V x V:

\[
M_{xy}=\begin{cases}
0&x\le_Qy,\\
1&x\le_Py\text{ but }x\not\le_Qy,\\
?&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]

A rectangle is allowed to contain 1s and question marks but no zeros, and only the 1s must be covered. Then

\[
\operatorname{odim}_P(Q)=\operatorname{br}(M),
\]

where br is generalized Boolean rank, or the generalized rectangle-cover number [R07,R08]. Indeed, a bit U supplies U x (V\U). Conversely, any allowed rectangle A x B can be enlarged to the valid upset cut U x (V\U), where U=up_Q A: the absence of zeros says U intersects B trivially. The conflict graph above is the complement of the rectangle-cover compatibility graph on required entries. Thus the general covering/coloring mechanism is established mathematics, not an independently new type of dimension.

**Corrected complexity theorem.** For explicitly represented same-ground-set P,Q, deciding odim_P(Q)<=k is NP-complete. It is already NP-hard for k=3 when both orders have height at most one.

Given a graph H on vertices 1,...,m, create minima a_i and maxima b_i. In Q, put a_i<b_j and a_j<b_i exactly when ij is an edge of H. Let P add the m diagonal comparisons a_i<b_i. Both relations are partial orders of height at most one. Their demands are exactly (a_i,b_i), and the conflict graph is H. Thus odim_P(Q)=chi(H). The construction is polynomial. Membership in NP follows from the n-coordinate principal-ideal bound: a binary label certificate has polynomial size, and all ordered pairs can be checked directly. For k>=n the answer is immediately yes.

**Important limitation:** this repairs the unrestricted complexity claim, not the original assertion that hardness already holds when P is total. That restricted claim remains unproved in this audit.

**Useful immediate bounds.**

\[
\omega(\Gamma)\le\operatorname{odim}_P(Q)
\le\min\{|D|,|V|,\dim_2(Q)\},
\]

and odim=0 exactly when P=Q. The |V| upper bound uses principal Q-ideals as labels; dim_2(Q) is only an upper bound, not an equality. A one-bit realization exists exactly when Gamma has no edges (and D is nonempty for equality to one).

**Exact target-antichain case.** If Q is the antichain on V and h is the maximum number of elements in a chain of nonempty P, then

\[
\operatorname{odim}_P(Q)=\lceil\log_2 h\rceil.
\]

Along a P-chain all labels must be distinct, proving the lower bound. Assign each element its longest-chain rank. Choose h distinct subsets of a k-set in reverse linear-extension order of the Boolean lattice. If rank(x)<rank(y), the assigned subset at x is not contained in the subset at y. Therefore every strict P-comparison is deleted. This gives the upper bound. For V empty define the value to be zero separately.

This shows especially clearly why Sperner's classical antichain embedding bound is not the right bound for this relative problem.

**Exact label minima for named examples.** The five-state compensating block has minimum one bit for its final Q, namely (1,0,0,0,1), even though its originally chosen two coordinates each behave differently. The thirteen-state torsion pair in A5 has minimum two bits. The eight-state noncollapse pair has minimum three: its original three-bit labels give an upper bound, while the demands (0,3), (2,5), and (3,6) form a triangle in the conflict graph. These three conflicts follow respectively from 0<=_Q5, 2<=_Q6, and reflexivity at 3. Thus the known eight-state pair cannot simply be relabelled with two bits. `minimize_named_labels.py` supplies independent standard-library certificates for all three statements.

## A3. Relative Mayer-Vietoris interaction sequence

Let A=K_1 and B=K_2 be the one-coordinate retained subcomplexes of K=Delta(P). Set I=A cap B and U=A cup B. Work over any commutative coefficient ring. There is a natural degreewise short exact sequence

\[
0\longrightarrow C_*(K,I)
\overset{d}{\longrightarrow}C_*(K,A)\oplus C_*(K,B)
\overset{e}{\longrightarrow}C_*(K,U)\longrightarrow0,
\]

where d([c])=([c],[c]) and e([a],[b])=[a-b]. This is exact simplex by simplex: a simplex is in both subcomplexes, only one, or neither. Hence

\[
\cdots\to H_{n+1}(K,U)\to H_n(K,I)
\to H_n(K,A)\oplus H_n(K,B)
\to H_n(K,U)\to\cdots.
\]

**Interaction corollary.** If both coordinate inclusions induce homology isomorphisms, then naturally

\[
H_n(K,I)\cong H_{n+1}(K,U).
\]

The failure of joint homological neutrality is precisely the shifted defect of the union of the two individually retained complexes. This is a useful application of relative Mayer-Vietoris [R18], not a novel exact-sequence construction.

**Minimal test.** On the three-chain, the profiles 010 and 101 retain two different two-edge trees. Their union is the boundary of the original triangle, while their intersection is one edge plus the remaining isolated vertex. Thus H_2(K,U)=Z and H_1(K,I)=Z. The interaction is detected by an isomorphism in the connecting map. It is not just an unexplained change in Betti numbers.

For more coordinates, iterating this sequence or using the usual Cech double complex of intersections gives higher-order bookkeeping. No new spectral sequence is claimed here, and introducing one is not recommended without an example or theorem unavailable from this two-coordinate sequence. Homological conclusions do not automatically become homotopical conclusions.

## A4. Direct relative collapse is equivalent to a unique fitting orientation in height two

For an arbitrary block thinning Q contained in P of height at most two, let B be the relative edge-triangle matrix. Its bipartite support graph has deleted edges on one side and deleted triangles on the other. A perfect matching is a fitting orientation.

**Theorem.** The following are equivalent:

1. K collapses directly to L by deleted edge-triangle pairs.
2. The support graph has an acyclic perfect matching.
3. The support graph has exactly one perfect matching.

The empty matrix has the single empty matching and corresponds to the identity collapse.

**Proof.** A collapse gives a complete acyclic matching. Relative acyclic matching gives a collapse, since all unmatched cells form the subcomplex L. Alternatively, this implication follows directly by topologically ordering matched pairs.

For a perfect matching, a directed cycle in the reversed incidence graph is exactly an alternating cycle. Flipping such a cycle produces a second perfect matching. Conversely, the symmetric difference of two perfect matchings is a disjoint union of alternating cycles. Thus a perfect matching is acyclic exactly when it is the unique perfect matching. For a direct free-face argument, orient dependencies from a matched edge to every other edge in its triangle. An acyclic dependency graph has a source with no occurrences in other matched triangles; that deleted edge is free. Recurse. QED.

**Scope.** This is stronger than v0.5's stated sufficient condition, but it is standard matching/discrete-Morse reasoning [R03,R19]. It does not say that every homotopy-equivalent inclusion collapses directly. The package's eight-state example has three perfect matchings, all cyclic, yet both endpoint posets are beat-contractible.

## A5. Explicit block torsion and a general construction

### General realization

Let X be a connected finite two-dimensional simplicial complex, P its nonempty face poset, and K=Delta(P)=sd(X). In the comparability graph of P, take the bipartite subgraph joining rank-zero faces to all incident positive-dimensional faces. It is connected. Choose a spanning tree in this graph and retain precisely its oriented comparisons as Q. It is a poset because it has only two levels, so no new transitivity requirements arise. L=Delta(Q) is a tree containing every vertex of K.

Since L is nonempty and contractible,

\[
H_k(K,L;\mathbb Z)\cong\widetilde H_k(X;\mathbb Z)\quad(k\ge1).
\]

The block-universality construction, with a(v)=down_Q(v), realizes Q as an observation thinning of P. Wedges of finite triangulated Moore spaces therefore realize arbitrary finite abelian relative H_1-torsion in height two. This is an adaptation of face-poset realization and standard relative homology, not a new existence theorem about torsion in complexes.

### A clean 13-state Z/2 example

Use the regular CW decomposition of RP2 obtained by quotienting the boundary of an octahedron by the antipodal involution. It has three vertices a,b,c, six edges AB+,AB-,AC+,AC-,BC+,BC-, and four triangular cells indexed by signs (s,t) in {+,-}^2. The boundary edges of cell (s,t) are AB_s, AC_t, BC_(st). Each cell contains all three vertices. The face poset P has 13 elements, 36 strict comparisons, and 24 three-element chains. A spanning-tree suborder Q retains twelve vertex-to-positive-cell comparisons.

The resulting relative matrix is 24 x 24, with Smith diagonal

\[
(1,\ldots,1,2),\quad |\det B|=2.
\]

Therefore H_1(K,L;Z)=Z/2 and H_2(K,L;Z)=0. Over F2, the relative Betti numbers in degrees 0,1,2 are (0,1,1); over F3 and F5 they are all zero.

The complete order, original principal-ideal labels, relative matrix, and Smith output are in `torsion2_RP2_13.json`. The conflict-coloring theorem A2 compresses this same Q to **exactly two bits**, with labels in the JSON vertex order

    (0,1,3,1,2,3,2,1,1,0,0,0,0).

Direct comparison of every P-pair verifies that these labels give exactly the same Q. A conflict edge rules out one bit. Thus this is already a **two-observation** torsion example. It is rationally (and F3-) homology-neutral but not F2-neutral, so any proposed two-bit preservation theorem must retain the F2 hypothesis. The compression and lower-bound certificate are in `torsion2_RP2_13_minimal_labels.json`. The underlying 13-point RP2 model belongs to established finite-space topology [R15]. This is not claimed to be the smallest arbitrary relative torsion pair: lower bounds on absolute torsion do not by themselves prove lower bounds for every relative pair. It is a small clean construction, and minimality holds only within the absolute-torsion/tree-target route if one invokes R15's thirteen-point lower bound.

### A 79-state Z/3 example invisible to F2 homology

Construct the simplicial mapping cone of a degree-three covering map from a 9-cycle to a 3-cycle. Denote the base vertices by v_j (j modulo 3), domain vertices by u_i (i modulo 9), and cone vertex by w. For every i, with j=i modulo 3, take the three triangles

\[
[u_i,v_j,v_{j+1}],\quad [u_i,u_{i+1},v_{j+1}],\quad[w,u_i,u_{i+1}].
\]

The complex has f-vector (13,39,27), with H_1=Z/3 and H_2=0. Its face poset has 79 points. Apply the same spanning-tree construction. The relative 162 x 162 matrix has Smith diagonal (1,...,1,3). Over F2 and F5 it is invertible; over F3 its relative Betti vector is (0,1,1).

Thus an observation block may be F2-homology-neutral but not integrally homology-neutral and hence not homotopy-neutral. This answers the coefficient-sensitivity question constructively. The example is explicit, reproducible, and not claimed minimal. Files: `torsion3_base_complex.json`, `torsion3_Moore_79.json`.

## A6. One bit already realizes arbitrary topology in higher height

Let R be any nonempty finite poset and choose a minimal element z. Add a new greatest element t, forming P=R union {t}. Define b(z)=b(t)=0 and b(x)=1 for all other x in R.

**Theorem.** The thinning Q retains all comparisons of R and precisely the extra comparison z<t. Therefore

\[
\Delta(P)=\operatorname{cone}(\Delta R),\qquad
\Delta(Q)=\Delta R\cup_{\{z\}}[z,t],
\]

and Delta(Q) collapses to Delta(R). In particular,

\[
\Delta Q\hookrightarrow\Delta P\text{ is a homotopy equivalence}
\iff\Delta R\text{ is contractible},
\]

and

\[
H_k(\Delta P,\Delta Q;\mathbb Z)
\cong\widetilde H_{k-1}(\Delta R;\mathbb Z)\quad(k\ge1).
\]

**Proof.** Since z is minimal, every old comparison is either 0->1 or 1->1 (besides identities); none is lost. All comparisons x<t with x!=z are 1->0 and are deleted. The comparison z<t survives. The top vertex makes Delta(P) a cone, and t is a leaf in Delta(Q). The relative formula follows from the long exact sequence and contractibility of the cone. QED.

**Consequences.**

- Unrestricted homotopy-neutrality of the order-complex map is undecidable already for one bit, non-splitting refinement, and a coarse poset with a greatest element. Take R to be the face poset of an input finite nonempty complex. The reduction is effective; the classical unrestricted contractibility theorem supplies the impossibility [R05]. This statement concerns order-complex homotopy equivalence, not an unqualified ordinary finite-space homotopy decision problem.
- Taking the 13-point RP2 model for R gives a 14-state, height-three, one-bit refinement with relative H_2=Z/2. Its F2 relative Betti vector is (0,0,1,1).
- Taking the 79-point Moore model gives an 80-state, height-three, one-bit refinement with relative H_2=Z/3. It is F2-homology-neutral but not integrally neutral. Its F3 vector is (0,0,1,1).
- Taking an acyclic noncontractible finite complex, such as a triangulated punctured Poincare homology sphere, gives integral homology-neutrality without homotopy-neutrality for one bit in a higher-height regime.

This is a sharp explanation of why v0.4 requires its height restriction. A universal one-bit acyclic 'first descent' matching cannot exist, even when the coarse complex is a cone. Proposed higher-height matching theorems must impose real extra hypotheses, not just a bounded/coarse-contractible endpoint.

The construction and its checks are in `higher_height_and_edges.py` and the two `onebit_height3_...json` files. Its ingredients are elementary; its specific refinement formulation remains a candidate adaptation rather than an established novelty claim.

# Corrections and patches

**Audit:** 24 September 2026. These are proposed replacements, not silently edited versions of the supplied manuscripts. Original files remain unchanged in the source snapshot. Claim IDs refer to `CLAIM_AUDIT_TABLE.csv`; proofs A1-A6 are in `AUDIT_ADDITIONS_AND_PROOFS.md`.

## Submission-blocking mathematical corrections

### C01. Delete the equality with classical 2-dimension

**Original:** v0.5, Proposition `prop:2dim`, TeX line 248: for a total coarse order P, odim_P(Q)=dim_2(Q).

**Verdict:** FALSE. This is structural, not a missing technical hypothesis.

Let P=Q be the two-element chain. No observation is needed, so odim_P(Q)=0, whereas classical Boolean-lattice embedding dimension is 1. Even forbidding the zero-coordinate example does not rescue the statement: if P is the two-chain x<y and Q the two-point antichain, one bit b(x)=1,b(y)=0 works, but the antichain needs Boolean-lattice dimension 2.

The failed proof forgets that P already blocks reverse ordered pairs. An observation label need not be injective or reflect every ordered pair, whereas an ordinary Boolean-lattice embedding must do both. The defect is not repaired by requiring positive k or nonredundancy.

**Replacement:** retain dim_2(Q) only as an upper bound. Put D={<_P comparisons absent from Q}. On D make demands (x,y),(u,v) adjacent exactly when x<=_Q v or u<=_Q y. Then

    odim_P(Q) = chromatic number of this conflict graph.

Equivalently, it is generalized Boolean rank of the matrix with zeros on Q, ones on P minus Q, and question marks elsewhere. Full proof: A2. Credit the generalized covering framework in R07-R08. Whether this precise restricted poset family has previously received a dedicated name remains unclear; do not market it as a wholly new dimension theory.

### C02. Withdraw the inherited total-order NP-completeness proof

**Original:** v0.5, “Complexity inheritance,” line 263, downstream of C01.

**Verdict:** NEEDS MAJOR REPAIR. The proof fails; this audit does not prove the asserted total-coarse-order restriction either true or false.

**Replacement proved in this audit:** given explicit finite relations Q subset P on the same vertex set and k, deciding odim_P(Q)<=k is NP-complete. Hardness holds already for k=3 and height(P)<=1. For a graph H, take minima a_i and maxima b_i; Q contains a_i<b_j for edges ij, and P additionally contains a_i<b_i. The demands' conflict graph is H. A certificate uses at most n coordinates, giving NP membership. This reduction is polynomial in the explicit relation input.

**Downstream impact:** the original proposed Paper C loses its foundational identification and its advertised restricted-hardness proof. No chain-topology, repair-forest, block-matrix, or interaction theorem depends on this equality; those branches survive. Replace ledger summaries and abstracts that say NP-completeness “inherits” from ordinary 2-dimension.

### C03. Repair the rooted-forest translation's missing rows

**Original:** v0.5, setup before Theorem `thm:rootedtranslation`, line 339: G is generated by the deleted triangles, and its nonroot edges are identified with all deleted edges.

**Problem:** a deleted edge need not lie in a triangle. For a two-chain with bit word 10, there is one deleted edge and no triangles. The original G is empty, but the actual relative matrix has one row and no columns. Thus the asserted general matrix identification is false as written.

**Minimal corrected setup:** take G to contain the **entire coarse one-skeleton**, together with precisely the deleted triangles, and let R contain all vertices and retained edges. Then the reduced boundary rows are exactly all deleted edges. Alternatively, explicitly detect unsupported deleted edges first and reject neutrality before using the triangle-generated G.

If the relative matrix is square and nonsingular, an unsupported deleted edge is impossible, so the main nonsingular/rooted-forest equivalence and the named neutral examples survive. This is a local setup repair, not a failure of the Bernardi-Klivans determinant theorem. For rectangular matrices, state the full kernel/cokernel rather than a determinant.

## Smaller mathematical and source repairs

### C04. Restore the missing v0.3 source

`ProLT_Controlled_Refinement_Regimes_v0.3.tex` is **zero bytes** in the supplied archive. Its 15-page PDF was readable and was audited. Restore the actual TeX before a source-level freeze; do not reconstruct it silently from a different version. The core is supplied only as PDF, so source-build reproducibility for it was not available either.

### C05. Qualify nonempty universality

v0.2 Theorem `thm:universality` and Corollary `cor:alltypes` should say nonempty finite poset/complex when the coarse quotient is a point on a nonempty carrier. A surjective signature map from a nonempty carrier cannot have empty image. Empty carriers may be handled separately; specify the convention for the void complex and reduced degree -1 homology. The undecidability reduction uses nonempty complexes and is unaffected.

### C06. State the current state carrier consistently

Use S subset Omega_P for an allowed current model set. A post-T0 carrier with n states need not be the entire 2^m-valuation space. Every finite example can be realized on a definable restricted carrier by minterms. For unrestricted full-carrier formulations, explicitly construct a suitable fiber realization or padded instance instead of assuming an arbitrary n is a power of two. This is particularly important for three-, five-, and thirteen-state examples. The finite-poset theorems themselves are unaffected.

### C07. Keep three different homotopy notions separate

The finite Kolmogorov quotient is an ordinary homotopy equivalence. McCord's realization map is a weak homotopy equivalence. The Quillen/Barmak results in v0.2 concern homotopy or simple-homotopy equivalence of **order complexes**; the source correctly states the simple version already. Beat-point contractibility of a finite poset is stronger than contractibility of its order complex. Do not replace order-complex contractibility with a beat-reduction test as an unrestricted equivalence.

The undecidability claim is about Delta(r), not ordinary homotopy equivalence of finite spaces. Finite-map homotopy is a finite combinatorial problem, so conflating those decision problems would materially misstate the result.

### C08. Fix the syzygy phrase in v0.1 Example B

For I=(x1*x2*x3), the quotient S/I has the standard minimal resolution

    0 -> S(-3) -> S -> S/I -> 0.

Hochster's formula records beta_(1,{1,2,3})(S/I)=1. This is the minimal generator of I as seen in the quotient resolution; the principal ideal itself has no nontrivial first module syzygy. Replace “unique first syzygetic/topological event” with this precise statement. The triangle-boundary homology and inconsistency-ideal calculations are correct.

### C09. Preserve Horn and semilattice hypotheses

v0.4's Horn/dual-Horn corollaries are valid **as qualified**. Keep the ambient realized meet/join-semilattice, restriction of the model/falsity set, and upper/lower cofinality assumptions. “Horn observations preserve homotopy” is not an acceptable abbreviated theorem. NOR on the full Boolean square already illustrates how a plausible Boolean fragment slogan can fail without the right anchor conditions.

### C10. Specify normalized induced chain maps

A monotone map may identify vertices of a simplex. In the normalized simplicial chain complex the image of that simplex is zero when degenerate. This is standard and does not invalidate v0.1 functoriality, but should be written in the implementation contract. An unqualified formula that always sends a k-chain to a k-chain of distinct vertices would be wrong.

### C11. Preserve metric monotonicity hypotheses

Retain old weights and only add nonnegative new weights when asserting d_new>=d_old. Renormalization can violate this: a pair at old distance 1 can have distance 1/2 after adding a constant observation and averaging over both coordinates. Its edge then enters, rather than leaves, a fixed-scale Rips complex. Indexed weights and duplicate observations are presentation data, not topology invariants.

### C12. Clarify the information lost by relative groups

U and G are well-defined relative homology of model-signature restrictions, not complete invariants of premise semantics or entailment. If the only observation family is empty on two distinct valuations, a proper nonempty premise restriction may leave the same singleton signature poset. All relative groups vanish although the premise removed a valuation. Likewise, zero inference-gap homology does not imply semantic entailment.

The actual signature-difference cochain is exact by definition. Nonzero H1 integration obstructions arise for independently prescribed local edge data, as in v0.1 Example E, not from the genuine signature differences themselves.

### C13. Correct scope of combinatorial computations

Rename the last height-two repair-forest CSV column to make explicit that it counts **nonredundant neutral** cases. Redundant profiles also give the empty rooted forest. Report fixed-natural-linear-extension enumeration, not all labelled posets or one representative per isomorphism class. Preserve successful run limits; the attempted six-state two-bit extension did not finish and contributes no exhaustive result.

Rename Betti-only variables/reports labelled “homotopy” to “homology” unless a separate collapse/beat/fundamental-group argument is actually used. Keep -O disabled, since the supplied and independent scripts use assertions.

## Strengthenings worth incorporating, without claiming new general machinery

A1 extends the height-two one-bit theorem integrally and computes both relative groups from a rooted graph; all such relative homology is torsion-free. A3 replaces unexplained two-coordinate interaction with relative Mayer-Vietoris. A4 upgrades unique fitting orientation from sufficient to equivalent to direct relative collapse in the two-layer setting. A5 supplies explicit coefficient-sensitive block counterexamples. A6 shows that height three already admits one-bit torsion and that one-bit refinement has unrestricted higher-height universality.

These are separate audit additions. Cite their actual proofs and established ingredients rather than declaring the original notes to have already proved them.

## Suggested compact replacement theorem statement

Let P be a finite poset with no chain of four elements, let b:P->{0,1}, and define x<=_Q y iff x<=_P y and b(x)<=b(y). Write K=Delta(P), L=Delta(Q). Then the integral relative boundary from deleted triangles to deleted edges is a reduced oriented graph-incidence matrix. Consequently, the following are equivalent: L->K is a homotopy equivalence; it is a simple-homotopy equivalence; K collapses to L; it induces homology isomorphisms over any one field; it induces integral homology isomorphisms; and every component of the associated incidence graph is a tree with exactly one designated root. The complete relative integral homology is free, with ranks equal to the rootless-component count in degree one and cycle rank in degree two.

This is the strongest clean theorem to carry into the focused manuscript. Its general mathematics is graph incidence plus relative collapse; its contribution claim must concern the exact binary order-thinning characterization.

# Literature sources and search record

Audit date: 24 September 2026. The identifiers below are used throughout the reports and claim table. URLs are included for independent checking. A title in this list does **not** mean that every result in that source was audited. Access scope is stated explicitly. This was a web-based primary-literature investigation, not a MathSciNet/Zentralblatt subscription search or a certified exhaustive novelty search.

## R01. Finite-space realization
Michael C. McCord, *Singular homology groups and homotopy groups of finite topological spaces*, Duke Mathematical Journal 33 (1966), 465-474. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1215/S0012-7094-66-03352-7 . Bibliographic entry and the relevant realization theorem were checked through R02. McCord's realization map is a **weak** homotopy equivalence. The finite Kolmogorov-quotient equivalence also has the elementary representative-section proof given in the master report; do not attribute an ordinary equivalence between every finite space and its order-complex realization to McCord.

## R02. Poset fibers, comparable maps, and Dowker duality
Jonathan A. Barmak, *On Quillen's Theorem A for posets*, Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A 118 (2011), 2445-2453. https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.0538 ; inspected full HTML: https://arxiv.org/html/1005.0538v1 . Exact overlaps: Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 (principal lower-fiber criterion and simple-homotopy strengthening), Proposition 2.2 (pointwise comparable monotone maps), Theorem 4.4 (Dowker duality, even simple type), and Theorem 5.4/Corollary 5.5 (homological versions). Dual upper-fiber versions follow by reversing orders. The paper's convention for lower-set topology must not silently replace the core's upper-set convention.

Related background: J. A. Barmak and E. G. Minian, *Simple homotopy types and finite spaces*, Advances in Mathematics 218 (2008), 87-104; located in R02's bibliography. This related paper was not independently read in full during this audit.

## R03. Higher-dimensional rooted forests and fitting orientations
Olivier Bernardi and Caroline J. Klivans, *Directed rooted forests in higher dimension*, Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 23(4) (2016), P4.35. DOI: https://doi.org/10.37236/5819 . https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.07757 ; inspected HTML and selected PDF pages: https://arxiv.org/html/1512.07757v4 . Exact overlaps: definitions of rooted forests and fitting orientations; Lemmas 14 and 17 on reduced boundary determinants/relative homology; Proposition 30 on the signed fitting-orientation expansion. These are the established objects underlying v0.5, not independent ProLT inventions.

## R04. Total unimodularity and relative torsion
Tamal K. Dey, Anil N. Hirani, and Bala Krishnamoorthy, *Optimal homologous cycles, total unimodularity, and linear programming*, SIAM Journal on Computing 40(4) (2011), 1026-1044. https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.0338 ; inspected https://arxiv.org/html/1001.0338v3 . Theorem 5.2 connects total unimodularity of boundary matrices with torsion-freeness for suitable relative pairs. Graph-incidence total unimodularity is considerably more elementary; the audit gives its direct proof rather than pretending that a new general TU theorem is needed.

## R05. Contractibility undecidability
Martin Tancer, *Recognition of collapsible complexes is NP-complete*, Discrete & Computational Geometry 55 (2016), 21-38. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00454-015-9747-1 . https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.6254 ; inspected Appendix A, Theorem 11 and its proof/discussion in the PDF. The stated safe form is undecidability of contractibility for finite complexes of dimension at most d, for every d >= 5. The appendix discusses a dimension-four strengthening. The audit needs only the d >= 5 form; it makes no claim about the present status of every lower-dimensional recognition problem. This is an effective undecidability reduction, not an NP-hardness reduction requiring compact formula encodings.

## R06. Classical poset 2-dimension
Michel Habib, Lhouari Nourine, Olivier Raynaud, and Eric Thierry, *Computational aspects of the 2-dimension of partially ordered sets*, Theoretical Computer Science 312 (2004), 401-431. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tcs.2003.10.029 . Primary institutional record: https://hal-lirmm.ccsd.cnrs.fr/lirmm-00108552 . Paper text was inspected in an author-paper copy at https://www.academia.edu/19100821/Computational_aspects_of_the_2_dimension_of_partially_ordered_sets . Definition: an order embedding into a Boolean lattice must preserve and reflect **all ordered pairs**. Theorem 17 and Corollary 18 give the relevant NP-completeness result. They do not establish the package's false equality with relative observation dimension.

## R07. Generalized Boolean rank and covering graphs
Reka Agnes Kovacs, *On Minimally Non-Firm Binary Matrices*, ISCO 2022. https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04089 ; inspected https://arxiv.org/html/2206.04089v1 , especially Section 2. Generalized matrices have entries 0, 1, and question marks; rectangles must avoid zeros and cover all ones, while question marks need not be covered. The section also gives the associated covering-graph formulation. This is an exact existing optimization framework for the corrected observation-design parameter. R07 attributes the generalized formulation to R08.

## R08. Earlier generalized Boolean basis problem
Anna Lubiw, *The boolean basis problem and how to cover some polygons by rectangles*, SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics 3(1) (1990), 98-115. Located through R07, reference 13. The original paper was not obtained in full. Therefore the audit attributes the framework via the inspected R07 account; it does not claim to have verified a particular theorem number in Lubiw's original paper.

## R09. Ferrers-graph prior art for chain profiles
Anders Claesson, Sergey Kitaev, Kari Ragnarsson, and Bridget Eileen Tenner, *Boolean complexes for Ferrers graphs*, 2010 version. https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.2307 ; inspected https://arxiv.org/html/0808.2307v3 . Its introduction announces that the independence complex of a Ferrers graph has the simple homotopy type of two points in the rectangular case and a point otherwise. The cited source is Richard Ehrenborg and Sergey Kitaev, *Ferrers graphs, their independent sets and independence complexes*, listed **in preparation**. Repeated title/author searches did not locate that underlying proof. Thus there is strong prior-art overlap with the chain homotopy classification, but the original proof's publication status remains unresolved.

Important: the **Boolean complex** studied in the body of R09 is not the **independence complex** used in our translation. The relevance is the explicit introduction statement about the latter, not an identification of these two constructions. Isolated-vertex cases in the chain translation are handled by the elementary cone observation.

## R10. Boolean functions and order/relative complexes
Anders Bjorner, Mark Goresky, and Robert MacPherson, *Topological aspects of Boolean functions*, Pure and Applied Mathematics Quarterly 20(3) (2024), 1029-1063. Author-hosted primary paper: https://www.math.ias.edu/~goresky/pdf/BooleanPAMQ.pdf . Inspected Sections 2-3 and relevant later discussion, including PDF images. Section 2.5 explicitly uses the order complex of true Boolean vectors; Section 3 uses relative homology of associated pairs. This is significant prior art against broad claims that associating order or relative homology to Boolean data is new. It is not an exact theorem about every observation-refinement map in the package.

## R11. SAT/hypergraph topology
James Conant and Oliver Thistlethwaite, *Boolean formulae, hypergraphs and combinatorial topology*. https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.0739 ; inspected https://arxiv.org/html/0808.0739v2 . Proposition 1 identifies the theta complex with the Alexander dual of an independence complex; Theorems 1-2 describe the resulting dualities. These are different constructions from the positive-observation compatibility nerve, but they are essential comparison literature before claiming a new topology of satisfiability or inconsistency.

## R12. Formal contexts, hypergraphs, and Dowker structures
Robert E. Green, Cliff A. Joslyn, Audun Myers, Michael G. Rawson, and Michael Robinson, *The Topological Structures of the Orders of Hypergraphs* (2025). https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.11760 . Abstract and metadata inspected. The paper explicitly relates binary relations, hypergraphs, formal contexts, orders, and Dowker constructions. This is a verified nearby research connection, not a claim that every theorem in the paper was checked or that it proves the package's refinement results.

## R13. Rough-set attribute reduction
Yiyu Yao and Yan Zhao, *Discernibility matrix simplification for constructing attribute reducts*, Information Sciences 179(5) (2009), 867-882. Author-hosted paper: https://www2.cs.uregina.ca/~yyao/PAPERS/is_reduct_construction.pdf . Relevant search-indexed primary text and bibliographic data inspected; not a page-by-page audit. Fixed-family attribute reducts lead to discernibility covers/hitting-set formulations. The package permits designing arbitrary new Q-upsets, which is a different feasible family. The exact link is to separation/covering, not an automatic equivalence to every rough-set reduct problem.

## R14. Persistent Quillen-McCord theory
Vitalii Guzeev and Kohei Tanaka, *Quillen-McCord theorem for persistence finite posets* (12 May 2026). https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11615 ; inspected https://arxiv.org/html/2605.11615v1 . Theorem 3.8 concerns finite-type filtrations and an interleaving bound under persistent fiber hypotheses, in an appropriate weak-equivalence/localized setting. The package's reference to this recent work is genuine. A two-parameter filtration constructed merely by inclusions is not itself this quantitative theorem.

## R15. Small finite models and torsion
Nicolas Cianci and Miguel Ottina, *Poset splitting and minimality of finite models* (2015 preprint). https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.06088 ; inspected https://arxiv.org/html/1512.06088v1 . Theorem 5.7 treats small fundamental groups; Theorem 5.9 gives a thirteen-point lower bound for finite spaces with torsion homology. The thirteen-point projective-plane model is established prior art. Absolute-torsion lower bounds do not automatically prove minimality for all relative torsion pairs.

## R16. Cohomology of contextuality
Samson Abramsky, Shane Mansfield, and Rui Soares Barbosa, *The Cohomology of Non-Locality and Contextuality* (2012). https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.3620 . Abstract and relevant primary text inspected. The obstruction uses measurement-support/presheaf data. It is not identical to the constant-coefficient equation delta(lambda) on a signature order complex. Calling a signature coboundary an obstruction to contextuality would require an additional construction and proof.

## R17. Zigzag persistence
Gunnar Carlsson and Vin de Silva, *Zigzag Persistence*, Foundations of Computational Mathematics 10 (2010), 367-405. https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.0197 . Relevant primary abstract/text inspected, including interval-decomposition and examples. Changing directions in an indexed diagram justify zigzag methods. Merely mentioning both observation and premise changes does not determine whether a particular diagram is ordinary, multiparameter, or zigzag persistence.

## R18. Relative homology, cones, and Mayer-Vietoris
Allen Hatcher, *Algebraic Topology*, Cambridge University Press, 2002. Official free-book page: https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/ATpage.html . Chapters 2-3 are the standard background. The audit independently writes out the relative chain short exact sequence used for interaction, so no uninspected theorem-number claim is needed.

## R19. Discrete Morse theory
Robin Forman, *Morse Theory for Cell Complexes*, Advances in Mathematics 134 (1998), 90-145. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1006/aima.1997.1650 . Primary-paper copy: https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/forman5.pdf . Relevant primary text located. Complete relative acyclic matchings and elementary collapses are standard machinery. The audit gives a direct alternating-cycle/free-face proof for the two-layer special case.

## R20. Boolean closure properties
Peter Jeavons, David A. Cohen, and Marc Gyssens, *Closure properties of constraints*, Journal of the ACM 44(4) (1997), 527-548. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1145/263867.263489 . Institutional primary record: https://documentserver.uhasselt.be/handle/1942/6848 . Metadata/abstract inspected. Horn model sets are meet-closed and dual-Horn model sets join-closed, with the usual finite Boolean-domain conventions. The observation-preservation statements additionally require the ambient realized semilattice and cofinality hypotheses; closure properties alone do not prove preservation.

## R21. Relative homotopy of relational structures
P. J. Witbooi, *Relative Homotopy in Relational Structures*. Author-hosted primary paper: https://math.uchicago.edu/~may/PEOPLE/Witbooi/witbooi8825.pdf . Theorem 5.3 was located in indexed primary text; venue/year not verified. It treats relative homotopy in relational/poset settings. This is nearby established language, not an exact identification of the package's mapping-cone invariant.

## R22. A recent terminology collision, not an equivalence
Dominik Durrschnabel, Jedrzej Hodor, Piotr Micek, Gerd Stumme, and William T. Trotter, *Relative Dimension of Posets* (September 2026). https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.05166 ; inspected https://arxiv.org/html/2609.05166v1 , Section 1.4. Its relative dimension uses a different realizer-based concept. It does **not** define odim_P(Q). It is a reason to avoid the unqualified title 'Relative Dimension of Posets', not evidence that the two parameters are equal.

## Search coverage and unresolved literature questions

Queries were organized by mathematical equivalence, not just ProLT terminology: finite T0 quotients/McCord; principal-fiber versus point-fiber theorems; deleting poset comparabilities; binary words/Ferrers independence complexes; rooted incidence forests and relative collapses; Horn/dual-Horn closure; poset 2-dimension/Boolean-lattice embeddings; generalized Boolean basis and question-mark matrices; attribute reducts/discernibility; Boolean-function and SAT/hypergraph topology; Dowker/formal-context topology; persistence and persistent Quillen theorems; constant-coefficient integration versus contextuality; and minimal finite-space torsion.

The major unresolved bibliographic issue is the Ehrenborg-Kitaev independence-complex paper announced in R09. The exact restricted observation-design problem for a prescribed total coarse order was not identified with a verified published complexity theorem. No exact earlier theorem was located with all of the one-bit height-two order-thinning hypotheses and collapse equivalences together. These are **limits of the search**, not positive novelty evidence.

No databases, papers, or private referee opinions are represented as consulted unless described above. No claim of an independent human review panel or formal proof-assistant verification is made.

# Next research program: one active theorem, two bounded follow-ups

## Immediate prerequisite, not a research branch

Apply the correction register and freeze an auditable baseline. Restore the empty v0.3 TeX; remove the false 2-dimension equality and total-order hardness proof; repair the rooted-forest row support; attach exact execution instructions and certificate files. Do not start another expansive mathematical continuation before this baseline exists.

## Priority 1 — the only active mathematical target

### Exact question

Let P be a finite poset of height at most two and a:P->{0,1}^2. Let Q retain exactly the P-comparisons whose labels are coordinatewise ordered. If Delta(Q)->Delta(P) induces an isomorphism on F2 homology, must Delta(P) collapse directly to Delta(Q)?

Equivalent matrix form: must every invertible F2 relative deleted-edge/deleted-triangle matrix arising from a **two-bit** label admit a unique perfect matching?

### Why this is the highest-value question

One bit gives the proved rooted-incidence theorem. Three bits admit the independently verified eight-state counterexample with determinant one and three cyclic matchings. All two-bit profiles through five vertices passed the stronger direct-collapse property. Thus this is a sharply defined boundary between a complete theorem and a known failure, not an open-ended hunt for more examples.

The five-vertex evidence covers 337,920 profiles; it is evidence, not a conjecture proof. Exact conflict-coloring shows that the existing eight-state pair needs three bits, so simple relabelling cannot settle the question. The thirteen-state Z/2 torsion witness already uses two bits and disproves the rational-homology version: the F2 assumption is essential. The six-vertex two-bit attempt timed out and adds no coverage.

### Machinery and attack plan

Exploit the four-label diamond structure rather than treating B as an arbitrary matrix. Classify the possible label patterns on deleted triangles, their signed supports, and how alternating cycles can propagate through transitive coarse orders. An invertible matrix with multiple perfect matchings is the exact obstruction. Compare the resulting support restrictions with total balance, sign-nonsingularity, and discrete-Morse dependency graphs, crediting existing matrix theory rather than renaming it.

For counterexample search, encode transitivity, height<=2, two-bit labels, square relative cell counts, invertibility, and an alternating cycle. Use symmetry reduction on label classes and poset isomorphisms. Export any candidate as an explicit relation list and integer boundary matrix; validate it with the independent checker. A computational search result without a compact certificate is insufficient.

### Falsification strategy

Try to compress the known three-bit eight-state example into four labels without changing its critical deleted incidences. Separately construct cyclic matching supports allowed by two-bit triangle types, then ask whether those supports are realizable by a transitive poset. This separates the algebraic obstruction from the realization obstruction.

### Stopping criterion

Stop when there is either (a) a complete structural proof, or (b) an explicit verified counterexample and an explanation of the mechanism. If neither is reached within a fixed, predeclared search/theorem-development budget, freeze the statement as a conjecture with the existing n<=5 evidence. Do not automatically increase vertex bounds indefinitely. The article can still be written around the proved one-bit theorem and the three-bit limit.

### Destination

Preferred Paper A sharpness section; if the result is sufficiently substantial, it supplies the missing central theorem for conditional Paper B.

## Priority 2 — certification and minimization, after Priority 1 stops

### Exact question

Can the key counterexamples be given short, independent certificates with reduced observation counts, and which minimality claims can actually be proved?

### Why it matters

The 13-state Z/2 block has now been compressed to exactly two bits, and the eight-state noncollapse pair provably needs three. The 79-state Z/3 labels are not optimized. Minimum **vertex counts** for the relevant relative pairs remain unresolved. Smaller or better-certified examples improve exposition; vague claims of “smallest” would hurt credibility.

### Machinery

Exact Smith normal forms, conflict-graph coloring for label minimization, finite-poset symmetries, and explicit spanning-tree/regular-CW constructions. R15's absolute torsion lower bound applies to the tree-target route, not automatically every relative pair.

### Falsification and stopping

Test the claimed minimum only within an explicitly stated family. Stop once the existing examples have a second independently written certificate checker and, at most, one successful simplification. Do not pursue global minimum-state torsion across all relative poset pairs unless a separate structural bound appears. This is a finite quality-improvement task, not a new paper by itself.

### Destination

Supplement or short examples section of Paper A/B.

## Priority 3 — conditional dimension problem, not active in parallel

### Exact question

For Q contained in a **specified total coarse order** P, characterize the conflict graphs on deleted comparisons. Is this graph class algorithmically tractable for coloring, or does it realize a known hard class?

### Why it matters

It is the exact unresolved restriction left behind by the false v0.5 2-dimension equality. The corrected general problem is already a generalized Boolean rectangle-cover problem and is NP-complete at height one. A nontrivial special-family theorem is what could justify a dimension paper.

### Machinery

Generalized Boolean rank, directed separation demands, interval/overlap representations, graph coloring and perfect-graph criteria, and exact poset transitivity constraints. Do not assume the conflict graph is an interval graph, Ferrers graph, or perfect graph; each needs proof or a counterexample.

### Falsification and stopping

Enumerate small target suborders of a fixed chain and seek forbidden induced subgraphs of candidate tractable classes. Any proposed equivalence must be checked against both two-vertex counterexamples to classical dim2. Stop if the family is identified with existing literature without a new useful corollary; document the established name and keep this as a technical note. Activate only after Priority 1 is resolved or frozen.

### Destination

Conditional Paper C; otherwise corrected technical note.

## Do not reopen now

Premise/inference-gap homology, Stanley-Reisner syzygies, generic persistence, higher-order Cech interaction machinery, broad Horn/affine/bijunctive classification, and mental-space applications remain deferred. They may be reopened only with a precise theorem or data problem not already covered by the frozen foundations. The one-bit higher-height universality theorem rules out an unrestricted complete descent matching; any proposed generalization must add genuine structural hypotheses.

## Explicit decision rule

At the end of Priority 1, choose a paper boundary and write. A proved specialization with an honest prior-art section is more valuable than indefinitely expanding a catalogue of connections. New attractive directions go into the frozen register, not into the active queue.
