# Paper U v0.2 — fresh hostile priority review

Review date and literature cutoff: **29 September 2026**. This is a fresh analytical review by a separate model agent, not independent human peer review. The inherited priority map supplied leads; its conclusions were not accepted as evidence. Primary passages were reopened and compared with the present theorem contracts. Search is bounded, English-language, and not an exhaustive certification of priority. Dates returned by search engines as “published” were not accepted without primary metadata.

## Verdict

The manuscript survives this priority review **as a short synthesis/correction note**, subject to accurate source verification elsewhere in this review and the three citation repairs below. Original mathematical research novelty is **not established**. No basis was found for reinstating earlier claims to a new observation/latent-state architecture, a new partition topology, or a new general reconstruction theory.

There is a concrete reason to keep the note: it prevents four distinct mistakes in one explicit setting—confusing ultrametric similarity with indistinguishability, treating every collapse as metric, identifying completion with an incomplete starting space, and forming a quotient group from an arbitrary finite-index refinement. That is a defensible expository purpose. Its value is conditional on an audience that encounters those errors. Correct elementary mathematics alone would not justify a research-paper submission.

## Findings requiring or supporting repair

### P1. Add the exact fixed-scale quotient predecessor

The published paper by **Mémoli, Smith and Wan (2023), §2.1, equation (5), Definition 10, printed p.87**, gives precisely the closed-radius equivalence relation and the quotient distance retained between distinct classes. This is a direct mathematical predecessor for Paper U's threshold quotients. It was absent from v0.2's bibliography. The 2021 preprint uses Definition 9; citing that number against the journal publication would be wrong.

Verified journal record: [Journal of Computational Geometry 14(1), 78–143](https://jocg.org/index.php/jocg/article/view/3706), DOI [10.20382/jocg.v14i1a4](https://doi.org/10.20382/jocg.v14i1a4). The [published PDF](https://jocg.org/index.php/jocg/article/download/3706/3365/13424) contains the checked passage.

Recommended insertion at the tower setup: “The quotient metrics are the $t$-closed quotients of Mémoli, Smith and Wan [§2.1, equation (5), Definition 10], with $t=r_k$.” Their definition allows any ultrametric space and $t\geq0$; finiteness here follows separately from total boundedness and positive radius. This repairs attribution, not a false theorem.

### P2. State the Ishiki specialization explicitly

[Ishiki, arXiv:2302.00305v3](https://arxiv.org/html/2302.00305v3), Definition 2.2 and Proposition 2.31, permits continuous **pseudo**-ultrametrics inside disjoint clopen pieces. Take the finite index set to be the cells, its ultrametric to be $\delta_{\mathcal P}$, range set $[0,\infty)$, and all internal pseudo-ultrametrics to be zero. His construction is then exactly $d_{\mathcal P}$. The additional “pleasant” hypothesis concerns genuine compatible internal metrics and is unnecessary here. Proposition 2.32 concerns density and is not needed for this specialization.

Recommended replacement: “The collapse is a special case of Ishiki’s pseudo-ultrametric amalgamation [Proposition 2.31], taking every within-cell pseudo-ultrametric to be zero.” Paper U's inter-ball lemma still supplies representative independence and agreement with the original cross-cell distances. This is more exact attribution than “closely related.”

### P3. Tighten the Kleiner locator

[Kleiner's 2020 text](https://arxiv.org/html/1907.03223v2) develops the automorphism-orbit relation and quotient in **§3.3, equations (3.3)–(3.8)**. Section 3.4 interprets the resulting accessible references. Change “Section 3.4” to “Sections 3.3–3.4.” The underlying attribution is substantively correct. The source concerns intersubjective relabelling/non-collatability, not the same cognitive mechanism or same finite-resolution metric construction as Paper U.

## Theorem-level assessment

| Paper U ingredient | Fresh comparison | Classification |
|---|---|---|
| Partition topology; indistinguishability classes | [Iyer–Shrivastava 2012](https://ijpam.eu/contents/2012-74-3/3/3.pdf), Definition 1, printed p.313, defines topology from partition blocks as a basis | Established construction |
| Kolmogorov and metric identification | [Pirttimäki 2019](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.01157), Theorem 5.3, printed p.18, identifies the zero-distance metric quotient with the quotient topology | Established theorem; exact locator correct |
| Finite adaptive ball collapse | P2 above applies to general disjoint clopen cells once a cross-cell ultrametric is specified | Standard construction specialized to ball geometry |
| Greatest dominated collapsing pseudometric | Once admissibility of the displayed collapse is proved, maximality follows pointwise: every competitor is zero inside cells and at most the original distance outside | Immediate extremal corollary, not evidence of separate novelty |
| Calibrated finite quotient tower | P1 above plus elementary uniform-error and nested-partition arguments | Standard threshold quotient with explicit calibration |
| Inverse limit / completion | [Stacks tag 08ZY](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08ZY), Lemma 5.22.2, proves the compact Hausdorff totally disconnected / finite-discrete-limit correspondence. [Dovgoshey 2025](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.04228v1), Theorem 10.25, identifies isometric completions through labelled representing trees | Standard topology plus a proved metric identification; no new general reconstruction theorem |
| Tree/end-space representation | [Hughes 2004 author PDF](https://math.vanderbilt.edu/hughescb/Publications/2004_Trees.pdf), Theorem 6.9 and the introductory category descriptions | Much broader categorical context with specified morphisms; manuscript's cautious statement is appropriate |
| Frontier expansions and refinement | [Lawson–Vdovina](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.13254), §12, Lemma 12.1, treats expansions of maximal generalized prefix codes; ordinary free-monoid prefix codes are a specialization | Standard prefix-code combinatorics |
| Full-tree sections and stabilizers | [Bartholdi–Grigorchuk–Šunić, Branch Groups](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0510294v2), §§1.2.2–1.2.3: local permutation portraits, level transitivity, section homomorphisms, and full-group product decomposition | Standard ingredients for Paper U's adaptive theorem |
| Adaptive exact normality criterion | No exact prior named statement was located by the searches logged separately; the short argument below derives it from the preceding ingredients | Useful explicit corollary; priority unresolved, originality unsupported |
| Index versus entropy | Counting allowed local permutations has no probability weights; a Shannon chain-rule sum does. Their numerical disagreement is expected | Clarification, not a new information theory |

The source is not treated as an infallible authority: for example, the Branch Groups HTML has an overbroad sentence about arbitrary subgroup stabilizers being normal in the ambient automorphism group. The full-automorphism-group facts used here are independently evident and are the applicable part of its discussion.

## Independent reconstruction of the adaptive priority target

Write $A=\operatorname{Aut}(T_m)$. Fixing the finite frontier pointwise fixes the entire finite upper skeleton. Each remaining descendant tree supports an arbitrary independent element of $A$, so $G_F=\prod_{s\in F} A_s$. Replacing one leaf by its $m$ children imposes exactly one local permutation constraint, with index $m!$. There are exactly $|I(F')\setminus I(F)|$ such constraints. Multiplication of indices is legitimate even when the final subgroup is not normal.

For normality, first observe that the $G_{F'}$-orbits on the boundary are exactly the frontier cylinders. If $G_{F'}\triangleleft G_F$, these orbits are permuted by $G_F$. Inside a fixed old cell $C_s$, the full section $A_s$ is transitive on every relative level. Therefore, if one frontier cylinder occurs at depth $h$, all cylinders at that relative depth occur. Prefix freeness and completeness rule out any other depth in that subtree. Conversely, a full relative level is the kernel of a finite-tree restriction homomorphism. The product of these kernels over old cells is normal, with the stated finite-tree product quotient.

This argument proves correctness under the stated contract and explains why an exact citation may be hard to locate: it is an elementary consequence of customary machinery, not an independently developed general theory. “Not found” must not be converted into “first proved here.”

A direct independent obstruction is $F=\{\varnothing\}$, $F'=\{0,10,11\}$ in the binary tree. A root swap sends this frontier to $\{1,00,01\}$, changing its pointwise stabilizer. By contrast $F=\{0,1\}$, $F'=\{00,01,1\}$ does give a normal inclusion: relative depths may differ between different old cells. Pointwise versus setwise is essential; replacing one by the other changes the groups and the count.

## Required cognitive predecessors rechecked

[Khrennikov 2007](https://arxiv.org/html/q-bio/0610013v3), §4, explicitly introduces associations as equivalence classes and writes their fixed-prefix descriptions. Thus “concepts as prefix classes” cannot be presented as Paper U's new cognitive idea. The source's dynamical assumptions are additional; they do not supply the entire present quotient theorem.

[Khrennikov–Yurova 2017](https://arxiv.org/html/1704.04681v1), §4, identifies states whose outputs agree for all inputs, constructs the factor-state set, and requires transition compatibility. Section 9 then uses an ultrametric/p-adic latent state model. This confirms a substantive latent-state / restricted-observation / quotient predecessor. It is not an assertion that every output-equivalence class is a metric ball, nor a proof of arbitrary adaptive-frontier dynamics.

These checks support v0.2's narrowed claims. They do not validate its empirical or psychoanalytic interpretation. Primary Matte-Blanco and Lauro-Grotto source fidelity is reviewed in the separate historical workstream.

## Recent literature and access limits

* [Dovgoshey, 6 February 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.04228), Theorem 10.25, is directly relevant as above. Its hypotheses are nonempty totally bounded ultrametric spaces; its conclusion concerns isometric **completions**, not necessarily isometric original spaces.
* [Bartoš–Kubiś–Kwiatkowska–Malicki, v2, 16 June 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.13608v2), §§2.2–2.3, uses two-sorted distance-carrying structures, ball trees, and Cauchy chains. Its morphisms may change the distance sort. It supplies current representation context, not a discovered statement of Paper U's adaptive criterion.
* [Martino, 29 July 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.26644v1), Proposition 3.7, reconstructs a locally finite rooted tree from nested finite clopen equivalence relations encoded by an admissible overlap function. Its §5 concerns automorphism-invariant refinements of finitely generated weakly branch actions. This is relevant recent reconstruction/refinement work, but a different contract from normality of two full-group frontier stabilizers.
* [Xin Li, March 2026](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.03362v1), §3.1, discusses contextual indexing and metric dynamics; the inspected passages do not supply the finite-ball quotient theorem. Do not cite merely for similar vocabulary.
* [Anagnostopoulou-Merkouri, Bailey and Cameron](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.10461v2), on permutation groups and partition lattices, supplies block-structure context. The inspected normal-subgroup passages did not state the exact frontier criterion.
* The [2010 category-as-ball article](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1134/S2070046610010012) and the [2017 topological-unconscious article](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1134/S2070046617010071) still exposed only subscription previews/abstracts. Their unseen contents were not ruled out. The 1997 book chapter and final 2014 cognitive article were not newly obtained in this pass.
* Search-only leads, including ideal-subgroup normality in Sylow tree groups and recent observation-framework preprints, were not promoted to verified theorem matches.

No coverage is claimed after 29 September 2026. No source-access gap proves priority. These gaps do not veto an explicitly non-priority synthesis, but they would veto a “first topological repair” or “first adaptive normality theorem” claim.

## Publication-fit judgment

The eight-page form is coherent if the abstract and introduction identify a practical conceptual correction, and the theorem displays are understood as a reusable worked synthesis. A pure topology or tree-group research audience would reasonably find the mathematical contribution too elementary. A foundations/modeling/expository audience may find the separation of geometry, observation, symmetry, and information useful. No specific journal policy or likelihood of acceptance has been verified.

For the overall scorecard, this workstream recommends: **attribution passes after P1–P3; original research novelty remains unestablished; contribution fit passes only for the explicitly narrowed note and suitable audience**. Historical source fidelity and all mathematical/reproducibility vetoes must be decided separately. Do not let a numeric aggregate override a failure in those gates.

Next required action in the parent review: apply P1–P3, reconcile the separate proof and source audits, and then decide submission readiness. No additional priority search is required for the present non-priority claim; reopen it if stronger novelty language is proposed.

# Publication-readiness scorecard: v0.3

Assessment date: 29 September 2026. Form being assessed: **short synthesis/correction note**, not a new mathematical theory, a clinical study, or an original topology/group-theory research paper. Final PDF: nine pages including references. These are ordinal editorial judgments by AI review roles, not acceptance probabilities or independent human referee scores.

## Independent veto gates

| Gate | Decision | Evidence and limits |
|---|---|---|
| Mathematical correctness | **PASS after local repairs** | Every mathematical environment and substantive appendix/entropy assertion reconstructed. Explicit ultrametric hypotheses and the completion-map continuity step repaired. Separate cross-check found no remaining substantive gap. Finite computations do not substitute for the proofs. |
| Contribution fit | **PASS for the specified note form only** | The useful purpose is to prevent specific conflations of geometry, observation, completion, symmetry and information. Standard mechanisms and an exact adaptive boundary make a coherent worked clarification. This gate would fail if the same manuscript were offered as a substantial new general theory. No target journal's current policy has yet been selected or verified. |
| Attribution / priority | **PASS for non-priority claims** | Direct Mémoli–Smith–Wan predecessor added; Ishiki overlap strengthened; Kleiner locator repaired; required cognitive predecessors freshly checked. Bounded literature search includes 2026 sources through September 29. Exact adaptive criterion priority remains unresolved. No first-use or first-correction claim is authorized by this assessment. |
| Source fidelity | **PASS for retained limited claims** | All ten requested Matte-Blanco pages visually checked in the authorized Routledge reprint; consulted edition identified; external-observer qualification restored. Lauro-Grotto's perceptual analogy credited from author-posted text. No physical-1975-copy collation or fresh Lauro-Grotto page-image collation is claimed. |

No unresolved veto remains for the *specified content and publication form*. A change of claims, hypotheses, source interpretation or venue expectations can reopen a gate. Scores below cannot overrule these decisions.

## Ordinal diagnostic scores

Scale: 0 = fails the requirement; 1 = major unresolved defects; 2 = substantial work remains; 3 = adequate for the stated form with explicit limits; 4 = strong evidence and no material defect found in scope. There is no weighted total.

| Dimension | Score / 4 | Reason |
|---|---:|---|
| Conditional mathematical correctness | 4 | Reconstructed proofs, adversarial edge cases, and independently checked repair. This is still not a formal proof-assistant certificate. |
| Contribution / audience fit | 3 | Coherent and useful correction/synthesis, with modest originality and a specialized audience. A research-only venue is inappropriate on the present evidence. |
| Attribution and priority discipline | 3 | Closer exact source added and stronger claims avoided. The literature search is bounded and some cognitive texts remain inaccessible. |
| Historical fidelity | 3 | Requested primary pages checked and fair wording repaired. Claims remain deliberately narrow; source access levels are documented. |
| Reproducibility | 4 | Original suite passes; output comparisons recorded correctly; independently authored targeted ternary regression passes; code, data and logs included. |
| Exposition and technical presentation | 3 | Self-contained note with clear limits, correct bibliography and readable nine-page PDF. A specific journal may require shortening, different notation or house style. |

Original-research novelty is **not established** and is deliberately not folded into an average. Empirical cognitive validity is **not assessed or claimed**. A high correctness score does not change either statement.

## Submission decision

**Is submission reasonable? Yes, as an explicitly labeled synthesis/correction or expository modeling note, to a venue that accepts that form.** The content package is ready for venue selection and ordinary journal-specific preparation. This is not an unconditional declaration that it meets an unnamed journal's originality threshold or submission checklist.

**Is original mathematical research novelty established? No.** No exact published predecessor for the adaptive iff criterion was located, but the theorem is a short deduction from standard full-tree machinery. Absence of a located citation is not an originality certificate.

**What remains before an actual submission?** Select the venue, verify its current note/article policy, and apply its required formatting, declarations and author metadata. Obtain the author's explicit instruction before uploading or sending a submission. No additional broad research pass or theorem expansion is required for the present scope.

**What remains unverified?** Exact adaptive-theorem first priority; inaccessible earlier cognitive full texts; wording variants across physical editions; fresh Lauro-Grotto page images; empirical adequacy; journal-specific acceptance fit. The first four limitations are disclosed rather than concealed. None supports expanding the current claims.

## Next task recommendation

Continue venue selection and formatting in this task while the current evidence and author decisions are useful. A capable general model such as gpt-6-sol at medium reasoning is sufficient for that bounded editorial work; no measured cost saving is asserted. Defer another specialist theorem or historical review unless a proposed substantive change or an editor's objection reopens one of the gates. Do not start a fresh general-research task merely to make the note larger.

# Paper U: independent hostile review and disposition

Date and literature cutoff: 29 September 2026. Reviewed version: v0.2; repaired version: v0.3.

## Decision

**The note survives as a short synthesis/correction note. Original mathematical research novelty remains unestablished.** Its defensible contribution is a precise separation of latent ultrametric geometry, observation-induced indistinguishability, and full-tree symmetry, with explicit counterexamples to invalid generalizations. Submission is reasonable to a venue that accepts such exposition or conceptual-methodological corrections. It is not a suitable original-research submission based on a claimed new general mathematical theory.

No central theorem was refuted under its intended hypotheses. Local hypothesis/proof omissions were repaired; closer prior art was added; historical framing was made fairer. The prior conclusion was retested, not treated as a certificate. The scorecard is in `PUBLICATION_READINESS_SCORECARD.md`; no average score can override its veto gates.

## How independence was implemented

A root reviewer reconstructed the topology, metric, completion and information arguments. Three separately instantiated AI agents handled tree groups and a new regression, hostile priority searches, and historical/modeling source fidelity. The tree reviewer then independently cross-checked the revised topology proof. These are distinct AI analytical roles in one shared task, not human referees, blinded independent experiments, or four unrelated laboratories. They read the required prior materials as leads and fallible claims. Their written proofs, search records, source access and executable evidence are the basis of the decision.

## Findings and their disposition

| ID | Finding | Action and present status |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | Coordinate-free theorem/tower should explicitly state the ultrametric hypothesis; total boundedness alone does not make threshold closeness transitive. | Added the hypothesis. Local omission resolved. |
| T2 | The compact-to-Hausdorff argument needs continuity of the completion coding map. | Added positive separation, clopenness of cell closures and coordinate continuity; also made the isometry argument explicit. Cross-checked independently. |
| T3-T5 | Undefined 'complete family' terminology, implicit zero diagonal, and a loose entropy/cardinality sentence. | Replaced by all cell-constant observables; gave zero diagonal; restated refinement and corrected the quantity description. |
| G1 | Finite index does not imply a quotient group; pointwise and setwise stabilizers differ. | Existing theorem survives. Full proof and independent finite conjugating witnesses confirm its exact boundary. No group theorem weakened. |
| P1 | A direct fixed-threshold quotient predecessor was missing. | Added Mémoli–Smith–Wan, published 2023, §2.1 Eq.(5), Definition 10, p.87; the construction was already in their 2021 preprint. |
| P2 | Ishiki was only called 'closely related', understating direct overlap. | Identified Proposition 2.31's zero-internal-pseudometric specialization explicitly. |
| P3 | Kleiner locator omitted the section defining the quotient. | Changed §3.4 to §§3.3–3.4. |
| H1 | Matte-Blanco's strong identity language needs his own external-observer qualification. | Added the qualification, verified on printed pp.148–149. |
| H2 | Lauro-Grotto already invokes a distant-object perceptual analogy. | Credited that analogy; did not attribute a general indiscrete-topology theorem to her. |
| H3 | The inherited Matte-Blanco primary-page evidence was only OCR-supported. | All requested ten printed pages visually inspected in an authorized Routledge/Google Books reprint. Bibliography now names the consulted reprint and original 1975 provenance. |
| R1 | Transfer layout had moved the manuscript away from the old shell builder's expected parent directory. | New PowerShell and POSIX builders resolve the actual handoff layout. Original files remain unchanged in the preserved transfer archive. |

## Strongest hostile objections

**'The mathematics is standard.'** This objection succeeds against a research-novelty claim. Partition topology, metric identification, threshold quotients, profinite reconstruction and full-tree stabilizer machinery have direct predecessors. The exact adaptive normality criterion was not located as a published named theorem, but its short derivation from standard ingredients gives no warrant for a first-priority claim. The paper's value must be expository and corrective.

**'The correction is directed only at the author's own thesis.'** There is an explicit error in that thesis, independently rechecked in the supplied PDF: it connects ultrametricity to indiscrete topology and to topological indistinguishability. The note also clarifies the mathematical status of cluster/perceptual arguments in the cited literature. The historical revision credits their existing observational analogy; it does not manufacture a stronger error for them to have made. The adaptive nonnormality example and completion boundary make the note more useful than a bare thesis erratum. An editor may nevertheless find its audience too narrow; that is a contribution-fit risk, not a mathematical defect.

**'The cognitive language is post hoc.'** No theorem chooses meaningful features, their ordering, an observer, or a psychological time scale. The criticism is valid against empirical or full-bi-logic claims; v0.3 makes neither. The note is a conditional mathematical clarification, and should be judged as such.

**'The p-adics are unnecessary.'** Correct for the general theorems. They remain a compact specialization giving canonical residue-ring maps. No new arithmetic theory is advertised. No XOR, martingale expansion, noisy-channel theory, or Paper F machinery has been imported.

**'The group result assumes the symmetry it needs.'** The full regular-tree contract is indeed strong. It is explicit and is exactly what permits independent sections and transitivity on infinite rays. Counterexamples for smaller groups and nonregular geometries are part of the review and manuscript. This is a limitation rather than an invalid theorem.

## Reproducibility and its limits

The original standard-library Python verifier was rerun successfully under Python 3.12.14. It reproduced both CSVs byte-for-byte and the JSON exactly after CRLF/LF normalization; parsed JSON equality also passed. Claiming byte-for-byte JSON identity on Windows would be false. All 40 original transfer-manifest entries matched SHA-256.

The original suite covered 677 adaptive frontiers and 2,772,992 collapsed-distance triple checks, 258 comparable binary/ternary frontier pairs, 757 lattice pairs, 11,264 sample/frontier checks and 78 entropy identities. These are finite checks, not proofs of infinite statements or observations of cognition.

The independently authored extension constructs a ternary height-two permutation group by generator closure, enumerates factor stabilizers, distinguishes pointwise from setwise fixation, and tests nonuniform old cells with mixed relative depths including zero. It confirms a normal refinement of index 60,466,176 and a nonnormal refinement of index 362,797,056 with an explicit witness. It does not enumerate the huge product group: the composite conclusion uses the separately proved direct-product structure. It additionally checks 81 lattice pairs and all 512 subsets of nine distinct sample codes. See the exact contracts in `tree_review/TREE_GROUP_REVIEW.md`.

## Source verification: what changed and what remains limited

Matte-Blanco printed pp.38–39, 45–46, 107–108 and 146–149 were visually read in the publisher-authorized Google Books reprint. The title/copyright material was checked. This supersedes the earlier OCR-only limitation for the retained claims. It is not a collation against a physical 1975 copy or every edition. Source images are not redistributed; the access log provides direct page URLs and inspection extents.

Lauro-Grotto was freshly checked in author-posted full text with printed page markers. Fresh article page images were inaccessible and are not claimed. The modest paraphrase and fairness correction are supported at that access level.

The priority search includes required primary theorem passages and recent 2025/2026 work through 29 September. It is bounded, not a full database or all-language search. Full-text gaps remain for some earlier cognitive publications, and exact adaptive-theorem priority remains unresolved. Those gaps prevent first-priority claims; they do not invalidate a transparently non-priority synthesis.

## What publication readiness does and does not mean

The independent content gate supports submission of this narrowed note, subject to normal venue selection and formatting. It does not predict acceptance, verify a particular journal's present policy, or authorize external submission. A pure topology/group-theory journal demanding substantial original results would have a sound reason to reject it. No theorem expansion is required to finish this request; expanding claims would reopen correctness, priority and historical gates.

The next useful step is to identify a venue that explicitly accepts synthesis/correction notes, then adapt only its required format. Continue in this task while these decisions and evidence are active. A general-purpose capable model such as gpt-6-sol at medium reasoning should be sufficient for that bounded editorial task; this is a suitability recommendation, not a measured price or cache-saving claim. External submission remains a separate action requiring the author's explicit instruction.

# Independent topology, ultrametric and information review

Review date: 2026-09-29. Input: the archived v0.2 TeX and eight-page PDF. This is an AI analytical review, not a report from a human specialist. Proofs below were reconstructed rather than inferred from the prior ledger or finite regression results. Correctness does not certify novelty.

## Disposition

The mathematical claims survive under the intended nonempty ultrametric-space hypotheses. Two local repairs are warranted: make the ultrametric hypothesis explicit in the coordinate-free theorem and tower setup, and explicitly prove continuity in the completion/homeomorphism argument. The latter is a short missing justification, not a counterexample to the conclusion. No theorem needs to be weakened under its intended contract.

## Findings requiring or motivating changes

| ID | Finding in v0.2 | Severity and disposition |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | Theorem 2.2 refers to `(X,d)` without repeating that it is ultrametric; Section 3 begins with merely 'totally bounded'. The intended assumption is evident, but the latter sentence alone allows non-ultrametric spaces, for which threshold closeness need not be transitive. | Local hypothesis omission. Explicitly say 'ultrametric' in both places. For example, `{0,1,2}` with ordinary distance and threshold 1 defeats the unrestricted formulation. |
| T2 | Proposition 3.1 invokes compactness/Hausdorffness to turn a bijection into a homeomorphism without explicitly establishing continuity. | Local proof omission. The finite, positively separated closures of level cells are clopen in the completion. Coordinate maps are therefore continuous. Add this step. |
| T3 | Introduction uses 'complete family of cell-level observables' before defining completeness. | Expository ambiguity. Use agreement under all cell-constant observables, as in the actual theorem. |
| T4 | Prefix metric formula specifies only distinct arguments; the zero diagonal is implicit. | Definition clarity. State `d_lambda(x,x)=0`. |
| T5 | Entropy identity uses refinement without a local reminder; 'Neither cardinality' follows an entropy calculation, although entropy is not a cardinality. | State `F <= F'` and replace the final sentence with an explicit warning about interpreting either quantity as a count of conscious states. |

## Independent proof reconstruction

### Lemma 2.1: constant cross-distances

Let B be an open ball of radius r about b, x,x' in B, and y outside it. Ultrametric recentering gives d(x,x') < r <= d(x,y). For a closed ball, the inequalities become d(x,x') <= r < d(x,y). In both cases the inner distance is strictly smaller than the cross-distance. The two strong triangle inequalities force d(x',y)=d(x,y): a strictly smaller value would imply d(x,y) <= max(d(x,x'),d(x',y)) < d(x,y). Apply the same reasoning to the other ball to get representative independence on B x C. Radius-zero closed balls are singletons and cause no problem. The one-cell case needs no cross-distance statement.

### Theorem 2.2: quotient, topology and maximality

For three different cells, choose one representative in each; the quotient inequality is precisely the original ultrametric inequality. Repeated cells reduce it to zero or equality. Off-diagonal quotient distances are positive, so the finite quotient is discrete; when it has only one point this remains true without taking a minimum over an empty set. Pulling the quotient metric back gives exactly zero within cells and the original metric across cells. A sufficiently small positive ball at any point is its whole cell, so its topology consists of all unions of cells.

Topological indistinguishability in that topology is exactly common-cell membership. Any continuous map into a T0 target must identify two points with identical open neighborhoods: otherwise a distinguishing target open set has an impossible preimage. Surjectivity of q gives the unique factor, and the factor is continuous because the finite quotient is discrete. The actual quotient topology is also discrete, since preimages of all subsets are open. This is the Kolmogorov quotient of the *partition topology*, not of the original Hausdorff metric topology. The original metric space itself has singleton Kolmogorov classes.

T0 is essential to the unconditional continuity implication. From an indiscrete two-point domain to an indiscrete two-point target, the identity is continuous but is not constant on the single domain cell. There is no contradiction with the set-theoretic assertion, which separately requires cell constancy. Nor does continuity from the *original* metric topology imply cell constancy. The source topologies cannot be silently exchanged.

For set-valued maps, define the factor at B to be f(x) for any x in B; constancy is precisely well-definedness. If the map is both cell-constant and nonexpansive for d, then for different cells the factor distance is bounded by d(x,y)=delta(B,C). Inside one cell it is zero. No extension or compactness theorem is being invoked.

For maximality, an admissible pseudometric e is zero inside a cell and is at most d across cells. These are exactly the two cases defining d_P, so e <= d_P pointwise. Since d_P is itself admissible, it is a greatest element, not just maximal. This is an elementary order observation once admissibility is proved; it does not establish a new optimization principle.

One-cell X and a singleton X give d_P=0 and a singleton quotient. A partition into singleton cells gives d_P=d; for finite X it gives the original discrete topology. The theorem does not assert indiscreteness of the whole latent metric space. The clopen hypothesis also makes the observation q continuous from the original metric topology.

### Example 2.3 and the geometric hypothesis

With blocks {00,10}, {01}, {11}, the collapsed distances obey d_P(10,01)=1, d_P(10,00)=0 and d_P(00,01)=1/2. Thus even the ordinary triangle inequality fails. Quotient-set existence alone does not license the cross-distance-preserving formula. Conversely, a non-ball block in an equilateral finite space can be collapsed, so the ball condition is sufficient rather than necessary.

### Proposition 3.1: thresholds and completion

Assume explicitly that X is a nonempty totally bounded *ultrametric* space. Positive thresholds make `d <= r_k` an equivalence relation. An open cover by balls of radius less than r_k admits a finite subcover, each member of which lies in a single threshold class; hence there are finitely many classes. Each class is a closed r_k-ball and is open, since an open r_k-ball about each of its points lies in it. All statements allow a singleton X and a positive r_0 despite diameter zero.

The collapse error is zero between classes and equals d <= r_k inside them. Refinement can only change a collapsed distance from zero to d, which proves monotonicity. Each partition-open set is metric-open; every metric neighborhood contains a sufficiently small threshold class. It is the topology *generated* by the union of level topologies that equals the original topology. The union need not be closed under arbitrary unions. The first distinguishing index exists because the thresholds tend to zero; since level zero is one cell, its bounds are `r_kappa < d <= r_(kappa-1)`.

Give the inverse limit the subspace topology inherited from the product of finite discrete quotients. Compatible cells are nested, nonempty, with diameters tending to zero. Representatives form a Cauchy sequence, so their closures in the completion have exactly one common point. At any fixed level, distinct cells have constant positive cross-distances. Finite many cells cover X; their closures cover the completion, remain disjoint, and remain positively separated. They are therefore clopen. Each completion point yields a unique compatible sequence, and the coordinate maps are continuous. The completion is compact (complete plus totally bounded), and the inverse limit is Hausdorff. This *continuous* bijection is a homeomorphism. This supplies the omitted continuity step in v0.2.

Density of X follows without compactness of X: a basic cylinder condition specifies finitely many compatible coordinates and therefore contains the image of a point of their deepest cell. For metric precision, if two compatible sequences first differ at level j, all subsequent intercell distances equal that same positive cross-distance, because finer cells are subsets of the earlier cells. Thus `D(a,b)=lim delta_k(a_k,b_k)` is zero on the diagonal and is eventually constant and positive off it. Taking limits in the strong triangle inequality makes D an ultrametric. For the corresponding completion points, continuity of the extended distance yields exactly D. This also proves the claimed isometry without circularly relying on density alone.

The eventual-zero binary sequences demonstrate the essential incompleteness issue: every finite prefix is attained, so the limit is the full binary boundary; the all-ones sequence is missing from X. Total boundedness alone does not identify X with its completion. Empty spaces are excluded by the manuscript's global nonemptiness convention.

### Prefix calibration and p-adic specialization

For distinct branches, the common-prefix inequality gives the strong triangle inequality for lambda^ell. A length-k cylinder is the closed lambda^k-ball and, for k>=1, the open lambda^(k-1)-ball. An open lambda^k-ball fixes k+1 coordinates. Boundary/radius equalities therefore matter. A first distinction at coordinate ell has observation index ell+1. These equalities depend on the specified scale, not on arbitrary threshold choices.

Countably many finite cylinders form a basis, so their Boolean algebras generate the Borel sigma-algebra. They are not generally themselves a sigma-algebra or a topology. In the prime case, the least-significant-first digit map is bijective onto Z_p and the first nonzero digit of a difference gives its p-adic valuation. Residue compatibility reconstructs unique digits. No field structure or p-adic dynamics enters any earlier proof.

### Section 5: entropy

For one split let w=mu(C_v)>0 and child masses w_a=w p_a. Subtracting the parent term from child entropy gives `-sum w_a log_2 w_a + w log_2 w = w(-sum p_a log_2 p_a)`. If w=0, all child masses are zero and the contribution is zero without defining a conditional law. Sum over any refinement order. Each newly internal vertex is split once, so the displayed identity follows. Under the uniform law, the weights are m^(-|v|); the group log-index has no such weights.

Balanced binary leaves have four masses 1/4 and entropy 2 bits. The comb has masses 1/8,1/8,1/4,1/2 and entropy 3/8+3/8+1/2+1/2=7/4 bits. Both have three splits and index 8. Changing the probability law while holding a frontier fixed is another immediate obstruction to identifying these quantities. This is not a cognitive-data result.

## Limits of this review

The proofs establish the intended conditional mathematics. They do not select a psychologically valid hierarchy or observation map, certify empirical adequacy, settle historical source fidelity, or establish original priority. Tree-group and appendix reconstructions are separately documented. The supplied numerical suite is corroboration only.

Part (iii)'s nonexpansive clause is read with the cell constancy established in the preceding sentence; its use of “also” adequately signals the extra hypothesis. Constant positive cross-distances persist under completion limits. The resulting finite partition is positively separated and hence clopen (a singleton partition is clopen directly). Thus its coordinate map is continuous, and the map into the inverse limit is continuous by the product topology. Nested cells of diameter tending to zero give a bijection independently of that continuity. Complete plus totally bounded gives compactness of the completion, so compact-to-Hausdorff now validly yields the claimed homeomorphism.

For distinct compatible sequences a and b, let j be their first differing coordinate. Every finer pair of cells lies within those two distinct j-cells, so delta_k(a_k,b_k) is the same positive cross-distance for all k>=j. The proposed limit D therefore exists. Choose x_k in a_k and y_k in b_k. These sequences converge in the completion to the already constructed corresponding points. Continuity of the extended metric gives d_hat(lim x_k,lim y_k)=lim d(x_k,y_k)=D(a,b). For a=b all quotient distances and D are zero. Hence D is the pullback of the completion metric and the isometry conclusion follows without using the desired isometry as an assumption. There is no need to invoke density alone to justify it.

The named findings are proportionate: **T1** is a local hypothesis omission/formal clarification under a context whose intended ultrametric contract was already evident; **T2** is an omitted routine continuity justification, not a counterexample or substantial theorem defect. # Independent tree-group review of Paper U v0.2

Review date: 29 September 2026. Reviewer: a separately instantiated AI tree-group review role, not an independent human referee. The role read the current v0.2 source, the theorem ledger, strengthening study, adversarial report, and next-review instructions. Prior verdicts were treated as hypotheses, not proof. This report covers the adaptive theorem, its corollary and limitations, information comparison, and frontier appendix. It does not claim an independent literature search; the parallel priority role handles sources and exact-predecessor searches.

## Verdict

The adaptive theorem is correct under its stated contract: **full rooted automorphism group of the infinite regular tree, finite complete frontiers, and pointwise fixation of frontier vertices**. No mathematical repair is required in this part of v0.2. Different old cells may be refined to different relative full levels, including level zero. Mixed relative depths within any one old cell prevent normality. A nonuniform old frontier creates no extra condition. The manuscript draws these distinctions correctly.

The appendix statements and entropy comparison also survive reconstruction. Their mechanisms are elementary and standard. Correctness of these statements does not establish original research novelty or decide publication fit. A claim to a new general group-theoretic or information-theoretic theory would fail this review. As a tightly framed correction/synthesis, these statements can support the note, subject to the separate contribution-fit and source-fidelity gates.

## 1. Contract and potential ambiguities

Let the alphabet have m >= 2 letters. Vertices are finite words, including the empty word e. An automorphism preserves the root and adjacency. A finite complete frontier F is prefix-free and meets every infinite ray once. Write I(F) for all proper prefixes of frontier words and C_s for the infinite cylinder at s. The group G_F fixes every s in F **individually**.

Fixing a vertex s is equivalent to preserving its cylinder C_s as a set; it does not require fixing the boundary points of that cylinder. Fixing every frontier vertex individually is different from preserving the collection F setwise. The latter permits exchanges of frontier cells with compatible tree positions. These distinctions are already explicit in v0.2 and are essential, not terminology.

For example, with F equal to all first-level vertices, the setwise stabilizer is the whole tree automorphism group, whereas the pointwise stabilizer is the first-level kernel and has index m!. Thus the main formula would immediately fail if the paper silently meant setwise stabilization.

The group in the theorem is an abstract group; every restriction map in the proof is also continuous for the usual profinite topology, but no topological-group claim is needed. T_(m,0) must mean the one-vertex rooted tree, whose automorphism group is trivial. This is the standard height convention and is consistent with the formula as written.

## 2. Independent proof reconstruction

### 2.1 Frontier structure and sections

The finite upper tree has vertex set I(F) union F. Every vertex in I(F) has all m children in that upper tree: completeness forces every child subtree to meet F. Fixation of every frontier vertex fixes all its ancestors, so G_F fixes this entire upper tree pointwise. Conversely, independently choose a rooted automorphism of the descendant tree at each s in F, and act identically above F. The actions have disjoint supports and glue to a rooted automorphism. Restriction to these descendant trees and gluing are inverse homomorphisms. Hence G_F is the direct product of |F| copies of Aut(T_m).

This is a direct product, not a semidirect product, precisely because no old frontier cells may be permuted. Under setwise stabilization an additional permutation action can be present.

### 2.2 Boundary orbits

Every element of G_F preserves C_s for each s, so an orbit cannot cross a frontier cell. For any two rays in C_s, choose child permutations successively along the source ray to send its next edge to the next edge of the target ray. Choose arbitrary compatible permutations elsewhere. This constructs a rooted automorphism of the full subtree at s sending one ray to the other; glue it with identity in all other old cells. Thus C_s is a single orbit.

No countability, finite-support, or selected-generator restriction is permitted here. In particular, finite-level transitivity by itself does not prove transitivity on infinite rays.

### 2.3 Exact finite index

Refinement is equivalent to I(F) being contained in I(F'). Split vertices in I(F') minus I(F) in an order in which ancestors occur first. Each next vertex is then a leaf of the current frontier, and splitting it into its m children produces the next frontier. Every added internal vertex is split once, so the number of operations is exactly N.

At one such leaf s, the current pointwise stabilizer has a full independent section at s. Its action on the m children is a surjection onto Sym(m). The kernel fixes these children individually and is exactly the stabilizer of the new frontier. Consequently one split has index m!. Multiplicativity of subgroup indices along the finite chain gives [G_F:G_F'] = (m!)^N.

Multiplicativity of index does not require each intermediate subgroup to be normal in the original group. The proof correctly avoids inferring a quotient-group structure from a finite index. Equality F=F' gives N=0 and index one. Every strict refinement has N>0 and therefore is a proper subgroup because m>=2.

### 2.4 Normality: necessity by boundary orbits

Put H=G_F'. If H is normal in G=G_F, then for every boundary point x and g in G, g(Hx)=H(gx). Therefore g permutes the H-orbit partition, already shown to consist exactly of the cylinders of F'. Fix s in F and choose t in F' below s at relative depth h. The full section of G at s is transitive on the m^h words at this relative depth. Every cylinder at that depth is therefore the image of C_t and must also be an H-orbit. Distinct tree vertices have distinct cylinders for m>=2, so every word of s Sigma_m^h belongs to F'. Those cylinders already cover C_s. Prefix-freeness excludes any other frontier vertex under s. Thus the refinement inside each old cell is exactly one full relative level.

This argument does not force a common h across old cells, because G_F cannot exchange those cells. It also does not force a common absolute depth. If h=0, t=s and the old cell is left unchanged.

### 2.5 Independent alternative necessity argument

The same conclusion follows without infinite boundary orbits. Suppose the relative frontier inside an old cell has unequal leaf depths. At the minimum leaf depth h there is a leaf u and also an internal vertex v; otherwise there would be no deeper leaf. A rooted automorphism of that old cell can send u to v, because they have equal relative depth. A nontrivial child permutation supported below u lies in H, since u is a frontier vertex and its descendants are unrestricted. Its conjugate is supported below v with nontrivial first-level action. Completeness guarantees frontier descendants under the moved children of v, so this conjugate moves a frontier vertex and is not in H. Hence H is not normal.

This is also an explicit mechanism for nonnormality: a symmetry allowed below an unsplit leaf can be conjugated to a location where the finer observation already resolves it.

### 2.6 Normality: sufficiency and quotient

If the relative frontier under s is Sigma_m^(h_s), its pointwise stabilizer in the section group is the kernel of restriction to the finite rooted tree of height h_s. Restriction is onto: extend a finite rooted automorphism below its terminal vertices using the natural labelled descendant-tree identifications. The kernel is normal, and the quotient is Aut(T_(m,h_s)). Taking the product over old cells proves both sufficiency and the stated quotient formula.

At h_s=0 the restriction has trivial target and the kernel is the entire factor. Leaving a cell unchanged therefore contributes an index-one, trivial quotient factor. Different h_s cause no difficulty. The height-h finite-tree group is an iterated wreath product in its natural action; it should not be replaced by Sym(m^h). For example, at m=3 and h=2 its order is 1296, much smaller than 9!.

### 2.7 Corollary and example

For a uniform frontier at depth k there are m^k factors. Refining all once gives quotient Sym(m)^(m^k). Refining only a subset S once gives relative heights one on S and zero elsewhere, hence quotient Sym(m)^|S| and normality. S may be empty.

For the binary refinement {e} to {00,01,1}, I(F') has two vertices, so index four is correct. Root interchange transports the fine orbit partition to {C_0,C_10,C_11}; these are different partitions. Normality fails. Successive local normal inclusions can indeed have a nonnormal composite inclusion. The manuscript's example and its interpretation are correct.

## 3. What cannot be generalized without new hypotheses

For an arbitrary subgroup K of Aut(T_m), a pointwise frontier stabilizer may not have independent arbitrary sections. Its available local permutations may be proper subgroups of Sym(m), correlated between cells, or trivial. The index formula and orbit clause need not survive. The trivial subgroup is the simplest failure.

A stronger warning is the finitary automorphism group: it is countable and transitive on every finite level, but each infinite-boundary orbit is countable while a cylinder is uncountable. Thus even finite-level transitivity is insufficient for the boundary orbit clause. The full-group assumption in v0.2 is substantive.

For a nonregular rooted tree with a finite complete frontier, independent sections still yield a product of the automorphism groups of the actual descendant trees when the full rooted automorphism group is used. The factors may differ and their boundary actions may fail to be transitive. Child permutations can only exchange isomorphic descendant trees. There is no universal factorial index based only on the number of children and no universal strictness statement. The three-point ultrametric example in v0.2 is correct: c is distinguished by its distance pattern, while a and b can be exchanged, so the full isometry orbits are {a,b} and {c}, unlike the one-cell observation partition.

No additional manuscript repair is needed; the stated limitations already block the false extensions.

## 4. Frontier appendix, including edge cases

The association F -> I(F) is a bijection between finite complete frontiers and finite prefix-closed sets of vertices, with the empty internal set allowed. Given an internal set I, stopping at the first vertex outside I gives a finite complete frontier, and its proper prefixes are exactly I. Refinement becomes inclusion of internal sets. Union and intersection remain finite and prefix-closed, so they give join and meet and satisfy distributivity. The empty set corresponds to the root frontier, the bottom. Splitting any leaf gives a strict finite refinement, so there is no finite top.

In the finite upper full tree, counting edges as m times the number of internal vertices and also as total vertices minus one gives |F|=1+(m-1)|I(F)|. This includes F={e}. Under the uniform measure, frontier cylinders are disjoint and covering, giving Kraft equality. Conversely, a **finite** prefix-free family with total cylinder measure one must cover: its complement is open, and a nonempty open complement contains a positive-measure cylinder. Finiteness is needed for that argument. For instance, the infinite binary prefix code {0,10,110,...} has total mass one but misses the all-ones ray. The manuscript expressly states the finite hypothesis.

For a finite set A of distinct infinite rays, every prefix containing at least two samples is a common prefix of a distinct pair. Each pair has finitely many common prefixes; a finite union is finite. Prefix-closure is immediate. If a frontier separates A, every vertex of I_A must be internal: otherwise a stopping ancestor contains the same pair. Conversely, splitting exactly I_A stops only at cylinders containing at most one sample. Thus a frontier separates A iff its internal set contains I_A, which proves the unique least refinement and the minimum-leaf formula.

For A empty or a singleton, I_A is empty and the least frontier is {e}, with one leaf. Unoccupied branches still contribute leaves because the frontier must cover the entire boundary, not merely the sample. The word "distinct" is important: repeated observations of one identical infinite ray cannot be separated as different latent points by prefix observations. Feature order and allowed tests remain fixed; no optimal arbitrary-query decision-tree result follows.

These edge cases require no correction. An optional single sentence recording the empty/singleton case could help readers, but adding it is not a correctness prerequisite.

## 5. Information calculation

For a split at v of mass M>0 with child masses M p_a, subtracting the old contribution -M log_2 M from the child contributions gives M times the finite distribution entropy of p. If M=0, all child masses are zero and the gain is zero. Iterating over the newly split vertices gives the exact displayed formula, independently of split order. No division by zero occurs under the manuscript's convention.

For uniform independent digits, M=m^(-|v|), whereas logarithmic group index contributes log_2(m!) per split regardless of depth or mass. The binary balanced-versus-comb calculation is correct: three split vertices produce index eight in both cases, while the entropy is 2 versus 7/4 bits. More starkly, a point-mass source has zero entropy at every frontier while every strict refinement has positive logarithmic group index. Thus index is not an information gain without extra structure; neither count identifies conscious states.

## 6. Independently authored bounded regression

Files: `check_mixed_ternary.py`, `mixed_ternary_results.json`, and `mixed_ternary_run.log`. Run with Python 3.10.11 using only the standard library:

```powershell
python .\check_mixed_ternary.py --out .
```

The script constructs eight local adjacent-swap permutations on the nine terminal vertices of T_(3,2), then computes group closure by breadth-first search. It does not use the theorem's order formula to manufacture or count group elements. The closure contains 1296 elements. Pointwise stabilizers are selected by testing preservation of each individual cylinder; setwise stabilizers are separately selected by preservation of the partition collection. Normality is tested by conjugating every subgroup element by each ambient generator, stopping upon an explicit counterexample. As the chosen adjacent-swap generators are involutions and generate the ambient group, successful testing on these generators establishes normality in this finite group.

| Relative frontier | Pointwise order | Setwise order | Index | Normal |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| {e} | 1296 | 1296 | 1 | yes |
| {0,1,2} | 216 | 1296 | 6 | yes |
| all nine length-two words | 1 | 1296 | 1296 | yes |
| {00,01,02,1,2} | 36 | 432 | 36 | no |

The concrete uncertainty addressed is **normality for m>2 when both the old frontier and refinement depths are nonuniform**. Use the old frontier F={0,10,11,12,2}, with old absolute depths one and two. The finite permutation image needed for these checks is a product of five copies of the explicitly enumerated group, acting on 45 terminal nodes, two further levels below each old cell. Its order is 3,656,158,440,062,976; the full product is not enumerated. The factor stabilizers and conjugations are enumerated, and product membership supplies the finite composite check.

* Relative full heights (2,1,0,1,2) produce a normal subgroup. The global old/new frontiers directly give N=10. The index obtained from the enumerated factor orders is 60,466,176=6^10. New absolute frontier depths are two and three. This tests mixed h_s and h_s=0 together.
* Replace the relative frontier below old cell 10 with {00,01,02,1,2}. The global count becomes N=11 and the index is 362,797,056=6^11. The inclusion is nonnormal. New absolute depths are two, three, and four. An explicit witness in that factor has g interchange first digits 0 and 1 and h interchange terminal vertices 11 and 12. The element h fixes the uneven frontier individually, but g h g^(-1) interchanges 01 and 02 and therefore does not. The complete permutations are retained in JSON.

This extends the supplied fixed-small-global-depth checks by targeting nonuniform old cells and different relative refinements, without trying to enumerate an infeasibly large full product. It is finite-image evidence, not a substitute for the infinite proof. The factorwise direct-product step is supported by the proof in Section 2, not independently discovered by the computation.

Additional exact appendix checks enumerate all nine ternary complete frontiers through depth two, all 81 meet/join pairs, and all 512 subsets of the nine depth-two sample codes. They verify Kraft equality with rational arithmetic, the leaf formula, and the least separating frontier and unique minimum leaf count. The ten empty/singleton sample cases explicitly give the root frontier. These finite sample codes stand for distinct infinite rays with arbitrary fixed tails; their first two digits already distinguish them.

All checks passed. No test failure was edited away; there was one run of the completed regression. The computation makes no cognitive or empirical claim.

## 7. Manuscript action and remaining gate

Required tree-group/appendix repair: none. Optional clarity only: spell out that height zero gives the trivial finite-tree automorphism group, and that empty/singleton samples use the root frontier. The existing pointwise qualifier and full-group hypotheses should remain explicit in any shortening.

This role supports mathematical survival of the narrowed note, not an unconditional submission verdict. Exact theorem priority, historical fidelity, overall contribution fit, and publication venue remain separate gates. In particular, the short proof and standard mechanisms make the adaptive statement useful for precision without supplying evidence of original research novelty.

# Build, reproduction and final visual QA

Date: 29 September 2026. Final artifact: `01_CURRENT_MANUSCRIPT/Paper_U_Resolution_Limited_Ultrametric_Concepts_v0.3.pdf`.

## Build result

PASS. The Windows PowerShell builder ran pdfLaTeX, Biber, and two further pdfLaTeX passes. Final output is a nine-page Letter-size PDF with 20 resolved bibliography entries. The generated `.bbl` is supplied alongside the `.tex` and `.bib`. No final undefined-reference/citation warnings, rerun requests, overfull boxes or underfull boxes were found in the final TeX log. The PDF is a standard untagged LaTeX PDF; no accessibility tagging is claimed.

Observed tooling: MiKTeX pdfTeX 1.40.25 / MiKTeX 24.1; LaTeX2e 2023-11-01 patch 1; Biber 2.19. Biber reported an environment locale fallback from C.UTF-8 to C, then completed successfully. The rendered accented author names and bibliography were checked. This nonfatal environment warning is retained in `build_logs/biber_output.txt`.

The initial sandboxed build could not create MiKTeX's per-user cache/configuration directory. A scoped escalated local build was approved and exposed a missing `logreq.sty`. The unmodified logreq 1.0 package was then downloaded from official CTAN into this workspace, and its `.sty`/`.def` were copied to the build directory. Automatic MiKTeX package installation stayed disabled. No global package installation was performed. The original upstream ZIP and README/license are in `latex_support/`; source: https://ctan.org/pkg/logreq and https://mirrors.ctan.org/macros/latex/contrib/logreq.zip.

The final PowerShell build was executed successfully. The POSIX shell equivalent is supplied for portability but was not executed on this Windows host. It expects an already installed TeX distribution and Biber. Build logs identify the exact final passes. The new builders resolve this package's manuscript path; the prior transfer's moved shell script did not.

## Visual QA

All nine final pages were rendered with Poppler using `pdftoppm -scale-to 1600 -png`. Pages 1–8 were inspected in two contact sheets; page 9 was inspected directly. The input v0.2 PDF was also inspected before revision. No clipped equations, missing glyphs, black replacement boxes, overlapping text or unreadable bibliography entries were found. Numbered theorem/proof continuations and the continued bibliography have normal page breaks. The final page contains references 17–20; it is not a blank extra page.

The justified additions expand the original eight-page note to nine pages including references. Font size and margins were not compressed merely to preserve the old page count. Own-manuscript QA images are included in `visual_qa/`. Copyrighted external source pages are excluded from this handoff.

## Original verification suite

Executed with bundled Python 3.12.14, standard library only. All checks passed. Both generated CSVs match the earlier evidence byte-for-byte. The JSON has Windows CRLF rather than original LF, and is equal both after newline normalization and after JSON parsing. Exact hashes and comparisons are in `REPRODUCTION_RECEIPT.json`. The original verifier is supplied unchanged as `verify_paper_u.py`.

The prior input archive was safely extracted into a new task directory; all 40 entries in its SHA-256 manifest matched. The complete original ZIP is preserved byte-for-byte in `04_PRIOR_TRANSFER/`, and its hash is recorded in the receipt.

## Independent extension

The tree reviewer authored and ran `02_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW/tree_review/check_mixed_ternary.py` independently of the supplied verifier. Its log reports Python 3.10.11. Generator closure, enumerated factor stabilizers, conjugation witnesses, mixed old-cell depths, relative height zero, ternary branching and pointwise/setwise distinctions were tested. Output: PASS. The proof-dependent product composition is explicitly disclosed rather than represented as enumeration of the entire product group.

The same folder contains JSON results and the run log. No redundant rerun was performed after the unmodified tests passed. No computational claim is a proof of an infinite theorem or empirical support for a model of mind.

## Other validation

Final package assembly checks citation keys, expected files, JSON readability, source-file hashes, generated unified diffs and all archive entries. Archive hashes and integrity results are recorded in the adjacent ZIP receipt. The workspace's existing unrelated untracked folders were left untouched; no commit, push, publication or external submission was made.

# Carrier-Aware Bounded Width + SAT Four-Corner CM — Phase 3 Master Report

**Project:** The MIND / Gluing Concepts / Succinct Structured Factorization  
**Date:** 29 September 2026

## Executive result

Both requested branches were completed.

### Branch A — bounded-width theorem

A full finest-partition FPT result is available when the parameter is the treewidth of the **combined incidence graph** containing both semantic CNF clauses and carrier minimal nonfaces. The proof uses an exact pair-separation formulation: two attributes belong to different prime structured factors exactly when there exists a carrier-compatible cut separating them on which the four-corner CM defect is identically zero. This becomes a fixed-alternation QBF whose incidence width grows only by a constant factor. Bounded-treewidth fixed-alternation QBF is FPT, so `O(n^2)` pair queries recover the unique finest simultaneous partition.

This theorem is mathematically sound and useful, but the priority audit found that its algorithmic core sits close to established QBF bi-decomposition and bounded-width QBF/knowledge-compilation theory. It should currently be treated as a **carrier-aware synthesis theorem**, not advertised as a fundamentally new treewidth result.

### Branch B — SAT four-corner algorithm

An exact DIMACS-generating implementation was built. For a fixed cut it encodes

\[
D_f=(F_{00}\wedge F_{11})\mathbin{\Updownarrow}(F_{01}\wedge F_{10})
\]

with two input copies per original variable and four internal copies of the semantic circuit/CNF.

- SAT => a concrete nonzero-minor witness, hence rank `>1` and nonseparability.
- UNSAT => implicit CM rank `<=1`, hence exact AND-factorization.

The implementation includes a pure-Python DPLL only for reproducibility, DIMACS export for industrial solvers, witness decoding/verification, and recursive refinement restricted to carrier-block unions.

## New theorem statement

Let \(G_{K,\varphi}\) be the combined incidence graph of attributes, CNF clauses, and carrier minimal nonfaces, and let \(\tau=\operatorname{tw}(G_{K,\varphi})\). Then the canonical finest partition on which both the simplicial carrier and CNF semantics factor is computable in

\[
F(\tau)\operatorname{poly}(|K|+|\varphi|).
\]

The proof and exact QBF contract are in `docs/BOUNDED_WIDTH_CARRIER_AWARE_THEOREM.md`.

## Priority correction

The search found strong antecedents that materially narrow any claim:

- SAT-based Boolean bi-decomposition and automatic variable partitioning were already developed by Lee--Jiang--Hung (DAC 2008).
- Chen--Janota--Marques-Silva (DATE 2012) explicitly treat OR/AND/XOR bi-decomposition and use QBF to optimize unknown variable partitions.
- Capelli--Mengel establish FPT algorithms for bounded-treewidth quantified CNF with bounded quantifier alternation.
- bounded-treewidth Boolean circuits/CNFs have mature d-DNNF compilation theory.

Therefore neither "use SAT/QBF for AND decomposition" nor "bounded treewidth makes the quantified decomposition decision FPT" should be claimed as new.

The project-specific content is the coupling of the simplicial carrier constraint, CM four-corner rank certificate, and recovery of the canonical *simultaneous* finest factor partition.

## Computational evidence

- 200 random fixed-cut CNF tests: four-corner SAT encoding vs exhaustive implicit-matrix minors, **0 failures**.
- 80 random carrier-aware factor-recovery tests vs exhaustive partition/product verification, **0 failures**.
- on those 80 tiny examples, carrier blocks reduced the mean raw cut space from 19.35 to 2.4125 and recursive recovery used 1.825 SAT calls on average. These are illustrative only.

## Recommendation for the next convergence gate

Do **not** continue by merely proving another generic bounded-width corollary. The next research phase should compare three stronger possibilities:

1. **structured-d-DNNF direct factor extraction:** can the finest carrier-aware partition be read/recovered in singly exponential (or polynomial in compiled size) time without the generic QBF tower?
2. **incremental SAT implementation:** use one shared four-copy circuit with cut-control assumptions, preserving learned clauses across candidate cuts; benchmark against independent-cut SAT and against existing bi-decomposition formulations.
3. **CM/LM operator-DAG subclass:** search for a syntactic condition under which the prime factor partition is recoverable directly from the typed operator graph, yielding an actual representation-specific theorem rather than a restatement of general Boolean decomposition.

The first and third offer the strongest theorem-level novelty prospects; the second offers the strongest near-term computational evidence.

# Bounded-Width Carrier-Aware Structured Factorization

**Date:** 29 September 2026

## 1. Input contract

Let `V` be the attribute set. The carrier is represented by its minimal-nonface hypergraph
\(\mathcal N(K)\), and the semantic layer by a CNF \(\varphi\) on `V`.

Define the **combined incidence graph** \(G_{K,\varphi}\) with three kinds of vertices:

- attribute vertices \(v\in V\);
- semantic clause vertices \(C\in\varphi\);
- structural hyperedge vertices \(N\in\mathcal N(K)\).

Join an attribute to a semantic clause when it occurs in the clause, and to a structural vertex when it belongs to that minimal nonface. Signs of semantic occurrences are labels and do not alter the underlying graph. Let

\[
\tau=\operatorname{tw}(G_{K,\varphi}).
\]

The connected components of the structural minimal-nonface hypergraph are the canonical carrier join factors.

## 2. Four-corner condition

For a cut \(S\mid \bar S\), introduce two assignments \(a_0,a_1\) on \(S\) and two assignments \(b_0,b_1\) on \(\bar S\). Define

\[
D_{\varphi,S}
=
(\varphi(a_0,b_0)\wedge\varphi(a_1,b_1))
\mathbin{\Updownarrow}
(\varphi(a_0,b_1)\wedge\varphi(a_1,b_0)).
\]

The cut is an AND-factor cut exactly when \(D_{\varphi,S}\) is false for every four-corner assignment. Equivalently, the implicit CM flattening has \(\mathbb F_2\)-rank at most one.

A cut is **carrier-compatible** exactly when no minimal nonface crosses it. Equivalently, the cut is a union of carrier prime blocks.

## 3. Pair-separation QBF

For attributes \(p,q\), define `SEP(p,q)` to ask whether some valid structured cut separates them:

\[
\exists S\;[
 p\in S\wedge q\notin S
 \wedge \operatorname{CarrierClosed}(S)
 \wedge \forall a_0,a_1,b_0,b_1\;\neg D_{\varphi,S}
].
\]

For a CNF/QDIMACS implementation, membership in \(S\) is represented by existential cut-control variables. The four assignments are universal variables. Tseitin variables for the four copies of the semantic computation may be quantified existentially after them, giving a fixed three-block prefix of the schematic form

\[
\exists S\;\forall U\;\exists Z\;\Psi_{p,q}(S,U,Z).
\]

The structural constraints enforce equal cut-control bits on every minimal-nonface hyperedge (a spanning forest of each structural component suffices). A multiplexer per input selects the appropriate corner value according to the cut-control bit.

## 4. Width-lift lemma

### Lemma

If the combined incidence graph has treewidth \(\tau\), then the QBF matrix \(\Psi_{p,q}\) can be constructed with incidence treewidth \(O(\tau)\).

### Proof sketch

Start from a tree decomposition of \(G_{K,\varphi}\). Replace each attribute occurrence in a bag by a constant number of local copies: its cut bit, its two left/right assignment copies, and the constant-size multiplexer auxiliaries. Replace each semantic clause by four corner copies and constant-size gate auxiliaries. Structural minimal-nonface vertices receive only constant-size compatibility gadgets. Every original incidence edge is therefore replaced by a constant-size local gadget whose vertices can be inserted into the bags containing that edge, with at most a constant-factor bag expansion. The final rank-defect XOR/AND gadget is constant size and can be attached at the root/output bags. Hence the new width is at most \(c(\tau+1)-1\) for an absolute constant \(c\).

The exact constant depends on the chosen Tseitin encoding and is not the conceptual point; the parameter is preserved up to a constant factor.

## 5. Main FPT theorem

### Theorem (carrier-aware bounded-incidence-width factorization)

For a simplicial carrier supplied by minimal nonfaces and a CNF semantic layer, the canonical finest simultaneous carrier/semantic AND-factor partition is computable in

\[
F(\tau)\,\operatorname{poly}(|K|+|\varphi|)
\]

time, where \(\tau=\operatorname{tw}(G_{K,\varphi})\).

### Proof

For every pair \(p,q\in V\), decide `SEP(p,q)` using the fixed-alternation QBF above. The QBF has bounded incidence treewidth as a function of \(\tau\). Known bounded-treewidth QBF algorithms therefore decide each query in FPT time for the fixed number of quantifier blocks.

Define

\[
p\equiv q \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \neg\operatorname{SEP}(p,q).
\]

Let \(\Pi_*\) be the canonical finest simultaneous factor partition.

- If \(p,q\) lie in the same block of \(\Pi_*\), no valid factor partition can separate them, because every valid partition is a coarsening of \(\Pi_*\).
- If they lie in different blocks, regroup the blocks of \(\Pi_*\) into a bipartition placing the block of \(p\) on one side and that of \(q\) on the other. Regrouping preserves both join and Cartesian/AND products, so a valid structured cut separates them.

Thus the equivalence classes of \(\equiv\) are exactly the blocks of \(\Pi_*\). At most \(O(|V|^2)\) pair queries are required, which preserves fixed-parameter tractability.

## 6. What this theorem does and does not establish

This is a useful **carrier-aware synthesis theorem**, but the current priority evidence does **not** support claiming the bounded-width algorithmic mechanism as fundamentally new. QBF-based Boolean bi-decomposition with unknown variable partitions dates at least to Chen--Janota--Marques-Silva (2012), SAT-based bi-decomposition earlier to Lee--Jiang--Hung (2008), and bounded-treewidth/fixed-alternation QBF is already FPT in the knowledge-compilation literature.

The mathematically specific contribution of the present program is therefore the alignment of:

1. the canonical simplicial carrier partition;
2. the CM four-corner/rank-one certificate;
3. carrier-constrained cut variables;
4. exact recovery of the *simultaneous* finest partition.

A publication claim should be framed as a synthesis/application unless a more specialized complexity bound, lower bound, or representation advantage survives a dedicated priority audit.

## 7. Lower-bound boundary

The carrier block count \(k=|\Pi_K|\) alone is not a useful FPT parameter for general CNF: the previous phase established coNP-hardness already for \(k=2\). Thus bounded **semantic/combined interaction width**, rather than merely a small number of carrier components, is essential to the tractability theorem.

# SAT-Based Four-Corner CM Factorization Algorithm

## 1. Goal

Given a CNF/circuit \(f\) and a fixed carrier-compatible cut \(A\mid B\), decide whether

\[
f(a,b)=g(a)\wedge h(b)
\]

without materializing the exponentially large correspondence flattening.

The CM theorem gives

\[
f=g\wedge h
\iff
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb F_2}[f]_{A\mid B}\le 1.
\]

The test therefore searches directly for a nonzero `2 x 2` minor.

## 2. Defect formula

Create two input copies per original variable. For a variable in `A`, corner `(i,j)` uses copy `i`; for a variable in `B`, it uses copy `j`. Compute the four outputs

\[
y_{00},y_{01},y_{10},y_{11}.
\]

Then constrain

\[
(y_{00}\wedge y_{11})\mathbin{\Updownarrow}(y_{01}\wedge y_{10})=1.
\]

- **SAT** gives a rank-defect certificate and proves the cut is not separable.
- **UNSAT** proves every `2 x 2` minor vanishes, hence rank at most one and exact AND-separability.

For a CNF, the implementation treats each clause as an OR gate and the formula as an AND gate and applies a Tseitin encoding. Only the two input copies are shared; internal gates are copied per corner.

## 3. Size

For `n` input variables and a circuit/CNF of size `s`, the encoding uses

- `2n` assignment-input variables;
- four copies of the semantic internal computation;
- a constant-size top defect gadget.

Thus the encoding size is `O(n+s)` with a modest constant factor, not `O(2^n)`.

## 4. Carrier-aware refinement baseline

The provided program also contains a recursive factor recovery baseline. Given the already-computed carrier blocks \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\), it enumerates only cuts that are unions of those blocks. When it finds an UNSAT defect cut, it recursively factors the two sides. Any sequence of valid splits eventually reaches the unique finest semantic grouping of the supplied carrier blocks.

Worst-case SAT calls remain exponential in `k`; this is deliberate. The baseline provides an exact practical comparator for the bounded-width/QBF route and directly quantifies how much the carrier prunes the search space:

\[
2^{n-1}-1 \quad\longrightarrow\quad 2^{k-1}-1
\]

possible unordered nontrivial cuts before recursive pruning.

## 5. Priority boundary

SAT- and QBF-based Boolean bi-decomposition are established logic-synthesis techniques, including AND bi-decomposition. Accordingly, the SAT use itself is **not claimed novel**. The present implementation is useful because it puts the project's CM rank condition into a transparent four-corner certificate, integrates carrier-block restrictions, exports ordinary DIMACS, and supplies exact witnesses that can be checked back against the original function.

The strongest future implementation step is **incremental SAT**: retain the four semantic circuit copies while changing only cut-control assumptions, allowing learned clauses to survive across related carrier-compatible cuts. That requires an industrial incremental SAT API; the bundled pure-Python DPLL is intentionally only a reproducibility validator.
