# Defect supports as soft structural evidence

`probe_defects` probes fixed candidate cuts using the same real persistent SAT
backend as exact refinement. An UNSAT cut is a separability certificate. A SAT
cut yields clone assignments x0,x1 and supports U on one side and W on the
other. The stored object is `(U,W)`, not just their unlabelled union and not a
clique of asserted pairwise dependencies.

The reproduced support lemma proves only that some semantic prime factor
intersects both U and W. It does not prove that all variables in either support
belong together. The code emits `singleton_must_link` only when both supports
are singletons. Larger supports may bias a vtree objective softly; they may
never be used to impose exact variable merging or prune possible factor cuts.
Even a certified singleton pair is merely optional search evidence: final
correctness still comes from SDD certificates and exact residual SAT.

Each variable has a permanent gated equality

    e_v -> (x_v^0 == x_v^1).

For one current witness of support D, setting e_v for every coordinate outside
D ensures a future witness uses only D. The deletion test for v adds e_v as
an assumption. On SAT, the decoded smaller support replaces D. On UNSAT, v
is retained. Repeating for the initial coordinates yields an inclusion-minimal
support. Assignments and contexts may change after each SAT query; merely
editing a previous assignment would not implement this search.

If the initial support width is d, at most d deletion queries follow the
initial witness query. The proof is elementary: every coordinate is considered
at most once; each successful test permanently tightens the equality set;
an earlier UNSAT deletion remains UNSAT under further equality constraints.
Thus every remaining coordinate is necessary relative to the final permitted
support. This is not minimum-cardinality support, a bound on d, a pairwise
localization theorem, or a runtime bound independent of SAT difficulty.

For each failed deletion the implementation records the equality assumptions
appearing in the solver's UNSAT core. These cores also depend on the complete
cut-selector assumptions and the permanent defect formula; the stored subset
is diagnostic only. No minimal-core claim, pairwise inference, group-testing
speedup, or additional use of cores in the objective is made. Deterministic
coordinate deletion was chosen to keep the query accounting and evidence
sound and reproducible.

The all-equal relation with models `0^n` and `1^n` is implemented as a CNF
equating every variable with x1. For n=3 through 8, the real backend confirms
that balanced-cut shrinking retains all n coordinates. No singleton pair is
emitted. Additional seeded random cases verify the four decoded truth values,
support crossing of an independently computed semantic prime, and deletion
minimality with fresh equality assumptions. Raw witnesses and counters are in
`data/hybrid_validation.json`.

The real-backend run completed 46 witness checks and 80 fresh support-deletion
minimality queries with zero discrepancies, including all six all-equal
instances n=3..8. These are finite implementation checks, not an extension of
the infinite-family proof by experiment.

Defect extraction incurs encoding, SAT probing, shrinking, and support
processing costs. The benchmark must charge all of them to M4/M5 even when
the resulting hyperedges do not change the selected vtree. A reduction in
residual work alone does not establish a total-runtime improvement.

# Persistent exact four-corner SAT

`code/hybrid_core.py::FourCornerSession` constructs one fixed Tseitin CNF and
one PySAT `g4` (Glucose 4.1 binding) session. The construction independently
reimplements the logical encoding in archived Phase 4
`code/incremental_four_corner.py`; no archive file is modified or imported at
runtime. The new package is self-contained.

For each original variable there are assignment clones x0,x1 and a selector
s. Two ITE outputs supply the mixed corner coordinates. Every original CNF
clause output, formula output, ITE, and conjunction is defined by an
equivalence. In particular the encoder supports empty clauses and empty CNFs.
The four formula outputs F00,F01,F10,F11 satisfy the permanent defect assertion

    (F00 AND F11) XOR (F01 AND F10).

One complete selector assumption vector specifies a candidate cut. SAT
returns an explicit rank-two four-corner witness. UNSAT certifies that all
nonzero rows of the cut matrix agree, hence exact AND separability for the
nonfalse function. The persistent solver and base clauses are reused across
every residual query in one factorization, so learned clauses remain available
under normal assumption semantics. We measure solver counters directly through
`accum_stats()`; reuse is an implementation fact, not a claimed speed advantage
over fresh solving without a paired experiment.

The hybrid first obtains a certified direct partition from actual SDD
structure. Each singleton is complete. Every nonsingleton is recursively
tested across all unordered nontrivial bipartitions, with its least coordinate
on the first side and a fixed increasing-cardinality order. A successful UNSAT
cut produces two independently certified factors and recursion continues.
Exhausting the cuts certifies the block prime. There is no truth-partition
shortcut for a block which an evaluator happens to know is prime.

Queries use the original global function: the proposed sub-block is on side
A, and all other variables are on its complement. This is sound because all
outside residual blocks are already certified independent factors. Multiplying
by a nonfalse outside factor cannot change whether the active factor is
separable across the proposed cut. This argument requires nonfalsity and a
certified starting partition; `exact_refine` documents that precondition and
does not accept a guessed partition as a certificate.

The exact semantic result is assembled before applying carrier information.
The returned simultaneous partition is the least common coarsening of the
semantic prime partition and the supplied carrier partition. This is exact
but can spend more work than a comparator which directly restricts residual
cuts to unions of carrier blocks. We intentionally preserve this distinction:
the benchmark measures semantic factorization plus carrier assembly, and
does not claim an optimal carrier-constrained residual implementation.

Residual metrics include base construction time, SAT wall time, SAT calls,
variables/clauses, accumulated conflicts/decisions/propagations/restarts, and
complete residual wall time. No conflict, learned-clause, or solver speedup is
inferred merely from a reduced encoding or number of queries.

Worst-case enumeration is exponential in unresolved block size. If initial
block sizes are b_i, this implementation uses at most

    sum_i (2^b_i - b_i - 1)

four-corner oracle calls, counting recursive queries. The simpler sum of
`2^(b_i-1)-1` only bounds a single pass, not all recursive retesting. This is
an oracle-query bound, not an FPT runtime theorem: the global SAT encoding
still contains all original variables and clauses.

`code/validate_hybrid.py` compares the persistent backend to independent model
projection/cardinality criteria on every nontrivial cut of its small-function
and seeded CNF test subset. Complete semantic results and carrier LCCs are
also checked against separate brute-force relation/graph implementations.

The recorded backend validation passed 1,390 independent cut comparisons and
881 complete semantic-factorization comparisons, together with 881 carrier
LCC comparisons. There were zero discrepancies. These finite computations
support the implementation; the mathematical correctness argument remains
separate from empirical testing.

## Measured reuse diagnostic

Real Glucose4 comparisons completed 180 runs and 14,220 exact cut-answer checks. Persistent/fresh-same-base paired geometric end-to-end ratio is 0.124832; persistent/fresh-cut-specific-Phase3 ratio is 0.106228. This closes the archived claim's measurement gap only on a small training-only all-cuts workload. It is known incremental-SAT engineering, not a new vtree-search gain or a measured learned-clause count. Full scope and component times: SUPPLEMENTARY_DIAGNOSTICS.md.

# Actual compressed-SDD pipeline

The implementation is `code/hybrid_core.py::compile_extract`. It uses PySDD's
C-backed SDD manager, with an explicit complete vtree read from a temporary
`.vtree` file. Input labels and CNF variables are one based. The word
"industrial" in the requested filename denotes use of an actual maintained
compiler backend; it does not establish industrial-scale performance.

Each CNF clause is built by SDD disjunction, and the formula by conjunction.
Automatic garbage collection and minimization are disabled during ordinary
compilation to preserve the specified input vtree. The finished root is
referenced before optional `manager.minimize()`. B2 uses this actual library
operation; the returned tree is read back from the manager after minimization.
Other searches compile their candidate trees explicitly, charging every
compilation to the method. Recompilation is consequently a material limitation
against the library's in-place dynamic search.

`sdd_size = root.size()` counts reachable decision elements and
`sdd_count = root.count()` counts reachable decision nodes. Constants and
literals have zero decision size; neither measure is a truth-table emulation.
These root-reachable quantities differ from manager-wide live/dead allocations.
Compilation time includes vtree serialization/read, manager initialization,
and CNF Apply operations. Extraction and optional minimization are separate
times. Overall benchmark wall time must additionally include search, defects,
residual SAT, final assembly, and cleanup.

Extraction follows the reproduced compressed-cut criterion. At a decision
node normalized at its vtree split, there is an AND split exactly when one
nonfalse sub remains. Its prime and sub become the two factors. Two or more
nonfalse subs leave the entire scope unresolved. True scopes and literal
scopes factor into singleton coordinates, including free variables.

PySDD uses trimmed nodes. A node can be normalized strictly below the current
declared vtree scope. The extractor locates that descendant subtree and treats
the other branch as true; it does not inspect the descendant's decomposition
as though it were the ancestor's decomposition. This normalization is required
for sound extraction in the presence of omitted/free variables. Extraction is
tested both before and after library minimization.

The result is the finest partition whose blocks are vtree clusters, not in
general the semantic prime partition. Every exposed nonsingleton block remains
a residual block until exact SAT refinement finishes. Therefore "direct block
count" is a legitimate objective, whereas "direct prime count" needs an
independent evaluation comparison. Only singleton exposed blocks are counted
as directly resolved in ground-truth-free operational statistics. If an
evaluation table counts nonsingleton exposed prime factors, that statistic
must be explicitly marked evaluation-only.

False formulas are reported as `satisfiable=false` and `direct_partition=null`.
The canonical nonfalse factorization contract does not assign them a claimed
prime partition. The benchmark runner must retain and report such cases under
its fixed eligibility rule rather than silently treating false as true.

`code/validate_hybrid.py` compares actual extracted partitions against a
separate exhaustive relation-projection test for all functions through three
variables, all three labelled unordered three-leaf vtrees, random cases up to
eight variables, free/literal/trimmed-node cases, and dynamically minimized
trees. Machine-readable counts are in `data/hybrid_validation.json`; the
principal validation stdout is archived in `logs/hybrid_validation.log`.

The actual backend run passed: 903 compilations, including 113 dynamic
minimizations; 881 nonfalse direct partitions agreed exactly with independent
model projections, and all 22 false inputs were reported explicitly. No
discrepancy occurred. The complete combined validation took 9.06 seconds on
the recorded environment; this is correctness-validation time, not a method
performance comparison.

No unrestricted structured-d-DNNF factor-extraction claim is made.

The API contracts used here were checked against the maintained
[PySDD SddNode documentation](https://pysdd.readthedocs.io/en/latest/classes/SddNode.html)
and [Vtree documentation](https://pysdd.readthedocs.io/en/latest/classes/Vtree.html)
on 29 September 2026. Installed-version execution is the operational authority;
the documentation's displayed release label is older than the installed wheel.

# Focused literature and priority audit

Search date and cutoff: **2026-09-29**. Scope: the claims in this Phase 5B implementation and the frozen structural results. This is a focused web audit, not a systematic review or proof that no antecedent exists. Primary publisher pages, author-hosted papers, author repositories, and author-deposited artifacts support the entries. Search queries and limitations are recorded in `data/literature_search_log.json`.

**Priority verdict:** dynamic vtree search, SDD minimization, graph/hypergraph-guided compilation, independent-component decomposition, SAT/QBF bi-decomposition, and monotone support deletion are established techniques. The Phase 5B contribution is a verified application and a bounded experimental evaluation of the factor-exposure objective. The proofs can survive even if the algorithmic result is a NO-GO, but their validity is not a novelty certificate. No firstness claim is made.

## Claim-by-claim matrix

| Claim or ingredient | Primary antecedent / evidence | Classification and safe claim |
|---|---|---|
| Dynamic vtree rotations and child swaps | Choi and Darwiche, AAAI 2013 [R1] | Established prior art; never claim the neighborhood itself is new |
| Optimize compressed SDD size by dynamic search | [R1] | Established baseline; must compare with the library's own minimizer |
| Treewidth/dtree/vtree-guided compilation | Bova and Szeider 2017 [R6]; de Colnet 2024 [R5]; TDD 2026 [R10] | Established theory and practice; a basic min-fill implementation is only a modest baseline |
| Dynamic hypergraph partitioning and components | Lagniez and Marquis 2017 [R4] | Established compiler design; carrier/defect inputs do not confer novelty on partitioning |
| Persistent SAT across Boolean bi-decomposition queries | Lee, Jiang and Hung 2008 [R2] | Established technique; selectors are a concrete encoding, not a new paradigm |
| QBF partition optimization for decomposition | Chen, Janota and Marques-Silva 2012 [R3] | Established technique and disjointness/balance objectives |
| Direct compressed-cofactor cut test | Mathematical proof in this package, grounded in SDD cofactor semantics | Valid elementary consequence; exact first appearance not determined |
| Global factor-exposure optimum F1 | Mathematical proof in this package | Valid project formulation; existence does not imply efficient search or new general decomposition theory |
| Laminar carrier/semantic obstruction F2 | Standard hierarchy/clade property, proof supplied | Known combinatorial fact applied to the project; do not market as discovery of laminarity |
| Defect support crosses some prime block F3 | Explicit rank/product proof supplied | Supported theorem; exact prior formulation unresolved; only existential crossing is certified |
| Pairwise localization NO-GO for the two-point equality relation | Explicit proof and checks supplied | Supported counterexample; elementary structure, no firstness claim |
| Read-once CM gate-rank recursion | Classical read-once functions [R14]; proof supplied | Compact CM formulation within a well-studied class; not a new efficient read-once factorization paradigm |
| Canonical Cartesian prime factorization | World-set relation factorization [R15] | Established broader concept; representation-sensitive complexity matters |
| Greedy equality-assumption support minimization | MSMP literature [R7,R8] | Known technique applied to a CM defect predicate |
| Output-sensitive group-deletion query bound | Generic monotone-predicate/group-deletion reasoning [R7,R8] | Proved here for clarity; not asserted novel, not a SAT-runtime/FPT result |
| Soft support hyperedges in a factor-exposure score | The concrete implementation and experiments | Potentially distinctive application; no comprehensive priority clearance, no correctness content beyond F3 |
| Compilation objectives beyond representation size | QBF decomposition quality [R3], query-dependent utility [R11], circuit-aware simplification [R9] | Broad novelty claim is untenable; distinguish the exact factor-exposure objective from adjacent objectives |
| Semantic vtree construction | 2026 NeSy author artifact [R12] | Closely adjacent recent work; paper-level comparison remains a publication prerequisite |
| Circuit graph/min-cut vtree initialization | 2026 TPM workshop [R13] | Direct recent antecedent for weighted interaction-graph/static construction |
| Industrial total-runtime improvement | Requires this package's preregistered held-out evidence | Empirical contribution only; maintained tools on small instances are not industrial-scale validation |

## Primary references and implications

**[R1] Arthur Choi and Adnan Darwiche. Dynamic Minimization of Sentential Decision Diagrams. AAAI 2013.** The paper explicitly navigates vtrees using rotations and child swaps and evaluates a dynamic size-minimization heuristic. Both operations and the search paradigm predate this project. [Publisher and DOI](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/8690).

**[R2] Ruei-Rung Lee, Jie-Hong Roland Jiang and Wei-Lun Hung. Bi-Decomposing Large Boolean Functions via Interpolation and Satisfiability Solving. DAC 2008.** Incremental SAT and interpolation are used to explore decompositions and variable partitions. A four-corner implementation cannot claim priority for incremental SAT bi-decomposition. [Author-hosted paper](https://alcom.ee.ntu.edu.tw/assets/publications/dac08-bd.pdf).

**[R3] Huan Chen, Mikoláš Janota and João Marques-Silva. QBF-Based Boolean Function Bi-Decomposition. DATE 2012; preprint 2011.** It optimizes disjointness and balancedness of variable partitions. This is relevant both to decomposition machinery and to objectives other than representation size. It does not by itself establish antecedence for the exact SDD-exposure objective here. [Author preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2313).

**[R4] Jean-Marie Lagniez and Pierre Marquis. An Improved Decision-DNNF Compiler. IJCAI 2017.** d4 combines disjoint-component analysis, component caching, and dynamic hypergraph partitioning. These are essential prior-art boundaries for syntax and hypergraph baselines. [Publisher](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2017/93).

**[R5] Alexis de Colnet. On the Relative Efficiency of Dynamic and Static Top-Down Compilation to Decision-DNNF. SAT 2024.** It studies dynamic graph partitioning versus static tree-decomposition guidance, showing separations in both directions for the modeled strategies. Therefore this pilot cannot claim one broad strategy universally dominates the other. [Publisher](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.SAT.2024.11).

**[R6] Simone Bova and Stefan Szeider. Circuit Treewidth, Sentential Decision, and Query Compilation. PODS 2017.** This is an established connection between treewidth, SDD structure and compilation parameters; factor-width terminology already has an independent technical meaning. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1145/3034786.3034787). The citation and topic were cross-checked in the current SAT 2026 TDD reference list [R10]; no uninspected theorem details from this paper are relied upon.

**[R7] João Marques-Silva, Mikoláš Janota and Anton Belov. Minimal Sets over Monotone Predicates in Boolean Formulae. CAV 2013.** This is direct prior art for reducing many minimal-set tasks to a common monotone-predicate problem. Equality-limited defect existence is another such predicate. [Author-hosted paper](https://sat.inesc-id.pt/~mikolas/cav13.pdf). See also the expanded reductions discussion in [Marques-Silva and Janota, 2014](https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.3011).

**[R8] Mikoláš Janota and João Marques-Silva. On the Query Complexity of Selecting Minimal Sets for Monotone Predicates. Artificial Intelligence 233, 2016.** It studies oracle-query bounds, including stronger witness-oracle results under structural restrictions on minimal sets. This makes a generic deletion or group-testing query bound a poor standalone novelty claim. The package's simple proof does not purport to reproduce all results of this paper. [Publisher/DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.artint.2016.01.002).

**[R9] Vincent Derkinderen and Jean-Marie Lagniez. Circuit-Aware d-DNNF Compilation. IJCAI 2025.** It uses original circuit structure and identifies/eliminates don't-care variables during compilation, with empirical benefits in solved instances and circuit size. Decomposition-aware use of semantics and original structure is an active area; the current project must identify its precise objective and certificate rather than claim generic semantic awareness. [Publisher](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2025/496).

**[R10] Florent Capelli, YooJung Choi, Stefan Mengel, Martín Muñoz and Guy Van den Broeck. A Canonical Generalization of OBDD. SAT 2026, published 2026-07-16.** It introduces Tree Decision Diagrams as structured d-DNNFs and relates compilation to treewidth and factor width. This is a nearby alternative representation, not evidence that arbitrary structured d-DNNFs support all SDD operations. [Publisher](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.SAT.2026.10).

**[R11] Kengo Nakamura, Masaaki Nishino and Norihito Yasuda. Variance Computation for Weighted Model Counting with Knowledge Compilation Approach. AAAI 2026, publisher date 2026-03-14.** It studies a downstream query that is tractable on structured d-DNNF but harder on several neighboring languages. It illustrates why query utility can matter beyond raw circuit size; it is **not** a direct antecedent for the factor-exposure search score. [Publisher](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/39007).

**[R12] Alexis de Colnet and Stefan Szeider. LLM-guided Semantic Vtrees for SDD Compilation. NeSy 2026.** The author-deposited artifact, published 2026-08-12, contains implementation, prompts, experimental data and a supplementary proof, and is independently listed in the NeSy program. Its semantic-vtree focus is close enough that an exact comparison is required before a submission. This audit inspected artifact metadata and conference listing, not the complete paper and supplement; no inference about an identical factor-exposure theorem is made. [Author artifact](https://zenodo.org/records/21900606), [conference program](https://2026.nesyconf.org/program/).

**[R13] Sander Verwimp, Annegret Seibt and Vincent Derkinderen. Growing Vtrees from Variable Orderings: Novel Static Heuristics for SDD Compilation. TPM 2026 workshop.** The workshop abstract describes a fan-in heuristic and a weighted interaction graph recursively partitioned by minimal cuts. This is directly relevant to graph-guided vtree initialization. Treat workshop status separately from archival publication. [Workshop abstract](https://tractable-probabilistic-modeling.github.io/tpm2026/papers/), [author dataset, published 2026-08-03](https://doi.org/10.48804/MQYNKZ).

**[R14] Functions That Are Read-Once on a Subset of Their Inputs. Discrete Applied Mathematics 46, 1993.** This primary paper builds on classical read-once characterizations. It is evidence of the established theory, not a theorem-by-theorem match for the arbitrary essential-binary-gate CM recursion. That exact match remains unresolved. [Publisher](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0166218X9390105W).

**[R15] Dan Olteanu, Christoph Koch and Lyublena Antova. These support the archive's decision not to assume cheap arbitrary structured-d-DNNF normalization. They do **not** prove that every possible direct factorization algorithm is impossible. Date: 2026-09-29. **Primary decision: D. MATHEMATICAL NOTE SURVIVES; ALGORITHMIC NO-GO.**

The frozen Phase 4/5 record reproduced, and a real PySDD + persistent Glucose4 exact pipeline now works. The new bounded pilot ran **2,100 trials** with **0 failures/timeouts** and no correctness disagreement. Against validation-selected B3, the primary carrier+defect+exposure method M5 had a paired geometric total-runtime ratio **2.212** (95% descriptive interval **[2.008, 2.428]**). Runtime and practical residual-work criteria are respectively **FAIL** and **FAIL**. This is a maintained-tool small-instance campaign, not industrial-scale validation.

## What is mathematically proved

Under their explicit nonfalse, compression, support-disjointness and essentiality hypotheses, the frozen compressed-SDD cut/exposure theorem, exposure optimum, laminar carrier obstruction, defect-support crossing lemma, equality-family localization obstruction, positive irredundant-CNF baseline and CM read-once recursion survive independent proof review. A new application note proves sound inclusion-minimal support shrinking and a group-deletion oracle-query bound. These do not imply minimum-cardinality support, FPT SAT runtime, efficient global vtree search or novel priority.

One prose claim is corrected: an externally certified prime-aligned tree needs no residual search, but an ordinary solver cannot infer primeness from a failed vtree cut. Every nonsingleton exposed block is exact-refined in this implementation, including the oracle tree. This correction is in the new ledger; historical files are unchanged.

## What is computationally reproduced

All six frozen campaigns and eleven archived artifacts match, excluding only timing/newline differences. Independent checks cover 458,745 cuts, 983,025 n=4 function/vtree pairs, 121,500 n=5 score calls and all 540 seeded n=5 inputs. Key counts remain 2,601 decomposable n=4 functions, fixed-tree full exposure 225, and exhaustive exposure optimum correct on all 65,535 nonfalse functions. Real-backend tests add 903 SDD compilations, 113 minimizations, 881 direct/semantic/carrier comparisons each and 1,390 SAT cuts, all with zero discrepancies.

## What is newly observed

Actual SDD element/node sizes, Glucose conflicts/decisions/propagations, wall times and process memory are now measured. The primary 70-instance/ten-method/three-repetition experiment freezes inputs and code, excludes oracle truth from all heuristic payloads, and charges recompilation/probe/refinement overhead. The held-out results and separate move/SAT-reuse diagnostics are recorded with full machine-readable data. The actual runtime conclusion is specific to this implementation and synthetic generator mix.

## What is prior art

Dynamic vtree rotations/swaps, SDD size minimization, graph/treewidth/hypergraph compilation, component decomposition, SAT/QBF bi-decomposition, Cartesian relation factorization, and monotone-predicate minimization all have substantial antecedents. The current audit includes 2025–2026 circuit-aware, semantic-vtree and alternative-representation work. No firstness claim is supported by absence from a web search.

## What failed and what remains open

The registered primary improvement gate was not cleared, and there is no practically meaningful residual-work rescue. Do not develop an algorithm paper around a post-hoc metric switch. Universal pairwise defect localization remains refuted. No efficient exposure-optimal search theorem, general small-support guarantee, unrestricted structured-d-DNNF extraction theorem or industrial runtime improvement is established. Native integration of alternative objectives is untested; the current custom search pays full recompilation costs. Carrier-compatible early residual refinement could avoid work done by the current semantic-first/final-LCC variant.

Six internal reviewer roles cover SDD, SAT/decomposition, graph/vtree, engineering/statistics, novelty and mathematics. They found and prompted provenance safeguards and the exposed-factor/prime-certificate correction, and imposed explicit limits on the relabeling-heavy tiny benchmark, modest graph baseline and biased candidate prefix. # Phase 4/5 frozen-claim reproduction audit

Date: 2026-09-29. Status: **PASS for the specified frozen campaigns, with scope qualifications below.**

## Execution and archive preservation

`code/reproduce_frozen.py` copied the eight archived Python sources byte-for-byte to `reproduction/frozen_original/`. It then wrote executable copies under `reproduction/relocated/` with only the archived Linux absolute import/output paths replaced by paths in this Phase 5B directory. No algorithm or random-number call was changed. The transformation manifest records every replacement and original/relocated SHA-256. Archived source hashes were checked again after execution and remained unchanged. Python bytecode generation was disabled.

All six campaigns exited successfully. Eleven frozen output artifacts match after parsing JSON/CSV or comparing text lines. The sole ignored JSON key is the archived `runtime_seconds`; platform newline differences are ignored. The JSON comparison retains all counts, examples, partitions, records, seeds and other values. Raw logs and machine-readable comparison results are in `reproduction/logs/` and `reproduction/frozen_comparison_report.json`.

The runtime was Python 3.10.11, Windows 10 build 19045, standard-library validation paths. The frozen subprocesses used `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` and `-B`. These reproductions make no industrial SAT or SDD runtime claim. Versions and commands are preserved in `reproduction/runtime.json` and the comparison report.

## Frozen campaign results

| Campaign | Reproduced result | Measured wall seconds |
|---|---|---:|
| Phase 4 compressed-cofactor/direct extraction | 65,535 nonfalse functions; 0 root-cut failures; 0 laminar-extraction failures; 2,601 decomposable; 2,376 hidden by the fixed balanced vtree | 19.419 |
| Phase 4 read-once operator trees | 10 essential binary connectives; 35,210 instances; 0 failures | 11.869 |
| Phase 4 controlled SAT comparator | 120 instances; 516 cut queries; 0 discrepancies; example DIMACS and assumption stream match | 3.197 |
| Phase 5 exhaustive n=4 | 65,535 functions; 15 non-plane labelled rooted binary vtrees; 225 fixed-balanced alignments among 2,601 decomposable functions; 65,535 global optima reach the prime partition | 14.029 |
| Phase 5 defect family | n=3,4,5,6; empty pairwise rank-two graph; one semantic prime; minimum balanced-cut witness support n | 0.187 |
| Phase 5 n=5 benchmark | Seed 20260929; 540 accepted instances, 180 per family; all 2,700 method records and 15 summary rows match | 1.857 |

The n=4 random-vtree alignment probability among decomposable functions is `0.2193771626297578`. The operator campaign is exhaustive for the frozen ordered-leaf tree families through n=4 and samples 30,000 n=5 draws with seed 123; sampling is with replacement and is not a claim of 30,000 distinct trees. The incremental seed is 41.

## Independent checks against circular scoring

Merely rerunning Phase 5 would be insufficient: its n=4/n=5 exposure scores are computed from the already known semantic prime partition. The new audit therefore implemented independent relational-projection computations.

For a nonempty relation R and disjoint L,R covering a variable set U, Cartesian factorability is checked by

`|projection_U(R)| = |projection_L(R)| * |projection_R(R)|`.

Projection sets are constructed directly from satisfying assignments. Factor extraction recursively applies this product-cardinality check and never receives the prime partition as an input. To compute the n=4 reference prime partition independently, all 15 set partitions are enumerated and their projection-product cardinalities checked; the unique valid partition with most blocks is selected. This implementation is separate from the archive's rank-cut intersection construction.

- All 65,535 independently derived n=4 prime partitions agree with the archive.
- All 458,745 unordered n=4 cut checks agree between directly constructed compressed nonzero cofactor sets and the projection-product criterion.
- All 983,025 n=4 function/vtree direct-exposure partitions agree with the archive's prime-derived shortcut.
- All 952,569 prime-aligned n=4 function/vtree pairs return the full prime partition under the independent extraction.
- During an instrumented replay of the frozen n=5 seed, all 121,500 exposure calls agree with independent direct projections; frozen outputs still match. Instrumentation consumes no random numbers.

The n=5 accepted CNFs, truth-table integers, family and instance identifiers are now saved explicitly in `reproduction/frozen_n5_accepted_instance_manifest.json`. The archive supplied a generator and seed but did not preserve these per-instance CNFs. The new manifest is a reconstruction, not an original archived artifact.

Machine-readable evidence is in `reproduction/independent_n4_audit.json` and `reproduction/independent_n5_audit.json`. These checks validate the frozen shortcut's values. They do **not** convert exhaustive oracle-assisted search into a scalable, non-oracle heuristic. The frozen n=5 carrier modes also consult the known prime partition to construct aligned/crossing cases; that is labelled benchmark generation/control, not information a production objective may consume.

## Assumptions and limitations carried forward

1. **Nonempty relations.** The SDD and prime-partition theorem statements exclude the false function. All exhaustive n=4 and accepted n=5 campaigns obey this. A replay of the frozen incremental generator finds 16 false formulas among its 120 trials (IDs saved in `reproduction/assumptions_audit.json`). Four-corner encoding equivalence still holds on them, but they cannot establish uniqueness of a nonempty-relation prime factorization. New pipelines should handle false inputs explicitly before using prime-factor claims.

2. **Prime alignment is a promise or certificate.** If all semantic prime blocks are vtree clades, direct extraction returns the full partition; this mathematical implication is correct. However, a failed root SDD cut says only that this particular cut fails. It does not certify that the resulting unresolved block is semantically prime. On the balanced tree `((0,1),(2,3))`, both `(x0=x2) AND (x1=x3)` (truth bits 33825) and the all-equal function (truth bits 32769) return one direct block, although the former has two crossing semantic primes. Thus a measured zero-residual shortcut requires independently certified primeness or an explicit theorem-class/prime-alignment promise. An oracle-aligned control must not silently supply that certificate to heuristic runs.

3. **Local truth-table coordinate order.** The Phase 4 `row_patterns` routine expects truth bits in the order `leaves(tree)` and does not remap global variable indices. Its frozen fixed-order use is correct. Reusing it on arbitrarily permuted vtrees requires a truth-table permutation. The independent audit uses original-coordinate projection masks and avoids this issue.

4. **Representation restrictions.** The compressed-SDD criterion assumes a complete compressed partition with exhaustive, disjoint, nonfalse primes; “at most one nonfalse sub” relies on compression. Uncompressed or arbitrary structured d-DNNF syntax does not inherit this syntactic test. True/free variables require singleton handling; false functions require a separate convention. The operator result assumes essential connectives and support-disjoint, read-once leaves, not general shared DAGs.

5. **Correctness versus performance.** The archived controlled comparator restarts its bundled DPLL search. It verifies the encoding and witness semantics; it does not demonstrate learned-clause amortization. Frozen n=4/n=5 scripts manipulate exact tables/prime partitions and do not measure maintained-library SDD size or an end-to-end industrial runtime. The separate archived clause-emission table has no bundled standalone generator; this audit does not present it as newly reproduced timing evidence.

6. **Proof versus finite evidence.** Finite exhaustive checks support implementations and discover counterexamples; they do not replace general proofs. The n=3..6 defect computations instantiate the archived all-equal counterexample family. The general family argument remains a mathematical statement, not a conclusion inferred solely from those four computations.

## Reproduce

From the Phase 5B directory, with its sibling `continuity_archive/` present:

```powershell
python -B code/reproduce_frozen.py
```

Use `--mode frozen` to run only the archived campaigns, or `--mode independent` to rerun the independent audit using the relocated copies. The script writes only inside `phase5b_output/reproduction/`; a rerun replaces its own reproduction outputs. Approximate complete wall time on the recorded machine was under two minutes. No external package installation is required.

The frozen-result gate is satisfied. Subsequent adaptation claims must use the new non-oracle pipeline and its separately frozen benchmark split; the archived oracle scores remain explicit controls/evaluation only.

# Phase 5B research ledger

Date: 2026-09-29. All new work is under `phase5b_output`. The sibling `continuity_archive` preserves the submitted archive byte for byte. The original ZIP SHA-256 is `21dcbd6747c407bbd7c0ceaf8f9fab87e64e8a8822db95931f46d69f9b85000a`.

## Orientation and reproduction

- Extracted the 117-file archive safely, rejecting traversal/symlink paths and refusing to overwrite an existing extraction target. Read the five requested handoff files in order, then the Phase 5 master/gate/theorem note and Phase 4 master/SDD/SAT/hybrid/operator documents. Treated the invoked Phase 5B prompt as the scoped work specification; unrelated broader-context files remain provenance, not new instructions.
- Copied frozen code before executing. Relocated only hard-coded `/mnt/data` paths in executable copies, recording hashes and every substitution. No archived source or data was overwritten.
- Reproduced all six campaigns and eleven archived output artifacts. Added independent model/projection/cofactor checks rather than relying solely on archived exposure computed from semantic truth. Reproduction gate passed before any new method run.
- Confirmed two interpretation boundaries: sixteen frozen random SAT-validation inputs are false (encoding equivalence still holds), and the fixed-order truth-table helper needs coordinate remapping on permuted trees.
- Corrected the Phase 4/5 prose implication that apparent prime alignment eliminates all residual certification. A true externally certified alignment promise suffices; an ordinary failed vtree cut does not certify unrestricted primeness. New code refines every nonsingleton exposed block.

## Tooling and exact implementation

- Installed actual PySDD 1.0.6 and PySAT 1.9.dev15/Glucose4, plus pinned supporting packages. Initial pip attempts stalled writing the external cache. A traceback identified that path; `--no-cache-dir` resolved it without changing permission settings. Logs preserve the attempts and dependency check.
- Implemented real compressed-SDD extraction, trimmed-node handling, native minimization, persistent four-corner SAT, equality-assumption witness shrinking, and exact final carrier LCC. The pipeline semantically refines direct blocks before final carrier assembly; this is sound but may do avoidable work compared with carrier-compatible residual refinement.
- Real-backend validation passed: 903 compilations, 113 minimizations, 881 direct/semantic/carrier comparisons each, 1,390 cut checks, 46 witness checks and 80 minimality checks. False inputs are separately identified.

## Protocol and review before outcomes

- Froze 70 generated CNFs, ten named families, train/validation/held-out splits, three replicate seeds, ten methods, 12-candidate M search budgets and fixed unit coefficients. No weights were tuned. Primary is total exact runtime, with M5 versus validation-selected B2/B3. Registered a separate practical residual-work threshold before data.
- Internal graph/statistics review found structurally overlapping relabelled families, a modest min-fill-order baseline, label-biased candidate prefixes, and native-minimization versus full-recompilation asymmetry. These restrict interpretation; the manifest and budget were not post-hoc improved.
- Repaired split receipt overwriting before benchmark runs. Resumption now requires identical source/protocol hashes, and rows carry the run fingerprint. Added baseline-selection guard, full-cell/fingerprint checking, and explicit zero/censoring rules before held-out.
- Heuristic workers receive only inputs and seeds. Oracle Pi enters only O; evaluator truth and direct-prime labels are attached after workers finish. Defect unions are soft span features; witnesses retain U/W and only singleton/singleton supports are flagged as sound pairwise links.

## Theorems and priority

- Independently reconstructed the cut/exposure, laminar compatibility, defect-support, equality counterexample, positive irredundant CNF and essential read-once CM proofs with explicit hypotheses.
- Proved equality-assumption greedy inclusion-minimization (at most initial support width extra queries), and a balanced group-deletion output-sensitive bound. These are applications of established monotone-predicate minimization, not novelty claims or FPT runtime theorems. The pilot uses greedy shrinking; the group variant is an independent theorem/check.
- Current primary-source search covered dynamic vtrees, size minimization, graph/hypergraph compilation, SAT/QBF decomposition, alternative objectives and 2025–2026 work. Recent semantic-vtree work and MSMP antecedents narrow any priority claim. No firstness or publication readiness is established.

## Final outcome and subsequent checks

Principal-run receipts, validation selection, statistical summary, move diagnostics, SAT reuse comparison, public smoke controls and final six-role review are the authoritative machine-readable outcome record. The master report and next gate state the single final decision. Source archives are checked again during package assembly; package checksums cover every delivered file.

No source changes, new weights, or new primary benchmark families are allowed in response to held-out outcomes. Any future algorithm change requires a fresh preregistered campaign. This task continues through packaging because the active provenance and review state are needed; a later independently designed scaling campaign should use the concise next-gate handoff.

# Independent engineering, statistics and graph-baseline review

Date: 2026-09-29. Review performed by the frozen-reproduction agent, separate from the primary benchmark implementation. This is an internal adversarial review, not an external peer review. No held-out method was run for this review; findings below follow from source and protocol inspection before benchmarking.

Reviewed SHA-256 values at the final inspection:

| File | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md | c6a535c34ff11e67ed0056baa09f0d82c36cdeeee45ac13ca97a45052f6ff43a |
| code/make_benchmarks.py | 62a07cf7e66e6481f0cd395df595a8c758463c90c497db22aec1384b8d53ca8d |
| code/benchmark.py | 0b14e6fd55a05113a30b9f2ec886cc87fb787d8f5153f2867ade2c026e04ad25 |
| code/hybrid_core.py | c162c115fc8c97e82f5eaa6d05429ebf5b07a7ea61dc68e060875182b54c0abc |

## Verdict

The design is suitable for a **small maintained-backend implementation pilot**, subject to completing the preregistered analysis/selection checks below. It cannot support an industrial-performance GO under any observed result. No semantic-ground-truth leakage was found in the non-oracle objective or exact residual algorithm. The exactness argument appears sound under its stated nonfalse input and certified direct-partition contracts; backend tests remain necessary and are reported separately.

## Issues requiring action or explicit restriction

### E1 — Structural overlap makes held-out generalization weak [high; reporting restriction]

Most n=6/n=8 train, validation and held-out inputs are variable-renamed copies of one structure per family. Clean/aligned/crossing cases share the same conjunction-of-equalities semantics. The bounded-treewidth family is a directed implication path, the read-once family is an AND of binary OR clauses, and the indecomposable control is an equality chain. Redundant and repeated-module families add a fixed pattern of implied cross-clauses. Most variation is variable naming; n=10 introduces a size change, not a new structural family. Only the planted random-CNF family has substantially different clause structures across seeds.

**Required treatment:** report this as a fixed-generator/relabeling pilot. Instance-bootstrap intervals quantify variation within this specific finite mix and are not independent evidence of generalization to industrial circuits or unseen structural families. The primary split must remain unchanged now that registered; an expanded independently structured benchmark is a later gate, not a post-hoc substitution. A numerical pilot GO is at most authorization to investigate further. An industrial algorithmic claim remains NO-GO/not established regardless of the pilot ratio.

### E2 — Resume could silently mix source versions [high; repaired before runs]

Initial inspection found that `run_split` overwrote the split receipt while reusing existing result rows. A repair was requested immediately. The rechecked implementation now rejects changed source/protocol/manifest hashes, rejects existing rows without a receipt, retains the first receipt, and adds a `run_fingerprint` to each new row. This resolves the identified flaw for new runs. Correctness repairs after data collection must preserve old rows in an explicitly invalidated run directory; they cannot inherit the old successes.

**Analysis follow-through:** verify row fingerprints against the receipt and reject duplicate/missing `(instance, method, replicate)` cells. A receipt match by itself does not prove the JSONL is complete.

### E3 — Baseline selection and analysis must be frozen before held-out [high; operational check required]

The protocol correctly selects B2 or B3 on validation and names M5 as the sole primary challenger. At review time the runner accepts `heldout` without checking a saved baseline-selection artifact, and no aggregation script was part of the requested review.

# SDD and SAT specialist adversarial audit

This is a self-audit of the backend implementation, not an independent
external referee report. A separate agent should still inspect the benchmark
and aggregate claims. Validation counts below are stored in the machine-readable
test report rather than copied before the run completes.

Backend validation is now complete: 903 real SDD compilations, 113 dynamic
minimizations, 881 direct/semantic/carrier comparisons of each type, 1,390 SAT
cut comparisons, 46 witness checks, and 80 deletion-minimality queries; zero
discrepancies. The 22 false cases were correctly marked outside the nonfalse
factorization contract.

1. **Trimmed nodes can invalidate a naive extractor.** A literal or decision
   normalized below the queried vtree node is not the ancestor's decision
   partition. Resolution: the implementation descends the appropriate branch,
   splits the complementary true scope into free singleton factors, and checks
   the final partition against model projections, including after minimization.

2. **One exposed block is not automatically one proved prime.** A failed root
   split may conceal cross-vtree factors. Resolution: all nonsingleton direct
   blocks receive exact residual search. Objective terms based on exposed
   nonsingletons are labelled block exposure/residual estimates; any actual
   direct-prime statistic requires evaluation-only truth labels.

3. **False formulas have no claimed canonical nonfalse prime partition.**
   Resolution: the compiler returns an explicit false status; benchmark
   eligibility/censoring must preserve the preregistered rule and record them.

4. **Global residual queries can be unsound without certified outside
   factors.** Resolution: exact_refine requires a partition returned by sound
   extraction; the global-query argument uses nonfalsity and independently
   certified outside factors. An arbitrary heuristic partition must never be
   supplied as though it were a certificate.

5. **A reused encoding is not necessarily a reused solver.** Resolution: the
   new backend holds one PySAT g4 solver across all residual cuts, with complete
   cut assumptions. Clauses and auxiliary equivalences remain permanent. Solver
   counters are read directly. No fresh-versus-persistent speedup is claimed
   without a separate experiment.

6. **Full four-corner equivalence is essential.** One-direction Tseitin
   implications would admit spurious defects. Resolution: all clause,
   conjunction, ITE and formula outputs are equivalences, including empty
   clause/formula cases; validation compares queried cuts directly to finite
   relations rather than to another copy of the same encoder.

7. **Shrinking fixed assignments is not support minimization.** Resolution:
   the SAT session enforces clone equality outside a candidate support while
   allowing the witness context to change. Final supports are tested for
   deletion minimality. The claim is inclusion minimality, not smallest width.

8. **Hyperedges do not imply all-pairs dependence.** Resolution: U and W remain
   separate supports; only singleton/singleton records carry a must-link flag.
   Soft similarity derived from a larger hyperedge must not become a correctness
   constraint. All-equal n=3..8 test cases force higher-order witnesses.

9. **Dynamic baseline and recompilation search have different overheads.**
   Resolution: B2 uses actual manager minimization while custom candidate
   searches explicitly recompile. This favors the established baseline in a
   realistic way and limits conclusions about objective quality apart from
   implementation overhead. All such overhead belongs in total wall time.

10. **Carrier-constrained residual search is potentially stronger than this
    implementation.** Resolution: we first solve semantic primes then apply
    LCC, which is exact but may expend unnecessary work. Claims must name this
    pipeline and cannot assert dominance over all carrier-aware exact solvers.

11. **Oracle-query bounds are not runtime theorems.** Resolution: the stated
    bounds count queries only. The global CNF still contains all input variables;
    no parameterized time guarantee for this implementation follows merely
    from small direct blocks or narrow returned supports.

12. **Actual backends do not make tiny synthetic inputs industrial evidence.**
    Resolution: reserve industrial-performance claims for sufficiently large,
    representative held-out inputs and meaningful paired total-runtime gains.
    Tool availability establishes an implementation gate only.

## Independent audit of principal benchmark integration

The backend author separately reviewed the root agent's `code/benchmark.py`
(SHA256 `b377a3a8def9ddbcf426a5a5549313546160ff4faf55a8b57cde5ccdaad1d2b0`)

backend author's own work.

comparison limitation.

leakage blocker found. Non-oracle worker payloads do not contain truth
partitions; their objectives never call the exhaustive baseline. All exposed
nonsingleton blocks enter the exact residual solver. Evaluation-only prime
counts are attached after the worker returns. M4/M5 retain raw U/W witnesses,
although the soft penalty uses their union. Such a union penalty is a heuristic
preference, not a theorem asserting all those variables belong together.

The worker's algorithm clock starts after imports/input parsing and ends after
exact residual and carrier assembly. This matches the registered definition.
The 15-second process watchdog also includes startup/imports, so the effective
algorithm-time limit is slightly smaller and environment-dependent; record the
separate process wall time and any censoring. No material consequence can be
assumed until failure counts are inspected.

Required follow-through: the principal worker records structural move deltas
and compilation/extraction costs but deliberately omits measured residual SAT
cost for each candidate. `code/move_diagnostics.py` supplies this separately
after all primary runs, with independent exact agreement checks, a per-work
item watchdog, complete mapping back to every source move, and explicit reuse
of one measured residual result per unique instance/partition. The resulting
timings are exploratory and cannot be fed back into frozen objectives or
presented as independent per-occurrence timing replicates.

Review recommendation before results: permit the frozen pilot to run after the
PASS backend gate; retain all listed limitations and require the registered
held-out stopping rule. Neither these finite tests nor the integration audit
supports an industrial-runtime or novelty claim by itself.

SDD/SAT correctness blocker identified.** The completed principal campaign has
2,100 trials, no timeouts/errors, and agreement with independent semantic and
simultaneous partitions. M5/B3 has held-out paired geometric runtime ratio
2.211513, with M5 slower on all 30 held-out instances. The registered runtime
and practical residual-work gates fail. These findings support an algorithmic
NO-GO for this implementation and campaign, not a universal impossibility
claim about defect/exposure objectives or native SDD search.

The final master/results/statistics/next-gate reports preserve that distinction.
They explicitly retain the recompilation cost, weak graph baseline, fixed
neighbor-prefix bias, small structurally repetitive families, and absence of
industrial-scale evidence. They do not recast factor counts, query counts,
or an oracle-aligned control as a runtime improvement. The separate surviving
mathematical note is correctly labelled a working note without publication-ready
novelty; omitting a new paper draft is consistent with that priority outcome.

instance/partition residual measurements have zero errors, timeouts, or
semantic/simultaneous disagreements. Timings are reused explicitly across
occurrences, with full mapping, and are not independent repeated timing
measurements. The separate diagnostic provides the previously missing actual
parent/candidate SAT costs without contaminating the frozen heuristic.

One illustrative observed tradeoff is `repeated_module_heldout_n6`: a candidate
increases SDD elements from 17 to 18, exposes two direct blocks instead of one,
and reduces residual calls from 7 to 5. Its single cached SAT-wall observation
is approximately 0.092 ms lower. This is an exact structural/count observation
and a tiny exploratory timing difference; it neither proves a relation between
globally optimal objectives nor rescues the failed end-to-end gate. Most
explored moves have unchanged exposure; the full negative distribution must
remain alongside this example.

The training-only solver-reuse diagnostic uses an archived Phase 4 controlled
encoding shared byte-for-byte by its persistent and fresh-solver arms, while
its third arm rebuilds the Phase 3 cut-specific encoding. This isolates a
useful implementation question more cleanly than attributing encoding-size
differences to persistence. It uses real counters and independent cut checks,
and never measures or infers a learned-clause count. Any advantage in this
fixed-cut training workload must stay separate from the held-out vtree-method
NO-GO; it cannot establish a carrier/defect-search benefit.

The public documentation examples are appropriately labelled smoke controls.
They do not meet the separate future requirement for a meaningful licensed
public industrial corpus. A future native-objective experiment needs new
preregistration and structurally distinct held-out data; none is authorized
merely by this review. No additional algorithm work is required to accept the
current negative result and complete its reproducibility archive.

# Supplementary measured diagnostics

These experiments ran after all principal trials and baseline selection were final. They do not tune objectives, change the primary metric, or rescue the failed algorithmic gate.

## Actual persistent versus fresh SAT

Twenty training instances, three repetitions and three implementations yielded 180 complete runs and 14,220 independently checked cut answers, with zero discrepancies/timeouts. All cuts have the same deterministic order. The persistent/fresh-same-base comparison uses byte-identical controlled clauses; the third method constructs the original cut-specific Phase 3 formula. The controlled diagnostic deliberately uses the frozen Phase 4 encoder, without the new optional equality-support gates.

| SAT workload | Runs | Median end-to-end ms | Median solve ms | Total conflicts | Total propagations |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| persistent_controlled | 60 | 2.501 | 1.143 | 4545 | 483630 |
| fresh_solver_same_base | 60 | 26.476 | 2.045 | 16134 | 761217 |
| fresh_phase3_per_cut | 60 | 26.902 | 1.388 | 16821 | 571269 |


On paired instance medians, persistent/fresh-same-base geometric ratio is **0.124832**, and persistent/fresh-Phase3 is **0.106228**. This is real timing evidence for this small fixed-cut workload, including setup and encoding costs. It is not an encoding-size ratio. Repeated solver setup dominates much of the gap; neither retained learned-clause counts nor a causal attribution of all savings to learning is measured. Persistence is established prior art and already common to every principal method, so this result does not establish a new vtree adaptation benefit. Raw per-query counters/times and source hashes are preserved in data/sat_reuse_results.json.

## Move-by-move objective relation

The diagnostic maps all **10,440** evaluated move occurrences onto **1,020** distinct input/tree-pair moves and **174** distinct certified-partition residual measurements. Every measurement completed and agreed with independent semantic and simultaneous truth. One fresh process measures each unique input/partition once, then the measurement is explicitly reused in every matching move record. This is exploratory profiling, not repeated timing inference.

Size/exposure classes: {"both_equal": 417, "exposure_equal_size_changes": 457, "size_down_exposure_down": 0, "size_down_exposure_up": 0, "size_equal_exposure_changes": 0, "size_up_exposure_down": 145, "size_up_exposure_up": 1}.

Size/SAT-call Pareto classes: {"candidate_dominates_size_calls": 40, "equal_size_calls": 417, "parent_dominates_size_calls": 562, "tradeoff_size_calls": 1, "unavailable": 0}.

The one observed tradeoff is `repeated_module_heldout_n6`: actual SDD element size **17 to 18**, directly exposed blocks **1 to 2**, residual SAT calls **7 to 5**. The pure SAT solve-time diagnostic changes from 0.4224 to 0.3302 ms, while its complete residual-stage diagnostic changes from 22.587 to 27.750 ms. This illustrates why fewer calls and a tiny SAT-time difference are not automatically a total-runtime benefit. The latter timings are single measurements, not robust speed estimates.

`data/size_exposure_tradeoff_example.json` records CNF, both vtrees, partitions and measurements. It is a computational example of nonidentical size/exposure objectives. It does not show that globally size-optimal and globally exposure-optimal trees are necessarily disjoint, nor prove a general objective dominance theorem. No held-out move is selected to revise the frozen heuristic.

## Public controls

All three MIT-licensed official PySAT documentation CNFs passed, including one false formula handled outside the nonfalse prime-factor contract. Source URLs are in code/public_controls.py and data/public_control_results.json; attribution is retained in licenses/PySAT_LICENSE.txt. These are public smoke checks only. No public industrial corpus was run, and no result is described as industrial-scale validation.

# Phase 5B theorem, counterexample, and proof audit

Date: 2026-09-29. These are mathematical statements with explicit hypotheses; the pilot measurements are separate. None of the proofs establishes publication priority or an industrial speedup. Archived Phase 4/5 files have not been edited.

## Conventions

Let V be a finite declared Boolean variable set and let f be nonfalse. A valid disjoint AND partition P satisfies f = AND over B in P of f_B(x_B). Free variables remain singleton blocks, with the factor true. The canonical finest partition is Pi_f; every valid factor partition is its coarsening. This follows from the finite Cartesian-relation factorization property: if a nonempty relation is a product on two partitions, its projection on a block of either partition is itself the product of the projections on intersections, hence the relation also factors on the common refinement. Repeating over finitely many valid partitions gives the unique finest one. The nonfalse hypothesis matters to this projection argument; an implementation must report unsatisfiability separately rather than quietly applying these proofs to the empty relation.

A vtree is a rooted full binary tree with one leaf per declared variable. Mathematical exposure ignores left/right orientation, while actual SDD sizes and compiler behavior can depend on orientation. There are (2n-3)!! unordered-child labelled vtrees for n>=2: 15 at n=4, 105 at n=5.

## P4-SDD: exact compressed-SDD cut criterion

At a complete compressed decision on X|Y write f = OR_i (p_i AND s_i), with nonfalse, disjoint, exhaustive primes and semantically distinct subs. Each X-assignment satisfies exactly one prime, so its Y-cofactor equals that prime's sub. If f=g(X) AND h(Y), every such cofactor is either false or h. Conversely, if there is exactly one nonfalse sub h, its associated prime g satisfies f=g AND h. Nonfalse f rules out zero nonfalse subs. Therefore the criterion is exactly one nonfalse element, equivalently at most one under the nonfalse assumption.

This is also CM rank one: over F_2 every nonzero row of a rank-one Boolean matrix equals the same row. Trimmed implementations may place a node strictly below the requested vtree node; skipped sides are free and must be handled explicitly. Counting elements at an unrelated normalization node is not the stated criterion.

Apply this criterion at the current subtree. On success recurse into both factors, including true sides. On failure retain the subtree as one block. Any partition into proper clades below this subtree would separate its two children, contradicting the failed cut. Induction proves that E_T(f) is the finest valid partition whose blocks are clades of T. Failure does **not** imply unrestricted semantic primeness.

## F1: factor-exposure optimum

For every nonfalse f, max_T |E_T(f)| = |Pi_f|.

Proof: each E_T(f) is a valid partition and hence a coarsening of Pi_f, establishing the upper bound. Build a subtree on each prime block, then join these subtrees with an arbitrary binary skeleton. Each split in this skeleton separates unions of prime blocks, so the exact cut criterion succeeds until every prime-block root is reached. Within a prime block no nontrivial disjoint split succeeds. This vtree attains Pi_f. No assertion is needed about arbitrary internal splits *inside* a nonsingleton prime block. QED.

This proves existence of an optimal tree and correctness of a ground-truth-free exposure-count objective. It proves neither efficient search nor the ability to recognize that a found tree is globally optimal. All extraction certificates are factor certificates; they are not automatically prime-factor certificates.

### Certification correction: oracle alignment does not erase unknown work

If an external theorem or independently verified certificate establishes prime alignment, E_T(f)=Pi_f and no further SAT is needed. Without that certificate, a nonsingleton exposed block must still be tested for hidden cross-vtree factors. Even on an oracle-built aligned tree the ordinary solver cannot infer alignment merely from a failed subtree cut. Oracle evaluation may report true alignment or true directly exposed prime blocks after the run, but must not silently use those labels to stop algorithmic refinement or remove residual certification time.

A concrete failure is f=(x0 OR x2) AND (x1 OR x3), on T=((x0,x1),(x2,x3)). The root fails but Pi_f={{0,2},{1,3}}. Keeping the root as a final prime block would be incorrect.

## F2: carrier/semantic laminar obstruction

Two partitions P and Q of V can simultaneously be represented by vtree clades iff P union Q is laminar: intersecting blocks must contain one another.

Necessity: two rooted-tree clades are disjoint or one contains the other. Sufficiency: add V and every singleton to the laminar family, remove duplicates, and connect each proper member to its unique minimal strict superset. Children are disjoint and cover their parent because singleton sets were added. This is a rooted hierarchy with leaves V. Resolve every node with more than two children into a binary tree; existing clades persist. QED.

This is the standard laminar-hierarchy property, applied to the project partitions; no firstness claim is made. Example crossing partitions {{0,1},{2,3}} and {{0,2},{1,3}} cannot both be hard subtree constraints. Compatibility of a carrier with the current exposed coarsening does not certify compatibility with the unknown prime partition. A soft score is safe for efficiency; an unsupported hard lock is not.

For the simultaneous carrier/semantic problem, the required exact partition is LCC(Pi_K,Pi_f), the least common coarsening. Refining semantic factors first and taking this LCC is sound. Taking LCC with an incompletely refined exposed partition gives a valid coarsening, but need not give the finest simultaneous answer.

## F3: defect support and its exact information content

Fix cut A|B, row assignments a0,a1 and column assignments b0,b1. Let U be their differing coordinates in A and W their differing coordinates in B. A defect means

    f(a0,b0) f(a1,b1) XOR f(a0,b1) f(a1,b0) = 1.

Some prime block meets both U and W. To prove it, suppose no block does. After fixing all nonvarying coordinates, each prime factor depends on the row only, the column only, or neither. Its corner matrix is an outer product, possibly zero. Entrywise multiplication of such matrices remains an outer product. The determinant must vanish, contradiction. QED.

For U={x}, W={y}, x and y must belong to the same prime block. For larger supports, the assertion is existential. It does **not** say all of U union W lies in one prime block, or identify a sound edge for each cross pair. The natural certificate is the ordered support pair (U,W), with the witness assignments and four truth values retained. A single unlabelled hyperedge loses some of this information and is only a heuristic feature.

Counterexample to treating a whole support union as a must-link: EQ(x0,x1,x2) AND EQ(x3,x4), cut {0,3}|{1,2,4}, admits a defect whose support is all five variables, although its prime blocks have sizes three and two. The supplied independent check verifies this witness-support existence.

## F3-NO-GO: pairwise localization can fail completely

For n>=3 let f_n be true exactly at 0^n and 1^n. Every nontrivial Cartesian decomposition would combine the all-zero projection of one side with the all-one projection of the other, yielding a forbidden mixed model. Thus Pi_f={V}. Fixing n-2 coordinates leaves at most one satisfying entry in any two-variable slice, so every such slice has determinant zero. Across any nontrivial cut the full matrix has only two nonzero entries: the all-zero and all-one row/column pairs. A rank-two minor must select both, and its varying support is all n variables. This disproves universal singleton localization, even for a single semantic prime block. QED.

## P5-POS: irredundant positive CNF

Assume f is a conjunction of nonempty positive clauses, with duplicate clauses removed and no clause properly containing another. Its clause-interaction connected components, with isolated declared variables included, equal Pi_f.

For a positive clause C, f entails C iff some input clause is contained in C: the reverse direction is immediate; otherwise set all variables in C to zero and all other variables to one to obtain a countermodel. Thus the input antichain is exactly the set of positive prime implicates. Given any nonfalse disjoint factorization, its factors can be chosen as monotone projections by fixing satisfying assignments outside each factor. A prime clause C cannot span multiple factors: if no factor implies its local part of C, choose a satisfying assignment for each factor falsifying that local part, contradicting f entails C. If a factor implies a strict local part, C is not prime. Hence each clause lies inside one semantic block, forcing every interaction component into one block. Conversely the CNF explicitly factors across its interaction components. Both directions give equality. QED.

Irredundancy is essential. For f=x0 AND (x0 OR x1), the raw clause graph connects both variables but f=x0 with x1 free. This is a baseline structural fact, not a claim of a new factorization algorithm.

## P4-CM: read-once essential-gate recursion

Assume each leaf occurs once, children have disjoint supports, and every binary gate is essential in both inputs. Induction shows every descendant variable is essential: sensitize it in its child and select an attainable value of the other child that sensitizes the gate. Use the gate's 2x2 Boolean matrix over F_2, complemented entrywise when the requested output polarity is complemented.

Among the ten essential binary gates, rank one occurs precisely for the four signed conjunctions (one nonzero matrix entry); recursively concatenate the prime partitions of the children with the corresponding requested signs. In the rank-two case choose any left variable x and right variable y and independently sensitize each child. The resulting fixed-context two-variable matrix is the gate matrix up to row/column permutations, so its determinant is one. F3's singleton corollary puts x and y in the same prime block. Every cross pair is tied, so the whole support is one block. Leaves give singleton blocks in either polarity. This proves the two-polarity recursion. QED.

The read-once/disjoint-support hypothesis is indispensable: x XOR x is constant despite a rank-two XOR gate. A general shared DAG is outside the theorem. This elementary CM formulation does not supersede the established read-once Boolean-function literature.

## P5B-T1: output-sensitive defect-support minimization

Fix a cut and a correct permanent four-corner SAT encoding Phi. For S subset V define D(S) to mean that Phi is satisfiable together with x_v^(0)=x_v^(1) for every v outside S. Equality is imposed for coordinates outside S, without fixing their common value. Witnesses are allowed to change after each query. D is upward monotone: enlarging S removes equality constraints.

Given a known feasible starting support S0 of size m, sequentially try deleting each coordinate. Retain a deletion exactly when its SAT query succeeds. There are at most m additional queries and the final S is feasible and inclusion-minimal. Indeed a failed deletion at an earlier larger set stays infeasible at every smaller set by monotonicity. Every final witness uses all of S; otherwise its strictly smaller actual support would be feasible. The witness therefore certifies F3 on its two nonempty cut-side supports. This is inclusion-minimality, not minimum cardinality.

A balanced group-deletion variant has the output-sensitive bound

    number of SAT queries <= 1 + 2 d ceil(log2 m),

where d is the size of the support actually returned (m>=1). Place the initial support into any fixed balanced binary hierarchy of height ceil(log2 m). To process a group G, query D(current minus G). If SAT, delete G. If UNSAT and G is not singleton, recursively process its children; otherwise retain that singleton. A final support S is feasible. Every failed group intersects S: if it did not, S would be a feasible subset of the earlier candidate current minus G, contradicting UNSAT. At any depth the disjoint failed groups thus number at most d. Only children of failed groups are queried, so there are at most 2d queries at each nonroot depth and one root query. At every retained leaf, its failed deletion persists, proving inclusion-minimality. QED.

No uniqueness assumption is required for this output-sensitive bound. If every inclusion-minimal support has size at most a structural parameter d0, substitute d0 for d. Merely promising that *some* support has size d0 is insufficient: for EQ(x0,x1,x2) AND EQ(x3,x4) across {0,3}|{1,2,4}, minimal supports {0,1,2} and {3,4} coexist. Deletion order can return the larger one. The supplied finite check demonstrates both outcomes.

This is an application of generic monotone-predicate minimization/group deletion, not a new general minimization theorem. It counts oracle queries; SAT queries can still be hard. It gives no FPT wall-time result, does not prove a small residual partition, and gives no universal pairwise witness. Unsat cores of equality assumptions may accelerate an implementation only with a separate correctness argument: a core is not itself a defect witness and must not be converted automatically into semantic must-link edges. The production pilot uses sequential minimization; the group version is validated independently here as a theorem target, not an experimentally established performance advantage.

## Independent finite checks

`code/theory_independent_checks.py` imports no archived code. It checks laminar representability against all unordered-child labelled vtrees and all pairs of partitions through n=5, f_n support behavior across every nontrivial cut through n=8, the five-variable minimal-versus-minimum counterexample, and both deletion algorithms over every nonempty upward support predicate and every coordinate order through n=4. Data are `data/theory_independent_checks.json`; stdout is `logs/theory_independent_checks.log`. These finite checks support implementation confidence and do not replace the proofs above.

## What is not proved

There is no polynomial-time unrestricted semantic factor extraction theorem for arbitrary structured d-DNNFs here; no guaranteed vtree-search convergence bound; no general small-defect-width promise; no minimum-cardinality support bound from greedy deletion; no FPT hybrid runtime theorem; and no theorem that smaller SDDs expose more factors. Empirical Pareto cases must be labeled computational observations. The F1 optimum does not imply that a practical local optimum is semantically optimal.

## T4 implementation observation: size and exposure can trade off

A recorded real-SDD move for repeated_module_heldout_n6 increases size 17 to 18 while increasing exposure 1 to 2 and reducing residual calls 7 to 5. This is a reproducible finite computational observation, not a theorem about global optima or a priority claim. Exact inputs/vtrees are in data/size_exposure_tradeoff_example.json; timing limitations are in SUPPLEMENTARY_DIAGNOSTICS.md.
